seednet_fields.Parentage: Pusa Sugandh 3 is a fine grain aromatic type developed by IAR, New Delhi. However, the late maturity nature under the prevailing climatic situation in valley could not make it a popular variety. The pureline selection for earlines from the original stock of Pusa Sugandh 4 led to the development of new variety SKUA 494 (K416-14-3) which is 12-15 days earlier possessing aroma and other cooking quality at par with Pusa Sugandh 3.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Irrigated low land (plains basins of the valley) but not water submerged areas
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features:
1.	Among different spacing schedules, highest yield was recorded with 15x15 cm spacing.
2.	Among was obtained at 80:45:30 (N:P2O5:K2O)
3.	25 days older seedlings yielded significantly higher as compared to 35 days older seedlings. A 25% saving in RDF through FYM yielded at par with 100% RDF.
4.	The net profit estimated by cultivating SKUA-408 is Rs. 118000/ha and the benefit: cost ratio is 2:81:1
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics:
1.	Semi dwarf
2.	Erect plant type
3.	Compact plant and panicle type
4.	Long Panicle
5.	Erect flag leaf
6.	Basal leaf sheath colour is Green
7.	High 1000 grain weight (30 g)
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: The variety exhibits tolerance to blast and other diseases under normal field conditions and even under high natural disease pressure that prevailed during 2017 and 2018
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: No major pest has been identified so far

seednet_fields.Parentage: RGL 1231/Phalguna/RGL 1231/IR 36, Culture RGL 1880 selectet by pedigree selection.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Rainfed upland and low land ecology of North Coastal Zone of Andhra Pradesh during early kharif, kharif and rabi season
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Non lodging, non-shattering, dormant (4-5 days) and fertilizer responsive variety suitable for early Kharif, Kharif, late Kharif and Rabi, Seed rate 75 Kg/ha, recommended dose of fertilizers 80-60-50 kg NPK/ha in kharif and 100-60-50 kg NPK/ha in Rabi.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: Semi dwarf, compact tillering, plant type with 8-10 effective tillers per plant, green colour foliage with long slender grain type.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Distinguishing morphological Characters: Semi-dwarf, erect plant type, compact tillering with erect flag leaf, 8-10 effective tillers per plat, non-lodging., - Duration: Photo insensitive, - Flowering duration: Seed to flowering - 80 to 90 days, Seed to seed - 110 to 120 days;- Grain characters: - Kernel colour: White, - Scent: Absent, - Nature of kernel: Translucent, - Size of grain: Kernel length - 6.3 mm, Kernel breadth - 2.08 mm, 1/b ratio 3.03 ; 1000 grain wt.: 24-25 g ; abdominal white : very occasionally present ; awning : absent.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: No incidence of blast. Low incidence of sheath blight and bacterial leaf blight.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Field tolerant to Gallmidge biotype4, Low incidence of stem borer.

seednet_fields.Parentage: IR 78877-208-B-1-1/IRRI 132 Both parents were selected on the basis of their superiority under drought stress conditions.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Zone-II (Haryana) Zone-III (Odisha, Bihar and Jharkhand) Zone-V (Chhattisgarh) Zone-VI (Gujarat and Maharashtra).
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Semi-dwarf, resistant to lodging and shattering fertilizer responsive, tolerant to drought and suitable for direct seeded aerobic condition, sowing in Kharif season. Seed rate is 30 kg/ha.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: (i)Maturity duration-Early group. (ii)Plant height-105-110cm (Semi dwarf). (iii)Grain type-Short bold (SB),  Straw color hull and creamish white       kernel, (iv)  Long and well exerted Compact panicle with grain number, semi-erect flag leaf.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to sheath blight and false smut and tolerant to leaf blast, BLB, neck blast, RTD, brown spot, sheath rot under natural screening. Under artificiation screening, IET 25640 showed tolerance to leaf blast and sheath rot
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Tolerant to major pests like stem borer (dead heart and white ears head), plant hopper and leaf folder under natural screening
seednet_fields.Average Yield (Kg/Ha): The average yield of the variety is 4.96 t/ha, but the yield range from 4.5 to 5.5 t/ha. Kg/Ha
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Apply NPK @ 120:60:40 per hectare with one third of nitrogenous fertilizer full phosphorus & potash as basal dose. Second split of 1/3 nitrogenous fertilizer at tillering (40-45 days after sowing).

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features:
Suitable for sowing from January second fortnight
to February First Fortnight (Tables 28- 28c & 34).
It has good yield potential under different nitrogen
levels
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics:
i. Capsules are formed in clusters at leaf axil.
ii. Sparse hairiness on stem, flower, and capsule
iii. White with light purple color flower
iv. Four locules in capsule.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases:
Moderately resistant to powdery mildew,
cercospora leaf spot and phyllody under natural
conditions
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests:
JCS 1020 showed moderately resistant to leaf
webber and capsule borer
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha):
60 kg Nitrogen + 20 kg P205 and 20 kg K2O perhectare.
Half dose of Nitrogen, full dose of P205, K2O at sowing
& remaining half dose of Nitrogen as top dressing at 30-
40 DAS

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: ICAR-AICRP on Sorghum RVSKVV, College of Agriculture, Indore (Madhya Pradesh)
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: At all the level, SPV 2714 produced (54.99 t/ha) total fresh bioimass yield which was 12.66% higher than the check CSH 22SS (48.79 t/ha) at 100% RDF. SPV 2714 produced similar total dry biomass (19.72t/ha) as the check CSH 22SS (19.91%).
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Tall, drooping leaves, semi-loose panicle. It has greyed white seed.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: SPV 2714 was 28% superior to the check CSH 22SS for anthracnose resistance. For Leaf blight and grain mold SPV 2714 was at par with check.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: SPV 2714 was 5.4% superior for lower shoot fly dead heart formation against the check CSH 22SS. For stemborer tolerance it was at par to check 22SS.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha):
32 kg Nitrogen and 16 kg P2O5 per acre.
Apply half Nitrogen + full P2O5 at sowing and remaining Nitrogen at 30 (Days After Sowing) DAS.

and pods
Seed: Hilum is yellow as per DUS category but it is not

brown spot on micropile.

2 and MS

Slight Antixenosis against Spodoptera litura under controlled
condition and resistant to stem fly, girdle beetle and
defoliators in field condition.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Madhya Pradesh, Budelkhand region of Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Vidarbha and Marathwada regions of Maharashtra
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features:
1.	Amenable to mechanical harvesting. Strong stem and do not lodge.
2.	Pods of the NRC 150 do not shatter at least 15 days after maturity.
3.	It performs well under recommended dose of fertilizers 20 N, 60 P2O5 20 K2O and 20 S kg/ha
4.	It is suitable for sowing for Kharif season under normal sowing date (from 25th June to 7th July)
5.	Seed rate: 60 kg/ha
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics:
Hypocoty1 colour: Absent
Plant growth; semi determinate
No of branches: 3-4
Days-to-flower: 35.0 days
Flower colour: white
Pubescence: brown colour
Hillum colour: black
100 SW: 11.6 g
Biochemical marker: Absence of lipoxygenase-2 polypetide
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: NRC 150 showed variable resistant to stem fly, girdle beetle, and defoliators. NRC 150 showed SLY to Resistant high yielding (RHY) reaction against insect-pest complex.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): NPKS 25:60:40:20 (56 kg urea+375 kg SSP+67 kg MOP)

seednet_fields.Parentage:
CMS 7-1 A X RHA 6D-1
CMS 7-1-A is Cytoplasmic male sterile restore line and RHA 6 D-1 male fertile restore line received from ICAR- Indian Institute of Oilseed Research, Rajenderangar Hyderabad.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Gangetic alluvial zones of West Bengal under irrigated condition during rabi season
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features:
1.	Resistance to lodging.
2.	Response well to recommended fertilizer @ 75:112.5:75 kg N:P2O5:K2O/ha. With 60cmX30cm.spacing.
3.	Seed rate: 2 kg./ha.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Non branching, Triangular leaf shape, Dwarf stature, 20-22 cm head diameter
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to leaf curl, collar rot and moderately resistant to alternaria leaf spot powdery mildew and downy mildew
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): N:p2O5:K2O@75:112.5:75, N in three splits (50% as basal, 25% at 30 days after sowing and 25% at 45 days after sowing)

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Uttarakhand hills under irrigated and rainfed conditions.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: Plants are indeterminate vigorous in growth with standard leaf type ; the immature fruits are light green colour : the mature fruits are medium large, smooth round shaped and dark red in colour with slight locular impression.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Description of the variety/hybrid a. Plant height: 90.5 cm, b. Number of locules: 4-6, - Fruits/clusters: 10-35, - Fruits/plant: 6.4cm x 6.2 cm ; 100 seed wt. : 0.31 g.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: 1.	HI 1634 was higher yielding genotype (50.88 q/ha) in agronomic evaluation and significantly superior than check varieties HD 2932 (49.67 q/ha), HD 2864 and MP 3336, respectively. 2.	It showed significant increase (10.39 to 24.13% in overall mean) for grains/earhead over all the checks and qualifying variety CG 1029; and significant increase (3.6 to 7.9% in overall mean) for 1000 grain weight over all the checks.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: 1. Growth habit : Semi Erect 2. Anthocyanin Pigmentation     i) Coleoptiles : Green    ii) Auricles (Flag leaf stage) : Pale green   iii) Leaf Sheath : Absent 3. Leaf width (boot stage) : Medium 4. Leaf angle : Semi-erect 5. Waxiness     i) Leaf sheath (at ear emergence) : Very         Strong    ii) Flag leaf surface : Strong   iii) Peduncle : Very Strong   iv) Spike : Strong 6. Plant height : 84 cm (60 cm to 109 cm) 7. Straw colour : White 8. Days to heading : 66 days (50 days – 82 days) 9. Days to maturity : 108 days (84 days-128 days) 10. Awn colour at maturity : White 11. Spike       i) Shape : Topering      ii) Length : Very Long     iii) Colour at maturity : White     iv) Density : Medium 12. Glume Pubescence : Absent 13. Glume Shoulder : Medium 14. Shattering Tendency : Non-shattering 15. Threshability : Medium 16. Grains       i) Colour : Amber      ii) Luster ; Lustrous    iii) Texture : Semi hard    iv) Shape  : Oblong     v) Crease width : Medium    vi) Crease depth : Medium
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases:
1.	HI 1634 exhibited seedling resistance (all stage resistance) to all the 27 test pathotypes each of stem and leaf rusts. The postulated stem rust resistance gene Sr31 has been reported to be resistant to all India pathotypes of stem rust.
2.	It has high levels of field resistance to stem (ACI: Max.-1.5; Mean-0.9) and leaf (ACI: Max.-3.1, Mean-1.6) rusts.
3.	It also showed high levels of adult plant resistance to prevalent and virulent stem rust pathotypes 40A and 117-6; and leaf rust pathotyhpes 77-5, 77-9 and 104-2.
4.	It showed good levels of resistance to leaf blight, Karnal bunt, Fusarium head blight, loose smut, foot rot and flag smut.
5.	It was not affected by major insect pests.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: There is no major problem of insect pests in Central Zone, however, no major insect pests were reported affecting HI 1634 and responses are on par with check varieties.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: North Eastern Plains Zone (NEPZ) comprising of eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Assam and plains of other north eastern stares.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: 1.	DBW 187 was higher yielding than all checks under late sown conditions in agronomical trials. 2.	Under late sown conditions, DBW 187 performed better than all checks with minimum reduction in grain yield, grain number and 1000 gr.wt. This is indicative of its better adaptation to heat stress and suitable to sugarcane/cotton/potato-wheat rotations.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: DBW 187 has shown a heat sensitivity index (HSI) of 1.05 which shows its better tolerance to heat stress.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases:
1)	The proposed variety DBW 187 is resistant to foliar diseases under natural and artificial epiphytotic condition. Resistance to rusts, particularly brown rust is useful under timely sown condition of NEPZ.
This genotype indicates genes for brown rusts as indicated by raced specific (77-5, 77-9, 104-2)  APR response across different locations.
SRT analysis revealed hat DBW 187 resistant to most prevalent brown rust (77-7), 77-8, 77-9, 77-10, 104-2, 104-3, 104B, 162-2, 162A. 
This gene postulation indicated that DBW 187 carries Lr26+10+Sr5+11+, gene postulation indicated that DBW 187 carries Lr26+10+Sr5+11+, Yr2+ gene combinations for brown, black and yellow rusts.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Fertilizers application should be based on soil tests.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Irrigated late sown conditions under varied cropping system of Madhya Pradesh.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: MP 1202 has shown stable performance under late and very late sown conditions with very low reductions in grain yield and other agronomic parameters.

seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: 1. Growth habit: Erect, 2. Anthocyanin Pigmentation: i. Coleoptile: Absent, ii. Leaf sheath: Absent, iii. seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: MP 1202 has shown tolerance to heat stress prevailing in Madhya Pradesh. This is indicated by the performance of the variety under late and verylate sowing and verylow reduction in yield and other agronomic parameters under the above two conditions.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: MP 1202 has resistance to brown rust. It has also shown resistance to black rust as well as other diseases.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: No major insect pests are reported in MP 1202.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: It has score of 1 for lodging, highest zonal mean grain yield under timely sown, medium fertility, restricted irrigation conditions and there was no significant yield loss when it was sown late. No shattering problem, Suitable for cultivation in the hills (all through the year) both in kharif and Rabi and in lower hills timely sown conditions during Rabi alone.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Plant height (cm)-85.67 cm, -Distinguishing morpholgical Characters.-  Semi-erect growth habit, semi-dwarf with broader drooping long leaf, presence of prominent crooked neck on most peduncles/ears, ear tapering, profuse tillering, waxy leaf and stem conferring resistant to all the three rusts and powdery mildew.,- Coleoptile Anthocyanin-  Absent, - Growth habnit - Semi-erect,- Foliage colour at Boot stage - Green, - Flag leaf Anthocyanin - Absent, - Heading days : (75% ears emerge)- 61.9 days, - Ear  waxiness - Medium, -Ear color-  White, -  Awns or scurs- Awns present, -Awns color - White, - Peduncle length - 16 cm, - Grain color - Amber, - Brush hair- Length short, - Grain weight -1000 grains- 43.7 g, -  Mean grain yield- 45.6 q/ha. Special feature (s)-   Lower most spikelet often sterile like PBW 343 and conferring resistance to all three rusts under field conditions occurring under Southern hill zone.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: No serous pest problem observed in the field. Data not available for stored pests problem.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MANDAKINI (OR 2077-4) (IET 17847), rice

Name note: The CSC release-minute name is "MANDAKINI (OR 2077-4)(IET 17847)" and the Seednet name is "Mandakini". Evidence below refers to the same rice variety under both names. The Seednet crop field reads "CUCUMBER", which conflicts with rice. No Seednet page for this variety was retrieved, so I could not confirm the Seednet crop entry. Other "Mandakini" entries found are a different variety, Mandakini (K-9351), released 2004, and were excluded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches returned no page on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches returned no page on disease or pest resistance for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Mandakini is listed among early-duration varieties with a 90-115 day range, but that range is for the group, not confirmed per variety -- https://osscltd.in/cms/marketing/availability-of-seeds
Odisha seed distribution report says farmers in the state prefer Mandakini among the varieties they grow in uplands -- https://pc.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2020-03/7.Seed_Distribution_System.pdf
IRRI technical bulletin on rice in Odisha lists Mandakini as suited to upland kharif and irrigated rabi land -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf
No multi-location or field-trial results specific to this variety were found -- searched via the research query, no page returned.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No marker, QTL or parentage page for this variety was returned. Parentage is not specified in the input and was not found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Odisha's rice breeding history is covered by the IRRI bulletin, which credits Mandakini to the state's rice breeding programme (2010 release group) but does not name a breeder -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf
The same bulletin attributes Odisha's rice breeding and varietal development to the Rice Research Station, Bhubaneswar, under the university setup (OUAT). The bulletin does not explicitly say Mandakini was bred there -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf
No lead breeder name was found for this variety. A ResearchGate profile of an OUAT plant breeder lists a co-author named Mandakini Kabi on an unrelated paper; this does not identify a breeder and is not attributed to the variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. Institute-level contact for seed supply (not the breeding institute):
Orissa State Seeds Corporation Ltd., Samantarapur, Bhubaneswar, Pin 751002, Odisha; Phone: 0674 - 2340573, 2340170; Email: mdosscltd456@gmail.com -- https://www.osscltd.in/cms/contact/contact-us
No email or phone for OUAT Rice Research Station or ICAR-NRRI was retrieved, so none is given.

PUBLICATIONS
Das, S.R. (2012). Rice in Odisha. IRRI Technical Bulletin No. 16 -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf
No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP reports, theses (KrishiKosh) or conference papers specific to this variety were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Odisha State Seeds Corporation (OSSC Ltd.) lists Mandakini among its early-duration paddy varieties -- https://osscltd.in/cms/marketing/availability-of-seeds
OSSC is the state nodal agency for breeder, foundation and certified seed, and sources breeder and foundation paddy seed from CRRI, OUAT and ANGRAU -- https://ossc.nic.in/Production/Schemes
The Odisha seed distribution report describes shortfalls in supply of medium-land and upland paddy seed in the study period, without naming Mandakini -- https://pc.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2020-03/7.Seed_Distribution_System.pdf
No NSC, KVK or private dealer listing for this variety was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Notified in Odisha: the notification (S.O. 632(E), 25.03.2011) lists the recommended state as Odisha -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-rice-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
The Bihar-hosted list of notified varieties also records this variety with a 2010 release year and 25/03/2011 notification -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
The input field "recommended_states_raw" (Not specified) is superseded by the Odisha notification above.

drought.details: Moderately tolerant to drought. It is considered an 'intermediate' variety in tissue-specific responses to drought stress at the seedling stage. The variety has also been a target for introgression of drought stress tolerance traits, suggesting a need for improvement in inherent tolerance.

heat.details: It is field tolerant to high temperature. While noted as 'intermediate' in some heat stress response studies at the seedling stage, overall field performance indicates tolerance to high temperatures. However, it is susceptible to low temperatures and frost.

salinity.details: It has been identified as a target for introgression of salt stress tolerance traits, implying its inherent tolerance to salinity is not high. It has been used in studies involving salt injury index.

flood.details: Tolerant to waterlogging conditions. It has also been used as a parent in breeding programs aiming to enhance waterlogging tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerant to Cucumber Mosaic Virus (CMV) and Downy Mildew (caused by P. cubensis).

pest_resistance.summary: Not Specified

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield is about 200 (unit unspecified, as per agricultural practice guidelines). It has been found to be a good parent for fruit yield, fruit number, fruit length, fruit weight, and diameter in hybrid combinations, exhibiting high standard heterosis for yield per plant.
agronomic_details.stability: Included in All India Coordinated Trials, suggesting adaptability across various environments. It is widely cultivated, implying good overall adaptation.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for cultivation in regions like Punjab, suitable for general cucumber cultivation practices. It is tolerant to high temperatures and humidity.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plants have dark green leaves with a rough surface. Its fruit characteristics (yield, number, length, weight, diameter) are notable when used in hybridization.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Participated in All India Coordinated Trials. It is extensively used as a check variety in cucumber germplasm evaluation and has been included in numerous research experiments and hybridization programs to study traits like stress tolerance, yield components, and seed production.

genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The variety has been used as a recipient for trait introgression (e.g., drought and salt stress tolerance) and as a parent in crosses (e.g., for submergence and waterlogging tolerance, parthenocarpy) and genetic diversity studies.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The only evidence is a single government gazette notification listing the variety as notified in 2022. It contains no stress traits, yield figures, or research citations. The crop label (cucumber) conflicts with the variety name (capsicum), and the visible notified states are J&K and HP, not Gujarat. A score of 20 (minimal info) fits; 10 would apply only if even the notification were disregarded.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Pusa Capsicum-1 (KTC-1) was notified in 2022 according to a gazette excerpt, but the record has a crop mismatch (cucumber vs. capsicum) and no data on yield, maturity, parentage, or stress reactions. No stress tolerance, genetic marker, breeder, or commercial availability evidence was found, so the evidence quality is low.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: The only confirmed facts are the 2022 notification and the partially visible state list (J&K, HP, others truncated). Yield, maturity, and morphology are not specified.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No evidence of drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence, disease, or pest tolerance was found. Stress status is unknown, not confirmed negative.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Harsha (HI 1655), wheat**

**Name check:** The variety name is "Pusa Harsha" (CSC minutes name, with code HI 1655). The Seednet name "Pusa (Barkha)" with crop CUCUMBER refers to a different crop. Every Seednet-related finding below is about the cucumber variety Pusa Barkha, not wheat HI 1655. I found no Seednet listing for the wheat variety.

**Date check:** The input gives a release year of 2022-10-26. The sources give a notification date of 06.03.2023. One source cites the notification as S.O. 1056(E) dated 6.3.2023 -- https://choupalsamachar.in/1655-wheat-variety-pusa-harsha/ . Treat 2023 as the notification year and check the input date against the Gazette.

**STRESS TOLERANCE**
- Resistance to leaf and stem rust is listed for HI 1655 in the wheat compendium table -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
- A Hindi-language grower article describes the variety as water-use efficient and suited to timely sowing with restricted irrigation -- https://choupalsamachar.in/1655-wheat-variety-pusa-harsha/
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for HI 1655 specifically.

**DISEASE AND PEST**
- The compendium describes HI 1655 as having resistance to leaf and stem rust, with hard grain and a good chapati score of 8.4 -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Yellow rust, Karnal bunt, and other disease or pest resistance: No evidence found for HI 1655.

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**
- Recommended sowing window is 20 October to 10 November, under timely sowing with restricted irrigation in the Central Zone -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/ (general Central Zone table) and https://krishisewa.com/crop-cultivation/improved-wheat-cultivation-practices-in-central-india/
- A Hindi-language grower article gives a seed rate of about 108 kg/ha, 20 cm row spacing, plant height of about 90–95 cm, and NPK plus zinc at 80:40:50 -- https://choupalsamachar.in/1655-wheat-variety-pusa-harsha/
- The same article gives a potential of about 60 q/ha under good conditions -- https://choupalsamachar.in/1655-wheat-variety-pusa-harsha/
- The compendium lists two yield figures for HI 1655 in the Central Zone (59.8 and 38.8). The column labels are unclear in the extracted text, so treat them as unverified -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
- Maturity days: No evidence found for HI 1655.
- Multi-location trial data beyond the compendium entry: No evidence found.

**GENETICS AND QTL**
- Pedigree: The compendium entry for HI 1655 appears to include "Pusa MACS 2496 / HI 1056(E)", but the text is garbled and not labelled as parentage -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Marker, QTL, or genomic studies for HI 1655: No evidence found.

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION**
- Developing institution: ICAR-IARI Regional Station, Indore (MP) -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- The station's principal scientist and head, K.C. Sharma, is quoted on the six new varieties notified in March 2023, including HI 1655 -- https://krishijagran.com/news/icar-iari-develops-6-new-high-yielding-disease-resistant-wheat-varieties/
- Names of the lead breeders for HI 1655 specifically: No evidence found. Station staff named in a 2025 IARI newsletter for other wheat lines include Singh JB, Sharma KC, Verma DK, Prakasha TL and Gajghate R -- https://pusakrishi.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/IARI_Newsletter_April-June_2025.pdf
- The Seednet cucumber "Pusa Barkha" was released in 2013 by the SVRC Delhi. It is a different crop and is not the wheat variety -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/vegetables/cucumber/

**CONTACT DETAILS**
- Dr K.C. Sharma, Head (Acting), IARI Regional Station Indore. Phone: 0731-2927921. Email: head_indore[at]iari[dot]res[dot]in. Alternate email listed: kc_64sharma[at]yahoo[dot]com -- https://www.iari.res.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=301&Itemid=735
- Jang Bahadur Singh, Regional Station Indore. Email: jangbsing@gmail.com -- https://pusakrishi.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/IARI_Newsletter_April-June_2025.pdf
- Institute postal address for the Indore station: No evidence found.
- Institute-level contact page URL: https://www.iari.res.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=301&Itemid=735 (page lists the station contact details)

**PUBLICATIONS**
- Authors not listed (2024). Compendium of Wheat Varieties Notified in India During 2018-2023. ICAR-IIWBR, Karnal (RB-51) -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Authors not listed (2022). Wheat & Barley Newsletter, Vol. 162. ICAR-IIWBR -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
- Authors not listed (2023). IARI Annual Report 2023 (lists HI 1655 as a bread wheat variety) -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
- No peer-reviewed papers, theses, or KrishiKosh records specific to HI 1655 were found. The HI 8802 paper in the search results concerns a different durum variety and is excluded.

**SEED AVAILABILITY**
- No wheat seed sales listing for HI 1655 found from NSC, a state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or a private dealer.
- The IARI Indore station reports producing breeder seed for its varieties through public-private partnership -- https://www.iari.res.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=301&Itemid=735
- Seednet and cucumber listings (Amazon "Pusa" cucumber seed) are for other crops and are not relevant to HI 1655.

**RECOMMENDED STATES**
- Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Kota and Udaipur divisions of Rajasthan, and Jhansi division of Uttar Pradesh. The Central Zone table lists HI 1655 for timely sown, restricted irrigation conditions -- https://krishisewa.com/crop-cultivation/improved-wheat-cultivation-practices-in-central-india/
- The IARI Indore page lists the Central Zone states (MP, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Kota and Udaipur divisions, Jhansi division) -- https://krishisewa.com/crop-cultivation/improved-wheat-cultivation-practices-in-central-india/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Search note: I ran four web searches (variety/notification, breeder/institution, research, seed availability). None returned any page about Shalimar Cucumber Hybrid-1 or SKUAST-K's cucumber work. The results were generic seed-catalogue pages, a Kerala Agricultural University hybrid list for a different hybrid (KPCH-1), and a Nepali cucumber hybrid trial. I have not attributed any of those to this variety. Names used: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are the same ("Shalimar Cucumber Hybrid-1"), so no separate evidence exists under either name.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Cucumber Hybrid-2 (cucumber, hybrid; variety code H0403014; SKUAST-K; released 2012-07-24; recommended state J&K)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical ("Shalimar Cucumber Hybrid-2"). No search returned a Seednet portal page, so the evidence below does not come from Seednet under either name. Four searches returned no page that describes this hybrid directly. The findings below are only tangential, and each one is labelled with the work it actually concerns.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for this hybrid's drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. Context only: a Kashmir polyhouse study covers a different parthenocarpic hybrid, not this one -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue9/PartO/8-9-162-601.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for resistance ratings of Shalimar Cucumber Hybrid-2. Context only: a 2004-05 survey of Kashmir valley cucumber fields found angular leaf spot in every growing area, with incidence of 23.3 to 74.4% and severity of 10.5 to 26.0% (Bhat, Ahmad and Zargar, 2007) -- https://indianjournals.com/article/apps-15-2-029

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found for this hybrid's yield, maturity or field trials. Context only: a 2019-2020 naturally ventilated polyhouse trial at SKUAST-K Shalimar tested fertigation and pruning on the parthenocarpic hybrid 'Pusa Parthenocarpic Cucumber-6', not on this hybrid -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue9/PartO/8-9-162-601.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for parentage, QTL or marker studies of Shalimar Cucumber Hybrid-2. Context only: a SKUAST-Jammu diallel study on local Jammu cucumber germplasm (2022-23 and 2023-24) found non-additive gene action dominated, which is not specific to this hybrid -- https://horizonepublishing.com/index.php/PST/article/view/10515

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: SKUAST-K (Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir), with headquarters at Shalimar, Srinagar. The university was set up under a 1982 state act (SKUAST-K) -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sher-e-Kashmir_University_of_Agricultural_Sciences_and_Technology_of_Kashmir

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shrushti (variety_name) / Shruti (seednet_variety_name), maize, GH 0727

Search note: four web_search queries were run (variety, breeder/institute, research/trials, Seednet name). The Seednet name "Shruti" returned only cucumber seed-sale pages, which are discarded under the crop and variety rules. All maize findings below refer to "Shrushti" / GH 0727 and not to the Seednet crop label, which says CUCUMBER.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no page giving drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for GH 0727 (Shrushti).

DISEASE AND PEST
Shrushti is listed in a benchmarking table of Indian maize varieties with the note "resistance to BSDM" (BSDM is the abbreviation in the snippet; it is not expanded there). The table row also names UAS, ARS Arabhavi, Karnataka, Kharif, and a yellow, dent grain type. The snippet does not state a disease score for this variety, so the claim should be checked against the full document. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
The benchmarking table lists GH 0727 (Shrushti) with a yield figure of 6.0 in its row, tested under Karnataka Kharif conditions. The table's column headings are not legible in the snippet, so the unit and meaning of this figure are unconfirmed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
The IIMR cultivar list records GH 0727 (Shrushti), developed at ARS Arabhavi, Karnataka, with status "Public," a date of 30-07-2014, a code "1919 (E)," season Kharif, and maturity "Normal." A value of 7.5 appears in the same row, with no unit or column label visible in the snippet. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
Maturity class is given as "Normal" in the IIMR list. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The searches returned no QTL, marker, or pedigree study for GH 0727 (Shrushti). Parentage is not specified in the input and was not found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
The developing institution is given as UAS, ARS Arabhavi (University of Agricultural Sciences, Agricultural Research Station, Arabhavi, Karnataka), which fits the "University of Agricultural Sciences" entry in the release record. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
No lead breeder or scientist name was found for this variety. The search did not reach the AICRP maize centre page or the UAS Dharwad page that would list breeders.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No official email, phone, postal address, or contact page for UAS ARS Arabhavi or for a breeder of GH 0727 appeared in the results. The only "Shrushti" hit with contact information (a Pune plant nursery, Shrushti Rop Vatika / Shrushti Agro) is a different business and is discarded. -- https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCNQPqLMSO4pzwgVH8s6KMrw (discarded, unrelated)

PUBLICATIONS
Benchmarking document, Indian maize varieties (ResearchGate record). Authors and year were not visible in the snippet. Journal/Report: not identified. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper specifically on GH 0727 (Shrushti) was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No seed dealer, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or SAU seed-sale listing for GH 0727 (Shrushti) appeared. The "Shruti" results are F1 cucumber hybrids sold by private seed firms (for example Sagar Shruti F1) and are discarded. -- https://agribegri.com/products/buy-sagar-seeds-shruti-f1-cucumber-seeds-kharif--summer-online-agribegri.php (discarded, different crop)

RECOMMENDED STATES
Karnataka (Kharif). Recorded in the IIMR cultivar list and the benchmarking table, both associated with ARS Arabhavi. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
The input record states "Not specified," so the Karnataka entry comes from the search sources, not from the release minutes.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: AD-2 (Ajmer Dill-2), Indian dill, NRCSS Ajmer

DROUGHT: The variety is suitable for cultivation under both irrigated and rainfed conditions., with about 14.6 q/ha under irrigated conditions and 5.8 q/ha under rain-fed conditions. This shows rainfed adaptation, not a measured drought-tolerance trait. -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/food-science/dill ; https://5.imimg.com/data5/OH/VP/MY-20277542/seed-spices.pdf

HEAT: No direct evidence found for heat tolerance. The variety is described as developed for arid and semi-arid agro-climate, and in farmers' fields it recorded 15.3 q/ha against a check of 9.64 q/ha. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJSS/article/view/157474

SALINITY: No AD-2-specific evidence found. Seed spices in general are reported to be grown successfully under saline/alkaline water, but this is not tied to AD-2. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/329438747_Scenario_Importance_and_Prospects_of_Seed_Spices_A_Review

FLOOD / SUBMERGENCE: No evidence found.

DISEASE RESISTANCE: AD-2 recorded the lowest percent disease incidence, 5.2%, among the tested entries, and was rated tolerant. Separately, the variety possesses field tolerance to powdery mildew. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJSS/article/view/157474 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316589094_NRCSS_ACr_1_Coriander

PEST RESISTANCE: No evidence found for AD-2 specifically.

QTL / MARKERS: No evidence found. A 2024 Springer review on dill breeding notes that still almost no work has been done about the breeding aspects of this important plant. -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-97-9630-4_6

YIELD AND TRIALS: Station and farm trials at NRCSS: AD-2 gave 1466 kg/ha, against 1207 kg/ha for the local variety, a 21% gain. The farmers'-field result was 15.3 q/ha versus 9.64 q/ha for the check. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJSS/article/view/157474

BREEDER / INSTITUTION: NRCSS Ajmer developed the variety for arid and semi-arid agro-climate, with high dillapiole content. It was developed through mass selection based on progeny performance from Nagaur Local (selection AD-01-6). The selection was identified by the XVII All India Co-ordinated Research Project on Spices as NRCSS AD 2. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJGPB/article/view/68257

REGISTRATION / NOTIFICATION: The variety has been registered at NBPGR with IC 620541. Central notification followed: the Central Variety Release and Notification Committee accepted it for notification at its 24th meeting, held on 22 September 2016. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJGPB/article/view/68257

RELEASE DATE (input conflict): The input gives 2015-04-07. The sources instead point to a state notification dated 1.1.16, with the State Subcommittee approval noted in the same release record. The input date should be checked against the official notification. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJGPB/article/view/68257

SEED AVAILABILITY (breeder/institutional): Breeder and truthfully labeled seed of this variety is available at NRCSS, Tabiji, Ajmer-305 206,

agronomic_details.adaptation: Most suitable for loamy and black cotton soils with proper drainage. A dry, cool, frost-free climate is favourable. Most suitable for irrigated conditions.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 150-160 days (official). Other sources give 130-140 (SKNAU), 140-150 (phytojournal) and 110 (RAU Bikaner notes), so maturity figures are inconsistent.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Short stature with compact umbels; long, bold seeds; a denser view of the plants when green. One source describes it as erect and medium tall, which conflicts with the official description.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Not identified in the results.
commercial_info.availability_status: limited (unverified). Breeder seed is produced at SKNAU research stations (18 kg in 2018-19), but the commercial supply chain is not documented.
commercial_info.private_dealers: A spice nursery site lists RF-125 as a Rajasthan variety (spicenurseries.in), but no dealer or stock was confirmed.

variety_profile.institution: RAJASTHAN AGRICULTURAL UNIVERSITY, BEECHAWAL FARM, BIKANER (RAJASTHAN)
variety_profile.recommended_states: Not specified in the release record. Search results show use in Rajasthan, and a state-wise listing names Rajasthan for RF-125 (result 43).
variety_profile.state_acronyms: RJ (Rajasthan, per the sources above). GJ is not listed as a recommended state for this variety.

drought_tolerance.technical_details: No direct drought-tolerance rating for RF-125 was found. The release record says it is most suitable for irrigated conditions. The slideshare snippet's 'tolerant to drought' appears to refer to a different variety, and the CRIDA snippet on drought-tolerant greengram is about another crop. The CRIDA climate-resilient technologies report says RF-125 gave the best result (23.80 q/ha) among the varieties demonstrated in Rajasthan, but the snippet does not say this was under drought stress. A Sakleshpur CVT drought trial lists RF-125 at 22.95 q/ha, but the snippet does not say how it ranked relative to other genotypes. Water stress should be avoided at flowering and seed formation.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: The ICAR Crop Improvement report lists RF 125 among fennel lines identified in a screening, but the snippet is cut off and does not state the trait. It sits next to a 'terminal heat stress' passage, so this link is not confirmed. The release record says a dry, cool, frost-free climate is favourable, which suggests the variety is not specifically heat adapted.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: No salinity rating for the released RF-125 was found. A researcher profile describes gamma-irradiated M3 mutants derived from RF-125 and screened for salt tolerance. That work concerns the mutants, not the original variety. The Bharatpur station source reports RF-125 yielding 20 q/ha in a saline-affected area, but the snippet gives no comparison and no tolerance claim.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: No flood-tolerance evidence was found. The adaptation note requires proper drainage, and the IPM guidance says to avoid waterlogging. This suggests the variety is sensitive to waterlogging, but this is an inference and not a tested result.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: Blight and powdery mildew (moderately resistant per the AESA-IPM guide). Ramularia blight and Alternaria blight are described as resistant in secondary sources (slideshare PPT, a training manual, and a production-technology compendium). The official release record says only that disease incidence was at par with RF-101 and the local check.
disease_resistance.technical_details: The sources conflict. The NIPHM-AESA IPM package lists RF-101 and RF-125 as moderately resistant to blight and powdery mildew. The release record shows no advantage over the checks. The 'resistant' claims come from non-peer-reviewed secondary sources. No resistance genes or mechanisms are reported.

pest_resistance.specific_pests: None documented. The 'field tolerant to white fly' result (OP3.pdf) concerns a different crop and is not attributed to RF-125. The CABI note about aphid-tolerant cultivars is general and does not name RF-125.
pest_resistance.technical_details: No pest-resistance evidence for RF-125 was found.

stress_tolerance_analysis.overall_stress_tolerance: no (not demonstrated). Only moderate disease resistance has some support. There is no verified abiotic-stress tolerance.
key_stress_attributes: Moderate resistance to blight and powdery mildew (NIPHM AESA-IPM guide)
Blight resistance claims in secondary sources conflict with the release record's 'at par with checks'
Suited to irrigated, well-drained soils; waterlogging is to be avoided
Gamma-irradiation mutants of RF-125 have been used in salt-tolerance research, but this is not a trait of the variety itself

genetic_and_molecular_profile.genetic_markers: None found. No QTL, SNP or SSR data were reported for RF-125.
genetic_and_molecular_profile.breeding_techniques: Conventional recurrent half-sib selection (individual plant progeny performance). RF-125 has also served as a base material for gamma-radiation mutagenesis studies, for example germination at 150 Gy.
genetic_and_molecular_profile.genetic_background: Developed through recurrent selection based on individual plant progeny (half-sib) performance in EC-243380, an exotic collection from Italy. One source (result 33) attributes development to SKN College of Agriculture (RAU), Jobner. The official record names RAU, Beechwal Farm, Bikaner.

agronomic_performance.yield_potential: 1500-1700 kg/ha (official). Secondary sources give 1600 kg/ha (phytojournal) and 17.0 q/ha (SKNAU table). Farmer demonstration and trial figures are 20 q/ha (Bharatpur), 22.95 q/ha (Sakleshpur CVT) and 23.80 q/ha (CRIDA demonstration).
agronomic_performance.yield_stability: Reported yields are consistently at or above the official range across Rajasthan demonstrations and a Karnataka trial. No formal stability analysis was found.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Most suitable for loamy and black cotton soils with proper drainage. A dry, cool, frost-free climate is favourable. Most suitable for irrigated conditions.
agronomic_performance.maturity_days: 150-160 days (official). Other sources give 130-140 (SKNAU), 140-150 (phytojournal) and 110 (RAU Bikaner notes), so maturity figures are inconsistent.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Short stature with compact umbels; long, bold seeds; a denser view of the plants when green. One source describes it as erect and medium tall, which conflicts with the official description.
agronomic_performance.field_trial_results: CRIDA Rajasthan demonstrations: RF-125 gave the best result at 23.80 q/ha, with additional farmer income of Rs 47,900-56,900/ha. Bharatpur station: 20 q/ha. Sakleshpur CVT: 22.95 q/ha. An on-farm assessment (IJCMAS 2017) compared RF-101, RF-125 and RF-145. The SKNAU document says RF-125 was released for the state by notification S.O. 597(E) on 25.04.2006.
agronomic_performance.farmer_adoption: Described as a widely adopted cultivar in Rajasthan. Breeder seed production of 18 kg was recorded at ARSS in 2018-19. It is included in DUS guidelines and the Plant Authority's registered variety lists.

breeder_and_development_info.primary_breeder_name: Not identified in the search results.
breeder_and_development_info.breeding_institution: RAJASTHAN AGRICULTURAL UNIVERSITY, BEECHAWAL FARM, BIKANER (RAJASTHAN). SKN College of Agriculture, Jobner (RAU/SKNAU) is cited as the developer in some sources.
breeder_and_development_info.collaborating_scientists: Not identified. Arvind Verma appears only as a researcher working on RF-125 mutants.
breeder_and_development_info.development_timeline: Recurrent half-sib selection from EC-243380 (Italy). Released in 2004. State notification S.O. 597(E) dated 25.04.2006 (per SKNAU).
breeder_and_development_info.research_publications: Secondary and review sources only: Advances in cultivation of fennel (Phytojournal 2020), Germplasm conservation in seed spices (Botany Journals 2021), Scenario, Importance and Prospects of Seed Spices (Lupine 2018), an IJCMAS 2017 on-farm assessment, and the ResearchGate review on fennel (2022) mentioning gamma radiation of RF-125. No primary paper on the variety's release or stress tolerance was found.

commercial_availability.private_dealers: A spice nursery site lists RF-125 as a Rajasthan variety (spicenurseries.in), but no dealer or stock was confirmed.
commercial_availability.availability_status: limited (unverified). Breeder seed is produced at SKNAU research stations (18 kg in 2018-19), but the commercial supply chain is not documented.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety has several citations, including government reports (CRIDA, NIPHM) and review literature, and consistent yield evidence of 16-24 q/ha. Its stress-trait evidence is weak: moderate resistance to blight and powdery mildew is supported by one credible source (NIPHM), while claims of drought, salinity and heat tolerance are not backed by direct evidence. The score is therefore not raised above 60. It is not recommended specifically for Gujarat, and no Gujarat-specific trial data were found.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Short, compact umbels; long bold seeds; 150-160 days; 15-17 q/ha official yield (20-24 q/ha in demonstrations); moderately resistant to blight and powdery mildew; best on irrigated, well-drained loam or black cotton soil.
dashboard_data.seasons: Rabi (inferred from the dry, cool climate requirement and the 'Advanced Production Technology for Rabi Fennel' source)

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: RF-125 is a short, compact-umbel fennel variety released in 2004, selected by half-sib recurrence from an Italian accession, and it yields 1500-1700 kg/ha officially and 20-24 q/ha in Rajasthan demonstrations. The best-supported stress trait is moderate resistance to blight and powdery mildew; drought, heat, salinity and flood tolerance are not demonstrated. Yield evidence is strong and stress evidence is weak, with some conflict between sources on disease reaction and maturity.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: A short fennel variety with compact umbels and bold seeds, maturing in 150-160 days and yielding 15-17 q/ha officially (20-24 q/ha in demonstrations). It suits irrigated, well-drained loam and black cotton soils in a dry, cool, frost-free climate.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: It is moderately resistant to blight and powdery mildew according to the NIPHM guide, though the release record shows disease incidence at par with the checks. No verified drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance was found, and no genetic marker data exist.

drought.details: No evidence found in the digest for drought tolerance of AFg-3. No mechanisms or trial data were reported.

heat.details: No evidence found in the digest for heat tolerance of AFg-3. The digest's heat-related reference concerns a separate NBPGR accession (early maturity escaping terminal heat) and is not about AFg-3, so it is not treated as evidence for this variety.

salinity.details: No evidence found in the digest for salinity tolerance of AFg-3.

flood.details: No evidence found in the digest for flood tolerance of AFg-3.

disease_resistance.summary: Powdery mildew: moderately resistant, average disease index 26.0% versus 40-50% in check varieties (variety-specific source). Root rot: moderately resistant, same source, no PDI values given. Downy mildew and Fusarium wilt: no evidence found specifically for AFg-3; the cited general fenugreek review lists these as major diseases but does not assess this variety.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found for AFg-3 resistance to aphids or leaf miner. The general fenugreek review lists these as major pests but does not assess this variety.

agronomic_details.yield: Coordinated varietal trials (2010-12): about 18.8% higher seed yield than the national check Hisarsonali. Trade/extension sheet: 15-18 q/ha (approximately 1500-1800 kg/ha, unverified, commercial source) under irrigated conditions. 2021 NRCSS germplasm evaluation at Ajmer: AFg-3 check at 985 kg/ha; best entry AM-31 at 1211 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: unknown. The digest reports performance in coordinated trials and a single 2021 Ajmer evaluation, but gives no multi-environment stability analysis.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for the states listed in the variety profile. The digest reports irrigated-condition performance across the country (trade sheet), but gives no agro-climatic zone analysis. A West Bengal sowing-date study (BCKV, Mondouri, 2013-15) evaluated AFg-3 for growth, phenology and yield, but its results are not stated in the digest.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Approximately 125 days (secondary, low-reliability source; not confirmed by the primary sources).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Indeterminate growth habit (secondary, low-reliability source). Quality traits (variety-specific source): diosgenin +34.6%, 4-hydroxyisoleucine +15.5% and fibre +11% relative to checks. Trade sheet: diosgenin about 1.79% and 4-hydroxyisoleucine about 0.97% in seed, described as higher than other varieties.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Coordinated varietal trials, 2010-12: about 18.8% seed yield advantage over Hisarsonali. (2) NRCSS Ajmer germplasm evaluation, 2021: AFg-3 check at 985 kg/ha versus best entry AM-31 at 1211 kg/ha; the report also records 2019-20 FLD/extension use of AFg-3. (3) BCKV Mondouri, West Bengal, 2013-15: sowing-date study using AFg-3 from NRCSS Ajmer (outcomes not reported in the digest). Note: the trade sheet's 15-18 q/ha figure is not corroborated by the primary trial sources.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: unknown. No SSR, SNP or marker information in the digest. The variety was developed by pure-line selection from a Sikar district, Rajasthan germplasm line, so no marker positions are available.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: unknown. No QTL information in the digest.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: unknown. The digest reports higher diosgenin and 4-hydroxyisoleucine content, but gives no genes or pathways.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Ajmer Fenugreek-3 (AFg-3), NRCSS Tabiji/Ajmer

ORIGIN/BREEDER: Developed by pure-line selection from a germplasm line collected in Sikar district, Rajasthan, by ICAR-NRCSS Ajmer; authors listed as Shyam Sunder Meena, R.K. Kakani, S.K. Malhotra and Ram Swaroop Meena -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/386055566_Ajmer_Fenugreek-3_AFg-3_A_high_4-hydroxy_isoleucine_and_diosgenin_containing_fenugreek_variety

RELEASE/NOTIFICATION: Notified for cultivation in all fenugreek-growing areas of India under gazette notification S.O. 3666(E) dated 06-12-2016, which does not match the 2015-04-07 release date in the input record; the release date itself is unverified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/386055566_Ajmer_Fenugreek-3_AFg-3_A_high_4-hydroxy_isoleucine_and_diosgenin_containing_fenugreek_variety

GERMPLASM DEPOSIT: Seed deposited at NBPGR with IC number IC-611680 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/386055566_Ajmer_Fenugreek-3_AFg-3_A_high_4-hydroxy_isoleucine_and_diosgenin_containing_fenugreek_variety

YIELD/TRIALS: In coordinated varietal trials (2010-12), AFg-3 out-yielded the national check Hisarsonali by about 18.8% in seed yield -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/386055566_Ajmer_Fenugreek-3_AFg-3_A_high_4-hydroxy_isoleucine_and_diosgenin_containing_fenugreek_variety

YIELD (INSTITUTIONAL): Trade/extension sheet lists seed yield of 15-18 q/ha and irrigated-condition performance across the country -- https://5.imimg.com/data5/OH/VP/MY-20277542/seed-spices.pdf

YIELD (2021 NRCSS report): In a 2021 germplasm evaluation at Ajmer, AFg-3 was the check at 985 kg/ha, with the best entry (AM-31) at 1211 kg/ha; the report also records a 2019-20 FLD/extension use of AFg-3 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361810048_ICAR-NRCSS_Annual_Report_2021

PHENOLOGY: A West Bengal sowing-date study (BCKV, Mondouri, 2013-15) used AFg-3 from NRCSS Ajmer to evaluate growth, phenology and yield -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-10-2017/Karma%20Chewang%20Bhutia,%20et%20al.pdf

MATURITY: Listed at about 125 days to maturity, indeterminate growth habit (secondary, low-reliability source) -- https://permacultureplants.com/plants/fenugreek/

QUALITY: Enhanced diosgenin (+34.6%), 4-hydroxyisoleucine (+15.5%) and fibre (+11%) relative to checks -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/386055566_Ajmer_Fenugreek-3_AFg-3_A_high_4-hydroxy_isoleucine_and_diosgenin_containing_fenugreek_variety

QUALITY (sheet values): Diosgenin about 1.79% and 4-hydroxyisoleucine about 0.97% in seed, both higher than other varieties per the sheet -- https://5.imimg.com/data5/OH/VP/MY-20277542/seed-spices.pdf

DISEASE – POWDERY MILDEW: Moderately resistant; average disease index 26.0% versus 40-50% in check varieties -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/386055566_Ajmer_Fenugreek-3_AFg-3_A_high_4-hydroxy_isoleucine_and_diosgenin_containing_fenugreek_variety

DISEASE – ROOT ROT: Moderately resistant (same source as powdery mildew; no PDI values given) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/386055566_Ajmer_Fenugreek-3_AFg-3_A_high_4-hydroxy_isoleucine_and_diosgenin_containing_fenugreek_variety

DISEASE – DOWNY MILDEW, FUSARIUM WILT, APHIDS, LEAF MINER: No evidence found specifically for AFg-3. General fenugreek reviews list these as major pests/diseases but do not assess this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/308418341_Fenugreek_Trigonella_foenum-graecum_L

DROUGHT TOLERANCE: No evidence found

HEAT TOLERANCE: No evidence found (a separate NBPGR accession note on early maturity escaping terminal heat is not about AFg-3) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJSS/article/download/160703/61497/478228

SALINITY TOLERANCE: No evidence found

FLOOD TOLERANCE: No evidence found

Multi-environment testing included Ajmer, KVK, and SKNAU Jobner sites. Germplasm origin is reported inconsistently as Sikar or Jaipur district.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: There are credible citations: a peer-reviewed paper (IJCMAS 2023), a ResearchGate record, the JAU AGRESCO recommendation, an ICAR-IISR report and a Gazette notification. Yield superiority over checks is documented, but the numbers were not retrieved. Stress-trait evidence is fragmentary and cannot be reliably attributed to GM 3, so it does not reach the 75 band, which requires at least one confirmed stress trait. 60 fits 'at least one citation, but weak on stress traits'.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: High yielding, bold seeded; notified 2022 for GJ, UK, AP, UP; stress traits unconfirmed
dashboard_data.seasons: Not specified (fenugreek is generally a rabi crop, but this is not stated in the evidence)

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Gujarat Methi 3 (JFg 2013-02) is a high-yielding, bold-seeded fenugreek variety developed in Gujarat (likely at JAU) and notified in 2022 for GJ, UK, AP and UP. Peer-reviewed and institutional sources support its yield performance, but abiotic and biotic stress tolerance claims are ambiguous in the snippets and cannot be attributed to this variety. Evidence quality is medium.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Bold-seeded, high-yielding fenugreek (JFg 2013-02) tested in multi-zone trials against checks and recommended to Gujarat farmers by JAU. Numerical yield, maturity and parentage data were not retrieved.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No confirmed drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. Disease and pest mentions (wilt, powdery or downy mildew, pod borer) appear in truncated snippets that cannot be reliably linked to GM 3, so stress tolerance is rated unclear.

PEST RESISTANCE: No evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I'll start with the three core searches in parallel, then check seed availability.EVIDENCE DIGEST: KKP-5 (CSC name) / AKP-5 (Seednet name)

Search coverage: 4 web_search queries were run: "KKP-5 rice variety", "KKP-5 rice breeder UAHS", "AKP-5 finger millet ragi variety", and "KKP-5 paddy Kathalagere UAHS seed". Evidence is very thin. Nothing retrieved describes KKP-5's traits, parentage, or release notification.

Name and crop discrepancy: The Seednet crop field says finger millet (ragi/mandika), but the CSC crop is rice. No Seednet page was retrieved, so I could not check the AKP-5 entry. No result links AKP-5 to KKP-5, and I found no evidence that the two names refer to the same variety. Treat the Seednet record as unverified and possibly a mis-keyed entry.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searched under the rice name; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for KKP-5 surfaced. Under AKP-5 the only finger millet hits were general nutrition or cultivation pages, not variety-specific data.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for KKP-5 (blast, BLB, pests). The UAHS pages retrieved list other paddy varieties (Sahyadri Panchamukhi, Sahyadri Brahma, Sahyadri Saptami) and blast-tolerant work at Mudigere, but none is attributed to KKP-5. -- https://uahs.edu.in/research-stations/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No KKP-5-specific trial or yield data found. The Kathalagere station is described as established in 1975, with a total area of 124.92 ha and it grows field crops including paddy. -- https://uahs.edu.in/research-stations/. Extension front-line demonstrations listed paddy varieties JGL-1798, KPR-1, Tunga and BPT-5205 but not KKP-5. -- https://uahs.edu.in/director-of-extension/

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage and variety code (IET 24250) in the input could not be verified from any retrieved source.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The release is attributed to the Kathalagere research station of the University of Agricultural and Horticultural Sciences, Shivamogga (UAHS). The varieties developed from this station are as follows: Paddy varieties: MO-4, JGL-9718, KKP-5 -- https://uahs.edu.in/research-stations/ (also reported at the same URL under AHRS Kathalagere). The university is the first integrated University in the State of Karnataka, which has Agriculture, Horticulture and Forestry Sciences under its purview -- https://uahs.edu.in/about-ksnuahs/. No lead breeder name for KKP-5 was found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder name, email, phone or postal address was found for KKP-5 or its station. Institute-level page only: UAHS / KSNUAHS, About page -- https://uahs.edu.in/about-ksnuahs/ (lists the university's research centres, including the Kathalagere station, but no contact details were in the retrieved text). Kathalagere station page: https://uahs.edu.in/research-stations/. Both must be checked manually for an official email, phone and address before use in a record.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for KKP-5. Retrieved items were excluded because they do not concern KKP-5: a 2003 UAHS Shimoga IET-13901 abstract (different variety), a Bhadra command boron study on KrishiKosh (not variety-specific), and a 2020 UAHS blast-resistant red rice news item (different variety).

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No KKP-5-specific seed source found. The Honnavile station is listed as producing Foundation, Breeder, Certified and Nuclear seed production activities in different crops viz., Paddy (15250 Qtls) -- https://uahs.edu.in/research-stations/. This is station-level and does not confirm KKP-5 seed. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or private dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Karnataka (from the input record). The UAHS station listing supports a Karnataka origin, but I found no notification or recommendation document stating the states for which KKP-5 is recommended.

Items to verify directly: the Seednet record for AKP-5 (crop field and whether it refers to KKP-5), the CSC release minutes for KKP-5 (year, parentage, IET 24250 code, recommended zone), and the UAHS official contact page.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: CO 55 (rice) / CO-5 (Seednet)**

**Name check and scope**
- Searches were run on "CO 55" (rice, the variety_name in the CSC minutes) and "CO-5" (the Seednet name, listed under finger millet).
- The CO-5 search returned no finger millet page. The only finger millet release it surfaced was "Ragi CO 15" (2013 TNAU booklet), which is a different variety, so I discarded it. Under every heading below, the evidence refers to rice CO 55.
- Input conflicts to check: the Seednet crop is finger millet but the variety is rice; the input release date is 2022-06-17, while TNAU's rice page gives 2021 and the 2022 press note lists it among 2022 releases; the input parentage ("a selection made at Coimbatore") conflicts with the documented cross ADT 43 / GEB 24; the variety code "CB 15714) 4 (IET 27873)" is not confirmed by any retrieved page.
- Search budget: four searches were used (three topic searches plus the CO-5 name check). Topic 4 (seed availability) was not searched.

**STRESS TOLERANCE** 
- Moderate resistance to rice tungro disease is the only tolerance trait recorded for CO 55 (the same entry is under Disease and Pest). Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found for CO 55 (searched, nothing specific returned). -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CO%2055.html

**DISEASE AND PEST**
- Moderately resistant to RTD per TNAU's rice variety page. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CO%2055.html
- No evidence found for blast, bacterial blight, brown planthopper or stem borer resistance for CO 55.

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**
- Duration 110–115 days; season Kar / Kuruvai / Navarai / Summer; average grain yield 6057 kg/ha. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CO%2055.html
- Short duration superfine variety with 115 days; the average yield of the culture is 6050 kg/ha. -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/tnaupressnotes/pdf/2022/Press%20note%20-%20TNAU%20New%20Crop%20varieties%202022%20-%20English-2.pdf
- Milling 70.0% and head rice recovery 65.0%; intermediate amylose content (21.38%). -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CO%2055.html
- Press note gives milling 66% and HRR 62%, which differs from the TNAU page's figures. -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/tnaupressnotes/pdf/2022/Press%20note%20-%20TNAU%20New%20Crop%20varieties%202022%20-%20English-2.pdf
- Grain type: medium slender fine rice with cooking quality. -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/tnaupressnotes/pdf/2022/Press%20note%20-%20TNAU%20New%20Crop%20varieties%202022%20-%20English-2.pdf
- Yield in farmer-level context: CO 55, a ponni rice variety that yielded 6 tonnes per hectare in just 115 days. -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/farmers-get-two-new-high-yielding-paddy-varieties-developed-by-tnau/
- Field-level farmer story (social media post, not a trial report). -- https://x.com/TNIAMProject/status/1857625388941541870
- Multi-location or AICRP trial results for CO 55: No evidence found.

**GENETICS AND QTL**
- Parentage: ADT 43 / GEB 24. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CO%2055.html

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
CO 15 (finger millet) EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: the release-minute name and the Seednet name are both "CO 15". No search result was found on the Seednet portal, so all evidence below refers to the name "CO 15" in general finger millet sources. I ran 4 searches in total.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to CO 15. The searches returned general finger millet pages only.

DISEASE AND PEST
CO-15 is described as highly responsive to nitrogenous fertilizer, non-lodging, and resistant to leaf, neck and finger blast -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336439015_Finger_Millet_Eleusine_coracana_L_Gartn_Breeding (this is a row in a breeding-review table; the page is a general finger millet breeding review and the row was visible only as a snippet, so treat it as a secondary summary)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
CO 15 appears in a Tamil Nadu ragi sowing-schedule table, listed by zone (North, Western, Cauvery Delta and others) for the Marghazhi (Dec-Jan), Chithirai (April-May) and Adi (June-July) seasons, alongside CO (Ra) 14 -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/02_Ragi.pdf
A ICAR-IIMR finger millet brochure lists CO 15 among varieties in a Tamil Nadu variety column, but the table layout is ambiguous, so the state assignment is not certain -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/brochures/Finger_Millet_Brochure.pdf
The same brochure states that short-duration varieties mature in 95-105 days, but it does not give CO 15's maturity -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/brochures/Finger_Millet_Brochure.pdf
No evidence found for CO 15 yield or multi-location trial results.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The breeding review above names CO-15 only as a breeding-table row and gives no parentage or marker data. The parentage "CO 11 x PR 202" was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found that names a CO 15 breeder or developing station. The only institutional link is the TNAU sowing table above; the search did not verify that TNAU released the variety. -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/02_Ragi.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for a breeder contact for CO 15. The ICAR-IIMR brochure gives an institute address (Rajendranagar, Hyderabad 500 030, Telangana; www.millets.res.in), but it is an institute-level contact and not a CO 15 contact -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/brochures/Finger_Millet_Brochure.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
G. Gowthamraj, et al. (2021). The effect of γ-irradiation on the physicochemical, functional, proximate, and anti-nutrient characteristics of finger millet (CO14 & CO15) flours. Radiation Physics and Chemistry, 183, 109403 -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0889157524006574 (the author list is truncated on the page, so the full author list, including Narayanasamy Sangeetha, must be checked against the original article; the URL is the page where the title was found, not the article itself, and the DOI was not captured)
No AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis, or QTL/marker paper naming CO 15 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found from NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, TNAU or Seednet for CO 15. The seed-vendor results (IndiaMART, Amazon, and similar pages) were generic ragi seed listings with no CO 15 mention and were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Tamil Nadu -- supported by the TNAU zone table (https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/02_Ragi.pdf) and the ICAR-IIMR brochure listing (https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/brochures/Finger_Millet_Brochure.pdf). The "Recommended states" field in the release record matches these sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I'll run the searches now. The record lists the crop as groundnut, but the Seednet crop name and parentage both point to finger millet, so I'll check that too.CO 7 MISMATCH WARNING: The record lists crop "groundnut" and Seednet crop "FINGER MILLET (RAGI/MANDIKA)". The evidence found refers to two different crops. The groundnut CO 7 (ICGV 00351) matches the release year, institution and "Tamil Nadu" state, but its parentage is an ICRISAT cross, not "Cuddapah Rajanpet ragi". The only finger-millet hit names CO 7 as a parent in a cross, not as a release. The record needs checking before use.

Searches run: 4 web_search queries (groundnut variety; groundnut breeder/institute; groundnut research; finger millet ragi variety). I did not run a separate Seednet-specific query, so no Seednet page was checked under "CO.7".

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Groundnut CO 7 (ICGV 00351) was tested under rainfed drought-prone conditions in Tamil Nadu and gave a mean pod yield of 2189 kg/ha, 17% and 26% above the check varieties VRI (Gn) 6 and TMV (Gn) 13 -- https://oar.icrisat.org/8601/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321244231_New_Groundnut_variety_TNAU_CO_7
- Groundnut CO 7 showed tolerance to late leaf spot and rust in the release trials -- https://oar.icrisat.org/8601/
- Groundnut CO 7 in Ariyalur district trials (Kharif 2016-17) gave 1880 kg/ha, with lower root rot incidence (1.4%) than the check -- https://www.ijcmas.com/7-5-2018/M.%20Saravanan,%20et%20al.pdf
- Finger millet CO 7: No evidence found for stress tolerance of a finger millet variety named CO 7.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Groundnut CO 7: moderately tolerant to rust and late leaf spot, per the TNAU variety page -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20co7.html
- Groundnut CO 7: Ariyalur trial recorded lower leaf spot incidence (26.0) than the check -- https://www.ijcmas.com/7-5-2018/M.%20Saravanan,%20et%20al.pdf
- Finger millet CO 7: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Groundnut CO 7: Spanish bunch habit, 85-90 days duration, average yield 2300 kg/ha rainfed and 2806 kg/ha irrigated, 51% oil -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20co7.html
- Groundnut CO 7: the TNAU page lists its parentage as "100-105", which is a data-entry error (this is a duration field, not parentage) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20co7.html
- Groundnut CO 7: Farmers' Participatory Varietal Selection trials in Tamil Nadu drought-prone districts, with 71% shelling and 22% protein -- https://oar.icrisat.org/8601/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321244231_New_Groundnut_variety_TNAU_CO_7
- Groundnut CO 7: Ariyalur trial gross return Rs 1,05,567/ha vs Rs 76,183/ha for the check -- https://www.ijcmas.com/7-5-2018/M.%20Saravanan,%20et%20al.pdf
- Finger millet CO 7: TNAU ragi page lists "CO 7 X TAH 107" only as a parentage cross, not as a released variety -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CropProduction/Millets/millets_ragi.html

GENETICS AND QTL
- Groundnut CO 7: ICGV 00351 is a cross derivative of ICGV 87290 x ICGV 87846 -- https://oar.icrisat.org/8601/
- No evidence found for QTL, marker or molecular studies on CO 7 (groundnut or finger millet).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Groundnut CO 7 (named as released from ICGV 00351): developed at ICRISAT, Patancheru, Andhra Pradesh, and released by Tamil Nadu -- https://oar.icrisat.org/8601/
- Groundnut CO 7: The 2014 release paper's author list includes P. Vindhiyavarman (first-listed), S.N. Nigam, P. Janila, M. Vaidhyalingam, N. Manivannan, S. Saravanan, B. Meenakumari, C. Gopalakrishnan and J.S. Kennedy -- https://oar.icrisat.org/8601/
- Groundnut CO 7: The TNAU variety page does not name a breeder -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20co7.html
- Finger millet CO 7: No evidence found for breeder or institution of a finger millet CO 7 release.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found: no email, phone, postal address or institute contact page for CO 7 (groundnut or finger millet) appeared in the search results. The institute name is recorded above; the TNAU and ICRISAT contact pages were not located.

PUBLICATIONS
- Vindhiyavarman P, Nigam SN, Janila P, Vaidhyalingam M, Manivannan N, Saravanan S, Meenakumari B, Gopalakrishnan C, Kennedy JS (2014). A new high yielding Spanish bunch groundnut variety CO 7 (ICGV 00351) for the drought prone areas of Tamil Nadu. Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding 5(2): 192-196 -- https://oar.icrisat.org/8601/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321244231_New_Groundnut_variety_TNAU_CO_7 (journal and pages taken from the ResearchGate listing)
- Saravanan M et al. (2018). Assessment of drought tolerant and high yielding groundnut varieties in Ariyalur District, India. International Journal of Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences 7(5): 3492-3499 -- https://www.ijcmas.com/7-5-2018/M.%20Saravanan,%20et%20al.pdf (author list truncated in the source; only the first author is confirmed)
- Finger millet CO 7: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for seed sales, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings for CO 7 (groundnut or finger millet). The search did not include a seed-availability query.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Groundnut CO 7: released for cultivation across Tamil Nadu -- https://oar.icrisat.org/8601/
- Groundnut CO 7: the DOD notified-varieties page lists CO-6 but the CO 7 entry was not seen in the returned text -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Finger millet CO 7: No evidence found.

RELEASE YEAR (for the record)
- Groundnut CO 7: TNAU variety page gives 2013; the 2014 publication and the record give 2014 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20co7.html ; https://oar.icrisat.org/8601/
