search_metadata.evidence_digest:
DHRS 1 (finger millet/ragi). Variety name and Seednet name are both "DHRS 1"; no search result named either, so every heading below is "No evidence found" unless noted.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searches on "DHRS 1 finger millet variety" returned general finger millet drought and heat reviews and a Pharma Journal review of other varieties (CFMV 1, Indravathi), none naming DHRS 1.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The pages on blast or general finger millet protection did not name DHRS 1.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. A package-of-practices sheet and a Karnataka farm-guide page list other ragi varieties (GPU-28, GPU-67, KMR-204) but not DHRS 1.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. A genomic SSR diversity study lists many Indian finger millet genotypes, but DHRS 1 is not among them.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. The UAS Dharwad pages (seed unit, MARS, seed farms) describe breeder-seed work and station mandates but never mention DHRS 1. Institution-level pages found: https://uasd.edu/en/bsp/ and https://uasd.edu/en/seed-farms/. The "DHRS" strings in the results (DHARWHITE, DHARSCLVDR) are New Guinea Impatiens cultivars and were discarded, as were "Dharwad Dry" and the Prof. R.R. Hanchinal profile, which concern other varieties.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found for DHRS 1. The only contact details seen (UAS Dharwad faculty page, https://uasd.edu/en/faculty-and-staff-3/) belong to groundnut/soybean seed staff with no link to this variety, so they were not recorded. No institute address or contact page for the developing station was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh record naming DHRS 1 appeared. The finger millet reviews (e.g., https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11330411/, DOI 10.1007/s00425-024-04502-2) do not mention it.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The Seednet-related search returned ragi market-price and farming-guide pages and a Karnataka seed-village article (https://www.deccanherald.com/india/karnataka/seeds-of-change-the-women-who-revived-77-ragi-varieties-2843231), none naming DHRS 1. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. The only support for "KARNATAKA" is the institution field in the release record you supplied; no page confirmed the recommendation. Karnataka ragi sources (e.g., https://farming.organicmandya.com/crops/ragi-finger-millet-farming/) describe other varieties only.

Parentage (GPU 26 x SEL 11) and release date (2011-06-28): no evidence found. GPU-26 appears only as a germplasm entry in an SSR study (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4749518/), which does not establish this cross.

Searches run: 4 (the variety on its own, breeder/institute, research papers, seed availability). Recommended next steps: check the CSC release minutes and the Seednet record directly, and query KrishiKosh and the UAS Dharwad / UAS Bengaluru AICRP on small millets for the release notification.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- GN-5 (finger millet, white-seeded) is described as moderately resistant to leaf and finger blast, and as a late-maturing selection from local Waghai germplasm (WWN-20) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India ; https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance data specific to GN-5 were found. A generic drought-tolerance line appears only for the older GN 3 variety, so it is not attributed to GN-5 -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
- Lodging and non-shattering traits in the NAU feature list are attached to other varieties (Nagli-1 and others), not confirmed for GN-5 -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Blast (Pyricularia grisea) resistance: a 2017 NAU technology sheet lists GN-5 among finger millet genotypes with high total phenols that were found resistant to blast -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
- NAU's variety table describes GN-5 as moderately resistant to blast and foot rot, although the row layout is ambiguous -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
- No pest (stem borer, shoot fly, etc.) evidence specific to GN-5 was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration 120-125 days; average grain yield 3200 kg/ha, 24.9% above GN-3 (NAU sheet). Other sources give 120-130 days and 25-27 (presumably q/ha) -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India . The yield units and figures conflict between sources and should be checked against the original trial reports.
- Fertilizer recommendation for South Gujarat heavy rainfall zone I (AES-I), kharif: 75% RDF (40:20:00 NPK kg/ha) plus vermicompost at 2 t/ha -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
- GN-5 is named among older finger millet varieties in a comparison of recovery after a stress event, with no GN-5-specific data shown -- https://dhan.org/smallmilletfoundation/document/smallmillet-national-seminar1.pdf
- No AICRP multi-location trial data specific to GN-5 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. Searches returned QTL, marker and GWAS studies only for other crops or other finger millet genotypes.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Navsari Agricultural University (NAU), Gujarat, via the Hill Millet Research Station (HMRS), Waghai (Dangs). - Note on the institution name in the record: "Pearl Millet Research Station, Navsari Agri. University" does not match the evidence. The NAU station that developed GN-5 is HMRS Waghai, a finger millet station. The Pearl Millet Research Station at Jamnagar belongs to Junagadh Agricultural University, not NAU -- https://www.jau.in/main-pearl-millet-research-station-jamnagar
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. No source names the developer or breeder of GN-5.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
GNN-6 (variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "GNN-6", so every finding below refers to that name). Crop: finger millet (ragi/nagli), not pearl millet, although the input institution says Pearl Millet Research Station.

STRESS TOLERANCE
GNN-6 is described as moderately resistant to blast and foot rot disease, with a non-lodging, erect plant type -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
Leaf blast and finger blast: GNN-6 2016 120-130 28-30 Gujarat Moderately resistant to leaf blast and finger blast. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
Lodging: the release table lists it as a selection from local Waghai germplasm, with non lodging (semi erect) plant type -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
Drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found. The searches returned only generic statements about small millets being drought-tolerant, not GNN-6-specific data.

DISEASE AND PEST
Blast and foot rot: moderately resistant to blast and foot rot -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
Blast review: GN-5, GNN-6, GNN-7, GN-8, GPU-28, GPU-48, KOPN-235, KMR-204 and MR-6 having maximum amount of total phenols were found resistant to the blast disease -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380214295_Diseases_of_Finger_Millet_and_their_Management_A_Review
Recommendation for cultivation: GNN-6, GNN-7, GN-8 for cultivation -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380214295_Diseases_of_Finger_Millet_and_their_Management_A_Review
Insect pests: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Duration and yield: Finger millet GNN-6 (Brown seeded), duration 125 days, average grain yield 2536 kg/ha -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
National table: GNN-6 2016 120-130 28-30 Gujarat (maturity 120-130 days, yield 28-30 q/ha) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
Discrepancy: the NAU table gives a release year of 2014 with 2536 kg/ha, while the ICAR table gives 2016 with 28-30 q/ha. Both sources need checking against the CSC minutes.
Multi-location trial: GNN-6 is listed as recommended for Gujarat, moderately resistant to finger blast -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/377873918_Millet_varieties_across_regions
Trial data for GNN-6 beyond these comparisons: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: No evidence found. The release table gives its origin as a selection from local Waghai germplasm -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
Genomic or QTL studies naming GNN-6: No evidence found. The only mention is a germplasm list that includes GNN-6 among genotypes, with no marker data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378123480_Reproductive_Biology_Genetics_Evolution_and_Diversity_in_Finger_Millet_Eleusine_coracana_L_Gaertn

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing station: Improved varieties of Small Millets released by HMRS, NAU, Waghai for Gujarat state -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf. This is the Hill Millet Research Station (Waghai), not the Pearl Millet Research Station named in the input.
Selection origin: Selection from local Waghai germplasm, Navsari Agricultural University -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
Breeder name: No evidence found. One proso millet paper says Intwala et al. (2017) in the release of finger millet variety 'GNN-6'. This is a citation in another paper, not a confirmed breeder record, and Intwala's identity as this variety's breeder is not established by the sources -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355465828_A_new_high_yielding_proso_millet_variety_Panicum_miliaceum_L_PMV_442

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder contact: No evidence found.
Institute-level: Hill Millet Research Station, Navsari Agricultural University, Waghai, Dist. The Dangs, Gujarat; latitude 20.77' N and longitude 73.50' E -- https://nau.in/index
Institute page: https://nau.in
Phone and email: No evidence found in the returned pages.

PUBLICATIONS
Patil, H. E., Vadodariya, G. D., & Gami, R. A. (2023). Small millets: Conventional improvement, biofortification and practical achievement (chapter, Millet Conclave Compendium 2023). Compendium -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384431249_MILLET_CONCLAVE_COMPENDIUM_2023_-_FULL_BOOK
Note: this chapter cites GNN-6 as a local check in a WN-559 trial (WN-559 (3551 kg/ha) performed well with 15.02 % increase over local check 'GNN-6'). The item mentions GNN-6 but is not about its development.
Authors not shown (2024?). Diseases of Finger Millet and their Management: A Review. Review -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380214295_Diseases_of_Finger_Millet_and_their_Management_A_Review
Peer-reviewed or AICRP/KrishiKosh papers specifically on GNN-6: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, or SAU seed-sale listing for GNN-6: No evidence found. NAU states that under Mega Seed Project, NAU has produced 66617 q of breeder, foundation, truthful and certified seeds without naming GNN-6 -- https://nau.in/pages/about-navsari-agricultural-university-1548127676
Private dealer listings: The IndiaMart ragi results are generic grain listings, not GNN-6 seed, and were discarded -- https://dir.indiamart.com/ahmedabad/ragi.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
Gujarat: GNN-6 2016 120-130 28-30 Gujarat -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India. The ICAR brochure also lists GNN-6 under Gujarat -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/brochures/Finger_Millet_Brochure.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: HIMA (finger millet / ragi, variety code A0204123)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "HIMA", so the four searches covered one name. The searches ran as "HIMA finger millet variety", "HIMA finger millet breeder institute", "HIMA finger millet research paper" and "HIMA ragi seed availability Andhra Pradesh". No result was a HIMA-specific page. The only usable metadata is the input record itself (release 2013-01-18, Agricultural Research Station, Andhra Pradesh, parentage IE 2695 x PR 202), which I have not verified from any source.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found (searched; the finger millet hits were generic and did not name HIMA)

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found (searched; no HIMA-specific resistance data returned)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found (searched; the Springer "Finger Millet Processing: A Circular Economy Approach" review -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11947-025-04105-z -- is a general processing review and does not mention HIMA)

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found (searched; no HIMA QTL, marker or pedigree-confirmation study returned)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for HIMA. The only "Hima" hit is a name collision: Dr Hima Bindu Kudapa, a molecular breeder at ICRISAT working on chickpea and small millets -- https://www.icrisat.org/about/team/dr-hima-bindu-kudapa. Nothing links her to the HIMA variety, so do not record her as the breeder. The institution "Agricultural Research Station" is given only in the input record and is not confirmed by search.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute or station email, phone, postal address or contact page was returned for HIMA. Suggested next step: the Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) or the relevant AP Agricultural Research Station contact page, which must be confirmed directly.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper for HIMA was returned. The searches did not reach krishikosh.egranth.ac.in or AICRP-Small Millets pages.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for HIMA. The only seed result was an IndiaMART listing -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/ragi-seeds-22588354655.html -- for generic "Ragi Seeds" sold by a Rajahmundry, Andhra Pradesh dealer. It names no variety, so it is not evidence of HIMA seed availability.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Andhra Pradesh only, from the input record (recommended_states_raw). No search source confirmed this.

Limitations: the search tool returned poor HIMA-specific coverage. I used all four permitted searches, so no further queries were run. Before this record is used, check the seednet.gov.in variety page for A0204123, the CSC/AICRP-Small Millets release notification, and KrishiKosh for HIMA. Those sources were not reached.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Indira Ragi-1 / Indira Ragi-1 (BR-7), finger millet (ragi/mandika)

Name note: The evidence refers to "Indira Ragi 1" (the CSC release-minute name, as spelled in the ICAR-IIMR table). The Seednet name "Indira Ragi-1 (BR-7)" appears only through the code BR-7, which shows up in a state-wise list in the IIMR brochure. The BR-7 code is therefore only a weak link to this variety. Search 4 returned no Seednet page.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Indira Ragi-1. The IIMR table describes this variety as non-shattering, non-lodging, responsive to fertilizers and notes high finger number, but these are agronomic traits, not stress-tolerance data. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The IIMR table's blast-resistance entries belong to other rows (for example, the VL 376 row), so they cannot be attributed to Indira Ragi-1. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Physical and engineering grain and panicle properties of Indira Ragi-1 were measured for thresher design, with finger length ranged between 72 to 110 mm. The paper lists "Indira Ragi 1" alongside CG Ragi 2 and GPU-28 as prominent Chhattisgarh varieties. No multi-location yield trial data was found. -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/67%20Studies%20on%20some%20Physical%20and%20Engineering%20properties%20of%20Finger%20Millet%20for%20Designing%20Thresher%20Geeta%20Patel.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage is recorded as HR-911 x GE-669 (the table gives "HR 911 x GE 669"). No QTL, marker, or genomic study naming this variety was found. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The IIMR table records the origin as Jagdalpur, IGKVV (Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya), with release year 2012 and maturity of 120-125 days. No breeder name was found. The input says the institution is "Research Farm SGCARS," and this name does not appear in any search result. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone, address, or contact-page URL for IGKVV Jagdalpur or SGCARS appeared in the results. The IIMR brochure is an institute document, but its snippet has no contact details. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/brochures/Finger_Millet_Brochure.pdf

PUBLICATIONS --
Patel, G., et al. (2022). Studies on some Physical and Engineering properties of Finger Millet for Designing Thresher. Biological Forum – An International Journal 14(4): 387-393 -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/67%20Studies%20on%20some%20Physical%20and%20Engineering%20properties%20of%20Finger%20Millet%20for%20Designing%20Thresher%20Geeta%20Patel.pdf
(Author list is inferred from the file name and the "Patel et al." running head; the first name is not confirmed on the page.)
No other paper naming this variety was found. Searches also returned the Rapid Ragi speed-breeding paper (Sajja et al., 2025, https://plantmethods.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s13007-025-01403-7) and a 2018 IJCMAS ragi food paper, but neither names Indira Ragi-1, so both were discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The only seller hit is "Indira Traders" in Walajapet, Tamil Nadu, which is a name resemblance and was discarded. The other hits are generic ragi retailers and online stores that do not name this variety. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or Seednet listing was found. -- https://www.exportersindia.com/indian-suppliers/finger-millet-seeds.htm

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Chhattisgarh. The IIMR table lists Indira Ragi 1 under Chhattisgarh. The IIMR brochure's state-wise list includes Chhattisgarh-2, BR-7, GPU 28, PR 202, VR 708, which supports BR-7 being a Chhattisgarh variety but does not name Indira Ragi-1 directly. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf ; https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/brochures/Finger_Millet_Brochure.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Blast tolerance is reported for KMR-301 in a summary table of finger millet breeding: "High grain and straw yield, tolerant to blast" -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336439015_Finger_Millet_Eleusine_coracana_L_Gartn_Breeding
- A UAS Bangalore 2023 field study describes KMR-301 as a high-yielding, blast-tolerant variety -- https://uasbangalore.edu.in/images/2023-3rd-Issue/21.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to KMR-301. The searches returned only general finger millet material.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Blast tolerance is the only disease or pest trait found for KMR-301 (see Stress Tolerance above). No evidence found for other diseases or pests, or for pest resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A UAS Bangalore 2023 study used KMR-301 in an integrated nutrient management trial, planted at 25 x 15 cm, and reported growth and yield parameters -- https://uasbangalore.edu.in/images/2023-3rd-Issue/21.pdf
- A fertilizer-recommendation study reports nutrient availability in soil after harvest of KMR 301 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/319008258_Evaluation_of_different_approaches_of_fertilizer_recommendation_on_finger_millet_Eleusine_coracana_L_yield_nutrient_requirement_and_economics
- A speed-breeding protocol paper found KMR 301 did not flower under one nutrient regime but flowered early under Hoagland's solution, with reduced cycle time -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13007-025-01403-7
- Station trial data for KMR-301 appear only as a check variety. In a comparison, KMR-340 gave 48.00 kg/ha against KMR-301 at 40.55 kg/ha over three years, at VC Farm Mandya. Units as printed. KMR-301 was the check, not the test entry -- https://dhan.org/smallmilletfoundation/document/smallmillet-national-seminar1.pdf
- Agronomy table: yield entry of 55-60 for KMR 301, duration 120-125 days, pedigree MR 1 x GE 1409, developed at VC Farm Mandya, Southern Dry Zone of Karnataka. Yield unit not printed in the snippet -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
- Karnataka rabi advisory: KMR-301 is suitable for rabi and recommended for irrigated conditions -- https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/tips-for-farmers/icar-agri-advisory-for-rabi-2021-22/icar-rabi-season-agro-advisory-for-karnataka?lgn=en

GENETICS AND QTL
- A speed-breeding paper uses KMR 301 as a genotype in its protocol (see Agronomy and Trials). No QTL, marker or genomic study naming KMR-301 was found -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13007-025-01403-7
- Pedigree is recorded as MR 1 x GE 1409, not PR-202 x GE1409 as in the input record -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-16-9257-4_8 ; https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
- No evidence found for PR-202 as a parent of KMR-301 in the retrieved sources.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Name evidence: the search results refer to KMR-301 (not KMR-630 or "Gowri"). I did not run a separate search for KMR-630 or Gowri, so there is no evidence on whether those names refer to this variety.
- Developing institution: UAS Bengaluru, VC Farm, Mandya, Karnataka -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-16-9257-4_8 ; https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The sources name the station, not a breeder. A retired small-millets breeder at VC Farm is mentioned in a press item, but no link to KMR-301 is stated -- https://www.smartfood.org/project/now-white-ragi-gives-nutritious-food-a-makeover/ (not attributed to KMR-301)

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found for a breeder contact, email, phone or postal address. No institute contact page for VC Farm Mandya or the UAS Bengaluru millet programme was retrieved in these searches.

A farmer-impact study reports that KMR-204 is preferred for late sowing when rains are delayed, which is an agronomic preference rather than a measured drought-tolerance result. disease_resistance.summary: Neck and finger blast: (1) reported as a genetic advantage over local varieties and recommended for southern dry zone Karnataka; (2) rated resistant in a 2014-2016 natural-field screen of released and pre-released varieties; (3) used as a resistant check in a multi-location blast GGE-biplot study; (4) neck and finger blast scores of about 1-2% in Mandya trials for 2013 and 2014 as a check, on par with OUAT-2; (5) listed among blast-resistant genotypes in a review, alongside GPU-28 and MR-6. Foot rot (Sclerotium rolfsii): resistance reported under two artificial inoculation methods; the digest does not give a numeric severity score for this variety.

pest_resistance.summary: No insect-pest resistance data specific to KMR 204 were found in the searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: National release table: 30-35 q/ha (Karnataka). Farmer-level study (Mandya, 2016): somewhat more grain and straw yield than Indaf-9 under rainfed and irrigated conditions, but the difference was not significant. Multi-location station trials 2013-2015 at Mandya: mean grain yield about 41 q/ha, with KMR-204 as the check. The CSC record gives the average yield unit only as Kg/Ha, with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The digest does not report variety-level stability statistics; KMR-204 was used as a resistant check in a blast GGE-biplot study, but its stability result is not stated.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for southern dry zone Karnataka (farmer-impact study). Listed for Karnataka in the national release table.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 100-105 days (national release table; same figures in a decade-release table)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Described as high yielding and short duration (UAS Bengaluru release list). Morphological characteristics were not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Farmer-level study, Mandya, 2016: KMR-204 gave somewhat more grain and straw yield than Indaf-9 under rainfed and irrigated conditions; difference not significant. (2) Multi-location station trials 2013-2015, Mandya: mean grain yield about 41 q/ha; KMR-340 about 7-8% higher than KMR-204, which served as the check. (3) Natural-field blast screen 2014-2016 of released and pre-released varieties: KMR-204 rated resistant to neck and finger blast. (4) Mandya trials 2013 and 2014: neck and finger blast scores about 1-2% for KMR-204 as a check, on par with OUAT-2. (5) Multi-environment GGE-biplot blast study: KMR-204 used as resistant check. No additional trial results were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Blast tolerance is reported as a genetic advantage of KMR-204 over local varieties, and it was recommended for southern dry zone Karnataka -- https://zenodo.org/records/827430
- Preferred for late sowing when rains are delayed, per the same farmer-impact study -- https://ageconsearch.umn.edu/record/357095/files/Raghupathi1812017AJAEES34917.pdf
- Reaction to neck and finger blast was rated resistant in a 2014-2016 natural-field screen of released and pre-released varieties -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361506944_Identification_of_resistant_sources_of_finger_millet_varieties_against_neck_and_finger_blast_disease
- KMR-204 was used as a resistant check in a multi-location blast GGE-biplot study -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0885576525003121
- Resistance to foot rot (Sclerotium rolfsii) under two artificial inoculation methods -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42161-026-02273-1
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence specific to KMR 204 was found. The general dryland note in the ICAR brochure does not name this variety -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/brochures/Finger_Millet_Brochure.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Neck and finger blast disease scores in Mandya trials for 2013 and 2014 were about 1-2% for KMR-204 as a check, on par with OUAT-2 -- https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0004931
- Listed among blast-resistant genotypes in a review, alongside GPU-28 and MR-6 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380214295_Diseases_of_Finger_Millet_and_their_Management_A_Review
- No insect-pest resistance data specific to KMR 204 was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Released 2011-12 by UAS Bengaluru; described as high yielding and short duration -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/list-of-crop-varieties-hybrids-released-by-uasb-during-last-ten-years/
- Maturity 100-105 days and yield 30-35 q/ha, listed for Karnataka; release year given as 2012 in the table -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
- Same maturity and yield figures in a table of finger millet releases in the last decade -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- Farmer-level study (Mandya, 2016): KMR-204 gave somewhat more grain and straw yield than Indaf-9 under rainfed and irrigated conditions, but the difference was not significant -- https://zenodo.org/records/827430
- Multi-location trials 2013-2015 at Mandya: mean grain yield about 41 q/ha in station trials, with KMR-204 as the check; KMR-340 was about 7-8% higher -- https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0004931
- Recommended finger millet agronomy (spacing, seed rate, and similar) is generic and not variety-specific -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/brochures/Finger_Millet_Brochure.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- KMR-204 was one of two genotypes irradiated (gamma rays and EMS) in a mutant-population path analysis study -- https://doi.org/10.9734/ijecc/2022/v12i121676
- Parentage recorded as GPU 26 x GE-1409, with selection from a PR 1158-9 background noted in one source -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf
- No QTL or marker study specific to KMR 204 was found. The blast QTL map paper concerns other germplasm -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807240

- Developing body: University of Agricultural Sciences, Bengaluru (UASB), via the AICRP on Small Millets at ZARS, V.C. Farm, Mandya -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/small-millets-zars-vc-farm-mandya/
- Release listed by UAS Bengaluru in the 2011-12 list -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/list-of-crop-varieties-hybrids-released-by-uasb-during-last-ten-years/
- Lead breeder or scientist name for KMR 204: No evidence found. The Mandya small-millets unit page lists the variety with its release year but no breeder name -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/small-millets-zars-vc-farm-mandya/
- Release-year discrepancy: CSC minutes say 2014-02-14; the sources say 2011 or 2012 -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/small-millets-zars-vc-farm-mandya/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY RECORD: Phule Panchami (variety_name, CSC minutes; sorghum) / PHULE NACHANI (seednet_variety_name; Seednet lists it under finger millet)

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The search returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data for Phule Panchami. The drought-tolerance results were Ethiopian sorghum landrace studies that do not name this variety, so I discarded them. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9768483/ (discarded, not this variety)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The AICRP-Sorghum 2020-21 breeding report tests shoot fly and charcoal rot, but the retrieved text does not attach Phule Panchami to those tests. -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip20/Sorghum/reports20/Rb/1-Sorghum-Breeding-Rabi-agm21.pdf (not attributed)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Name evidence: Phule Panchami (sorghum). Popping-quality and yield trials at Rahuri appear in the AICRP reports below. The 2019-20 Rahuri popping entry shows grain yield 1535 kg/ha, 76 days to 50% flowering, 120 days to maturity, plant height 226 cm, and grain weight 2.08 g per 100 seeds. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip19/Sorghum/reports19/Rabi/1-Breeding-Rabi.pdf
Name evidence: Phule Panchami (sorghum). In the 2020-21 AICRP Rabi Sorghum breeding report, the check Phule Panchami yielded 2330 kg/ha and matured at about 121 days. A test entry, SPV 2630, yielded 2623 kg/ha, about 12% more than this check. -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip20/Sorghum/reports20/Rb/1-Sorghum-Breeding-Rabi-agm21.pdf
Name evidence: Phule Panchami (sorghum). A 2020-21 multi-location study at Dharwad, Vijayapura, and Nandyal (AICRP-Sorghum) ranked Phule Panchami among genotypes with superior nutritional and thousand-weight values. -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0733521023000267

GENETICS AND QTL
Name evidence: Phule Panchami (sorghum). The variety was bred from local landraces collected in the Nandurbar districts of Maharashtra, so the parentage is a landrace selection rather than a documented cross. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip09/rabi09/report/pr-rabi2009-10.pdf
Name evidence: Phule Panchami (sorghum). Related genetic stocks, RPOSV 3 as IC 573124 and RSV 1006 as IC 573124, were registered at NBPGR New Delhi. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip09/rabi09/report/pr-rabi2009-10.pdf
No QTL or marker study naming Phule Panchami was found. The trichome and glossiness QTL text in the 2020-21 report is general to the programme and does not name this variety. -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip20/Sorghum/reports20/Rb/1-Sorghum-Breeding-Rabi-agm21.pdf (not attributed)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Name evidence: Phule Panchami (sorghum). Dr. S. R. Gadakh is named as the breeder and as the Rahuri centre scientist who released the variety; M. S. Shinde is co-listed in the 2009-10 report. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip09/rabi09/report/pr-rabi2009-10.pdf

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to Phule Dhani. Dharani/TCGS-1043 rainfed drought results from a Chittoor trial were discarded because they concern another variety.

heat.details: No direct heat tolerance trial for Phule Dhani was found. A DSSAT simulation study (Dharwad, Karnataka) reported that JL-1085 showed the smallest anthesis-related duration reduction (six days) under warmer climate scenarios compared with other summer varieties. This is a modelling result, not a measured heat tolerance test, so no tolerance level is assigned.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to Phule Dhani.

disease_resistance.summary: Phule Dhani is described as resistant to foliar diseases. The same trait is listed for JL-1085 (Phule Dhani). Specific leaf spot, rust or stem rot scores: Not found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Phule Dhani is described as resistant to Spodoptera and thrips. The same trait is listed for JL-1085 (Phule Dhani). No pest-specific trial data were found.

agronomic_details.yield: Yield potential 3333 kg/ha (notified figure). Multi-location yield data beyond this figure: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location stability data were retrieved.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for central kharif cultivation in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. Oil content reported as 50%. A DSSAT simulation (Dharwad, Karnataka) suggested relatively small duration loss under warmer scenarios, but this is not a field validation.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: High shelling percentage and mostly three-seeded pods (as listed for JL-1085 (Phule Dhani)). Oil content 50%.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Summer groundnut fertilizer trial at MPKV using JL-1085 (Phule Dhani): dry matter responded to fertilizer level, and 100% RDF was on par with higher levels. (2) Biofertilizer trial (Rhizobium + PSB) with JL-1085 (Phule Dhani), reported in the Journal of Oilseeds Research 2018-2020 compilation; no numerical results were given in the digest. (3) DSSAT simulation study (Dharwad, Karnataka): JL-1085 showed the smallest anthesis-related duration reduction (six days) under warmer climate scenarios; this is a simulation, not a field trial. No other multi-location trial results were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Phule Dhani (JL 1085), groundnut
Name check: "Phule Dhani" (CSC minutes name) is the name the groundnut evidence uses. Under the Seednet name "PHULE NACHANI" (finger millet), every page found concerns a different crop, so none is attributed to this record. The Seednet portal page itself was not retrieved.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Dharani/TCGS-1043 drought results (Chittoor trial) are about another variety, so they were discarded. No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Phule Dhani. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370472451_Performance_of_Groundnut_var_Dharani_under_Rainfed_conditions_in_western_mandals_of_Chittoor_district (discarded, other variety)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Phule Dhani is described as resistant to foliar diseases and to Spodoptera and thrips. -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
- Same traits (foliar disease resistance, Spodoptera and thrips resistance, high shelling %, mostly three-seeded pods) are listed for JL-1085 (Phule Dhani). -- https://www.irjmets.com/uploadedfiles/paper/issue_1_january_2025/66214/final/fin_irjmets1736768730.pdf
- Specific leaf spot, rust or stem rot scores for Phule Dhani: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield potential 3333 kg/ha, kharif, oil content 50%, release year 2019. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Simulation study (DSSAT, Dharwad, Karnataka): JL-1085 showed the smallest anthesis-related duration reduction (six days) under warmer climate scenarios, compared with other summer varieties. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2022/vol11issue8S/PartU/S-11-8-193-158.pdf
- Summer groundnut fertilizer trial at MPKV using JL-1085 (Phule Dhani): dry matter responded to fertilizer level; 100% RDF was on par with higher levels. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348391300_Effect_of_inorganic_and_bio-fertilizers_on_growth_of_summer_groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L
- Biofertilizer trial (Rhizobium + PSB) with JL-1085 (Phule Dhani) reported in Journal of Oilseeds Research, 2018–2020 compilation. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/363336272_THE_INDIAN_SOCIETY_OF_OILSEEDS_RESEARCH_EXECUTIVE_COUNCIL_FOR_2018-2020_JOURNAL_OF_OILSEEDS_RESEARCH
- Multi-location yield data beyond the notified 3333 kg/ha figure: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No QTL, marker, pedigree or parentage study for Phule Dhani was retrieved. Parentage in the record is "Not specified."

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Notified as "Phule Dhani JL 1085", developed by MPKV, Rahuri, central notification, kharif. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.
- Oilseed Research Station (named in the record as the institution): no station-specific page found; only MPKV is confirmed as developer.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found for Phule Dhani.
- Institute-level address (MPKV, Rahuri, from a PPV&FR compendium entry that names MPKV; not a contact page for this variety): Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth, Rahuri - 413722, Dist. Ahmednagar, Maharashtra. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compendiumforextantnotified-nov-2021.pdf
- Official email, phone or Oilseed Research Station contact page: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Satpute A., Shinde T. S., Shende S. (year not stated). Effect of inorganic and bio-fertilizers on growth of summer groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.). Journal/report not stated (ResearchGate record; MPKV authors) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348391300_Effect_of_inorganic_and_bio-fertilizers_on_growth_of_summer_groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L
- Authors not shown (2022). Response of summer groundnut varieties to the changing climates in Dharwad district of Karnataka using DSSAT model. The Pharma Journal 11(8S) -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2022/vol11issue8S/PartU/S-11-8-193-158.pdf
- Authors not shown (2018–2020). Effect of biofertilizers on growth, yield and quality of groundnut (includes JL-1085). Journal of Oilseeds Research -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/363336272_THE_INDIAN_SOCIETY_OF_OILSEEDS_RESEARCH_EXECUTIVE_COUNCIL_FOR_2018-2020_JOURNAL_OF_OILSEEDS_RESEARCH
- CSC/AICRP-G research papers, ICAR annual reports, KrishiKosh theses on Phule Dhani: No evidence found in the retrieved results.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer stock of Phule Dhani. Returned pages were generic groundnut seed sellers (for example https://www.usaseedslimited.com/groundnut.html and https://www.gopalindustries.com/groundnut-seeds.html), which do not name this variety, so they were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka, kharif. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Notification S.O. 3220(E), dated 05.09.2019, lists Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka for central kharif cultivation. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
- Note: the DAC state-wise table snippet for Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka does not list Phule Dhani, so the recommendation rests on the release entry and notification rather than that table.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Chhattisgarh's ICAR state page lists Poornima among high-yielding, drought-tolerant early rice varieties suited to the state's upland drought constraint (name: Poornima; crop: rice) -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/17261
- No other stress-tolerance evidence (flood, submergence, salinity, heat) was found for Poornima. The POORNA/finger millet search returned nothing on stress tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for Poornima rice. The ICAR state page names gall midge and bacterial leaf blight as constraints but does not link Poornima to resistance -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/17261
- The Raipur AICRIP station page lists insect-resistant varieties developed there; Poornima is not among those named -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/06%20Raipur.pdf
- POORNA (finger millet): No evidence found. Results were unrelated ragi seed sellers and a finger millet varieties PDF that does not mention POORNA -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/finger_millets_varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The Raipur AICRIP station page gives the Poornima entry as IET 12284, notified under S.O. 360(E) dated 1-5-97, and describes it as high yielding with short bold grain of good quality -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/06%20Raipur.pdf
- Date conflict: the CSC metadata gives release year 2014, but the Raipur page gives a 1997 notification. Both are unresolved; the 1997 notification is the only dated record found.
- Poornima is named among early varieties to grow in Chhattisgarh, with a state productivity average of about 1.3 t/ha for rice -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/17261
- POORNA (finger millet): No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The Raipur page and search results contained no QTL or marker study on Poornima.
- Parentage (CO 1 x Aruna, from the CSC record) was not confirmed by any retrieved source.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Poornima is listed among rice varieties developed by IGKV, Raipur (Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya) -- https://www.extensionjournal.com/article/view/1113/7-9-77
- The Raipur Rice Research Station page names the institution's rice research centre under Dr. R. H. Richharia's leadership. No source links him or any named scientist to Poornima, so no individual breeder is attributed here -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/06%20Raipur.pdf
- Institution for POORNA (finger millet): No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. No IGKV Raipur or breeder email, phone, postal address, or contact-page URL was retrieved in any result.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated (year not stated). Area under different rice varieties in Chhattisgarh state. Extension journal article -- https://www.extensionjournal.com/article/view/1113/7-9-77
- Authors not stated (year not stated). AICRIP variety list naming Poornima (within a truncated list of varieties in an impact study; context not fully visible). Impact of breeder seed multiplication and certified quality seed distribution on rice production in India -- https://www.cabidigitallibrary.org/doi/full/10.1186/s43170-022-00099-2
- No research paper, thesis, or DOI specific to Poornima was found. No KrishiKosh record was retrieved.
- POORNA (finger millet): No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for Poornima rice. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, IGKV seed sales, or dealer listing was retrieved.
- POORNA (finger millet): No evidence found. No Seednet portal page for POORNA was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Chhattisgarh, per the CSC record and the ICAR state page that recommends Poornima for the state -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/17261
- The Raipur AICRIP page appears to list Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Assam, and Chhattisgarh near the Poornima entry, but the sentence is fragmentary and the state list cannot be confidently attributed to Poornima -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/06%20Raipur.pdf
- POORNA (finger millet): No evidence found. Seednet's finger millet crop label conflicts with the rice label in the CSC record.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CPRMV-1 / PRM-1 (millet)

Search note: four web searches were run in one batch. A fifth search, to check the crop identity of CPRMV-1, was blocked by the tool-use limit. The crop identity is therefore unresolved (see below).

CRITICAL CONFLICT: The only page that names CPRMV-1 describes it as a proso millet variety, not finger millet. The supplied record says finger millet (ragi/mandika) and the Seednet name is PRM-1 for finger millet. Verify the crop and the release notification before using any of this record.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for finger millet (CPRMV-1 or PRM-1) drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. -- No URL (searched; nothing relevant)

DISEASE AND PEST
- The Krishi Jagran article titled as a proso millet CPRMV-1 variety reports resistance to brown spot, leaf blast and leaf blight, and moderate resistance to banded blight. This applies to proso millet as described, not confirmed for finger millet. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/proso-millet-cprmv-1-a-disease-resistance-and-high-yielding-variety/
- No finger millet-specific pest or disease evidence found for PRM-1. -- No URL (searched)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found for CPRMV-1 or PRM-1 maturity, yield or multi-location trial results. The Krishi Jagran page (proso-titled) is the only variety-specific page returned, and its yield claims were not captured in the search results. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/proso-millet-cprmv-1-a-disease-resistance-and-high-yielding-variety/
- A paper on Trichoderma effects on ragi uses three unnamed ragi varieties. It does not identify PRM-1 or CPRMV-1. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9673954 (not evidence for this variety)

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. -- No URL (searched)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No evidence found naming a lead breeder or scientist for CPRMV-1 or PRM-1. The institution in the record is the ICAR-AICRP on Sorghum and Millets, Main Agricultural Research Station, University of Agricultural Sciences (no station location or SAU is specified in the record). -- No URL (searched)

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found for any breeder, institute-level email, phone, postal address or contact page. -- No URL (searched)

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. The returned items were not on this variety: a ResearchGate North-East India millet cultivation article (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/401198496_VOLUME_8_-ISSUE_3_-MARCH_2026_Insights_of_Millet_Cultivation_in_North-East_India_Article_ID_73023) and a ResearchGate paper on finger millet production systems in Tamil Nadu (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/326989228_Mapping_of_Diverse_Production_System_of_Finger_Millet_Eleusine_Corocana_L_in_Tamil_Nadu). Neither names CPRMV-1 or PRM-1.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer sales of CPRMV-1 or PRM-1. -- No URL (searched)

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The record's stated recommendation (Karnataka and Tamil Nadu) is not confirmed by any search result. The Tamil Nadu finger millet mapping paper lists Karnataka and Tamil Nadu among lead finger millet states generally, which is context only and not variety-specific. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/326989228_Mapping_of_Diverse_Production_System_of_Finger_Millet_Eleusine_Corocana_L_in_Tamil_Nadu

Open items to resolve: confirm the crop (proso vs finger millet) for CPRMV-1 against the CSC release minutes; confirm the Seednet entry PRM-1 for finger millet; then rerun the breeder, publication and seed searches.

drought.details: None of the search results mention VL Mandua 410. The sources only give general statements that millets are climate resilient and tolerant of drought and poor soils. These are crop-level claims and cannot be attributed to this variety. No variety-specific drought data were found.

heat.details: The sources state generally that millets tolerate heat and drought stress. No heat tolerance data exist for VL Mandua 410 in the results.

salinity.details: One snippet mentions alkalinity and salt problems in the context of millets in general. It gives no variety-specific salinity reaction.

flood.details: No flood tolerance information for this variety was found. A snippet notes that pearl millet is sensitive to waterlogging, which is a different crop.

disease_resistance.summary: The official record states the disease reaction is not specified. The sources identify blast (neck and finger) as a serious disease of finger millet in general, and mention other finger millet varieties resistant to blast, banded blight and foot rot. None of this is attributed to VL Mandua 410.

pest_resistance.summary: The official record states the pest reaction is not specified. A general statement says finger millet is relatively less affected by insect pests. No variety-specific data were found.

The 2024 ICAR-IIMR compendium lists the related variety VL Mandua 400 (CFMV5, FMV1162) for other states, which suggests the variety series is documented there, but VL Mandua 410 itself is not mentioned.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: VL Mandua 400 (CSC name) / VL Mandua 380 (Seednet name)

Searches run: 4 (variety and trial data; breeder and institute; research papers; seed availability). No dedicated contact-page search returned an email or phone number, so CONTACT DETAILS is limited.

Name note: The evidence is split. VL Mandua 400 (CFMV 5) appears in a millet extension table with the CSC recommended states. VL Mandua 380 appears on the ICAR-VPKAS seed portal and in a 2023 journal article. I found no source stating that the two names are the same variety, so the two entries below are kept separate.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- VL Mandua 380 is described as blast tolerant, and the 2023 article calls it a medium-maturing, high-yielding, blast-tolerant cultivar -- https://thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue12/PartM/12-11-90-482.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data specific to VL Mandua 400 or 380 were found. The general drought tolerance of finger millet in the ICN article is crop-level, not variety-level -- https://www.icnnational.com/millet-ragi-a-profitable-climate-resilient-cereal-for-indian-f

DISEASE AND PEST
- Blast (Pyricularia grisea) is named as the major finger millet disease in the ICAR brochure. This is crop-level, not variety-specific -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/brochures/Finger_Millet_Brochure.pdf
- VL Mandua 380 is described as blast-tolerant in the 2023 article. Resistance ratings for VL Mandua 400 were not found -- https://thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue12/PartM/12-11-90-482.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- VL Mandua 400 (CFMV5) is listed with maturity of 102 days and figures given as GY 34.77 and FY 84.80, with units not stated in the snippet -- https://www.millets.res.in/farmer/2025/Millets_chalisa/English/6Millets_chalisa_finger_mii (the 2025 millet extension chart)
- A seed-production table lists VL Mandua 400 at 100-102 days and 3,250 kg/ha. This is in a Himalayan context and appears to be a seed-production table, so the figure may not be a general yield claim -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385515627_Problems_and_Prospects_of_Seed_Production_in_Minor_Millets_and_Other_Potential_Crops_with_Special_Reference_to_Himalayan_States_of_India
- The same table lists VL Mandua 380 at 116-118 days and 1,820 (units unclear), with a 2019 notification reference (S.O. 1498(E), 01.4.2019) placed near the 380 entry. Its exact pairing with the 380 row is unclear -- same URL
- The 2023 article reports VL Mandua 380 trials under organic conditions over three years with 45 farmers in Uttarakhand, and IVT trials at 10 locations under inorganic conditions. The article's own grain-yield values were not extracted in the snippet -- https://thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue12/PartM/12-11-90-482.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No parentage or pedigree for VL Mandua 400 or 380 was found. The 2023 article gives the pedigree of the related VL Mandua 378 (GEC-440 x VL Mandua 149) and says it was developed by pedigree selection, not the 380 pedigree -- https://thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue12/PartM/12-11-90-482.pdf
- No QTL or marker studies were found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The 2023 article on VL Mandua 380 is from ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan (VPKAS), Almora, Uttarakhand. The breeder name for VL Mandua 380 is not stated in the retrieved text -- https://thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue12/PartM/12-11-90-482.pdf
- DC Joshi, Senior Scientist, Department of Plant Breeding, ICAR-VPKAS, Almora, is named as corresponding author of the closely related VL Mandua 378 article. Whether he bred VL Mandua 380 or 400 is not confirmed -- same URL
- No breeder or developer named for VL Mandua 400 (CFMV 5) was found.

CONTACT DETAILS

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Note: the search budget ran out during my second run. My first run had already made the four searches, but I re-ran them to get fuller snippets, which used up the limit. Everything below comes from the first run's truncated snippets, so several headings are thin. Please treat the findings as partial.

EVIDENCE DIGEST

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The searches returned no page on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for VL Mandua-352 or VL Mandua 382.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No page on disease or pest resistance for either name was retrieved.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. The only trial-type result was a Frontiers article (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2023.1198023/full) reporting millet yields in Mg/ha, but the snippet did not name VL Mandua-352 or VL Mandua 382, so I discarded it.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. Parentage "WR … 2 / VL 201" (the release record's garbled "WR ??? 2") could not be confirmed from any page retrieved.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Partial. The ICAR-VPKAS seed portal hosts product pages under the names "VL Mandua 352 / वी.एल. मंडुवा 352" (https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/index.php?route=product/category&path=74) and "VL Mandua 382 / वी.एल. मंडुवा 382" (https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/VLMandua382_%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%80.%E0%A4%8F%E0%A4%B2.%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%A1%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BE382). Both are VPKAS portal titles only; I did not see breeder names in the retrieved text. Breeder name(s): No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS: No breeder contact found. The only institute-level source is the VPKAS seed portal domain (https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/). No email, phone or postal address was retrieved, so none is listed.

PUBLICATIONS:
Gupta, A. and others (2015). Finger millet Variety VL Mandua 352. Journal/report not shown in snippet (ResearchGate record dated February 2015) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281060337_Finger_millet_Variety_VL_Mandua_352
Note: the snippet gave only the first author and "and others", so the full author list is unverified. The record is a variety description and I did not confirm its content.

SEED AVAILABILITY: Partial. The VPKAS seed portal lists VL Mandua 352 and VL Mandua 382 product pages (URLs above). Prices, stock and dealer details were not retrieved. The portal's URL for the "382" page and the release name "VL Mandua-352" are not the same string, so confirm with VPKAS which variety the seed portal's 382 listing refers to.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. The release record's text ("All finger millet growing states except Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra") was not confirmed by any retrieved page.

Name check: "variety_name" is VL Mandua-352 and "seednet_variety_name" is VL Mandua 382. The evidence above mostly refers to VL Mandua 352 (VPKAS page and ResearchGate record), with one portal page under 382. I did not confirm that the two names refer to the same variety.

Suggested next steps: check the VPKAS seed portal pages directly, the CSC/ICAR release notification for VL Mandua-352, and KrishiKosh for the 2015 publication, since the search could not verify these.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease resistance established. Purple blotch: in a Kolar (Karnataka) screen of 26 garlic genotypes, Bhima Omkar had the highest purple blotch disease index (65.20%) and was rated highly susceptible. The DOGR site lists the variety as susceptible to thrips (see pest_resistance).

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance established. Garlic thrips: the DOGR site lists Bhima Omkar as susceptible, so no thrips tolerance is established. The Kolar screen reported a thrips count for Bhima Omkar among genotype values, but the snippet gives no clear figure for this variety, so it is not relied on.

agronomic_details.yield: DOGR site: 8-14 t/ha. DOGR-era comparison table (ResearchGate): 8-10 t/ha. The two sources give different ranges. The CSC record lists the unit as Kg/Ha without a value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Delhi, Gujarat, Haryana, Rajasthan (DOGR). Photoperiod class: short-day white garlic (DOGR-era comparison table). No adaptation or ecology data beyond these were found.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Medium-sized, compact white bulbs (DOGR). Short-day white garlic (DOGR-era comparison table). High TSS of 35.93 Brix recorded in a 2019 garlic genotype comparison (IJCMAS).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Kolar (Karnataka) genotype screen of 26 garlic genotypes: purple blotch disease index 65.20%, highest among genotypes, rated highly susceptible; thrips count not clearly reported for this variety. (2) 2019 garlic genotype comparison (IJCMAS): TSS 35.93 Brix. (3) Tribal sub-plan demonstrations in Nandurbar, Maharashtra: 10 demonstrations involving 100 farmers. No yield trial data beyond the ranges above were found.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Not found in searched sources. A seed-production review states that Bhima Omkar seed is not produced on a commercial scale, and NHRDF is the only body producing certified garlic planting material.
commercial_info.private_dealers: No verified dealer found. A trader listing for "Pure Bhima Omkar Garlic" bulbs in Visakhapatnam exists, but it is a commercial produce listing with no seed-certification detail and is not treated as a verified seed source. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY NAME CHECK: "variety_name" and "seednet_variety_name" are both "Bhima Omkar", so every search and finding below refers to the same name. No Seednet portal page for this variety came up in any search, so no Seednet-specific evidence is recorded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Garlic thrips: the DOGR site lists this variety as susceptible to thrips, so no thrips tolerance is established -- https://dogr.icar.gov.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=80&Itemid=114&lang=en
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found. The search returned only general garlic irrigation and yield-response studies from other varieties or locations, which were discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Purple blotch: in a Kolar (Karnataka) genotype screen of 26 garlic genotypes, Bhima Omkar had the highest purple blotch disease index (65.20%) and was rated highly susceptible -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331199294_Reaction_of_garlic_genotypes_to_thrips_and_purple_blotch_in_South_India
- Thrips: in the same Kolar screen, Bhima Omkar's thrips count was reported among the genotype values, but the snippet does not give a clear figure for this variety, so only the DOGR susceptibility statement is relied on -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331199294_Reaction_of_garlic_genotypes_to_thrips_and_purple_blotch_in_South_India

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Recommended states, maturity and yield: the variety matures in 120-135 days with an average yield of 8-14 t/ha and produces medium-sized compact white bulbs -- https://dogr.icar.gov.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=126&Itemid=178&lang=en
- Same maturity, yield and bulb description on the DOGR garlic page, which also gives the recommended states -- https://www.dogr.res.in/index.php/component/content/article/garlicagropedia?layout=edit
- Photoperiod class: the DOGR-era comparison table lists Bhima Omkar as a short-day white garlic with 8-10 t/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332143333_Onion_and_garlic_research_in_India
- Sensory and quality: in a 2019 garlic genotype comparison, Bhima Omkar recorded a high TSS of 35.93 °Brix -- https://www.ijcmas.com/8-4-2019/S.N.%20Shibana%20and%20Jalaja%20S.%20Menon.pdf
- Field demonstrations: Bhima Omkar was used in tribal sub-plan garlic demonstrations in Nandurbar, Maharashtra (10 demonstrations, 100 farmers) -- https://www.dogr.res.in/index.php/component/content/article/tsp?layout=edit

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for QTL or marker studies on this variety. The search returned only in vitro, tissue-culture and biotechnology work on garlic, and those results were discarded unless they named Bhima Omkar.
- Tissue-culture material: an in vitro slow-growth conservation study used Bhima Omkar and Bhima Purple meristem-derived plantlets -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12320307/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Breeder name(s): No evidence found. No search returned a named lead breeder for Bhima Omkar.
- Developing institution: ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (DOGR), Rajgurunagar, Pune, is recorded as the developer of Bhima Omkar -- https://www.dogr.res.in/
- Notification: the Central Varietal Release Committee notified Bhima Omkar -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/view/87678
- Release year: the record's 2017-09-18 date could not be verified. DOGR-linked tables give 2009 as the year of release or identification -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332143333_Onion_and_garlic_research_in_India
- Discarded: the author of the DOGR agri-business extension folder is not identified as a breeder of this variety, so that person is not recorded here -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356833474_Agri_Business_Incubation_ICAR-DOGR_Pune_extension_folder

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute postal address: ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research, Rajgurunagar, Pune – 410 505 (MS) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356833474_Agri_Business_Incubation_ICAR-DOGR_Pune_extension_folder
- Institute websites: https://www.dogr.res.in/ and https://dogr.icar.gov.in/
- Official email, phone and breeder contact: No evidence found in any retrieved result.

PUBLICATIONS
- Khar A, Lawande KE, Devi A, Mahajan V. (2011). Bhima Omkar a promising garlic variety. National Symposium on "Alliums: Current Scenario and Emerging Trends", Indian Society of Alliums. -- Cited in https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue1/PartM/7-5-674-325.pdf (full text not verified)
- Murkute AA, Gawande SJ. (2018). Production of virus free planting material through meristem culture in short day garlic cultivars Bhima Omkar and Bhima Purple. Journal of Essential Biology 39: 286–290. -- Cited in https://www.mdpi.com/2077-0472/16/7/811 (secondary citation; DOI not shown)
- Shibana SN, Menon JS. (2019). Comparative Evaluation of Garlic (Allium sativum L.) Genotypes. IJCMAS. -- https://www.ijcmas.com/8-4-2019/S.N.%20Shibana%20and%20Jalaja%20S.%20Menon.pdf
- Authors not shown. (Year not shown). Reaction of garlic genotypes to thrips and purple blotch in South India. ResearchGate. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331199294_Reaction_of_garlic_genotypes_to_thrips_and_purple_blotch_in_South_India
- Authors not shown. (2025). Optimizing in vitro slow-growth conservation media for garlic under ambient conditions. Springer, BMC Plant Biology -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12870-025-06892-1 (DOI 10.1186/s12870-025-06892-1; year inferred from DOI, not shown in text)
- Authors not shown. (Year not shown). Onion and garlic varieties. Indian Horticulture, ICAR e-pubs -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/view/87678
- Authors not shown. (Year not shown). Quality Seed Production of Onion & Garlic for Harnessing Export Potential. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/404067815_Quality_Seed_Production_of_Onion_Garlic_for_Harnessing_Export_Potential

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Commercial seed supply: a seed-production review states that Bhima Omkar seed is not produced on a commercial scale, and NHRDF is the only body producing certified garlic planting material -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/404067815_Quality_Seed_Production_of_Onion_Garlic_for_Harnessing_Export_Potential
- DOGR licensing: DOGR has licensed onion varieties to private firms, and a proposal exists for garlic planting-material multiplication with a private firm. No licence for Bhima Omkar was found -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-07/QRT-DOGR-01.pdf
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales and dealers: No evidence found for this variety. A trader listing for "Pure Bhima Omkar Garlic" bulbs in Visakhapatnam exists, but it is a commercial produce listing with no seed-certification detail, so it is not treated as a verified seed source -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/pure-bhima-omkar-garlic-23782325562.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Delhi, Gujarat, Haryana and Rajasthan -- https://dogr.icar.gov.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=126&Itemid=178&lang=en
- Same four states on the DOGR garlic page -- https://www.dogr.res.in/index.php/component/content/article/garlicagropedia?layout=edit

disease_resistance.summary: No pathogen resistance is attributed to GJG-5 in the searched sources. The little leaf disease finding in the combined FVegetableCropsVR.pdf proforma was excluded because its attribution is uncertain beside brinjal material. The little leaf and jassid tolerance statement in Variety-11-years.pdf was excluded because it belongs to a different crop. Stem rot, thrips and jassid tolerance is not established for GJG-5; the JAU report's stem rot, jassid and thrips tolerance belongs to a groundnut variety and was excluded. Separately, the JAU proforma (Variety-13-years.pdf) reports that the rabi clonal-selection garlic (named Gujarat Junagadh Garlic 5 (GJG 5) on the source) was tolerant of bolting and jointed bulbs, with lower bolting and jointed-bulb percentages than the check varieties. Bolting and jointed bulbs are physiological disorders rather than pathogens, so they are reported here for completeness and not as disease resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. Jassid and thrips tolerance is not established for GJG-5 in any clearly attributed source. The jassid and thrips statements in the JAU report refer to a groundnut variety, and the jassid statement in Variety-11-years.pdf refers to a different crop; all were excluded.

agronomic_details.yield: Proforma (FVegetableCropsVR.pdf): mean yield 79.42 q/ha (approximately 7,942 kg/ha) and potential yield 81.32 q/ha. A second proforma in the same file gives potential yield 93.24 q/ha and average yield 89.33 q/ha, which conflicts with the first set. A JAU characteristics sheet gives bulb yield 7535 kg/ha, but this entry carries a 1993 release year and is treated as unverified. A JAU report records bulb yield about 23.3 percent higher than check GG-4 and about 26.9 percent higher than check G-282 in rabi trials.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Rabi trial results are reported for Saurashtra and Middle Gujarat, but no stability analysis across environments was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rabi season trials in Saurashtra and Middle Gujarat, Gujarat. No wider agro-climatic adaptation data was found. The 2021-22 herbicide study was conducted at Junagadh, Gujarat.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 169 days (medium maturity group) per the JAU vegetable proforma. A JAU characteristics sheet gives 135 to 140 days, but this entry is unverified because of its conflicting 1993 release year.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height 44.88 cm, 12.23 leaves per plant, 17.85 cloves per bulb. Bulbs are medium, compact and white. Bolting and jointed-bulb percentages were lower than in check varieties (JAU proforma).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Rabi trials in Saurashtra and Middle Gujarat (JAU report): GJG-5 gave about 23.3 percent higher bulb yield than check GG-4 and about 26.9 percent higher than check G-282. (2) JAU vegetable proforma: mean yield 79.42 q/ha and potential yield 81.32 q/ha; a second proforma in the same file reports 89.33 q/ha average and 93.24 q/ha potential, which conflicts. (3) JAU research-station page: 79.42 q/ha yield and 2014 release, which conflicts with the 2017-09-18 release date in the variety profile. (4) 2021-22 rabi herbicide study at the Weed Control Research Farm, Department of Agronomy, College of Agriculture, JAU, Junagadh, using cv. GJG-5: compared herbicide mixtures for weed control and bulb yield, with a seed rate of 500-600 kg cloves per ha and 15 x 10 cm spacing. Results of the herbicide comparison were not reported in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Under the Gujarat name for the rabi crop, the proforma lists a clonal-selection garlic that was tolerant of bolting and jointed bulbs, and that showed lower bolting and jointed-bulb percentages than the check varieties (name on source: "Gujarat Junagadh Garlic 5 (GJG 5)"; the JAU page says "GJG-5") -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Variety-13-years.pdf
No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for GJG-5 garlic was found. The general garlic temperature notes in the Indian Farmer production PDF do not name this variety, so I excluded them. -- No evidence found for variety-specific abiotic tolerance (search returned generic garlic production text: https://www.indianfarmer.net/uploads/Garlic%20COHJ%202025.pdf)

DISEASE AND PEST
A JAU proforma says the garlic showed lower incidence of little leaf disease in its disease and pest section, but the text sits in a combined vegetable document beside brinjal material, so attribution is uncertain -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/FVegetableCropsVR.pdf
A JAU variety-summary PDF records that the garlic bulbs were tolerant of little leaf disease and jassid in comparison with checks, but that statement appears in a block about a different crop, so I did not attribute it -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Variety-11-years.pdf
Garlic stem rot, thrips or jassid tolerance is not established for GJG-5 in any clearly attributed source. The stem-rot, jassid and thrips tolerance in the JAU report belongs to a groundnut variety, so I excluded it -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Variety-13-years.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
A JAU report records that GJG-5 gave about 23.3 percent higher bulb yield than check GG-4 and about 26.9 percent higher than check G-282 in rabi trials in Saurashtra and Middle Gujarat; its bulbs are medium, compact and white -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Variety-13-years.pdf (see also http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Variety-11-years.pdf)
The JAU vegetable proforma gives maturity as 169 days (medium maturity group), mean yield 79.42 q/ha and potential yield 81.32 q/ha, with plant height 44.88 cm, 12.23 leaves per plant and 17.85 cloves per bulb -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/FVegetableCropsVR.pdf
A second JAU proforma in the same file gives potential yield 93.24 q/ha and average yield 89.33 q/ha, which conflicts with the 81.32 and 79.42 figures; the two versions also disagree on the release year -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/FVegetableCropsVR.pdf
A JAU characteristics sheet lists GJG-5 with 135 to 140 days to maturity and bulb yield 7535 kg/ha, but the entry carries a 1993 release year that conflicts with the other records, so treat it as unverified -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//vrs_imp_charactristics_of_varities_20260512_1553.pdf
A JAU research-station page lists GJG-5 under Vegetable Research Station achievements with a 2014 release, 79.42 q/ha yield and clonal selection as the method -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/vegetable-research-station-junagadh
A 2021-22 rabi herbicide study at Junagadh (Weed Control Research Farm, Department of Agronomy, College of Agriculture, JAU) used cv. GJG-5 and compared herbicide mixtures for weed control and bulb yield -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379814828_Comparative_Bio-efficacy_of_Herbicides_for_Weed_Management_in_Garlic
Seed rate of 500-600 kg cloves per ha and 15 × 10 cm spacing were used in that study -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379814828_Comparative_Bio-efficacy_of_Herbicides_for_Weed_Management_in_Garlic

Parentage: the proforma states the genotype was collected from the local market at Visavadar in Junagadh district and kept in germplasm as line No. 260; breeding method was clonal selection; parentage is therefore a germplasm selection, not a cross -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/FVegetableCropsVR.pdf (same content at http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/FVegetableCropsVR.pdf)

No QTL or marker studies for GJG-5 were found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. No named breeder was attached to the garlic variety in the searched pages.
Developing institution: Junagadh Agricultural University, developed at the Vegetable Research Station, Junagadh; the station's mandate includes onion and garlic breeding for dehydration and export -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/vegetable-research-station-junagadh and https://www.jau.in/index.php/resources/2-init-content/research/103-vegetable-research-station
