search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: HG-17 (garlic, Allium sativum)

Name check: The CSC name and the Seednet name are both "HG-17". Seednet itself was not reachable through search, so no Seednet record was checked. The literature uses "HG-17", "HG17" and "Hisar garlic 17" interchangeably, and the findings below refer to that same name. The release year (2012-07-24) and institution come from the input record only and were not confirmed by any source.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for HG-17 specifically. Searches returned only general garlic cultivation notes: Garlic is a hardy crop and is tolerant to frost. -- https://www.horticultureguruji.in/garlic-cultivation/
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance were not found for HG-17.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for HG-17. No disease or pest resistance data was found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No HG-17-specific yield, maturity or trial data was found. The one HG-17 quality trial found was a comparison of seven varieties, which reported that Haryana garlic-17 (HG-17) variety showed significant quality as it yielded positive correlation with the maximum number of quality attributes. -- https://www.ifrj.upm.edu.my/30%20(06)%202023/16%20-%20IFRJ22563.R1.pdf
General garlic agronomy for Haryana (not HG-17-specific) notes that a spacing of 10cm × 7.5cm is suitable in Haryana -- http://hortportal.org/crop.php?alpha=G

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No parentage, marker, QTL or genetic-diversity data for HG-17 was found. The "Parentage: Not specified" entry in the input was not contradicted.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No named lead breeder for HG-17 was found in any source searched.
The institution is Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU), Hisar, the former Haryana Agricultural University. Per the source, On October 31st, 1991, it was renamed Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaudhary_Charan_Singh_Haryana_Agricultural_University
Garlic-related work at CCS HAU sits in the Department of Vegetable Science. The HKKP report says Research in vegetable crops is being carried out at the Department of Vegetable Science, CCS HAU, Hisar. -- https://hkkp.org.in/Reports/Report_on_Horticulture.pdf
The HAU Hisar Department of Vegetable Science is named as the source of garlic material in a 2018-19 processing study, which is the only station-level link found. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/128786/48771/344820

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact was found. No official email or phone number was found for HG-17 or its breeding team.
Institute-level address found: CCS Haryana Agricultural University Campus, Hisar-125004, Haryana, India (from the HKKP report cover page) -- https://hkkp.org.in/Reports/Report_on_Horticulture.pdf
No official email, phone or institute contact-page URL was retrieved in this session. The official HAU website should be checked directly for the Department of Vegetable Science contact.

PUBLICATIONS
Monika, Dua, A., Sharma, S., Gupta, S., & Mittal, A. (2024). Comparative study of antioxidant activities of Allium sativum (a novel variety, HG17) and Allium ampeloprasum (SMG): Revealing the higher potential of HG17 and analyzing its phytochemicals. Journal of Food Science, 89(7), 4250-4275. -- https://doi.org/10.1111/1750-3841.17133 (PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38829746). Abstract reports higher antioxidant activity of HG17 than SMG.
Prakash, P., & Prasad, K. (2023). Quality assessment of promising garlic (Allium sativum L.) varieties based on principal component analysis. International Food Research Journal, 30(6), 1540-1552. -- http://www.ifrj.upm.edu.my/30%20(06)%202023/16%20-%20IFRJ22563.R1.pdf
No AICRP/ICAR annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, conference paper or field-trial record for HG-17 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No HG-17 seed listing was found from NSC, a State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or a private dealer.
The state seed agency is the Haryana Seeds Development Corporation, a state undertaking whose objective of organizing production and distribution of certified seeds to the farmers of the State -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haryana_Seeds_Development_Corporation. No HG-17 stock was confirmed there. Note that the source is Wikipedia and the HSDC site should be checked directly.
A general 2025 report on quality seed production names NHRDF, NSC and MSSC as the main certified-seed agencies for onion and garlic -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/404067815_Quality_Seed_Production_of_Onion_Garlic_for_Harnessing_Export_Potential. This is not HG-17-specific.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No official HG-17 recommendation or notification was found. The input record lists only "Haryana" as recommended_states_raw, and nothing found confirms or contradicts it. Haryana is the state where the variety was developed and where the HAU Hisar material is referenced.

Search limits: four searches were run, one per topic. Seednet, the CSC minutes, and the ICAR/AICRP garlic reports were not directly reachable, so the Seednet, CSC and AICRP entries above are gaps and not negative findings.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Yamuna Safed-5 (G-189), garlic (Allium sativum)

Name note: The CSC name is "Yamuna Safed-5" (NHRDF code G-189). The Seednet name is "YAMUNA SAFED-3", which in the sources is a different variety, Yamuna Safed-3 (G-282). Every finding below refers to Yamuna Safed-5 (G-189) unless marked "Safed-3". I did not reach seednet.gov.in, so I could not check the Seednet record directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to G-189 -- searched via web_search (queries 1 and 3)
- Storage: in one NHRDF storage trial, G-189 was a check entry with low total weight loss, grouped with the best lines at Karnal and Nashik -- https://nhrdf.org/pdf/NHRDF%20Annual%20Report%202015-16.pdf
- Polyhouse vs open field (Kodaikanal): G-189 showed the highest physiological weight loss at 30 days of storage (31.29% open field, 32.67% polyhouse), and fewer cloves per bulb under polyhouse -- https://masujournal.org/109/x6rbe8gwWJrtdO9idrTqkwZ75h8Wyn.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for a rated disease or pest resistance score for G-189 -- searched via web_search (query 1)
- Planting-date recommendations for reduced disease and thrips were given for Yamuna Safed, Safed-2 and Safed-3, not for Safed-5 -- https://www.nhrdf.com/Potato.html (Karnal, 15 Sept; Nashik, 15 Oct)
- Thrips susceptibility was noted for Bhima Omkar, not G-189 -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/production-technology-of-garlic/72026426

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity: 150-160 days -- https://dogr.icar.gov.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=126&Itemid=178&lang=en ; NHRDF page gives 140-160 days -- http://www.nhrdf.com/Potato.html
- Yield: 17-18 t/ha -- https://dogr.icar.gov.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=126&Itemid=178&lang=en ; NHRDF page gives 150-180 q/ha -- http://www.nhrdf.com/Potato.html
- Bulb and quality traits: creamy white bulbs of 4.5-5 cm diameter, 22-30 cloves per bulb, about 42 degrees Brix TSS, 44% dry matter, 26 micromole/g pyruvic acid; the NHRDF page describes it as suited to processing and dehydration -- http://www.nhrdf.com/Potato.html ; also https://www.exportersindia.com/product-detail/white-yamuna-safed-5-g-189-garlic-5918827.htm
- Relative export position: Yamuna Safed-3 and Agrifound Parvati are the bigger-clove export types; G-189 is not listed among them -- https://dogr.icar.gov.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=126&Itemid=178&lang=en
- Trial data: G-189 appears as a check in NHRDF 2015-16 storage trials at Karnal and Nashik -- https://nhrdf.org/pdf/NHRDF%20Annual%20Report%202015-16.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for QTL, marker or genomic studies on G-189 -- searched via web_search (queries 1 and 3)
- Breeding-history table lists Yamuna Safed-5 (G-189) with release year 2011 and NHRDF, Karnal as the origin; this conflicts with the 2012-07-24 date in the record -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391810619_Genetic_variability_in_the_garlic_Allium_sativum_genotypes_for_growth_yield_and_yield_attributing_traits
- Parentage: No evidence found. The mass-selection origin in the sources applies to Yamuna Safed (G-1) and Agrifound White, not G-189 -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/yamuna-safed-1849040991.html

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Breeder name(s): No evidence found -- searched via web_search (query 2)
- Developing institution: National Horticultural Research and Development Foundation (NHRDF) -- https://nhrdf.org/Seeds.php ; https://dogr.icar.gov.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=126&Itemid=178&lang=en
- Station: Karnal is listed as the origin station for G-189 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391810619_Genetic_variability_in_the_garlic_Allium_sativum_genotypes_for_growth_yield_and_yield_attributing_traits
- NHRDF background: founded in 1977 under NAFED, head office moved to Nashik in 1989, registered office in New Delhi, five regional research stations -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/yamuna-safed-1849040991.html (third-party listing; not verified against NHRDF's own site)

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder contact: No evidence found
- Official NHRDF email, phone, postal address or contact page: No evidence found in the retrieved results. Official site known from results: https://nhrdf.org (Seeds page: https://nhrdf.org/Seeds.php)
- Registered office: New Delhi (per the third-party listing above, no street address given)
- Head office: Nashik, Maharashtra (no street address found)

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured (year approx. 2025 per ResearchGate ID). Genetic variability in the garlic (Allium sativum) genotypes for growth, yield and yield attributing traits. ResearchGate (journal not captured) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391810619_Genetic_variability_in_the_garlic_Allium_sativum_genotypes_for_growth_yield_and_yield_attributing_traits

Yamuna Safed-3 (Safed-3, not Safed-5). Journal not captured -- DOI 10.5958/0976-4615.2019.00042.5 (DOI reconstructed from a garbled extract; verify)
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI specific to G-189 found -- searched via web_search (query 3)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: "Yamuna Safed-8" (variety_name) returned no matching evidence. "Yamuna Safed-3" (seednet_variety_name) is the name that appears in the search results. All findings below refer to Yamuna Safed-3 unless stated otherwise.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The retrieved snippets contained no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for Yamuna Safed-3.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The retrieved snippets contained no disease or pest resistance data for Yamuna Safed-3.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Yamuna Safed-3 (G-282) was selected in a garlic genotype study for yield, quality and related traits; the snippet names it as a selected genotype -- https://journal.iahs.org.in/index.php/ijh/article/download/1713/625
Yamuna Safed-2 (G-50) and Yamuna Safed-3 (G-282) are named together as selected lines in that study; the snippet was truncated, so the full trial design and yield values were not retrieved -- https://journal.iahs.org.in/index.php/ijh/article/download/1713/625

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No QTL, marker or parentage data were retrieved. The record lists parentage as "Not specified".

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Yamuna Safed-3 is listed among NHRDF garlic varieties (with Agrifound White and Yamuna Safed to Safed-5) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_vegetables_garlic.html
NHRDF is named as a garlic research institution in an overview of onion and garlic research in India; the snippet does not name a breeder for this variety -- https://jhs.iihr.res.in/index.php/jhs/article/download/527/359
No lead breeder name was found for Yamuna Safed-3 or Yamuna Safed-8.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact was found.
No NHRDF institute email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL was found in the retrieved results. The record's institution field is "National Horticulture Research and Development Foundation".

PUBLICATIONS
Selection of garlic genotypes for yield, quality and better [title truncated in results] (year not retrieved). Journal: Indian Journal of Horticulture (IAHS) -- https://journal.iahs.org.in/index.php/ijh/article/download/1713/625
FOCUS: Onion and garlic research in India (year not retrieved). Journal of Horticultural Sciences (IIHR) -- https://jhs.iihr.res.in/index.php/jhs/article/download/527/359
Authors, DOI and full titles were not retrieved for either item.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Yamuna Safed 3 garlic seed is listed by a private dealer on IndiaMART at about Rs 60/kg, Wardha -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/yamuna-safed-3-garlic-seeds-2854957991062.html
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed listing was found. The Seednet portal was not retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No independent confirmation found. The record lists Jammu, Punjab, Delhi, Haryana and Rajasthan, but no search result confirmed this.

DATA DISCREPANCIES
Variety code: the record says G-384, but the journal snippet gives Yamuna Safed-3 as G-282. Verify against Seednet or the CSC minutes.
Release year: the record gives 2014-01-13 as the release date. This was not confirmed by any retrieved source.

LIMITATIONS
The search tool limit was reached during my second batch of queries, so the research is incomplete. The results I have are snippets only. Several items above were truncated, and the planned searches on contacts, Seednet, and KrishiKosh theses were not completed. A follow-up search is needed for the NHRDF contact page, Seednet's Yamuna Safed-3 entry, the CSC release notification, and any AICRP or KrishiKosh trial records.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistance to bacterial wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum) is the main reported trait. The IIHR variety page describes Arka Anand as a high-yielding F1 hybrid with resistance to bacterial wilt. In a bacterial wilt screening of brinjal genotypes, Arka Anand was used as the resistant check and was scored resistant. A Little Leaf or Phomopsis rating was not found, and Arka Anand is absent from the Little Leaf and Phomopsis resistant-variety lists. An IIHR e-compendium figure lists Arka Anand alongside captioned resistance to powdery mildew and ChiVMV, but the resistance is not clearly attributed to Arka Anand, so it was not recorded as a finding.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. Arka Anand appears only as a leaf-trait reference (medium leaf length class) in the PPV&FRA brinjal DUS descriptor, which is not a pest-resistance rating.

agronomic_details.yield: Sources conflict. IIHR variety page: 55-60 t/ha. IIHR-linked compendium (Slideshare): 60-65 t/ha. IIHR-linked brinjal page: 65-70 t/ha. CSC record: 60,000-65,000 kg/ha. The IIHR institute page (55-60 t/ha) is treated as the most authoritative of the three.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: One IIHR compendium states suitability for both Kharif and Rabi seasons. Extension material describes suitability for long-distance transport. The recommended state list comes from the CSC input only and was not confirmed by any retrieved source.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Fruits are green and medium long with good cooking quality. Average fruit weight is 55-60 g and keeping quality is good (IIHR-linked brinjal page). Leaf length class is medium (PPV&FRA DUS descriptor). Plant habit and other morphology: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: No multi-location AICRP trial data for Arka Anand was found. Reported yields in the sources are: 55-60 t/ha in 145-150 days (IIHR); 60-65 t/ha in 140-150 days with Kharif and Rabi suitability (IIHR-linked compendium); 65-70 t/ha in 140-150 days with average fruit weight 55-60 g (IIHR-linked page). Arka Anand was used as the resistant check in a bacterial wilt screening of brinjal genotypes and was scored resistant.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
ARKA ANAND (CSC name) / ARKA AMAN (Seednet name) -- brinjal (Solanum melongena)

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Bacterial wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum) resistance is the main reported trait; the IIHR page calls it a high-yielding F1 hybrid with resistance to bacterial wilt -- https://iihr.res.in/brinjal-arka-anand
- In a bacterial wilt screening of brinjal genotypes, Arka Anand was used as the resistant check and was scored resistant -- https://jhs.iihr.res.in/index.php/jhs/article/download/158/120
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for Arka Anand was found; the only irrigation-stress paper retrieved used other cultivars (Black Long, Nirala, Bemisal, Purple Queen) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345246593_Growth_and_Yield_Response_of_Different_Brinjal_Cultivars_to_Irrigation_Deficit_Conditions

DISEASE AND PEST
- Bacterial wilt resistance is the only disease claim confirmed for Arka Anand (see above) -- https://iihr.res.in/brinjal-arka-anand
- A "Little leaf" or Phomopsis rating for Arka Anand was not found; Arka Anand is absent from the Little Leaf and Phomopsis resistant-variety lists -- https://indianagriexam.com/courses/general-agriculture-for-competitive-exams/lesson/brinjal-solanum-melongena/
- An IIHR e-compendium lists Arka Anand under a figure about CGMS hybrids, but the captioned resistance (powdery mildew, ChiVMV) is not clearly attributed to Arka Anand, so it was not recorded as a finding -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359055082_e-Compendium_on_Advances_in_Horticultural_Technologies
- Arka Anand is a leaf-trait reference (medium leaf length class) in the PPV&FRA brinjal DUS descriptor -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/fbrinjal.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield is reported as 55-60 t/ha in 145-150 days -- https://iihr.res.in/brinjal-arka-anand
- A different IIHR compendium gives 60-65 t/ha in 140-150 days and states suitability for both Kharif and Rabi -- https://slideshare.net/slideshow/brinjalpptx-introduction-definition-topic/266803481
- An IIHR-linked brinjal page gives 65-70 t/ha in 140-150 days, average fruit weight 55-60 g, and good keeping quality -- https://brinjalcultivation.web.app/page4.html
- These yield figures conflict across sources; the IIHR institute page (55-60 t/ha) is the most authoritative of the three.
- Fruits are green and medium long with good cooking quality -- https://iihr.res.in/brinjal-arka-anand
- Extension and training material describes Arka Anand as suited to long-distance transport -- https://indianagriexam.com/courses/general-agriculture-for-competitive-exams/lesson/brinjal-solanum-melongena/
- No multi-location AICRP trial data for Arka Anand was found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: F1 hybrid from IIHR-3 x IIHR-322 -- https://iihr.res.in/brinjal-arka-anand
- The CSC/Seednet parentage field reads "Not specified", so the IIHR parentage is the only source for this entry.
- No QTL, marker or genomic study for Arka Anand was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found for Arka Anand. Searches returned no breeder attribution.
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru -- https://iihr.res.in/brinjal-arka-anand
- Division listed on the IIHR variety page is Vegetable Crops -- https://iihr.res.in/brinjal-arka-anand
- The IIHR institution page names bacterial wilt brinjal hybrid Arka Anand among its releases -- https://www.iihr.res.in/institution
- Station: IIHR headquarters at Hesaraghatta Lake Post, Bengaluru -- https://jhs.iihr.res.in/index.php/jhs/article/download/158/120
- Release year: the CSC date (2008-10-07) was not confirmed by any retrieved source.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.
- Institute address as found: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research, Hesaraghatta Lake Post, Bengaluru 560089, India -- https://jhs.iihr.res.in/index.php/jhs/article/download/158/120
- Institute website: iihr.res.in -- https://iihr.res.in/varieties-crop-name/brinjal
- Official email and phone: No evidence found in retrieved results.
- The ICAR publication (Sep-Oct 2021) names Drs A K Singh, M Sankaran and B N S Murthy as contacts, but that item is about horticulture scenario and does not name Arka Anand; it was not recorded as Arka Anand contacts -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-06/IH-Sep-Oct-2021.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Evaluation of brinjal genotypes against bacterial wilt caused by Ralstonia solanacearum. Journal of Horticultural Sciences (ICAR-IIHR, Bengaluru) -- https://jhs.iihr.res.in/index.php/jhs/article/download/158/120
- The IIHR-linked e-Compendium on Advances in Horticultural Technologies (year not shown) lists Arka Anand among brinjal hybrids -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359055082_e-Compendium_on_Advances_in_Horticultural_Technologies
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report or peer-reviewed yield paper specific to Arka Anand was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- M-Tech Gardens F1 hybrid seed, 50-seed pack, sold online (Flipkart) -- https://www.flipkart.com/m-tech-gardens-f1-hybrid-eggplant-brinjal-seeds-arka-anand-high-yield-disease-resistant-variety-vegetable-50-pack-yielding-55-60t-ha-145-150-days-seed/p/itm81fccde3c745f
- The IIHR seed portal allows online seed purchase, but the retrieved snippet did not confirm Arka Anand as a listed variety -- https://seed.iihr.res.in/
- IIHR states it produces breeder seed and sells seed under the Arka brand -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359055082_e-Compendium_on_Advances_in_Horticultural_Technologies
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK and SAU listings: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The state list (Punjab, Uttarakhand, Haryana, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Delhi, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka) comes from the CSC input only; no retrieved source confirmed it -- https://iihr.res.in/varieties-crop-name/brinjal (no state list shown)

NOTES
- Name and crop check: No evidence found for "Arka Aman" on Seednet. The Seednet crop field reads "GLADIOLUS", which conflicts with brinjal. All findings above refer to Arka Anand (brinjal). The Seednet record should be verified directly before use.
- The search budget was 4 queries (the maximum), so breeder names and contact details could not be checked further.

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance. Searches returned only disease-resistance data. The Nagpur sowing-window study (kharif 2018) reports longer maturity (114-127 days) for AMS-1001 across sowing dates but does not assess drought stress. Mechanisms: Not found in searched sources.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance in the digest. The sowing-window study reports maturity variation across sowing dates but does not assess heat stress. Mechanisms: Not found in searched sources.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance. Mechanisms: Not found in searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance. Mechanisms: Not found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: (1) Charcoal rot and yellow mosaic virus (YMV): reported as highly resistant. Field and sick-plot screening was done at Amravati (EJPB 2020 release paper). (2) Root rot (Rhizoctonia bataticola): the paper reports resistance under sick-plot conditions, and a Dr. PDKV thesis lists AMS 1001 among highly resistant genotypes. (3) A commercial seller page claims 'strong resistance' to YMV and charcoal rot. This is a seller claim, not an official source, and is not verified.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No evidence found for insect-pest resistance specific to this variety. The Maharashtra blog mentions girdle beetle and stem fly only for AMS-100-39, a different variety, and is excluded.

agronomic_details.yield: Average 2173 kg/ha with a range of 1800 to 2200 kg/ha (input data). ICAR-IISR zone table lists a yield value of 22 with units not stated in the snippet. Seller page claims 20-25 q/ha potential (unverified). Seed-rate study (RRS Amravati, 2025) recorded 2043 kg/ha. Sowing-window study (Nagpur, kharif 2018) recorded 5775 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Yield advantage reported across multi-location and state trials (see field_trials). Formal stability analysis across environments (e.g., AMMI or GGE): Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Vidarbha Regional of Maharashtra (input adaptation_ecology). Trials were conducted at Amravati, Nagpur and multiple state locations.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 95 To 100Days (input). Conflicting evidence: Mahabeej lists 75 days in the same row as 95-100 days. The Nagpur sowing-window study reports 114-127 days across sowing dates. The ICAR-IISR bulletin lists 95-100 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Medium maturity, determinate growth habit, purple flowers, dark green leaves (EJPB paper). Plant type determinate, semi erect (Mahabeej). 100-seed weight 10-11 g (seller claim, unverified). Morphological characteristics beyond these: Not specified in input data.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Multi-location trials: 24.17% above state check MAUS-71 and 20.58% above national check JS-335. (2) State multi-location trials: 36.01% above JS-335, 30.58% above JS-97-52 and 33.82% above MAUS-71. (3) Farmer adaptive trials: 23.90% above JS-335. (4) Seed-rate study (RRS Amravati, 2025): seed yield 2043 kg/ha, lower than AMS 100-39 in the same trial. (5) Sowing-window study (Nagpur, kharif 2018): yield 5775 kg/ha, at par with JS-9560. (6) ICAR-IISR zone table: 2019 release, 95-100 days, yield value 22 (units not stated). (7) Seller page: 20-25 q/ha potential, unverified claim.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: SSR primer Glysatt-180 is specific to AMS-1001 and is used for identification. Other marker details: Not found in searched sources. National identity number: IC 626343.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL or mapping study specific to this variety was found in the searched sources.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. A 2025 Biochem journal table describes AMS 1001 as the first KTI-free variety in India (source article authors not shown in snippet). Gene-level mechanisms: Not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME AND CROP CHECKS
variety_name "AMS-1001 Yellow Gold)" has a stray parenthesis. Evidence refers to "AMS-1001 (PDKV Yellow Gold)" and, in the ICAR-IISR bulletin, "AMS 1001 (PKV Yellow Gold)". Both are used below.
seednet_variety_name is garbled in the input ("AMS -1001"). No Seednet page was retrieved, so no evidence was found under the Seednet name.
seednet_crop_name is "GOBHI SARSON", which conflicts with the soybean crop field. All evidence is for soybean. Gobhi sarson is a Brassica crop, so the Seednet crop mapping needs manual correction.
variety_code "(PDKV Maharashtra" is malformed. No evidence was found for a separate code.
Release date: the input says 2019-06-01. The EJPB paper says the State Seed Sub Committee (SVRC) released it in 2018. Mahabeej and the ICAR-IISR bulletin list 2019. No CSC release minutes were found.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Highly resistant to charcoal rot and YMV; the paper also reports resistance to root rot under sick-plot conditions -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/download/926/763/1978
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. Searches returned only disease-resistance data. A sowing-window study (Nagpur, kharif 2018) reports longer maturity (114-127 days) for AMS-1001 across sowing dates, but does not assess stress tolerance -- https://www.journalofsoilsandcrops.com/Download/dec2020issue/28.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Charcoal rot and yellow mosaic virus (YMV) resistance is the main reported trait. Field and sick-plot screening was done at Amravati -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/download/926/763/1978
- A Dr. PDKV root-rot (Rhizoctonia bataticola) thesis lists AMS 1001 among highly resistant genotypes -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/421eeb85-b2c7-4663-85c0-1ccfd410ace8/content
- A commercial seller's page says it has "strong resistance" to YMV and charcoal rot. This is a seller claim, not an official source -- https://www.skbseeds.com/product/ams-1001-pdkv-yellow-gold
- No evidence found for insect-pest resistance specific to this variety. The Maharashtra blog mentions girdle beetle and stem fly only for AMS-100-39, a different variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Multi-location trials: yield 24.17% above state check MAUS-71 and 20.58% above national check JS-335 -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/EJPB/article/view/3400
- State multi-location trials: 36.01% above JS-335, 30.58% above JS-97-52, 33.82% above MAUS-71 -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/EJPB/article/view/3400
- Farmer adaptive trials: 23.90% above JS-335 -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/download/926/763/1978
- Medium maturity, determinate growth, purple flowers, dark green leaves -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/download/926/763/1978
- Maturity 75 days (listed as 95-100 days in the same row) and "plant type determinate, semi erect" -- https://www.mahabeej.co.in/cereals?id=9
- Seed-rate study (RRS Amravati, 2025): AMS 1001 seed yield 2043 kg/ha, lower than AMS 100-39 in the same trial -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2025/vol9issue10S/PartP/S-9-10-74-804.pdf
- Sowing-window study (Nagpur, kharif 2018): AMS-1001 yield 5775 kg/ha, at par with JS-9560 -- https://www.journalofsoilsandcrops.com/Download/dec2020issue/28.pdf
- ICAR-IISR bulletin zone table: AMS 1001 (PKV Yellow Gold), 2019, 95-100 days, yield value 22 (units not stated in snippet) -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/pdfdoc/ExtensionBulletin2023E_2.pdf
- Seller page: 20-25 q/ha potential, 100-seed weight 10-11 g. Seller claim, not verified -- https://www.skbseeds.com/product/ams-1001-pdkv-yellow-gold

GENETICS AND QTL
- Induced mutant of JS-93-05 (parentage confirmed) -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/EJPB/article/view/3400
- JS-93-05 seed was gamma-irradiated (150, 250, 300 Gy) at BARC Trombay in 2006; M1 was grown at Amravati in kharif 2006 -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/download/926/763/1978
- SSR primer Glysatt-180 is specific to AMS-1001 and used for identification -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/EJPB/article/view/3400
- National identity number IC 626343 -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/download/926/763/1978
- A 2025 Biochem journal table describes AMS 1001 as an induced mutant of JS 93-05 with 20-36% higher yield than checks, and calls it the first KTI-free variety in India. Source article authors not shown in snippet -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2025/vol9issue9S/PartS/S-9-9-250-484.pdf
- No QTL or mapping study specific to this variety was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Corresponding author and lead: S. S. Nichal (Soybean Breeder, RRC Amravati) -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/download/926/763/1978 and https://www.extensionjournal.com/uploads/archives/8-12-60-750.pdf
- Co-authors of the 2020 release paper: P. V. Patil, G. D. Chandankar, M. S. Dandge, Y. V. Ingle, S. S. Munje, H. H. Dikey -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/EJPB/article/view/3400
- Developing institution: Regional Research Centre, Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth (Dr. PDKV), Amravati -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/download/926/763/1978
- Release committee: State Variety Release Committee (SVRC), Maharashtra -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/EJPB/article/view/3400
- Seed-rate study authors (RRC Amravati): H. H. Dikey, R. S. Wankhade (ARS Achalpur), Shubhangi Shelke, S. S. Munje -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2025/vol9issue10S/PartP/S-9-10-74-804.pdf
- The S. K. Dhapke soybean breeder listed on the AICRP page is not linked to this variety in the evidence and is not attributed here -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4584

CONTACT DETAILS
- S. S. Nichal (corresponding author, Soybean Breeder and Head): E-Mail nichal_satish@rediffmail.com -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/download/926/763/1978
- Address as printed on the release paper: Regional Research Center, Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth, Amravati-444 601, Maharashtra, India -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/download/926/763/1978

- Institute phone number: No evidence found
- Official institute contact page: No evidence found (pdkv.ac.in research-station pages list RRS Amravati and Soybean Research Unit, Amravati, but no contact details were shown) -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=126

drought.details: GSC 7 is characterized by tolerance to drought, low soil fertility, and low moisture conditions. It is described as drought tolerant and is considered among highly drought tolerant genotypes.

heat.details: The variety exhibits tolerance to heat, including terminal heat stress, and high temperature at sowing time. It is listed among varieties with tolerance to environmental stresses such as heat.

salinity.details: GSC 7 is tolerant to salinity and is suitable for salt-affected soil and saline water conditions. It is also described as semi-tolerant to sodicity.

flood.details: No specific information regarding flood tolerance for GSC 7 was found in the provided search results.

disease_resistance.summary: GSC 7 is moderately resistant to white rust and shows tolerance to Alternaria brassicae (Alternaria blight).

pest_resistance.summary: GSC 7 is listed among varieties characterized by tolerance to pests.

agronomic_details.yield: The average grain yield is 8.9 quintals per acre (equivalent to approximately 2199 kg/ha). The reported yield potential ranges from 1911-2190 Kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: GSC 7 has shown significant yield improvement in various regions, including 33.4% in Uttarakhand, 41.0% and 33.9% in Himachal Pradesh, and 53.3% in Manipur, indicating adaptability across diverse environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: GSC 7 is a Gobhi Sarson (Brassica napus) variety, suitable for cultivation in both irrigated and rainfed conditions in Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, and Rajasthan. It has been successfully demonstrated in farmers' fields in Punjab.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: GSC 7 is a canola-type Gobhi sarson. It has an erucic acid content of 7-8%. It responds significantly to both irrigation and fertigation treatments, and seed priming with phosphorus and inoculation with microbial consortium have shown improved seed and oil yields.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Cultivation of GSC 7 was demonstrated in 51 farmer's fields by KVK Faridkot in 2019-20. Cluster Front Line Demonstrations (CFLD's) were conducted covering 21 hectares. Studies on phenological stages and agronomic efficiency have been conducted. Research also explores its performance in mustard intensification (SMI) systems.

drought.details: The variety is described as drought tolerant and tolerant to terminal moisture stress. Studies on 'Him Sarson 1' have investigated traits like root weight, shoot weight, relative water content, and drought susceptibility index, indicating its relevance in drought stress tolerance research.

heat.details: Him Sarson-1 is tolerant to terminal heat stress, exhibiting a seed yield reduction of equal to or less than 30% under such conditions. It is generally noted as tolerant to temperature stress.

salinity.details: The variety is listed as salt tolerant.

flood.details: There is no direct information available regarding Him Sarson-1's tolerance to flood conditions. A general mention of a trial failing due to waterlogging conditions in the field exists, but it is not specific to the variety's performance.

disease_resistance.summary: Him Sarson-1 (ONK 1) is tolerant to Alternaria blight. It is also resistant to wilt and tolerant to dry root rot. Furthermore, it is identified as cold tolerant. While one source states it is resistant to white rust in Himachal Pradesh, other sources that list white rust resistant varieties do not include Him Sarson-1.

pest_resistance.summary: No information specified.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield 1362 kgs/ha. It showed higher average seed yield at 125% recommended fertility level and performed at par with GSAL-1 under timely sown irrigated conditions in Zone-1. Under late sown conditions at Kangra, it showed the highest average seed yield, at par with the state check Neelam.
agronomic_details.stability: Demonstrates stability by showing higher average seed yield under both timely and late sown conditions. It responded well to 125% recommended nitrogen (112.5 kg N) and 40 kg/ha sulfur application, with unchanged P and K (60:40).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Zone-1, with optimal sowing period from 15th October to the first week of November for Gobhi Sarson. Recommended states include Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Medium bold, round to slightly flattened, reddish brown to dark brown colored seed. 1000-seed weight ranges from 37.9% to 42.2%, with an average of 40.3%. It showed higher seed yield with 30 cm row spacing and 125% recommended fertility at Kangra.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Field trials indicated superior performance under timely sown irrigated conditions, late sown conditions (Kangra), and responsiveness to increased fertility levels (125% RF).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for JGS 12-3 / Jammu Gobhi Sarson 123. The IAUA newsletter (Vol. 22 No. 3, Jul-Sep 2022) has a "Gobhi Sarson JGS 12-3" heading, and the same issue gives resistant to lodging and moderately resistant to white rust and Alternaria blight. These traits sit in a table that is not clearly attributed to this entry, so they are not used as evidence. -- https://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for this variety. The SKUAST-Jammu Rabi package of practices advises use of resistant varieties of rapeseed, mustard and gobhi sarson but names no variety. -- https://skuastjammu.ac.in/newsite/pdf/1693218114POP%20Rabi%20POP%202020%20SKUAST-Jammu.pdf.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Ambiguous, not used: the IAUA newsletter lists average yield, 16-18 q/ha and matures in 135-150 days in a table that sits next to, not under, the JGS 12-3 heading. The same newsletter places a JGS 12-3 heading above text about a tree fruit, so the attribution is unclear. -- https://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf
No evidence found for multi-location or AICRP trial results naming JGS 12-3. The DRMR AICRP 2020-21 report covers gobhi sarson trials at Chatha-Jammu but names other entries. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Parentage RSPN-25 x GSL-1 was not found in any result. RSPN-25 appears only as a separate gobhi sarson variety in the Rai profile. -- https://www.skuast.org/admin/admin/news/1728889742SKRai%20New%20(1).pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Dr. Sunil Kumar Rai, Chief Scientist and Incharge, is listed in his profile as Five Rapeseed-Mustard variety developed including "JGS 123 (Gobhi Sarson)". This is the closest match to this variety, and the name is an abbreviation of JGS 12-3 / Jammu Gobhi Sarson 123. The snippet does not give the station, so the institute-station link is unconfirmed. -- https://www.skuast.org/admin/admin/news/1728889742SKRai%20New%20(1).pdf
Not attributed: Dr. Naresh Kumar (Sr. Scientist, Pulses Research Sub-Station, Samba, SKUAST-Jammu) is credited with gobhi sarson among 19 varieties, but no variety is named, so this is not attributed to JGS 12-3. -- https://skuastjammu.ac.in/admin/admin/news/1728891335Dr.%20Naresh%20Kumar.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
Dr. Sunil Kumar Rai -- Chief Scientist and Incharge (role as shown on profile page). Email, phone and postal address: not found in the snippet. -- https://www.skuast.org/admin/admin/news/1728889742SKRai%20New%20(1).pdf
No institute-level SKUAST-Jammu contact, email, phone or address was found in the results. Institute contact page: not found.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found naming this variety. The SKUAST-Jammu research list includes papers on gobhi sarson cultivars in Jammu, but these do not name JGS 12-3 and are excluded. -- https://skuastjammu.ac.in/admin/backend/news/1715756202research-papers-2022-23.pdf.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The searches returned seed listings only for other gobhi sarson varieties (GSC 7, PGSH 2155). None was for JGS 12-3, and none from NSC, the J&K seed corporation, a KVK, SKUAST seed sales or a dealer was found. -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/ludhiana/pau-kisan-mela-to-showcase-rabi-seeds-vegetable-kits-farm-technologies/

RECOMMENDED STATES
Ambiguous: the IAUA newsletter gives "UT of J&K (sub-tropical area of Jammu division)" as the area of adoption, but it is not clearly tied to this entry. The DAC rapeseed-mustard notified-variety table does not list JGS 12-3. -- https://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf

NOTES
Searches run: 4 (general variety, breeder, research, seed). Name variants used: "Jammu Gobhi Sarson 123", "JGS 12-3" and "JGS 123". No CSC release minutes or Seednet entry was found under either name.
Excluded as other varieties or crops: Shalimar Gobhi sarson-1 (SKUAST-Kashmir, 2022), GSC-7, RSPN-25 and GSL-1 as separate varieties, and a tree-fruit description that shares the JGS 12-3 heading.

Search status: four web_search queries ran in one batch (variety/notification, breeder, research, seed availability). A follow-up query was refused by the tool's usage limit, so the evidence below is thin. The search output was also truncated to short snippets, so some findings below rest on partial text.

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "RSPN 25", so no separate name search was needed. All evidence below refers to "RSPN 25" as written; none of it confirms the Seednet listing itself.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The snippets returned did not mention drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for RSPN 25.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No snippet mentioned disease or pest resistance for RSPN 25.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- SKUAST annual report 2016-17 refers to a rapeseed variety RSPN 25 with an oil content of about 40%, and says these varieties are notified by the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards -- https://skuast.org/newsite/pdf/annual-report-2016-17.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A Jobner (Rajasthan) weed-management field trial from 2014-15 and 2015-16 was returned, but it does not name RSPN 25 in the snippet and is not evidence for this variety -- https://www.academia.edu/36359118/Research_Paper_1_Mustard_

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No parentage or marker/QTL information was returned. The input parentage field is "Not specified".

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- SKUAST (Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology) is the institution named in the input record, and the 2016-17 annual report lists RSPN 25 among its releases -- https://skuast.org/newsite/pdf/annual-report-2016-17.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No breeder name, station or developing division was found for RSPN 25.
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Pusa Mustard-25 (an early-maturing IARI-linked variety from a different developer, not RSPN 25) was returned by the variety search. It is not evidence for RSPN 25 and should not be recorded against it -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/230750581_Early_maturing_variety_Pusa_Mustard-25

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. The only institutional URL available is the SKUAST annual report above (https://skuast.org/newsite/pdf/annual-report-2016-17.pdf). No official email, phone or postal address was found in the snippets. Check the SKUAST site contact page directly before use.

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis or AICRP report specifically on RSPN 25 was found. The SKUAST 2016-17 annual report is the only record; it is a report, not a paper:
SKUAST (2017). Annual Report 2016-17. SKUAST annual report -- https://skuast.org/newsite/pdf/annual-report-2016-17.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed-related result returned was a generic NCDEX mustard seed commodity page, which says nothing about RSPN 25 seed sources -- https://www.ncdex.com/products/RMSEED. Check seednet.gov.in, the SKUAST seed unit, and the Kashmir/J&K state seed corporation directly.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The input field notes that All India Coordinated Trial data is missing, and no searched source named states or zones for RSPN 25. The SKUAST report indicates notification but not a recommended region.

Also noted: the input gives a release date of 14 February 2014. This is not confirmed by any search result. The annual report indicates notification, but its date and the notification number were not in the snippet.

VARIETY NAME NOTE: CSC name "Shalimar Gobhi Sarson-1"; Seednet name "Shalimar Gobhi Sarson-1 (KGS-32)". Evidence below names "Shalimar Gobhi Sarson 1" with no KGS-32 code unless stated. KGS-32 appears only in a DRMR table, and it is not clearly linked to this release.

STRESS TOLERANCE (evidence refers to "Shalimar Gobhi Sarson 1")
- Reported resistance to Alternaria blight and powdery mildew, with moderate resistance to aphids. -- https://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638494389134564757.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found for this variety. -- No evidence found (searched)

DISEASE AND PEST (evidence refers to "Shalimar Gobhi Sarson 1")
- Resistant to Alternaria blight and powdery mildew; moderately resistant to aphids. -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638494389134564757.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (evidence refers to "Shalimar Gobhi Sarson 1")
- Early maturing and high yielding at 12.5 q/ha, about 15.40% above the check Shalimar Sarson 1. -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638494389134564757.pdf
- Seed production is comparatively easy because the crop is often cross-pollinated. -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638494389134564757.pdf
- No multi-location or AICRP trial data specific to this variety found. Trial data found for "Shalimar Sarson-1" is for brown sarson (B. rapa), a different release, and is not used here. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/283831567_Effects_of_Brassica_alba_extract_on_yield_attribute_of_Paddy

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL or marker study for this variety found. -- No evidence found (searched)
- A DRMR fatty-acid and glucosinolate study lists "KGS-32" as a B. napus entry with origin given as IPK Germany, beside Shalimar Sarson-1. This does not establish KGS-32 as this release or give its parentage. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333718099_Genetic_variability_studies_for_quality_traits_in_rapeseed-mustard

drought_tolerance.technical_details: No source shows drought tolerance for Manjari Medika itself. Drought and salt tolerance in the results refers to rootstocks such as Dogridge and 140RU, not the scion. The ARI annual report mentions a 'water-stress tolerant genotype' in a separate context.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: The climate-change review lists Manjari Medika among varieties in an adaptation context, but the snippets give no heat tolerance data. Other 'heat' hits concern seed oil thermal processing and wheat, which are irrelevant.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: Salinity tolerance is attributed to the rootstocks (e.g., Dogridge, Salt Creek), not to the variety. A rootstock study found Manjari Medika grafted on 140RU performed best for cane biochemical parameters, which suggests a rootstock-dependent response rather than inherent tolerance.

submergence_tolerance.technical_details: No evidence found. The submergence hits refer to rice (Swarna Sub1) and appear only because they sit in the same documents.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: None confirmed. A metabolomics paper snippet says 'grapes can be said to be more disease-resistant' without specifying the variety or the disease. Anthracnose and downy mildew resistance in the Pharma Journal snippet refers to a different variety.
disease_resistance.technical_details: The metabolomics study compares Manjari Medika with its parents and links phenolic and anthocyanin content to possible disease resistance. This is an inference, not a field-tested result. A Xanthomonas study used Manjari Medika among varieties, but the snippet gives no resistance outcome.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: Many citations exist, including peer-reviewed papers (ScienceDirect, PMC, ICAR publications), but they cover nutraceutical and processing properties, seed oil, pharmacology and rootstock effects, not stress tolerance of the variety. Drought, salinity and disease tolerance in the snippets belong to rootstocks or other varieties. There is no yield value, no Gujarat-specific data and no confirmed stress trait. This fits the 60 band (at least one citation, weak on stress traits). The score is not 50 or lower because the citations are real and numerous, and not 75 because no stress trait is evidenced.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Colored juice grape from NRCG Pune (Pusa Navrang x Flame Seedless). High anthocyanins and phenolics. Seed oil rich in linoleic acid. Zero-waste use of pomace and seed. Performs well on 140RU rootstock.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Manjari Medika is an ICAR-NRCG Pune juice grape hybrid (Pusa Navrang x Flame Seedless) valued for its anthocyanin-rich colored juice, seed oil and pomace uses. The literature is substantial but concerns biochemistry, nutraceutical and pharmacological properties, and rootstock interactions. No direct evidence of drought, heat, salinity, flood, disease or pest tolerance was found for the variety, and no yield or Gujarat-specific data is available.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: A teinturier-type juice grape released by ICAR-NRCG Pune, with parentage Pusa Navrang x Flame Seedless. Yield, maturity, adaptation and recommended states are unreported, and release year conflicts (2017 vs 2022).
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: Stress tolerance is unproven. The salt and drought tolerance in the results belongs to rootstocks such as Dogridge and 140RU, and the disease-resistance statements are vague or about other varieties. Stress evidence is none to low.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: Several citations or publications mention the variety: ICAR documents, a PPV&FRA registration, peer-reviewed papers (PMC, Frontiers) and a trial in Tamil Nadu. Parentage and institution are confirmed. No stress, disease or pest tolerance is documented for this variety, because the drought, salt, submergence and resistance hits refer to other crops, rootstocks or varieties. No yield data are available, and there is no Gujarat-specific evidence. This fits the 'at least one citation, but weak on stress traits' tier (60).

dashboard_data.key_attributes: ICAR-NRCG black seedless table grape hybrid (Black Champa x Thompson Seedless); PPV&FRA registered (REG/2020/101); no documented stress tolerance or yield data

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Manjari Shyama is a black seedless table grape hybrid (Black Champa x Thompson Seedless) developed by ICAR-NRC for Grapes, Pune, and registered with PPV&FRA (REG/2020/101). The search results contain no variety-specific evidence for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance, or for disease and pest resistance, and no yield figures. Evidence is mostly institutional listings and studies using it as a host or comparison variety, so evidence quality is low to moderate.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Black seedless table grape hybrid (Black Champa x Thompson Seedless) from ICAR-NRCG, Pune. Yield, maturity, adaptation and recommended states are not documented in the evidence. It has been evaluated in Tamil Nadu (Cumbum valley) and grown by farmers in Maharashtra.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No variety-specific stress tolerance or disease and pest resistance was found. The drought, salt, submergence and resistance hits in the results belong to rootstocks, other grape varieties or other crops. Suitability for Gujarat's stress conditions therefore cannot be established and would need local trials.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance of BM 2003-2 in the retrieved pages.

disease_resistance.summary: Official central release table lists BM 2003-2 as resistant or tolerant to several diseases; the entry names BLS, anthracnose and WB. The table text is garbled, so the exact disease list is unclear. A commercial seller listing claims 'disease resistant' but names no test and is unverified; it is not treated as evidence. No resistance to a named disease was confirmed by a test in the retrieved sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Official table reports low incidence of bean thrips (presented as resistance/tolerance-related evidence in the table). In a whitefly screen, BM-2003-2 recorded the maximum whitefly population, and in the same study it was among the highest for jassid and among the highest for pod damage. These are susceptibility rankings, not resistance claims, so no pest resistance is established for whitefly, jassid or pod damage.

agronomic_details.yield: Official central release table: 8-11 q/ha (equivalent to 800-1100 kg/ha, matching the input record). Sowing-date trial: seed yield 1508 kg/ha and biological yield 2521 kg/ha. A 1012 kg/ha figure also appears in the same PDF, but the text is partly garbled and its context is unclear. Latur kharif trial: 7.41 g pod yield per plant and 4.43 g seed yield per plant (highest among the entries in that trial).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The rainfed sowing-date and variety trial (BM 2002-1, BM 2003-2 and others) is listed, but no stability results for BM 2003-2 are given in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Kharif season per the central release table. Suitable for irrigated conditions in spring/summer seasons per the same table. The Latur kharif trial and the sowing-date trials provide site-specific performance but no broader agro-climatic fit statement.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Kharif trial at Latur, fertilizer and variety combinations: BM-2003-02 gave the highest pod yield per plant (7.41 g) and seed yield per plant (4.43 g) reported in that trial. (2) Sowing-date trial: BM 2003-2 gave seed yield of 1508 kg/ha and biological yield of 2521 kg/ha and was reported as higher-yielding than Phule Vaibhav, BM-4 and PKV Green Gold; the PDF text is partly garbled. (3) Sowing-date and variety trial with BM 2002-1, BM 2003-2 and others under rainfed conditions: the digest lists the study but gives no BM 2003-2 result values. (4) Official central release table: 65-70 days maturity and 8-11 q/ha yield.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Listed as resistant or tolerant to several diseases, with low incidence of bean thrips -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf (the table text is garbled, so the exact disease list is unclear; the entry names BLS, anthracnose and WB)
- In a whitefly screen, BM-2003-2 recorded the maximum population of whitefly -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/326316873_EFFICACY_OF_SOME_INSECTICIDES_AND_BIOPESTICIDES_AGAINST_WHITEFLY_BEMISIA_TABACION_GREENGRAM (this is a susceptibility ranking, not a resistance claim)
- In the same study, BM-2003-2 was among the highest for jassid -- same URL
- Pod damage ranking also places BM-2003-2 among the highest damaged entries -- same URL
- Seller claim of "disease resistant" with no named test -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/bm-2003-2-moong-green-gram-seeds-2851521094388.html (commercial listing, unverified)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity and yield in the official table: 65-70 days and 8-11 q/ha -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf (yield unit as printed in the table, presumably q/ha)
- Kharif trial at Latur, fertilizer and variety combinations, where BM-2003-02 gave the highest pod yield per plant at 7.41 g and seed yield of 4.43 g per plant -- https://www.ijsr.net/archive/v3i7/MDIwMTQxMjQ5.pdf
- Sowing-date trial in which BM 2003-2 gave a seed yield of 1508 kg/ha and biological yield of 2521 kg/ha, and was reported as higher-yielding than Phule Vaibhav, BM-4 and PKV Green Gold -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2020/vol9issue2/PartH/9-2-17-115.pdf (the PDF text is partly garbled; the 1012 kg/ha figure also appears in it)
- Sowing-date and variety trial with BM 2002-1, BM 2003-2 and others under rainfed conditions -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384676279_IJFANS_INTERNATIONAL_JOURNAL_OF_FOOD_AND_NUTRITIONAL_SCIENCES_Response_of_green_gram_Vigna_radiata_L_to_varieties_and_different_dates_of_sowing

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. Parentage "selection from BMG 105" was not confirmed in any retrieved page. The marker and genomic papers returned concern other cultivars (for example VBNGg 2, CO 6, CO 7).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing station per the official table: ARS, Badnapur (Maharashtra) -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- No named breeder or scientist was found for BM 2003-2 in any search result.
- Agricultural Research Station, Badnapur is the institution the variety record names; the input record's "Agril Research Station" appears to be a shortened form of this (inferred, not confirmed).

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. No institute email, phone, postal address or contact page for ARS Badnapur or the breeding team was returned. The Latur paper lists the Department of Agronomy, College of Agriculture, Latur 413512, Maharashtra as an author affiliation (https://www.ijsr.net/archive/v3i7/MDIwMTQxMjQ5.pdf), but that is not a contact for this variety's breeders.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2020). Pharma Innovation Journal 9(2): 398-401, sowing date and variety trial including BM 2003-2 -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2020/vol9issue2/PartH/9-2-17-115.pdf
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown; about 2024 by the page age). Response of green gram (Vigna radiata L.) to varieties and different dates of sowing, IJFANS International Journal of Food and Nutritional Sciences -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384676279_IJFANS_INTERNATIONAL_JOURNAL_OF_FOOD_AND_NUTRITIONAL_SCIENCES_Response_of_green_gram_Vigna_radiata_L_to_varieties_and_different_dates_of_sowing
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown; about 2017 by the page age). Efficacy of some insecticides and biopesticides against whitefly on greengram, which includes BM-2003-2 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/326316873_EFFICACY_OF_SOME_INSECTICIDES_AND_BIOPESTICIDES_AGAINST_WHITEFLY_BEMISIA_TABACION_GREENGRAM
- Authors (Latur Department of Agronomy; individual names not shown). Growth and yield response of greengram to varieties and fertilizer grades, International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR), vol. 3, issue 7 -- https://www.ijsr.net/archive/v3i7/MDIwMTQxMjQ5.pdf
- No ICAR/AICRP annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, or DOI for BM 2003-2 was found in the searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Private dealer listing: Agronarmada Seeds Private Limited, Pune, offers BM 2003-2 moong seed in 5 kg packs, ₹ 250/Kg, listed as in stock -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/bm-2003-2-moong-green-gram-seeds-2851521094388.html (the company's primary business is onion and coriander seed; no NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listing was found)
- Seed company product list includes "B.M.2003-02" among moong varieties -- https://www.indiaseeds.com/products.html (company and listing not verified)
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sale evidence was found for this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Maharashtra, kharif season, per the central release table -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Release year is given as 2012 in the table; the input record's release year is NaT and remains unconfirmed by CSC minutes.

Name note: The evidence refers to "BM 2003-2" and to the variant "BM-2003-02" used in several papers. The Seednet name was not checked separately, as the search returned no Seednet page.

disease_resistance.summary: Reported as moderately resistant to leaf blast, neck blast, brown spot and sheath rot in AICRIP screening nursery trials for Kharif 2008-2010, as cited in the Bankura overview. The underlying AICRIP Progress Report (Screening Nursery 2008-2010, Directorate of Rice Research, Hyderabad) was not retrieved and no URL was found for it. The Bankura overview is the only source for this evidence.

pest_resistance.summary: Reported as moderately resistant to leaf folder in AICRIP screening nursery trials for Kharif 2008-2010, as cited in the Bankura overview. The AICRIP report itself was not retrieved. A ResearchGate figure page on BNKR-1 (Dhiren) mentions multiple pest resistance for 'Dhiren and Dhruba', but it describes BNKR-1 and gives no Dhruba-specific data, so it was excluded.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for West Bengal. Specific districts, ecosystem (for example irrigated late or shallow lowland) and maturity group were not confirmed for BNKR-2. The late maturity group is reported for the variety in the overview.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources. No plant height, duration in days or grain-type data for BNKR-2 was found.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Three years (2008-2010) of national testing under the then Directorate of Rice Research, reported in the Bankura overview. Screening nursery trials for Kharif 2008-2010 reported moderate resistance to leaf blast, neck blast, brown spot, sheath rot and leaf folder (raw AICRIP report not retrieved). Yield was reported as higher than other HYVs of the same late maturity group, with no numeric values. Following testing, the variety was released by the State Variety Release Committee, West Bengal, after a release proposal was submitted to that committee.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
BNKR-2 / BR-2 (rice), evidence digest. Name check: "BNKR-2" in the CSC minutes matches "BNKR-2 (Dhruba)" in the Rice Research Station, Bankura overview. The Seednet name "BR-2" was not found for rice in any result. Seednet lists it under green gram, so the seed-portal evidence is not used. The variety code "DHRU BA" is consistent with "Dhruba." The search found no rice page under "BR-2" or "BNKR-2 (Dhiren)." "Dhiren" is the name of BNKR-1, a different variety, so it is excluded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Reported as moderately resistant to leaf blast, neck blast, brown spot and sheath rot, and as moderately resistant to leaf folder, in AICRIP screening nursery trials for Kharif 2008-2010 (cited via the Bankura overview; the underlying report is the AICRIP Progress Report, Screening Nursery 2008-2010, Directorate of Rice Research, Hyderabad, no URL found) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359842948_Overview_of_Notified_high_yielding_rice_varieties_developed_at_Rice_Research_Station_Bankura
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to BNKR-2 / Dhruba. The only flood-related text found concerns folk rice in general and is not about this variety (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345063572_Indigenous_Rice_of_West_Bengal).

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderate resistance to leaf blast, neck blast, brown spot, sheath rot and leaf folder, as above -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359842948_Overview_of_Notified_high_yielding_rice_varieties_developed_at_Rice_Research_Station_Bankura
Caution: a ResearchGate figure page for BNKR-1 says that "Dhiren and Dhruba" both have multiple pest resistance. It describes BNKR-1 and gives no Dhruba-specific data -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Showing-the-morpho-agronomic-characteristics-of-BNKR-1-Dhiren-lET-20760_tbl1_278301784

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Released as BNKR-2 (Dhruba) by the State Variety Release Committee, West Bengal, after three years (2008-2010) of national testing under the then Directorate of Rice Research, which recommended submitting a release proposal to the State committee -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359842948_Overview_of_Notified_high_yielding_rice_varieties_developed_at_Rice_Research_Station_Bankura
Yield is reported as higher than other HYVs of the same late maturity group. No numeric yield, duration in days, plant height or grain-type data for BNKR-2 was found -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359842948_Overview_of_Notified_high_yielding_rice_varieties_developed_at_Rice_Research_Station_Bankura
Release year: the Seednet record gives 2015-10-12, but no source found gives a release year for BNKR-2. The year is unverified.

GENETICS AND QTL
Pedigree: a cross between IR 42 [IR1561/IR1737//CR9413] (female parent) and Patnai-23, a coastal West Bengal landrace (male parent), followed by pedigree selection -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359842948_Overview_of_Notified_high_yielding_rice_varieties_developed_at_Rice_Research_Station_Bankura
CONFLICT: the variety record gives parentage as "A SELECTION FROM BHAGALPUR LOCAL," which does not match the cross above. The variety record's parentage should be checked against the source.
No QTL, marker or genotyping study for BNKR-2 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Rice Research Station, Bankura (Nutanchati), West Bengal, which developed the variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359842948_Overview_of_Notified_high_yielding_rice_varieties_developed_at_Rice_Research_Station_Bankura
Lead breeder for BNKR-2: no name was found attached to BNKR-2 itself. Goutam Kumar Mallick of Rice Research Station, Bankura, is named as author of the BNKR-1 and BNKR-3 papers -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/283721470_BNKR-3_SAMPRITI_-_A_NEW_LATE_DURATION_HIGH-YIELDING_RICE_VARIETY_FOR_RAINFED_SHALLOW_LOWLANDS_OF_WEST_BENGAL_INDIA
A BNKR-1 page cites "Mallick et al. 2013, 2014" in connection with BNKR-2 (snippet only), so the attribution to Mallick is inferred, not confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/278376937_BNKR-I_Dhiren_-_A_newly_released_late_duration_high-yielding_rice_variety_an_alternative_to_Swarna_MTU_7029_for_West_Bengal_India

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level address (Rice Research Station, Nutanchati, Bankura): Rice Research Station, Nutanchati, Bankura – 722 101, West Bengal, INDIA -- https://journals.ansfoundation.org/index.php/jans/article/view/547
Name, role, email and phone for the BNKR-2 breeder: No evidence found. No official email, phone or institute contact page was found.
Mallick, Goutam Kumar (role: author/scientist, Rice Research Station Bankura): no email or phone was found -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/283721470_BNKR-3_SAMPRITI_-_A_NEW_LATE_DURATION_HIGH-YIELDING_RICE_VARIETY_FOR_RAINFED_SHALLOW_LOWLANDS_OF_WEST_BENGAL_INDIA

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not shown (Year not shown). Overview of Notified high yielding rice varieties developed at Rice Research Station, Bankura. ResearchGate overview (Report/PDF; contains the BNKR-2 (Dhruba) data above) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359842948_Overview_of_Notified_high_yielding_rice_varieties_developed_at_Rice_Research_Station_Bankura
Mallick et al. (2015). Cited in the overview as the source of the pedigree-selection details for another culture; BNKR-2 relevance is not confirmed. Full citation not found -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359842948_Overview_of_Notified_high_yielding_rice_varieties_developed_at_Rice_Research_Station_Bankura
AICRIP Progress Report, Screening Nursery 2008-2010, Directorate of Rice Research, ICAR, Hyderabad (cited in the overview; not retrieved, no URL found) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359842948_Overview_of_Notified_high_yielding_rice_varieties_developed_at_Rice_Research_Station_Bankura
Peer-reviewed or thesis papers specific to BNKR-2 / Dhruba: No evidence found. The BNKR-1 and BNKR-3 papers were excluded because they concern different varieties.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Searches for BNKR-2, Dhruba and BR-2 returned no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for this variety. The seed-related results were general West Bengal HYV seed reports and an unrelated Punjab Basmati 7 page (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/303525069_HYV_Rice_Seeds_Availability_and_Accessibility_in_Bangladesh_and_India_Stakeholders'_Perceptions). Seednet's "BR-2" entry is for green gram, so it does not support any rice seed claim.

RECOMMENDED STATES
West Bengal: the variety was released by the State Variety Release Committee, West Bengal, after the release proposal was submitted to that committee -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359842948_Overview_of_Notified_high_yielding_rice_varieties_developed_at_Rice_Research_Station_Bankura
Specific districts, ecosystem (irrigated late, shallow lowland, etc.) and maturity group for BNKR-2 were not confirmed. The late maturity group is reported for the variety in the overview, and irrigated-late cultivation is stated for BNKR-1 (https://journals.ansfoundation.org/index.php/jans/article/view/547).

agronomic_details.yield: Green fodder yield of 340-360 t/ha/year over seven harvests, against 270 t/ha/year for CO 2 (tnagriculture.in source). agronomic_details.stability: Ranked first at All-India level for green fodder yield, dry matter yield and crude protein yield in 2010, 2011 and 2012. No further stability analysis across environments was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Sowing is recommended throughout the year under irrigation, and in June to September or October to November under rainfed conditions, in all districts. The variety is reported to adapt to shade under coconut plantations.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: First harvest at 75-80 days after planting; later harvests every 40-45 days. The digest does not give a formal maturity-days value.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Perennial; profuse tillering; non-lodging; shade tolerant (2009 forage list describes high green fodder yield with shade tolerance). Morphological characteristics not specified in the digest.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Across multi-location trials, CO (GG) 3 gave mean green fodder yield, dry matter yield and crude protein yield of 1082.4, 229.3 and 20.5 q/ha/year, above the qualifying and national checks. It ranked first at All-India level for these three traits in 2010, 2011 and 2012. Management in the trial/recommendation data: spacing 50 x 50 cm with 40,000 rooted slips per hectare, basal FYM at 25 t/ha, and NPK at 50:50:40 kg/ha; first harvest at 75-80 days, then every 40-45 days. Note: the digest gives year of release as 2009 in agronomy sources and 2010 in the release paper, which differs from the ground-truth release date of 2014-06-02.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Shade tolerance and adaptation under coconut plantations are listed as special features of CO (GG) 3, along with profuse tillering and non-lodging. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/foragecrops_guineagrass.html
- The 2009 forage list describes CO (GG) 3 as shade tolerant with high green fodder yield. -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/pdf/forage%20varieties.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for CO (GG) 3. Searches returned only the shade and non-lodging features above.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for CO (GG) 3. The search returned only greengram CO 8 pages (yellow mosaic and stem necrosis resistance). These concern a different crop and were excluded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Year of release is 2009 and the variety is perennial, with green fodder yield of 340-360 t/ha/year over seven harvests, against 270 t/ha/year for CO 2. -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/10_Guinea_Grass.pdf
- First harvest is at 75-80 days after planting and later harvests come once every 40-45 days, with about 320 t/ha/year over seven harvests. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/foragecrops_guineagrass.html
- Spacing is 50 x 50 cm, with 40,000 rooted slips per hectare, basal FYM at 25 t/ha, and NPK at 50:50:40 kg/ha. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/foragecrops_guineagrass.html
- Recommended sowing season is throughout the year under irrigation, and June to September or October to November under rainfed conditions, in all districts. -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/10_Guinea_Grass.pdf
- Across multi-location trials, CO (GG) 3 gave mean green fodder yield, dry matter yield and crude protein yield of 1082.4, 229.3 and 20.5 q/ha/year, above the qualifying and national checks. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301694648_High_green_fodder_yielding_new_grass_varieties
- It ranked first at All-India level for green fodder yield, dry matter yield and crude protein yield in 2010, 2011 and 2012. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301694648_High_green_fodder_yielding_new_grass_varieties

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage is recorded as clonal selection from Mumbasa; the input's "Not specified" is therefore incomplete. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/foragecrops_guineagrass.html
- No QTL, marker or genetic-diversity study for CO (GG) 3 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The variety was developed at the Department of Forage Crops, Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301694648_High_green_fodder_yielding_new_grass_varieties

- C. Babu's profile lists Guinea grass CO (GG) 3 among his forage crops. -- https://sites.google.com/a/tnau.ac.in/cpbg/babucv

disease_resistance.summary: DGGV-2 is susceptible to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV). It is explicitly used as a 'susceptible check' in studies evaluating resistance to MYMV in other breeding lines and genotypes. There is no direct evidence that DGGV-2 itself possesses resistance to bruchid (Callosobruchus maculatus); rather, a cross involving DGGV-2 (V-02-802×DGGV-2) was noted to show resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: While a cross involving DGGV-2 (V-02-802×DGGV-2) showed resistance to bruchid, DGGV-2 itself is not explicitly stated to possess resistance to bruchid or other pests in the provided information.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields for DGGV-2 vary across studies. It was observed as a 'lowest yielder' at 393 kg/ha in one analysis. Another study recorded a seed yield of 701.3 kg/ha. However, with optimal management (sowing during the first fortnight of June and foliar spray of 2% DAP), DGGV-2 demonstrated a higher seed yield of 1380 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: The varying yield performance across different studies (393 kg/ha, 701.3 kg/ha, 1380 kg/ha) suggests its yield can be influenced by environmental conditions and specific agronomic practices.
agronomic_details.adaptation: DGGV-2 is suitable for sowing up to the end of June but not suitable for late sowing. It exhibits tolerance to shattering compared to Chinamung and Sel-4 varieties. It is responsive to fertilizer application at 25 N & 50 P kg/ha. Optimal performance was noted with first fortnight of June sowing combined with 2% DAP foliar spray.

agronomic_details.field_trials: DGGV-2 has been evaluated in field trials concerning yield performance under varying sowing dates and nutrition, and for reaction to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GBM-1 (greengram)

Name note: CSC minutes and Seednet both use "GBM-1". The only matching source, the DPD mungbean table, writes it as "GBM 1". None of the four searches returned a seednet.gov.in page, so Seednet's own listing (variety code A0305222) is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in GBM-1 returned only other moong varieties (Gujarat Mung-4, Gujarat Mung-7, Pusa Vishal) and unrelated pages.

DISEASE AND PEST
GBM 1, released 2016 by NAU, Gujarat, is listed as moderately tolerant to MYMV -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf (same table repeated at https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf, entry 34-9:10)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
GBM 1 is listed with a yield of 11-12 q/ha and 102-105 days to maturity, suited to rabi cultivation in Gujarat -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
No multi-location trial data, field-trial reports or AICRP reports naming GBM-1 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No parentage, marker or QTL study for GBM-1 was returned. The parentage field ("Not specified") was not confirmed.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
The DPD table lists the originating centre as NAU, Gujarat -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
No breeder name for GBM-1 was found. The Navsari Agricultural University pages returned (https://old.nau.in/alloprtitle.php, https://nau.in/pages/about-navsari-agricultural-university-1548127676) name pulse scientists and the Pulses and Castor Research Station, but none mentions GBM-1, so they are not attributed to it.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No NAU Pulse Research Station contact page or GBM-1 breeder contact was returned. The Pulse Research Station page returned (https://www.aau.in/college-menu/507) belongs to Anand Agricultural University, Vadodara, a different institution, and was not used.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. The search returned no peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper that names GBM-1. Greengram results were about other varieties or agronomy (for example https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/102-4-6-103-107.pdf on COGG 973, and https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5417, which cites NAU theses on nutrient management rather than varieties).

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Seller pages returned (https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/research-moong-seeds-8745067873.html, https://agribee.in/agriculture-seed/greengram-seeds/greengram-gujarat-4/, https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/mung-seeds-guj-4-11807325230.html) sell other moong varieties (Partech-668, Gujarat-4, Guj-4) and do not name GBM-1. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listing for GBM-1 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Gujarat -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf (matches the CSC input "['Gujarat']" and the 2016 release year)

heat.details: Tolerant to heat and high temperature. It is identified as a heat-tolerant genotype and has been a subject of research on physiological responses under heat stress.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerant to Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV), also known as Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Disease (MYMD), and Powdery Mildew (PM). It has also been included in screening programs for Cercospora Leaf Spot (CLS) resistance.
