agronomic_details.yield: Reported average yields typically range from 60-70 q/ha. It is a subject of studies on genetic variability parameters related to seed yield and is considered a valuable genotype for yield improvement research.
agronomic_details.stability: IPM 02-14 serves as a reference variety in comparative performance studies of green gram varieties. Its consistent performance, particularly under summer cultivation with increased irrigation facilities, contributes to its popularization.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Primarily adapted for Spring/Summer season cultivation under normal sown conditions. It is also suitable for cultivation with increased irrigation facilities during the summer.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: ERECT-UPRIGHT, DETERMINATE, SYNCHRONOUS MATURITY.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has been extensively evaluated in field trials for growth parameters, yield, and tolerance to various abiotic stresses including heat, drought, and salinity. It has also been screened for tolerance to pre-harvest sprouting and resistance/susceptibility to root-knot nematode.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: The marker CEDG 147 is associated with tolerance in green gram and has been observed in IPM 02-14. The variety has been utilized in SSR-marker assisted evaluations for genetic diversity. Furthermore, IPM 02-14 has been a target for genome editing to enhance traits such as anaerobic germination tolerance, early uniform emergence, and grain yield.

drought.details: Identified as a drought-tolerant genotype. It is among the high-yielding varieties recommended for adoption by farmers under drought conditions. Studies indicate it shows low genotype x environment interaction, contributing to yield stability. Physiological mechanisms contributing to tolerance include the overaccumulation of glycine betaine and adaptive morphological traits like higher Canopy Temperature Depression (CTD) and Membrane Stability Index (MSI).

heat.details: Recognized as a heat-tolerant green gram genotype capable of setting pods at high temperatures. It is discussed among heat-tolerant mung bean cultivars and genotypes that accumulate glycine betaine, which enhances tolerance to heat stress. IPM 02-3 also exhibits higher Canopy Temperature Depression (CTD), Membrane Stability Index (MSI), and total chlorophyll content under stress, indicating adaptive physiological responses.

salinity.details: Included in studies investigating abiotic stresses like salinity affecting mungbean production. It is mentioned in contexts related to mitigating NaCl stress and examining interactive effects of sodium and calcium on proline metabolism in salt-tolerant cultivars, suggesting some level of tolerance or inclusion in salinity tolerance research.

flood.details: Listed among varieties affected by waterlogging stress and included in studies on the response of mungbean to transient waterlogging at germination and seedling stages, but its specific tolerance level is not stated.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerant to Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV).

pest_resistance.summary: Screened against Meloidogyne incognita (root-knot nematode), but specific resistance level is not provided.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield of 994 kgs/ha was originally reported. Specific trials showed variations, with yields up to 1409 kg/ha (14.09 q/ha) in comparison trials, and 912 kg/ha (9.12 q/ha) in specific regional projects (Jammu, 2015-2016). It serves as a standard check variety against which newer varieties exhibit yield superiority.
agronomic_details.stability: Demonstrates low genotype x environment interaction, indicating good yield stability across different environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for normal sown conditions during the Kharif season, particularly adapted to the North West Plain Zone of India (Delhi, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Rajasthan). Historically, it has been a highly preferred variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Seed are shiny green and medium seed size with high protein content.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Extensive field trials include its evaluation under different NPK doses, inclusion in State Adaptive Trials, and performance comparisons against other varieties (e.g., Pusa M 2131, MH 02-15, ML 818). Its performance has been assessed in various regions including Jammu and Central Uttar Pradesh.

Specific trials showed variations, with yields up to 1409 kg/ha (14.09 q/ha) in comparison trials, and 912 kg/ha (9.12 q/ha) in specific regional projects (Jammu, 2015-2016). It serves as a standard check variety against which newer varieties exhibit yield superiority.
agronomic_performance.stability: Demonstrates low genotype x environment interaction, indicating good yield stability across different environments.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Suitable for normal sown conditions during the Kharif season, particularly adapted to the North West Plain Zone of India (Delhi, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Rajasthan). Historically, it has been a highly preferred variety.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Seed are shiny green and medium seed size with high protein content.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: Extensive field trials include its evaluation under different NPK doses, inclusion in State Adaptive Trials, and performance comparisons against other varieties (e.g., Pusa M 2131, MH 02-15, ML 818). Its performance has been assessed in various regions including Jammu and Central Uttar Pradesh.

seednet_fields.Parentage: (IPM 3-1 X SPS 5) 1.	IPM 3-1: A superior mungbean advanced line with medium tall plants, large, green and shining seeds, resistant to MYMV. 2.	SPS 5: A superior urdbean donor registered as INGR12006, having sympodial pod bearing and high level of resistant to MYMV.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Suitable for normal conditions during Spring and kharif season with recommended agronomic practices.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Erect plant with pubescent, green leaves, black pods at maturity, green, shining and medium large seeds.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Highly resistant to MYMV and Cercospora leaf spot and resistant to leaf crinkle and leaf curl diseases.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 1.	Basal: NPKS @ 20:50:40: 20 kg./ha, in case of zinc deficiency: 20 kgZnSo4. 2.	Foliar spray of 2% urea at the time of flowering.

disease_resistance.summary: Mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV): Central variety listing records IPM 312-20 as having moderate resistance to MYMV (Kharif season). The parent IPM 3-1 is described as resistant to MYMV, and the second parent SPS 5 as having high-level resistance to MYMV, which supports the MYMV resistance origin. Cercospora leaf spot: IPM-312-20 was included in a CLS resistance screening of mungbean germplasm, but the search snippet does not state its resistance rating. Host-plant resistance: a ResearchGate review of green gram and black gram diseases lists IPM 312-20 (Vasudha) among varieties cited for host-plant resistance in disease management. Anthracnose and powdery mildew: an InTechOpen listing describes a different variety as moderately resistant to these diseases, and the snippet does not attribute this to IPM 312-20.

pest_resistance.summary: Sucking pests: IPM 312-20 appears in a screening of mungbean germplasm against major sucking pests, but the snippet does not show the column headings, so no resistance rating can be assigned. Pod borer complex (Maruca vitrata and related): IPM 312-20 is listed in a germplasm screening against major insect pests with an infestation percentage, but the snippet is truncated and the value for this variety is not visible. Resistance level is therefore unknown.

One search snippet mentions drought-tolerant mung bean cultivars in general, but it does not clearly attribute that status to IPM 409-4. IPM 409-4 appears in a list of genotypes evaluated for abiotic stress constraints (drought, waterlogging, salinity, heat), but the snippet gives no individual result.

heat.details: IPM 409-4 is listed among mungbean genotypes with higher canopy temperature depression (CTD), membrane stability index (MSI), and total chlorophyll content, traits associated with heat tolerance (cited from Punia et al., 2019). Heat stress indices were used to identify physiologically efficient heat-tolerant genotypes, and IPM 409-4 appears in that screening. The search results give no quantitative values, so the level is rated medium on qualitative evidence only.

salinity.details: IPM 409-4 appears in a list of genotypes within a salinity-related reference set, but the search results do not confirm its individual salinity tolerance rating or mechanism.

flood.details: No search result provides flood or waterlogging tolerance data specific to IPM 409-4. Waterlogging is listed as a key abiotic constraint in mungbean generally.

disease_resistance.summary: Cercospora leaf spot (CLS): IPM 409-4 was included in a CLS resistance screening of mungbean germplasm, but the snippets do not state its reaction. Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV): the ACIAR Mung Central document refers to high resistance to YMV in lines developed from the same program, but the snippet does not clearly attribute this to IPM 409-4. Resistance status for IPM 409-4 is therefore not confirmed for any specific disease.

seednet_fields.Parentage: IPM 99-125 X Co-5 IPM 99-125: An elite mungbean variety released notified in 2004 for Spring cultivation in NEPZ, It has medium tall plants, large, green and shining seeds, and is resistant to yellow mosaic disease. Co 5: an elite mungbean variety released in 1991 for kharif season in Tamil Nadu. This variety is tolerant to yellow mosaic disease.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Suitable for normal sown conditions with recommended agronomic practices.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Erect East upright plant with pubescent green leaves, black pods at maturity, green shining and medium large seeds.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to yellow mosaic and cercospora leaf disease.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Resistant to thrips and white fly.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Basal: NPKS @ 20: 50: 40: 20 kg/ha, in case of zinc deficiency: 20 kg ZnSo4 Foliar spray of 2% urea at the time of flowering.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: MH-125 (chickpea / green gram)**

**Name check:** The CSC/chickpea name "MH-125" and the Seednet name "MH 125" point to the same entry. In the sources I retrieved, though, the record is a green gram (mungbean) variety, and the Seednet crop field reads GREEN GRAM. The retrieved sources give MH 125 the local name Basanti. Each line below says which name the evidence refers to. Treat the chickpea classification as unconfirmed.

**STRESS TOLERANCE**
- Resistance to mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV) is recorded for MH 125 / Basanti, shown as a resistance trait in the mungbean release table -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

**DISEASE AND PEST**
- A chickpea-listing row for "MH 125" (CCSHAU, 2010, Haryana) is marked resistant to MYMV, leaf crinkle, web blight and anthracnose, and moderately resistant to cercospora leaf spot. This row sits in a chickpea table but uses mungbean-type disease traits, so the classification is doubtful -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Pest resistance specific to MH-125: No evidence found.

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**
- Maturity of 64-70 days and average yield of 12-15 q/ha are listed for Basanti (MH 125) -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf (also https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf)
- A grower guide gives 64 days to harvest for MH 125 and recommends a seed rate of 8-9 kg/acre for kharif and 12-15 kg/acre for summer, with seed treated with Captan or Thiram at 3 g/kg -- https://apnakhetibazar.com/green-gram-moong/
- A Tamil Nadu multi-location stability study (33 mungbean genotypes, 3 locations) includes MH-125 in its tables. The extracted table is garbled, and one seed-yield-per-plant value of 17.239 appears against MH-125 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324637241_Stability_Analysis_in_Mungbean_Vigna_radiata_L_for_Micronutrients_Fe_Zn_and_Seed_Yield (refers to MH-125 as a mungbean line)
- Chickpea trials: No evidence found.

**GENETICS AND QTL**
- Parentage: the mungbean table lists Basanti's cross as Asha x PDM 90-1, released 2010 at 12-15 q/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339424589_Breeding_Progress_and_Future_Challenges_Biotic_Stresses (refers to Basanti / MH 125, mungbean)
- A 2021 mungbean association-mapping study lists Basanti with the pedigree Asha x PDM 90-1, developed at CCS HAU, Hisar, and genotyped with 89 SSR markers -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2021.749439/full (refers to Basanti, mungbean)
- QTL or marker studies specific to MH-125: No evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME AND CROP CHECK -- "MH 2114" (code DHBH 1397) appears only as a pearl millet hybrid, not green gram. The Seednet name "MH-1142" appears only as a green gram (moong) variety. The "millet" crop field matches MH 2114, and the Seednet crop field matches MH-1142. The two names look like different varieties, so I have kept their evidence under separate labels. The parentage "MH 421" is a green gram name, and no source links it to MH 2114. Searches: 4 of 4 used.

STRESS TOLERANCE
[MH 2114 / DHBH 1397, pearl millet] The AICPMIP release table describes the entry as highly resistant to downy mildew and tolerant to rust and insect pests, but the table text is ambiguous about which row these traits belong to -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
[MH 2114] Drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found.
[MH-1142, green gram] A seller page says it does not tolerate waterlogging; this is a commercial claim, not an official trial result -- https://sanjivaniseeds.com/product/moong-mh-1142

DISEASE AND PEST
[MH 2114 / DHBH 1397] Same AICPMIP table entry as above (downy mildew, rust, insect pests); row assignment uncertain -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
[MH-1142] Official-style release table lists it as moderately resistant to anthracnose and powdery mildew and resistant to MYMV -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
[MH-1142] The same claims appear in a Hindi release summary (CVRC 2020) -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-mh-1142/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
[MH 2114 / DHBH 1397] The 52nd Annual Pearl Millet Workshop proceedings list MH 2114 among hybrids in a trial at Jamnagar, SK Nagar, Aurangabad and Dhule -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/pw2017.pdf
[MH 2114] Yield and maturity data from a verified source: No evidence found.
[MH-1142] The release table gives 11-12 q/ha yield and 60-65 days to maturity -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
[MH-1142] Commercial pages give different figures (63-70 days; 5-6 quintals per acre), so the figures conflict -- https://market.plantix.net/en/products/seeds/fa0224bd-83b8-42ce-972d-3eb10b39329e/moong-mh1142-truthfully-labelled-seed-4-kg-cloth-bag/

GENETICS AND QTL
[MH 2114] No evidence found for markers, QTL or parentage (Muskan x BDYR 2 / MH 421).
[MH-1142] No evidence found for markers, QTL or parentage. The search returned a green gram Zn fertilizer study on MH 421, which is a different topic and is not attributed to this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
[MH 2114 / DHBH 1397] No breeder name found. Results about MPKV Dhule pearl millet units concern other hybrids and varieties (e.g., Dhanshakti, Phule Mahashakti) and are not attributed here -- https://www.acdhule.edu.in/wDepartment/Bajara-Research-Station.pdf
[MH-1142] The release table lists the originating centre as HAU Hisar, not MPKV Dhule -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
[MH-1142] No breeder name found.

CONTACT DETAILS
[MH 2114] No evidence found (no breeder, institute email, phone or address).
[MH-1142] No evidence found (no breeder, institute email, phone or address).

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not stated (2017). Proceedings of the 52nd Annual Pearl Millet Workshop, trial listing for MH 2114. AICPMIP -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/pw2017.pdf (year taken from file name)
Authors not stated (n.d.). Table

pest_resistance.summary: Exhibited high resistance against whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) with 6.80 whitefly nymphs per 3 plants and lowest leaf damage recorded at 6.5 percent. Identified as moderately resistant to Root-Knot Nematode (Meloidogyne javanica).

agronomic_performance.yield: Described as a high-yielding variety, though no quantitative yield data is provided.
agronomic_performance.stability: No explicit information on stability across environments beyond its use in photothermal efficiency studies under different sowing environments.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Suitable for normal sown conditions during the kharif season. It is a warm-season legume that thrives in high temperature conditions.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: MH-1142 has been utilized in various studies, including those on photothermal efficiency, whitefly resistance, root-knot nematode screening, nutrient optimization, and the effects of manuring and biofertilization, indicating its inclusion in diverse field trials.

breeder_and_contacts.institution: CCS Haryana Agricultural University

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MH 318 (greengram / moong)
Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "MH 318", so every finding below refers to that one name. Seednet (seednet.gov.in) did not appear in any search result, so no Seednet record was checked.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistant to MYMV (mungbean yellow mosaic virus); no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Listed as resistant to yellow mosaic virus, with its main characteristics described as well under rice-wheat rotation -- https://krishakjagat.org/news/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-mh-318/ (the search result shows the URL with "www." omitted in the source: https://www.krishakjagat.org/news/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-mh-318/)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to MYMV; no other disease or pest resistance recorded for MH 318 -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Dealer page says it has resistance to yellow mosaic virus; this is a commercial claim, not a trial result -- https://drseeds.in/moong/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity 60-65 days -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf ; https://www.krishakjagat.org/news/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-mh-318/
- Yield 14 q/ha in kharif and 10 q/ha in spring/summer -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf ; https://www.krishakjagat.org/news/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-mh-318/
- Dealer page gives 8-9 quintals per acre; units differ from the official figures, so treat it as unverified -- https://drseeds.in/moong/
- Pot-trial comparison of MH 318 with other genotypes under zinc fertilisation (CCS HAU, 2010-11). Per the snippet, MH 318 had among the lowest pods per plant (5.28) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/317594571_Green_gram_Vigna_radiata_L_Productivity_and_Grain_Quality_enrichment_through_Zinc_Fertilization
- No multi-location AICRP trial result for MH 318 found

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found (no parentage, breeding method or QTL/marker study in results). The DPD record gives no parentage either.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION

drought.details: MH-421 is resistant to drought stress and has been evaluated for drought tolerance under semi-arid conditions. It maintains physiological functioning under moisture-induced stresses. Differential responses to drought stress have been studied.

heat.details: MH-421 is tolerant to heat stress and terminal heat stress. It maintained high yield and physiological functioning under high temperature. It is considered an excellent heat-tolerant mungbean variety.

salinity.details: MH-421 has been used in studies evaluating the effects of salt stress on growth and biochemical changes in green gram, identified as a high yielding genotype in this context. However, its specific tolerance level to salinity is not explicitly stated as 'tolerant' or 'resistant' in the provided results.

flood.details: MH-421 is mentioned in a list of green gram varieties that include those considered for waterlogging tolerance. While studies on QTLs for anaerobic germination and tolerance to early submergence in mungbean exist, it is not explicitly stated that MH-421 itself possesses significant flood or submergence tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: MH-421 is resistant to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV/YMV). It is also reported to be resistant to all rusts. Two dominant genes govern MYMD resistance in crosses involving MH-421.

pest_resistance.summary: Not specified

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield reported between 10-12 quintals per hectare (q/ha) and specifically 12.00 q/ha in some instances. Other reports show 17.06 q/ha or 8.65 q/ha in specific contexts.
agronomic_details.stability: MH-421 maintained high yield and physiological functioning under high temperature stress, indicating good stability under abiotic stress conditions. It has been evaluated under semi-arid conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for the North Western Plains Zone (NWPZ) and Central Zone (CZ), specifically for cultivation in Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan, and Western Uttar Pradesh during the Summer season. Also suitable for Kharif season.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Medium-dwarf plant type, non-shattering pods, and medium bold shining green seeds.
agronomic_details.field_trials: MH-421 has been a subject of Cluster Frontline Demonstrations (CFLD) in Sirsa District, Haryana, and disseminated through farmers' participatory approaches in Hisar district, Haryana. It is a common variety used as a test crop in various agricultural studies.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No specific genetic markers (SNP/SSR) are detailed for MH-421 in the provided results.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: While studies mention QTLs for anaerobic germination and tolerance to early submergence in mungbean generally, no specific QTLs are attributed directly to MH-421 in the provided information.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Physiological, biochemical, and antioxidant enzyme activities are studied in MH-421 under stress conditions. Biochemical changes have been observed in response to stress. Resistance to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Disease (MYMD) in MH-421 is governed by two dominant genes.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: As a 'Central released variety' from CCSHAU, it is likely available through government seed corporations and agricultural departments.
commercial_info.availability_status: Readily available, indicated by its status as a Central released variety, its presence in KVKs, and its popularity for cultivation.
commercial_info.kvk: The variety MH-421 was collected from Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) in Rajasthan, indicating KVKs as a source of availability.
commercial_info.private_dealers: Mentioned as one of the 'Popular Varieties' for summer moong cultivation, suggesting availability through private agricultural dealers.

drought.details: ML 267 has been consistently reported as drought-resistant. It was utilized in studies evaluating source leaf responses to water-deficit stresses and in experiments where drought was induced by PEG (Polyethylene glycol). Agrobacterium mediated genetic transformation attempts were made for ML 267 specifically to enhance drought stress tolerance, indicating its potential or existing tolerance. It has also been used as a test crop in drought-related experiments.

heat.details: ML 267 is identified as a heat-tolerant mungbean genotype based on morpho-physiological parameters. It has been evaluated in crosses (e.g., ML 267 × LGG 528) for heat stress tolerance and yield attributes using generation mean analysis. Studies have also evaluated stress tolerance indices to identify heat tolerance, including ML 267.

salinity.details: ML 267 is listed among varieties for developing bio-fortified mungbean lines with enhanced stress tolerance, including salinity. Specific studies have investigated salt tolerance in mungbean cultivars like ML 267 and the interactive effects of sodium and calcium on proline metabolism in salt-tolerant mungbean involving this genotype.

flood.details: Waterlogging is mentioned as a key abiotic stress for mungbean generally, but no specific information on ML 267's tolerance or susceptibility to flood or waterlogging was found.

disease_resistance.summary: ML 267 is reported to be resistant to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV). However, it is classified as Highly Susceptible (HS) to the root-knot nematode, *Meloidogyne incognita*.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific pest resistance details found, apart from its susceptibility to *Meloidogyne incognita* (a nematode pest), which is listed under disease resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: While specific average yield values are not provided, ML 267 has been evaluated for yield and yield attributes in genetic crosses. Its 100-seed weight is reported as 12.0g. It is considered a popular cultivar.
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly specified.
agronomic_details.adaptation: ML 267 is a popular cultivar of greengram, adaptable for cultivation during both Kharif and Summer seasons. It is particularly recommended for the North Western Plain Zone. It shows good tolerance to the post-emergence herbicide imazethapyr, which is beneficial for weed management. It is also suitable for sowing as sprouted seeds in short-duration pulse rotations.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: HAIRINESS OF STEM AND BROAD; SLIGHT TINGE OF PURPLE COLOUR. The seed size is described as small.
agronomic_details.field_trials: ML 267 has been used as a test crop in strip plot design experiments investigating different tillage methods. It has also been extensively used in generational studies (P1, P2, F1, F2, B1, and B2 generations) to analyze yield and stress tolerance traits.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No specific genetic markers (e.g., SNPs, SSRs) or QTL positions are directly reported for ML 267 in the provided results.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: ML 267 has been utilized in genetic crosses for research purposes. A cross of ML 267 × LGG 528 was used for generation mean analysis to study the inheritance of yield, yield attributes, Water Use Efficiency (WUE), and heat stress tolerance. This cross also produced transgressive segregants for traits such as harvest index, Specific Leaf Area (SLA), Specific Leaf Weight (SLW), and relative injury (stress-related traits). Additionally, a cross between ML 267 and urdbean cv. Mash 114 was made for mapping Yellow Mosaic Disease (YMD) resistance, indicating that MYMV resistance in this cross is controlled by digenic recessive genes.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: ML 267 has been included in studies aimed at identifying heat-tolerant genotypes through morpho-physiological parameters and gene expression analysis related to abiotic stress tolerance. However, specific genes or pathways linked directly to ML 267's tolerance mechanisms are not detailed.

flood.details: No specific information regarding flood tolerance of ML 2015 (SML 2015) is available in the provided search results. This is not specific to ML 2015.

disease_resistance.summary: (1) Yellow mosaic virus (YMV; the field guide specifically names MYMV): listed as tolerant in the Kharif field guide (ResearchGate) and in the mungbean state-release table (dpd.gov.in). (2) Cercospora leaf spot: listed as a tolerance in the mungbean state-release table (dpd.gov.in). (3) Powdery mildew (PM): described as moderately resistant in a sheet whose layout is ambiguous about which row the entry belongs to; this must be verified before reliance. (4) Anthracnose and Cercospora/leaf spot: listed in the chickpea-labelled sheet (dpd.gov.in VARIETIES-Website.pdf), which the digest considers probably a mis-tabulated entry, so these are low-confidence. Original CSC record: disease reaction 'Not Specified'.

pest_resistance.summary: (1) Thrips: tolerance listed in the mungbean state-release table (dpd.gov.in). (2) Stem fly: tolerance listed in the same table. Original CSC record: pest reaction 'Not Specified'. No other pest evidence found in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: 13-15 q/ha (mungbean state-release table, dpd.gov.in). A chickpea-labelled sheet gives 12.00 q/ha, which the digest treats as unreliable given the crop conflict. Original CSC record average_yield field has units only ('Kg/Ha') with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability evidence found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Original CSC record: suitable for Kharif and Rabi seasons in all Telangana districts, other areas of Andhra Pradesh, and the southern zone of the country. Mungbean release table also lists Kharif and Rabi suitability.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 60 To 70Days (CSC record). The mungbean release table gives 65-70 days; the chickpea-labelled sheet gives 60-70 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: PODS MEDIUM LONG AND DARK GREEN WITH PROMINENT PURPLE SUTURE ; SEEDS ARE BOLD AND DARK GREEN IN COLOUR.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Mungbean release table: yield 13-15 q/ha, duration 65-70 days, Kharif and Rabi suitability. (2) Chickpea-labelled sheet: 12.00 q/ha, 60-70 days, flagged as unreliable. (3) 'Study on Selective Mechanization in Kharif Greengram (Vigna radiata L.)': trial at ARS Madhira farm, 2017-2018, authors not stated; not confirmed to involve this variety, and no results reported in the digest. (4) Multi-location trial results: no evidence found.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Madhira Pesara 347 (variety_name) / Madhira Pesara-347 (seednet_variety_name)

Crop check: the record says chickpea, but the Seednet crop is GREEN GRAM (MOONG BEAN/MOONG). Every source I found lists this variety under mungbean/green gram, and the chickpea-table hit is a mixed-up list. Treat the crop as green gram (Vigna radiata) unless the Seednet record shows otherwise. The Seednet portal itself was not reachable in these searches, so variety code A0305151 is unverified.

Name check: the sources use both "Madhira Pesara-347" (the dpd.gov.in mungbean sheets, which match the Seednet form) and "Madhira Pesara 347" (the other sources). The findings below refer to the same variety under both names.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Madhira Pesara-347 ... ARS, Madhira ... Moderately resistant to PM. The sheet's layout is ambiguous about which row this belongs to, so verify before relying on it. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
STRESS TOLERANCE -- The mungbean list gives Madhira Pesara-347 as a Telangana/AP release with YMV and Cercospora leaf spot listed as its tolerances. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
STRESS TOLERANCE -- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Field guide: Madhira Pesara 347 (Kharif) is tolerant to MYMV. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/265793473_Field_guide_to_Mungbean_and_Urdbean
DISEASE AND PEST -- The mungbean state-release table lists tolerance to thrips and stem fly alongside YMV and Cercospora leaf spot. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST -- The chickpea-labelled sheet also lists tolerance to Cercospora and leaf spot, plus anthracnose, for Madhira Pesara 347; this is probably a mis-tabulated entry. -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The mungbean release table gives duration of 65-70 days and yield of 13-15 q/ha, with Kharif and Rabi suitability. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
PKV GREEN GOLD (also AKM 9911). Evidence refers to the green gram / mungbean variety. Seednet lists the crop as green gram, but the input says chickpea. Chickpea sources in the results are about other varieties or are a probable listing error, so no chickpea evidence is attributed to this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
[Name: PKV Green Gold / AKM 9911; crop: green gram]
Moderately resistant to powdery mildew (PM abbreviation as printed; expansion inferred) -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. Searches 1 to 3 returned no such data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
[Name: PKV Green Gold / AKM 9911; crop: green gram]
Moderately resistant to PM (powdery mildew); bold seed and long pod noted as salient features -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
Chickpea listing gives "Tolerant to PM, suitable for kharif" for "PKV green gold PDKV" (crop mismatch; likely a misplaced row) -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
Pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
[Name: PKV Green Gold / AKM 9911; crop: green gram]
Released in Maharashtra's Vidarbha region for kharif; yield 10-12 q/ha; 64-72 days to maturity -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
Same yield (10-12 q/ha), maturity (64-72 days) and Vidarbha area of adoption, listed as 2007 (SVRC) -- https://www.journalcra.com/sites/default/files/issue-pdf/45672_1.pdf
Yield 10-11 q/ha and 57-80 days in chickpea-page listing (conflicting; see caveat) -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
Included as one of five green gram varieties in a sowing-date trial (different sowing dates, sub-plot varieties) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384676279_IJFANS_INTERNATIONAL_JOURNAL_OF_FOOD_AND_NUTRITIONAL_SCIENCES_Response_of_green_gram_Vigna_radiata_L_to_varieties_and_different_dates_of_sowing
Multi-location trial results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Parentage (input: "Not specified") was not found in any result. No marker or QTL studies were returned.

drought.details: The AICPMIP table lists PA 9072 (pearl millet) with moisture stress tolerance, but the row is garbled (medium confidence). A ProAgro dealer page describes tolerance to moisture stress and suitability for low-rainfall areas; this brand conflicts with Bayer and is treated as secondary. No quantitative drought data or physiological mechanisms were found. The mungbean PUSA-9072 remark about drought is general to the crop and is not attributed to PA 9072.

heat.details: No heat tolerance data found for PA 9072 or PUSA-9072.

salinity.details: No salinity tolerance data found for PA 9072 or PUSA-9072.

flood.details: No flood tolerance data found for PA 9072 or PUSA-9072.

disease_resistance.summary: PA 9072 (pearl millet): the AICPMIP table row associates it with resistance to downy mildew, blast, smut and ergot (garbled; low-to-medium confidence). The ProAgro dealer page lists downy mildew resistance (secondary, brand conflict). Mungbean PUSA-9072 (not attributed to PA 9072): resistant to dry root rot in a poly-house screen of 47 genotypes; moderately susceptible to mungbean yellow mosaic virus in a West Bengal field study; moderately resistant to YMV in a Pharma Innovation Journal screen of AICRP mungbean entries (rabi 2017).

pest_resistance.summary: PA 9072 (pearl millet): the AICPMIP table row associates it with shoot-fly tolerance (garbled; low-to-medium confidence). No other pest resistance data found for PA 9072. No pest data found for PUSA-9072 mungbean.

agronomic_details.yield: Not found in searched sources. No quantitative yield data (average_yield in input: Kg/Ha, no value) was found for PA 9072.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location yield data for the Bayer pearl millet PA 9072 was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Dealer page describes suitability for low-rainfall areas (secondary source). Recommended-state evidence points to Rajasthan and Haryana (see recommended states). Mungbean PUSA-9072 adaptation is not attributed to PA 9072.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 70-72 days (early, kharif-only), per ProAgro dealer page (secondary source; input field stated Not specified)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Lodging tolerance is listed in the AICPMIP table (garbled row) and on the dealer page. No other morphological or agronomic characteristics found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: No field trial results for the Bayer pearl millet PA 9072 were found. Trials found concern mungbean PUSA-9072 and are not attributed to PA 9072: (1) Intercropping with okra: YMD incidence reduced by about 28% versus the control. (2) West Bengal field study: moderately susceptible to mungbean yellow mosaic virus. (3) Poly-house screen of 47 genotypes: resistant to dry root rot. (4) Pharma Innovation Journal screen of AICRP mungbean entries, Kharif and Rabi 2017: moderately resistant to YMV.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. Parentage was not found; fragments 'PSP91 x' and 'PP107' appear near the PA 9072 row in the AICPMIP table but could not be reliably assigned.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. No PA 9072-specific QTL, marker or parentage study was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
PA 9072 EVIDENCE DIGEST

NAME AND CROP NOTE
- The CSC name PA 9072 (crop: millet) matches the Bayer pearl millet hybrid. The AICPMIP table lists PA 9072 among pearl millet hybrids from Bayer Bio Science, Hyderabad -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- The Seednet name PUSA-9072 (crop: green gram) is a different entity. Every source found for "Pusa 9072" concerns mungbean, not the Bayer hybrid. Treat the two names as unresolved and do not merge the evidence.
- The release date in the input (2018-08-10) could not be verified. The table's notification rows are garbled and I could not reliably tie any S.O. number to PA 9072 -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- Parentage: not found. The table text near the PA 9072 row contains fragments such as "PSP91 x" and "PP107", but the alignment is unclear, so I did not assign them -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

STRESS TOLERANCE
- PA 9072 (pearl millet) is listed with moisture stress tolerance and lodging tolerance -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf (garbled row; medium confidence)
- A dealer page for "PROAGRO PA 9072 HYBRID BAJRA" describes tolerance to moisture stress, suitability for low-rainfall areas, and tolerance to lodging -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Pearl_millet/PROAGRO_PA_9072 (brand conflict: ProAgro, not Bayer; treat as secondary)
- PUSA-9072 (mungbean): one drought-related remark is only general to the crop, not to this variety -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/growing-of-green-gram-vigna-radiata-l-in-an-inceptisol-of-alluvial-soil/ (no variety-specific drought data found)
- No heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data found for either name.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The pearl millet table row for PA 9072 associates it with downy mildew, blast, smut and ergot resistance, and shoot-fly tolerance -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf (garbled; low-to-medium confidence)
- The ProAgro dealer page lists downy mildew resistance -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Pearl_millet/PROAGRO_PA_9072
- PUSA-9072 (mungbean) was resistant to dry root rot in a poly-house screen among 47 genotypes -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/400607358_ASSESSMENT_OF_GENOTYPES_AGAINST_DRY_ROOT_ROT_OF_BLACKGRAM_VIGNA_MUNGO_L
- PUSA-9072 (mungbean) was moderately susceptible to mungbean yellow mosaic virus in a West Bengal field study -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324106596_STUDIES_ON_HOST_RESISTANCE_OF_MUNGBEAN_AGAINST_MUNGBEAN_YELLOW_MOSAIC_VIRUS_IN_THE_AGRO-ECOLOGICAL_CONDITION_OF_LATERITIC_ZONE_OF_WEST_BENGAL
- A Pharma Innovation Journal screen of AICRP mungbean entries rated Pusa-9072 as moderately resistant to YMV (rabi 2017) -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue12/PartU/10-11-245-127.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity is 70-72 days, early, kharif-only -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Pearl_millet/PROAGRO_PA_9072 (dealer page)
- Mungbean PUSA-9072 in intercropping with okra: YMD incidence reduced by about 28% versus the control -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324106596_STUDIES_ON_HOST_RESISTANCE_OF_MUNGBEAN_AGAINST_MUNGBEAN_YELLOW_MOSAIC_VIRUS_IN_THE_AGRO-ECOLOGICAL_CONDITION_OF_LATERITIC_ZONE_OF_WEST_BENGAL
- No multi-location yield data for the Bayer pearl millet PA 9072 was found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No PA 9072-specific QTL, marker, or parentage study was found.
- The PUSA-9072 mungbean descriptor sheet lists it as a test entry for flower colour (light yellow) -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/ggreen-gram.pdf (general descriptor, not a genetic study)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Bayer Bio Science Pvt. Ltd., Hyderabad (per the AICPMIP table) -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- No breeder or scientist name was found for PA 9072.
- The hybrid-breeding review notes Bayer Bio Science, Hyderabad among private firms that developed pearl millet hybrids -- https://researchgate.net/publication/283573439_Hybrid_breeding_in_pearl_millet_past_and_present_status
- The Pusa-9072 mungbean variety is not linked to a breeder name in the sources found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Bayer Bio Science Pvt. Ltd.: manager listed as Mr. Bhoopal Reddy; address 8-1-39, Qutub Shahi Tombs Road, Toli Chowki, Hyderabad, Telangana 500008 -- https://www.tradeindia.com/bayer-bio-science-pvt-ltd-3737672/

- Bayer's Hyderabad-area sites (Toopran, Shamirpet) are seed-processing sites, not breeding contacts -- https://www.bayer.in/en-in/about-us/sites
- Official email: not found for Bayer Bio Science.
- Institute-level contact page: not found.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, or thesis specific to PA 9072 was found.
- Singh, S. et al. (2014). Hybrid breeding in pearl millet past and present status. Research report (ResearchGate PDF) -- https://researchgate.net/publication/283573439_Hybrid_breeding_in_pearl_millet_past_and_present_status (context; names Bayer among hybrid developers)
- Pharma Innovation Journal (2021). YMV screening of green gram entries, Kharif and Rabi 2017, 10(12): 1449-1452. Journal article -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue12/PartU/10-11-245-127.pdf (PUSA-9072, mungbean)
- Blackgram dry root rot screening, which includes Pusa 9072 (ResearchGate, 2025). Journal/report not confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/400607358_ASSESSMENT_OF_GENOTYPES_AGAINST_DRY_ROOT_ROT_OF_BLACKGRAM_VIGNA_MUNGO_L (PUSA-9072, mungbean)
- Mungbean YMV host resistance study, West Bengal (ResearchGate). Journal/report not confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324106596_STUDIES_ON_HOST_RESISTANCE_OF_MUNGBEAN_AGAINST_MUNGBEAN_YELLOW_MOSAIC_VIRUS_IN_THE_AGRO-ECOLOGICAL_CONDITION_OF_LATERITIC_ZONE_OF_WEST_BENGAL (PUSA-9072, mungbean)

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Bayer Bio Science, Hyderabad lists hybrid pearl millet (bajra) seed for sale -- https://www.tradeindia.com/bayer-bio-science-pvt-ltd-3737672/ (listing; no PA 9072 SKU confirmed)
- Bayer Bio Science Private Limited lists hybrid bajra seed -- https://www.indiamart.com/bayer-bio-science-private-limited/
- ProAgro PA 9072 hybrid bajra is sold through a dealer/distributor page -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Pearl_millet/PROAGRO_PA_9072
- Bayer products are sold through authorised dealers and retailers -- https://www.bayercropscience.in/en/home
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, and SAU seed-sales listings for PA 9072 or PUSA-9072: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Western Rajasthan and parts of Haryana -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Pearl_millet/PROAGRO_PA_9072 (dealer page)
- The AICPMIP table lists the Bayer Hyderabad hybrid rows against Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, and others; the row-to-variety mapping is garbled, so it is unconfirmed for PA 9072 -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

STRESS TOLERANCE --
- Pairy Mung is not described with stress-tolerance traits in any source I found. A central-release table lists a powdery mildew resistance entry on the row beside a "TM 2000-2 (Pairy Mung)" line, but the layout is garbled and does not clearly attach that trait to Pairy Mung. Resistant to Powdery Mildew -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Pairy Mung. (Searched: Pairy Mung green gram variety.)

DISEASE AND PEST --
- The same table lists Pairy Mung's originating centre as IGKV, Raipur, but gives no MYMV, Cercospora or other disease reaction for it. Resistant to Powdery Mildew -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- No evidence found for insect or nematode reaction specific to Pairy Mung.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS --
- Central-release table entry: Pairy Mung, 2010 (SVRC), originating centre IGKV Raipur, yield 12 q/ha, 65-70 days to maturity, area of adoption CG -- https://www.journalcra.com/sites/default/files/issue-pdf/45672_1.pdf
- The same review lists a second row, TM 2000-2 Pairy Mung, with 88-90 days and 10-11 q/ha. The day-count conflict between rows is unresolved.
- Multilocation rabi trial (2017-18 to 2019-20): entry IGKM 05-18-2 showed an 8.29% yield increase over the best check, Pairy Mung (833.27 kg/ha). Pairy Mung served as the check, not the entry. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333435816_Towards_Development_of_Climate_Smart_Mungbean_Challenges_and_Opportunities
- AICRP on MULLaRP overview (general mandate, no Pairy Mung data): Summer and kharif pulses Mungbean and Urdbean, plus rabi pulses, are covered by the year-round project -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/aicrp-on-mullarp-en

GENETICS AND QTL --
- No evidence found on parentage, pedigree, QTL or marker studies for Pairy Mung. Parentage field "Not specified" remains unresolved.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION --
- Originating centre: IGKV, Raipur (Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya), per the central-release table -- https://www.journalcra.com/sites/default/files/issue-pdf/45672_1.pdf
- No breeder or lead scientist name found for Pairy Mung. (Searched: Pairy Mung green gram breeder developed by institute.)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I ran four searches, but the search tool then hit its usage limit, so I could not re-query the one source that mentions Pant Mung-5. Only one result (the DPD central-release compilation) contains the variety, and I saw only its first ~600 characters. Treat the findings below as thin and unverified.

EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: The search used "Pant Mung-5" for both the CSC release name and the Seednet name. Seednet did not appear in any result, so I could not confirm the portal name or variety code A0305153. The evidence below refers to "Pant Mung-5" as written in the DPD compilation.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Not found in the captured text. The snippet truncated before the salient-features column for this entry. No evidence on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance was captured. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- Pant Mung-5 is listed in the salient-features column as resistant to mungbean yellow mosaic virus (the text reads "Res. to mungbean yellow", truncated). The full resistance wording and rating were not captured. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The compilation lists yield of 10-12 q/ha and days to maturity of 62-79 for Pant Mung-5. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
The search budget ran out after four queries, and my fifth attempt was rejected, so this digest rests on four searches. Most results were short snippets, not full pages.

Identity conflict: the evidence points to Pusa 0672 being a green gram (mungbean) variety, not chickpea. The seednet name (Pusa-0672, green gram) matches that. The chickpea-oriented searches returned nothing about Pusa 0672.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Listed as resistant to MYMV (mung bean yellow mosaic virus) in a central-release table for green gram; evidence refers to the mungbean Pusa 0672 (seednet name Pusa-0672). -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
STRESS TOLERANCE -- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Listed as moderately resistant to powdery mildew (PM) in the same table; evidence refers to the mungbean Pusa 0672. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST -- Pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Table row shows bold seed and long pods; yield and days-to-maturity values are in the table but were not legible in the snippet. Evidence refers to the mungbean Pusa 0672. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Multi-location or field-trial results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for Pusa 0672 parentage (11/395 x ML 267) or markers.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Originating institution listed as IARI, New Delhi, in the central-release table for Pusa 0672 (year 2010); evidence refers to the mungbean Pusa 0672. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder or institute contact details found. The only institutional reference is "IARI, New Delhi" (no address, email or phone). No contact page URL was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found in the searches for peer-reviewed papers, AICRP reports, KrishiKosh theses or conference papers specific to Pusa 0672.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found (no NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing retrieved).

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Table entry for Pusa 0672 shows a zone code with J&K and "MN" (likely Manipur) in the "suitable for" column, and kharif season; Tripura was not visible in the snippet. Evidence refers to the mungbean Pusa 0672. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf

RECORD CORRECTIONS
- Crop: the central-release table places Pusa 0672 under green gram/mungbean, not chickpea. The crop field in the record should be checked.
- Year of release: the table gives 2010, so "NaT" should be replaced with 2010 (from the central-release table; a CSC notification should be checked before finalising).
- Parentage and institution: not confirmed beyond IARI, New Delhi.

seednet_fields.Parentage:
AAU 34 x T44
AAU 34 is a state recommended high yielding mungbean variety from AAU jorhat for summer sowing in Assam. T 44 is a national variety from CSAUAT, Kanpur.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Moderately resistant to pod borer, aphids, leaf rolleran to 15 kg N, 35 kg P2O5 15 kg K2O. Seed rate 20-22 kg/ha.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 10-15 kg N+35kg P2O5 15 kg K2O as basal application. DAP @ 75 kg/ha may be applied in lieu of urea and SSP in non- inoculated crop.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance evidence specific to SGC 20 found in searched sources. A pod bug management recommendation (quinalphos then dimethoate sprays) was accepted for kharif 2020 for greengram, but the source is not variety-specific and does not indicate SGC 20 pest resistance. No evidence on whitefly, thrips, aphid or other pest reactions.

No evidence found for resistance to powdery mildew, anthracnose or Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV) specific to SGC 20.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance evidence specific to SGC 20 found in searched sources. A pod bug management recommendation (quinalphos then dimethoate sprays) was accepted for kharif 2020 for greengram, but the source is not variety-specific and does not indicate SGC 20 pest resistance. No evidence on whitefly, thrips, aphid or other pest reactions.

agronomic_performance.adaptation: Recommended for summer and kharif seasons in Assam. Assam Package of Practices lists suitability for all zones of Assam except BVZ. Assam recommendation for summer greengram lists SGC-20 among high-yielding varieties for Goalpara district. A source mentioning Zone-III (West Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh) for an AAU mungbean variety was not attached to SGC 20 in the digest and is excluded.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources. Duration of 65-68 days is reported in the Assam Package of Practices, which conflicts with the 35-40 day maturity in the original variety data. Protein content of 24.40% is reported in the same source. Morphological characteristics not found.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: (1) Summer phosphorus and potassium fertilization trial: SGC-20 gave net returns of Rs 31464 and a B:C ratio of 1.25, with IPM 02-3 at the top of the comparison. (2) Assam summer greengram recommendation lists SGC-20 among high-yielding varieties for Goalpara district (no yield values given in digest). No other trial results for SGC 20 were found. An AAU extension programme (2020-2023) demonstrated SGC-16 through 14 KVKs, not SGC 20.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SGC 20 (AAU SHN Mung 02) greengram: evidence digest

Search budget: 4 web_search calls used (the maximum). The Seednet portal was not searched directly, so no evidence was found under the Seednet name "SGC 20 (AAU SHN Mung 02) (Buroi)" itself. The evidence below refers to the CVRC/AAU name "SGC 20 (AAU SHN Mung 02)" unless noted. Sources call it "AAU SGC 20 (AAU-SHN Mung 02)-Buroi", so the Buroi suffix appears only in some sources. Parentage (AAU 34 x T44) was not confirmed by any search result.

STRESS TOLERANCE
SGC 20 and Sonai were recommended for kharif season endowed with Cercospora Leaf Spot (CLS) and Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV) resistance capacity. -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to SGC 20.

DISEASE AND PEST
SGC 20 is listed as resistant to CLS and YMV, with a grain yield of 12-13 q/ha, 65-68 days duration and 24.40% protein -- https://www.aau.ac.in/ (Assam Package of Practices for Kharif Crops, 2015; https://diragri.assam.gov.in/sites/default/files/swf_utility_folder/departments/diragri_medhassu_in_oid_4/portlet/level_2/11(A).2.pdf)
Pod bug management in greengram (quinalphos then dimethoate sprays) was accepted for recommendation in Kharif 2020, but the source is not variety-specific -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/117
No evidence found for resistance to powdery mildew, anthracnose, or MYMV specific to SGC 20.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Yield, duration and protein figures above -- https://diragri.assam.gov.in/sites/default/files/swf_utility_folder/departments/diragri_medhassu_in_oid_4/portlet/level_2/11(A).2.pdf
In one summer P and K fertilization trial, SGC-20 gave net returns of ₹31464 and a B:C ratio of 1.25, compared with IPM 02-3 at the top -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/126362/52260/383879
Assam recommendation for summer greengram lists SGC-20 among high-yielding varieties for the Goalpara district -- https://www.icar-crida.res.in/CP-2012/statewiseplans/Assam/ASSAM26-Goalpara-10.02.2017.pdf
Sowing window for kharif is mid-August to mid-September, with PSB inoculation at 50 g/kg seed -- https://diragri.assam.gov.in/sites/default/files/swf_utility_folder/departments/diragri_medhassu_in_oid_4/portlet/level_2/11(A).2.pdf
Basal 40 kg P2O5/ha and Rhizobium plus PSB seed inoculation are recommended for greengram at Shillongani (not variety-specific) -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/117

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for QTL, marker or genetic studies specific to SGC 20. A DST-funded marker-assisted study on synchrony in greengram at AAU Jorhat is listed, but it is not variety-specific -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/12

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Release route: the variety was identified by the SSSC meeting held on 06-05-2022 for forwarding to CVRC -- https://www.aau.ac.in/research/directorate/directorate-of-research(agri)/rars-shillongani/faculty/10/117/profile/Dr.-Hironya-Kumar-Borah/249
Notification: Greengram variety AAU SGC 20 (AAU-SHN Mung 02)-Buroi was notified by the 90th CVRC meeting held on 02-05-2023 at New Delhi. -- https://www.aau.ac.in/faculty/profile/Dr-Hironya-Kumar-Borah/249
Lead breeder (per AAU profile): Dr. Hironya Kumar Borah, Assistant Pulse Breeder background at RARS Shillongani, who developed 4 greengram, 5 blackgram and three fieldpea varieties till date -- https://www.aau.ac.in/faculty/profile/Dr-Hironya-Kumar-Borah/249
Developing institution and station: Assam Agricultural University, AAU-Zonal Research Station (RARS), Shillongani, which is located at Shillongani, about 5 km North-west of Nagaon town -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/117
Co-listed station staff: Dr. Smrita Gogoi appears on the station achievements page; her role for this variety is not stated -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/117
Breeding department: Plant Breeding & Genetics, AAU Jorhat, lists two green gram varieties developed in the department and produces breeder seed of green gram -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/12

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder: Dr. Hironya Kumar Borah (Pulse Breeder, RARS Shillongani, AAU) -- profile page only; no email or phone found -- https://www.aau.ac.in/faculty/profile/Dr-Hironya-Kumar-Borah/249
Station: AAU-Zonal Research Station, Shillongani, Nagaon-782 002, Assam, India (address from affiliation line) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/400540260_Field_Evaluation_of_BIPM_Module_for_Insect_Pest_Management_in_Green_Gram_Vigna_radiata_L_in_Assam
Dr. Smrita Gogoi: role and contact not found in search results -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/117
Institute: Assam Agricultural University, website www.aau.ac.in, headquarters Jorhat (institute-level contact only; no phone or email found in search results) -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assam_Agricultural_University
No breeder email or phone found in any search result.

Assam's input review states the state has to depend on other states for its seed requirement -- https://www.arias.in/download/AMM/Assam%20Input%20Supply%20System%20Review%20Report%20(Complete%20Report%20Revised)%2001.06.2023.pdf
A 2020-2023 AAU extension programme demonstrated greengram SGC-16 through 14 KVKs, not SGC 20 -- https://aau.ac.in/department/department_details/133

RECOMMENDED STATES
Assam: SGC 20 (AAU SHN Mung 02): Suitable for Summer & kharif, Notified in 2023. -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/117
Assam (all zones except BVZ): Suitable for all zones of Assam except BVZ -- https://diragri.assam.gov.in/sites/default/files/swf_utility_folder/departments/diragri_medhassu_in_oid_4/portlet/level_2/11(A).2.pdf
A source states that a mungbean variety from AAU was identified by the Variety Identification Committee for Zone-III (West Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh) besides Assam, but the snippet does not clearly attach this to SGC 20 -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127 (unverified for this variety)

drought.details: General stress tolerance is mentioned, but specific drought tolerance mechanisms or direct evidence for SML-832's drought tolerance is not detailed in the provided results. It is listed among varieties tolerant to stress.

heat.details: SML-832 is identified as a heat-tolerant mungbean genotype, found to be more tolerant to heat stress than SML-668. Studies have investigated its reproductive biology, leaf function, yield traits, and morphological and physio-biochemical adaptive responses under heat stress conditions (e.g., >40/25°C day/night temperatures). It is used as a reference for heat tolerance in studies.

salinity.details: SML-832 has been included in studies investigating salt stress tolerance in mungbean and its quality under salt-affected conditions on farmer's fields. This suggests a degree of tolerance or focus on its performance in such environments.

flood.details: No information regarding flood tolerance for SML-832 is available in the provided search results.

disease_resistance.summary: SML-832 is tolerant to Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV) and resistant to powdery mildew. The establishment of bacterial leaf spot of green gram was also noted in studies related to PAU.

pest_resistance.summary: SML-832 has been screened against Meloidogyne incognita (root-knot nematode), but its specific reaction (resistance/susceptibility) is not provided.

agronomic_details.yield: 11-12 quintals per acre (or hectare, unit not explicitly stated but common for such tables)
agronomic_details.stability: It is tolerant to general stress and YMV, contributing to yield stability. Its suitability for both Spring and Summer seasons indicates adaptability across different cultivation periods.
agronomic_details.adaptation: SML-832 is well-adapted for cultivation in Punjab, particularly establishing a sizeable niche for summer moong in the central districts of the state. It is suitable for both spring and summer sowing.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Leaves are large in size and dark green in colour. Pods are dark brown colour at maturity. Pod husk/cover is thick. Seed septation in pods is distinct. It has an erect plant type with medium stature and bears pods. It produces shining medium bold grains.

drought.details: The variety SML 1827 has been the subject of investigation concerning germination parameters under drought stress during the Zaid season of 2022. Studies explored the effects of zinc and boron foliar application on primed SML 1827 mung bean under drought conditions.

heat.details: While Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) has conducted genetic mapping for heat stress tolerance in mungbean, specific details or resistance levels for SML 1827 are not provided in the search results.

salinity.details: SML 1827 has been used as a genotype in studies investigating Salicylic Acid- and Ascorbic Acid–Induced Salt Tolerance in Mung bean. It is also mentioned as a cross involving a salt-tolerant parent (S100), suggesting its potential or relevance in salt tolerance breeding, with a QTL for salt tolerance having been identified in related research.

flood.details: No information regarding flood tolerance is available in the provided search results.

disease_resistance.summary: SML 1827 is resistant and tolerant to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV) / Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV), a significant threat to greengram production. It is specifically recommended for cultivation in Punjab to manage this disease.

pest_resistance.summary: No information regarding pest resistance is available in the provided search results.

agronomic_details.stability: Not specified
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for irrigated conditions, particularly recommended for summer moong cultivation in Punjab.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: SML 1827 has an erect plant type with medium stature and an upright, determinate growth habit. One source, however, contradicts this by mentioning an indeterminate growth habit for SML 1827.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has been a focus of investigations conducted during the Zaid season, including studies on drought stress and the effects of zinc and boron foliar application.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: A QTL related to salt tolerance has been identified in a cross involving SML 1827, specifically in the context of its parentage with salt-tolerant S100.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: A QTL linked to salt tolerance was studied in a cross where SML 1827 was involved, specifically between S100 (salt tolerant) x Tokyo (salt sensitive).
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: SML 1827 was developed from the cross ML 881 × RBL 35. It is a highly YMD disease resistant variety, indicating successful breeding for this trait.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST
Variety: 4216 (CSC minutes name) / S 4216 (Seednet name, listed under GREEN GRAM). Crop: maize. Institution: Rasi Seeds. Four searches were run. No result named 4216 or S 4216 as a maize variety, so most headings are empty.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searched under "4216" and "S 4216". Results were general maize release and trial pages with no mention of this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found for 4216. The only company claim is general: It focuses on producing hybrid seeds for Indian agriculture, aiming to support farmers by improving yields and addressing nutritional needs through seeds with traits that resist biotic and abiotic stresses across varied agro-climatic conditions. This is company-level and does not name 4216. -- https://www.leadiq.com/c/rasi-seeds/5a1d7cb6240000240056990e

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found for 4216. Discarded: a Rasi listing for "RASI - 4212" gives a duration of 100-110 days and medium plant height. That is a different hybrid with a similar number, so it is not attributed here. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/maize-corn-rasi-4212-18708477155.html

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No breeder name for 4216 was found. Institution-level background only: Rasi Seeds was envisioned by Dr. M.Ramasami and was initiated in the year 1973 in Attur located in Salem District, India. -- https://in.linkedin.com/company/rasi-seeds
Also: Rasi Seeds (P) Ltd. was envisioned and initiated by Mr.Ramasami in 1973 at Attur, located in Salem District, India.. Rasi Hybrid Seeds has made rapid advances from seed production and supply ventures to a commendable position in Research and Development (R&D) and transformed as Rasi Seeds (P) Ltd. in 1986. -- https://m.indiamart.com/rasi-seeds-salem
Discarded: Rajagopalan Krishnamurthy is a Rasi cotton research director; his work is on cotton, not maize 4216. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajagopalan_Krishnamurthy

Rasi Seeds corporate office: Rasi Enclave, Green Fields, 737 C Puliyakulam Road, Coimbatore - 641045, Tamil Nadu, India. Phone: +91 422 4239800; +91-422-223 3845. -- https://www.rasiseeds.com/

seednet_fields.Parentage: (TKG 19A x Kadiri 3) x TKG 19A cross was made at DGR, Junagadh and supplied to RARI Durgapura for further selection at F5 stage.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: The proposed variety has responded well to the higher than recommended doses of nitrogenous and plosphatic fertilizers. RG 559-3 gave 7219 pod yield at 125% recommended dose of fertilizer compare to 7061 kg/ha at 100% RDF.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Virginia bunch, intermediate: growth habit; leaflets, medium green and lanceolate; Pod bold, Prominently reticulated, slight curved beak, slight constricted, 2-seeded: Kernels bold with saloman colour testa.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: For peanut bud necrosis disease the proposed variety RG 559 – 3 has shown much lower incidence (12.65%) as compared to all seven zonal checks viz; Girnar 2 (23.9%), GG 21 (32.83%) HNG 69 (15.23%), Utkarsh (22.93%) CSMG 19 (23.57%), Raj munfali-1 (20.23%) and HNG 123 (16.73%).

disease_resistance.summary: Peanut bud necrosis, late leaf spot and rust: the variety shows lower incidence than zonal check varieties (AICRP-G/ICAR-IIGR text). No formal resistance rating (for example, a scale score) was found for this variety, so the level of resistance is not quantified.

pest_resistance.summary: Reported tolerance to Spodoptera litura (tobacco caterpillar), leaf miner, leafhopper and thrips, with a reported 10-15% saving in plant-protection cost (AICRP-G success stories). A secondary source lists tolerance to Spodoptera litura, leaf miner and thrips. No formal resistance rating was found, and the digest does not give the mechanism or quantitative pest scores.

agronomic_details.yield: Pod yield 3173 kg/ha, 17-29% above zonal checks (Girnar 2, GG 21, HNG 69, Utkarsh, CSMG 19, Raj Mungfali-1, HNG 123). Kernel yield 2201 kg/ha. Oil content 49% (1078 kg/ha oil). Fertilizer trial (CSC data): 7219 kg/ha pod yield at 125% recommended dose of fertilizer compared with 7061 kg/ha at 100% RDF. The two pod yield figures come from different sources and conditions and are not reconciled in the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources, beyond use as a check entry in an AMMI/GGE genotype-by-environment study (kharif 2019-2020, 43 confectionery groundnut genotypes). The digest gives no stability parameters for this variety.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for the North-Western zone (Zone I), kharif season, in Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Punjab. Developed and tested at RARI Durgapura. Response to higher-than-recommended fertilizer doses is reported. No agro-climatic or soil-type detail was found.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 125 days (medium maturity), per AICRP-G/ICAR-IIGR variety listing
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Virginia bunch type. Shelling out-turn 69%, 100-kernel weight 65 g, fodder 2500-3000 kg/ha. Listed as large-seeded (secondary source). Morphological characteristics beyond growth habit and seed traits: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Multi-location testing carried out at RARI Durgapura before release (AICRP-G success stories). (2) Pod yield 3173 kg/ha, 17-29% above seven zonal checks (AICRP-G success stories). (3) Kernel yield 2201 kg/ha (AICRP-G success stories). (4) Shelling out-turn 69%, 100-kernel weight 65 g, oil content 49% (1078 kg/ha oil), fodder 2500-3000 kg/ha (ICAR-IIGR AICRP-G listing). (5) Fertilizer response trial: 7219 kg/ha at 125% RDF versus 7061 kg/ha at 100% RDF (CSC data). (6) Used as a check entry in an AMMI/GGE study of confectionery groundnut, kharif 2019-2020, 43 genotypes (Scientific Reports). Plot-wise yields, trial sites and seasons: Not found in searched sources beyond these summaries.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY NAME CHECK
variety_name (CSC release minutes): Central Groundnut Raj Mungfali 3. Most sources use "Raj Mungfali-3 (RG 559-3)"; the Directorate of Oilseeds Development (DOD) page uses "Central Groundnut Raj Mung-3(RG-559-3)".
seednet_variety_name: Central Groundnut Raj Mungfali 3 (RG 559-3). No Seednet portal page was returned by any search, so every Seednet-related finding below is "No evidence found".
Parentage discrepancy: the input says the material reached RARI at F5. The AICRP and ICAR-IIGR sources say F6 (for example, ICAR-IIGR "Varieties Developed" and the AICRP success-stories page).

STRESS TOLERANCE
Tolerance to Spodoptera litura, leaf miner, leafhopper and thrips, with a reported 10-15% saving in plant-protection cost -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/gnut/success-stories/
Listed as tolerant to Spodoptera litura, leaf miner and thrips, rated high-yielding and large-seeded -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue10/PartF/8-10-40-464.pdf
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance -- No evidence found. The searches returned no variety-specific data on these stresses.

DISEASE AND PEST
Lower incidence of peanut bud necrosis, late leaf spot and rust than zonal check varieties -- https://agri.bot/new-high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-developed/ (same text at https://icar-iigr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/AICRP-G-Varieties.pdf)
Pest tolerance as listed under STRESS TOLERANCE above -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/gnut/success-stories/
No resistance rating (for example, a formal scale score) was found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Virginia bunch type, medium maturity of 125 days -- https://icar-iigr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/AICRP-G-Varieties.pdf
Pod yield 3173 kg/ha, 17-29% above zonal checks (Girnar 2, GG 21, HNG 69, Utkarsh, CSMG 19, Raj Mungfali-1, HNG 123) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/gnut/success-stories/
Kernel yield 2201 kg/ha -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/gnut/success-stories/
Shelling out-turn 69%, 100-kernel weight 65 g, oil content 49% (1078 kg/ha oil), fodder 2500-3000 kg/ha -- https://icar-iigr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/AICRP-G-Varieties.pdf
Multi-location testing carried out at RARI Durgapura before release -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/gnut/success-stories/
Used as a check entry in an AMMI/GGE genotype-by-environment study of confectionery groundnut (kharif 2019-2020, 43 genotypes) -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-52938-z
Trial-level primary data (plot-wise yields, sites, seasons) -- No evidence found beyond the summaries above.

GENETICS AND QTL
Pedigree: (TKG 19A x Kadiri 3) x TKG 19A, three-way cross made at ICAR-DGR Junagadh -- https://icar-iigr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/AICRP-G-Varieties.pdf
Pedigree as listed in a review table (TKG-19A x Kadiri-3, SKNAU Durgapura) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
QTL, marker or molecular studies on this variety -- No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed at RARI Durgapura from breeding material supplied by ICAR-DGR Junagadh; RARI is an AICRP-G centre under SKNAU, Jobner, Rajasthan -- https://icar-iigr.org.in/varieties-developed/ and https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/gnut/success-stories/
Released in 2016 by the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Release and Notification of Varieties (Ministry of Agriculture) -- https://icar-iigr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/AICRP-G-Varieties.pdf
Lead breeder or scientist name(s) -- No evidence found. No page named a breeder for this variety.
Breeder listed under DGR Junagadh as a selection from DGR lines released from ARS Durgapura -- https://www.icar-iigr.org.in/index.php/about-dgr/unit-division/

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact, email, phone or institute-level contact for RARI Durgapura or SKNAU was found in any result. No evidence found.
Only address found: ICAR headquarters, Krishi Bhavan, Dr. Rajendra Prasad Road, New Delhi-110001, shown in the AICRP-Groundnut page footer (ICAR-Directorate of Groundnut Research, Junagadh, is also named there, without an address) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/gnut/

PUBLICATIONS
Chilwal, A.; Rajanna, G. A. (2025). Improved production practices for sustainable groundnut cultivation: An Indian perspective. International Journal of Research in Agronomy 8(10): 394-402 -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue10/PartF/8-10-40-464.pdf (author names from https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396544544_Improved_production_practices_for_sustainable_groundnut_cultivation_An_Indian_perspective). Variety appears in a summary table only.

Authors not captured (2021 or later, review). Genetic Enhancement of Groundnut: Current Status and Future Prospects -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects. Variety in a release table.
AICRP-G, ICAR (2016 release notice; undated institutional report). Raj Mungfali-3 (RG 559-3) release notice -- https://icar-iigr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/AICRP-G-Varieties.pdf
KrishiKosh theses, conference papers, AICRP annual reports naming this variety -- No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings for this variety -- No evidence found. The one seed-related search returned generic groundnut listings (Amazon, Meesho, IndiaMart, Silkroute) for unnamed or other varieties, which were discarded. Seednet listing -- No evidence found.
