search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
DH-232 is described as tolerant to foliar diseases such as late leaf spot and rust. -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to DH-232. Searched in the first query; the pages returned did not name DH-232 with those traits.

DISEASE AND PEST
Foliar disease resistance is the only trait reported for DH-232: Dh 232 (2017), Dh 245 (2017) and Dh 256 (2019) were developed under AICRP, UAS Dharwad, and are resistant to foliar diseases. -- https://www.extensionjournal.com/uploads/archives/8-6-102-410.pdf
No evidence found for pest resistance (including PBND or pod borer) specific to DH-232. A table fragment on a ResearchGate page lists PBND and pod borer next to other rows, but the DH-232 row cannot be separated from them, so I have not attributed them. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
DH-232 (2019): yield 1480 to 2340 kg/ha. -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
This is a secondary farming blog with no trial design or source for the figure. Its 2019 date conflicts with the 2018 release year in the record and with the 2017 date in the extension paper.
No evidence found for maturity duration, multi-location trial results or agronomic packages specific to DH-232.

GENETICS AND QTL
DH-232 is a derivative of GPBD 4 developed through EMS mutagenesis, alongside GPBD 5 (Motagi et al. 2022). -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Groundnut-varieties-released-in-the-last-20-years-2000-2020-for-their-cultivation-in_tbl2_357544986
A table fragment lists Dh-232 with parentage given as GPBD 4 × TG 37A. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
The parentage is therefore recorded as unverified, since the parentage field in the record reads "Not specified" and the table text is fragmented.
No QTL or marker study specific to DH-232 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Dharwad, Karnataka. Dh 232 was developed under AICRP, UAS Dharwad. -- https://www.extensionjournal.com/uploads/archives/8-6-102-410.pdf
Station: No DH-232-specific station was found. Groundnut breeder and seed production work is linked to the Main Agricultural Research Station (MARS), Dharwad, but no source links DH-232 to MARS.
Breeder name: No evidence found. The only named breeding or scientific staff in the results (for example, the AICRP groundnut and sorghum staff listed on the UASD Dharwad project page) were not linked to DH-232, so I have not attributed them. -- https://www.manage.gov.in/nf/resextn/research/RES-UAS-DHARWAD.PDF
The lead breeder for the DH-232 line is presumably linked to the Motagi et al. (2022) citation, but no full author list was retrieved.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level only; no breeder contact was found.
University: University of Agricultural Sciences, Dharwad. The university is on the Dharwad-Belgaum road (PB-4) campus. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Agricultural_Sciences,_Dharwad
Website: https://uasd.edu (from the UASD seed farms and BSP pages). -- https://uasd.edu/en/bsp/
Vice-Chancellor: Dr. N. B. Prakash, per Wikipedia; the older Dharwad document names Dr. M.B. Chetti, so the current incumbent should be verified. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Agricultural_Sciences,_Dharwad
No official email or phone number was found for the university, the groundnut AICRP, or MARS Dharwad.

PUBLICATIONS
Motagi et al. (2022). Full title and journal not retrieved; cited as the source of DH-232 as a GPBD 4 derivative. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Groundnut-varieties-released-in-the-last-20-years-2000-2020-for-their-cultivation-in_tbl2_357544986
Authors not captured (UAS Dharwad, Department of Agricultural Extension Education) (year not shown). A study on impact of groundnut production technologies in Dharwad and Haveri districts of north Karnataka, which names Dh 232 as a foliar-disease-resistant variety. -- https://www.extensionjournal.com/uploads/archives/8-6-102-410.pdf
No AICRP/ICAR annual report, KrishiKosh thesis or peer-reviewed trial paper specifically on DH-232 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for DH-232 on Seednet, NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or private dealer listings. The UASD seed farm pages list groundnut seed production at the Konnur and MARS stations, but name TAG-24 and DH-256, not DH-232. -- https://uasd.edu/en/seed-farms/
Institute-level groundnut breeder, foundation and certified seed programmes exist at UASD. -- https://uasd.edu/en/faculty-and-staff-2/

RECOMMENDED STATES
DH-232 is particularly well-suited for cultivation in Karnataka. -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
The Seednet/CSC release-notification record did not come up in any search, so the official recommendation could not be confirmed.

NAME CHECK (variety_name "DH-232" vs seednet_variety_name "DH-232")
Both names are identical. The Seednet portal page and CSC release minutes were not found; all evidence above refers to the "DH-232" / "Dh 232" name. No evidence found for the Seednet record itself, the release notification or the CSC minute.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
DH-245 (groundnut)

STRESS TOLERANCE
Foliar disease resistance is the only stress trait reported for this variety; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence was found for DH-245. A Dh 245 description says it is resistant to fungal foliar diseases and high-oleic (>70%) with about 10% higher pod yield than the check G2-52 -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=88
DH-245 is described as notable for high oleic content and resistance to late leaf spot (LLS) and rust, and as suited to Karnataka -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
Drought tolerance, heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found for DH-245. The drought-tolerant lines Dh-256 and Dh-257 appear in a Pharma Innovation Journal paper, but those are different varieties and were discarded -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2022/vol11issue9/PartE/11-8-475-872.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to late leaf spot and rust; no insect-pest reaction was given for DH-245 -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=88
DH-245 is listed as high oleic acid (>70%) with resistance to foliar diseases, recommended for Karnataka, in an AICRP-era variety table -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue10/PartF/8-10-40-464.pdf
Stem rot, collar rot, root rot and pest reactions specific to DH-245: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Pod yield reported as 1500-2900 kg/ha, kharif season, maturity group 105-108 days (medium), on the CSC/gazette description -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=88
A different summary gives DH-245 (2019) a yield of 1480-2340 kg/ha; this conflicts with the 2018 CSC record and the 2019 date should be treated as unverified -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
Multi-location or on-station trial data for DH-245 beyond the 10% yield-over-check figure: No evidence found. The conference entry below uses DH-245 as a check at UAS Dharwad in kharif 2016 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274256904_Marker_assisted_selection_for_high_oleate_trait_in_groundnut
Field-level farmer adoption of DH-245: No evidence found. A Karnataka extension study mentions Dh 245 only in its introduction -- https://www.extensionjournal.com/uploads/archives/8-6-102-410.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Origin: DH-245 is a gamma-ray (300 Gy) induced mutant of GPBD 4, which conflicts with the "Not specified" parentage on the input record -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=88
Mutagenesis origin is also described in a genetic enhancement review, which credits EMS/induced mutagenesis of GPBD 4 with producing Dh 245 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
QTL or marker study naming DH-245 as a mapped population or result: No evidence found. The QTL for LLS and rust found in the search came from donor GPBD 4 and does not name DH-245 -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Groundnut-varieties-released-in-the-last-20-years-2000-2020-for-their-cultivation-in_tbl2_357544986

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: AICRP Groundnut, UAS Dharwad centre developed the high-oleic mutant Dh-245 -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=88
Developer citation: Nadaf et al. (2017) is cited as the source for Dh 245 in a genetic-enhancement review. Only the surname and year were found; the full paper was not retrieved -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
Lead breeder full name and station address: No evidence found beyond the surname above.
Seednet lists the institution only as "University of Agricultural Sciences", which is consistent with UAS Dharwad but does not confirm it -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=88

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder name, role, email, phone, postal address and institute contact page for DH-245: No evidence found in any search result. The search returned no UAS Dharwad or AICRP-Groundnut contact page. Do not use contacts from the Junagadh (JAU) or Directorate of Groundnut Research pages, which concern other stations -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/main-oilseeds-research-station-junagadh

PUBLICATIONS

National Conference on Biodiversity and Bioresource Utilization, Saurashtra University (conference paper). DH-245 is used as a check in a kharif 2016 trial at MARS, UAS Dharwad -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274256904_Marker_assisted_selection_for_high_oleate_trait_in_groundnut
Nadaf et al. (2017). Dh 245 development paper (full title, journal and DOI not retrieved). Cited in a review -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR annual report, or peer-reviewed DH-245 paper: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or private dealers for DH-245: No evidence found. The seed-related results were generic groundnut sellers or unrelated seed-chain studies, and were discarded -- https://www.usaseedslimited.com/groundnut.html
Seednet portal listing (variety code A0402232): not retrieved in the search results.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Karnataka (Seednet and the reference lists agree on this state) -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: The variety has responded to higher fertilizer dose of 150% RDF but has not responded to higher seed rate with closer spacing.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Medium size leaf of wide elliptic shape. Pods with moderate constriction. Kernels have tan colour.

drought.details: The CSC record states drought tolerance as indicated by less reduction in pod yield under different moisture stress conditions compared with control. Secondary sources describe DH 257 as a drought and foliar-disease tolerant rabi-summer groundnut bred for intermittent drought in northern Karnataka's dry tract. A 2018 kharif breeding study at AICRP-G MARS Dharwad names Dh-257 as drought-tolerant, and Dh-257 was used as a drought-tolerant parent in two F2 populations (Dh-256 x Dh-257; Dh-257 x TG-76). The digest contains no quantified moisture-stress trial values, so the level is rated medium rather than high.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance in the searched sources.

flood.details: No measured flood tolerance result was found. A Deccan Herald report says farmers in north Karnataka asked UAS Dharwad for a groundnut resistant to wet drought (waterlogging) and that Dh-257 was released in response, but the article does not report a measured waterlogging-tolerance result. A farmer's own estimate reports 16 q/ha on waterlogged land in a bad year versus 28 q/ha in normal seasons; this is not a trial result.

disease_resistance.summary: Described as tolerant to late leaf spot and rust (secondary technology description; 'foliar-disease tolerant' also stated). No measured scoring data, pathogen strains, or trial conditions were found in the digest. The CSC record lists disease reaction as 'Not Specified'.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No evidence was found for insect pest resistance (e.g., Spodoptera, leaf miner) specific to Dh 257.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 3000-3500 kg/ha. Technology sheet: pod yield 3200-3500 kg/ha (range differs from CSC). Rabi trial, Northern Transition Zone of Karnataka: mean pod yield 3240 kg/ha; highest 3442 kg/ha when sown at the 48th standard meteorological week.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for formal multi-environment stability analysis. The farmer-level report indicates a yield difference between normal seasons (28 q/ha) and a waterlogged bad year (16 q/ha), but this is an estimate, not a trial.
agronomic_details.adaptation: All India Zone IIIA (Karnataka and Maharashtra states) per CSC. Described as a rabi-summer groundnut for northern Karnataka's dry tract with intermittent drought. Rabi trial site: Northern Transition Zone of Karnataka. Reviews list DH-257 among cultivars widely grown in rainfed Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka (no release details given).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: CSC record: Na. Kharif 2018 evaluation at AICRP-G MARS Dharwad (parsed table, column headers partly garbled): plant height 25.20, primary branches 4.00, pod yield per plant 17.00, kernel yield 10.39, test weight 25.03, shelling 60.72. Technology sheet lists maturity as 120-125 days (medium group) and season as rabi-summer. (3) Farmer-level report (not a trial): 28 q/ha in normal seasons; 16 q/ha on waterlogged land in a bad year.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
DH 257 (groundnut) -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: The CSC minutes name ("DH 257") and the Seednet name ("DH 257") are the same string. Sources spell it "Dh 257", "Dh-257" or "DH 257". The Seednet portal itself was not returned by any search, so all evidence below is from non-Seednet pages that name Dh 257 (or Dh-257) and groundnut.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Described as a drought and foliar-disease tolerant rabi-summer groundnut, bred for intermittent drought in northern Karnataka's dry tract -- http://www.agrinnovateindia.co.in/subTechnologyDescription?id=512&Subtitle=Dh+257+(Drought+tolerant+summer+groundnut+variety)&Techtitle=University+of+Agricultural+Sciences,+Dharwad+(UASD)
Same technology sheet, same claim, also listed on the institute page -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/institutes-wise.html?id=87
Dh-257 is named as a drought-tolerant groundnut in a 2018 kharif breeding study at AICRP-G MARS Dharwad -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2022/vol11issue9/PartE/11-8-475-872.pdf
Deccan Herald reports that farmers in north Karnataka asked UAS Dharwad for a groundnut resistant to wet drought (waterlogging), and that Dh-257 was released in response; the article does not report a measured waterlogging-tolerance result for Dh-257 -- https://www.deccanherald.com/india/karnataka/rain-hit-karnataka-farmers-pin-hopes-on-new-crop-varieties-1146281.html
Flood/submergence, heat, salinity: No evidence found for these stresses specifically. The searches returned only the waterlogging context above.

DISEASE AND PEST
Tolerant to late leaf spot and rust -- http://www.agrinnovateindia.co.in/subTechnologyDescription?id=512&Subtitle=Dh+257+(Drought+tolerant+summer+groundnut+variety)&Techtitle=University+of+Agricultural+Sciences,+Dharwad+(UASD)
Insect pest resistance (e.g., Spodoptera, leaf miner): No evidence found for Dh 257 specifically.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Pod yield listed as 3200-3500 kg/ha; maturity 120-125 days (medium group); season rabi-summer -- http://www.agrinnovateindia.co.in/subTechnologyDescription?id=512&Subtitle=Dh+257+(Drought+tolerant+summer+groundnut+variety)&Techtitle=University+of+Agricultural+Sciences,+Dharwad+(UASD)
Rabi trial, Northern Transition Zone of Karnataka: mean pod yield 3240 kg/ha, at par with Dh-256; 83.56% above check TMV-2; highest yield 3442 kg/ha when sown at the 48th standard meteorological week -- https://journaloffarmsciences.in/index.php/JFM/article/view/104
Same trial: net returns of about Rs 131,489/ha (Rs 143,423/ha at the 48th MW sowing) -- https://journaloffarmsciences.in/index.php/JFM/article/view/104
Kharif 2018 evaluation at AICRP-G MARS Dharwad (parsed table, column headers partly garbled): plant height 25.20, primary branches 4.00, pod yield per plant 17.00, kernel yield 10.39, test weight 25.03, shelling 60.72 -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2022/vol11issue9/PartE/11-8-475-872.pdf
Farmer-level report: 28 q/ha in normal seasons; 16 q/ha on waterlogged land in a bad year (farmer's own estimate, not a trial) -- https://www.deccanherald.com/india/karnataka/rain-hit-karnataka-farmers-pin-hopes-on-new-crop-varieties-1146281.html
Review lists DH-257 among cultivars widely grown in rainfed Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka (no release details given) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects is not the source; use https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue10/PartF/8-10-40-464.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage ICGV 07211 x ICG 2381 -- http://www.agrinnovateindia.co.in/subTechnologyDescription?id=512&Subtitle=Dh+257+(Drought+tolerant+summer+groundnut+variety)&Techtitle=University+of+Agricultural+Sciences,+Dharwad+(UASD)
Same parentage in the release table of the Motagi et al. review chapter -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
Dh-257 used as a drought-tolerant parent in two F2 populations (Dh-256 x Dh-257; Dh-257 x TG-76) studied for variability, heritability and genetic advance -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2022/vol11issue9/PartE/11-8-475-872.pdf
QTL or marker mapping for Dh 257: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: AICRP Groundnut, UAS Dharwad centre -- http://www.agrinnovateindia.co.in/subTechnologyDescription?id=512&Subtitle=Dh+257+(Drought+tolerant+summer+groundnut+variety)&Techtitle=University+of+Agricultural+Sciences,+Dharwad+(UASD)
Deccan Herald credits the University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Dharwad -- https://www.deccanherald.com/india/karnataka/rain-hit-karnataka-farmers-pin-hopes-on-new-crop-varieties-1146281.html

Yenagi (AICRP Groundnut, MARS Dharwad) appears only as an agronomist on an unrelated on-farm page and is not linked to Dh 257, so it is discarded.

STATUS: The search budget ran out. I ran 4 searches, but the last code run hit the tool limit before I could re-read full page text. I only saw the first ~400 characters of each result, so the findings below are partial and most headings are unverified.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: GG 40 (Gujarat Groundnut 40) / seednet name GG-6 (Gujarat Groundnut-6), ICGV 16668, groundnut

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found in the retrieved excerpts. The excerpts did not cover drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence traits. Not verified.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found in the retrieved excerpts. Not verified.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The Junagadh Main Oilseeds Research Station page describes intercropping recommendations for semi-spreading groundnut in South Saurashtra (groundnut + sesame 2:1 in kharif), but does not mention GG 40 in the excerpt -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/main-oilseeds-research-station-junagadh

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found in the retrieved excerpts. The parentage (CGC-3 x FESR-5-P6-B1-B1 1-1-1-B-B) is from the input record only, not verified externally.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- GG40 (ICGV 16668) was reported as developed by a team of groundnut breeders at ICRISAT in partnership with the Main Oilseeds Research Station (MORS), Junagadh Agricultural University, Gujarat -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/new-variety-of-heart-healthy-groundnut-to-benefit-all-of-india
Individual breeder names were not seen in the retrieved text.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder names, emails, phone numbers or postal addresses were seen in the retrieved excerpts. Institute-level pages to check: Main Oilseeds Research Station, Junagadh -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/main-oilseeds-research-station-junagadh ; ICRISAT press office -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/new-variety-of-heart-healthy-groundnut-to-benefit-all-of-india (contact fields not seen in the excerpt).

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP reports, KrishiKosh theses or DOIs were identified in the retrieved excerpts. Not verified.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No GG 40 or GG-6 seed source was seen in the retrieved excerpts. The Directorate of Oilseeds Development groundnut page has a state-wise notified varieties list under the Seeds Act, but its excerpt did not show GG 40 or GG-6 -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The input record lists Rajasthan, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Telangana. I did not confirm this against the CSC minutes or any official notification. The DOD page is the right place to check the notified-variety list.

NAME DISCREPANCY -- The ICRISAT evidence refers to "GG40" with code ICGV 16668. No retrieved source linked "GG-6" on the Seednet portal to this line. Both names still need confirmation on seednet.gov.in.

Suggested next steps (outside the search budget): check the seednet.gov.in entry for GG-6, the CSC release notification for the official name and states, and the JAU/MORS and ICAR-AICRP groundnut pages for breeder names, contact details and trial data.

drought.details: The Andhra Pradesh scarce-rainfall trial credits GJG-32 with resistance to several biotic and abiotic stresses, but the trial does not isolate drought tolerance as a mechanism. In that trial GJG-32 gave about 30.3% higher pod yield than the K-6 check in rainfed red soils in 2019 and 2020. The level is medium because the evidence is yield performance under rainfed conditions, not a characterised drought mechanism. Original variety data gives adaptation to Zone-V (Southern Maharashtra and Telengana).

heat.details: No heat tolerance evidence was found from an institute source in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No salinity tolerance evidence was found from an institute source in the searched sources.

flood.details: No flood tolerance evidence was found from an institute source. A commercial seller (Reno Agrigenetics) claims waterlogging resistance for a 'Reno GJG 32' product. This is unverified marketing and is not treated as evidence of flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Tikka (late leaf spot) and rust: rated resistant in the 2020 Journal of Oilseeds Research paper, with comparable reactions to other major diseases relative to checks. A JAU variety sheet (reproduced on a commercial page, treated as secondary) records resistance to tikka and rust, with comparable reactions to collar rot and stem rot. A 2025 agronomy review table lists GJG 32 (code ICGV 03043) as tolerant of rust and collar rot. Commercial listings (Pooja Hybrid Seeds) claim resistance to leaf spot and rust but are not official sources. A ResearchGate copy of the JOR paper reports moderate resistance to late leaf spot and rust, but it carries different yield and oil figures and may describe a different entry, so it was excluded from this summary.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance is established. The JAU variety sheet (reproduced on a commercial page, treated as secondary) records thrips damage comparable to checks and low leaf defoliator damage. These are observations relative to checks, not confirmed resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: Twenty-location, five-year rainfed kharif trials (2011-2016) gave a mean pod yield of 3392 kg/ha, 15-23% above the checks GG 7, GJG 9 and TG 37A. Yield figures conflict across records: 2909 kg/ha is listed for the 2016 Zone V release, 3392 kg/ha for the 2017 Gujarat release, and a second version of the paper gives 2710 kg/ha at national level.
agronomic_details.stability: Mean performance across 20 locations over five years is reported in the 2020 JOR paper. Variation across environments beyond the mean is not found in searched sources. The Andhra Pradesh trial reports about 30.3% higher yield than K-6 in rainfed red soils in 2019 and 2020.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Original variety data gives adaptation to Zone-V of India (Southern Maharashtra and Telengana). Recorded trial evidence comes from Gujarat rainfed kharif trials and rainfed red soils in the Andhra Pradesh scarce-rainfall zone.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Recorded inconsistently across sources: 109 days (JAU station table), 112 days (JAU station table, Gujarat row), 115-124 days (fuleseeds), 110-120 days (Pooja Hybrid Seeds) and 120-125 days (Reno Agrigenetics).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Kernel traits: 100-kernel weight 35.9 g, shelling 68.5%, oil 53.9%. Plant architecture and other morphological traits are not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Twenty-location, five-year rainfed kharif trials, 2011-2016: mean pod yield 3392 kg/ha, 15-23% above GG 7, GJG 9 and TG 37A. (2) Andhra Pradesh scarce-rainfall trial, 2019 and 2020, rainfed red soils: about 30.3% higher pod yield than K-6 check, with resistance to several biotic and abiotic stresses reported and drought tolerance not isolated.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- [GJG 32, CSC name] Tolerant of tikka and rust relative to the checks, with comparable reactions to other major diseases, per the 2020 Journal of Oilseeds Research paper -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/139726
- [GJG 32] The Andhra Pradesh scarce-rainfall trial credits GJG-32 with being resistant to several biotic and abiotic stresses, though it does not isolate drought tolerance as a mechanism -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358749421_Evaluation_of_climate_resilient_varieties_of_groundnut_for_scarce_rainfall_zone_of_Andhra_Pradesh
- [GJG 32] In that same trial, GJG-32 gave about 30.3% higher pod yield than the K-6 check in rainfed red soils, 2019 and 2020 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358749421_Evaluation_of_climate_resilient_varieties_of_groundnut_for_scarce_rainfall_zone_of_Andhra_Pradesh
- [GJG 32] No heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence was found from an institute source. A commercial seller claims waterlogging resistance for a "Reno GJG 32" product; this is unverified marketing -- https://www.indiamart.com/reno-agrigenetics-gujarat/groundnut-seeds.html
- [GJG 33, Seednet name] No stress-tolerance evidence was found for the GJG 33 name in the retrieved pages. The GJG 33 entry is a separate line (ICGV 07222), so no GJG 32 stress claim should be carried over -- https://www.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/AOilseedsCrops.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- [GJG 32] Rated resistant to tikka and rust in the 2020 JOR paper -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/139726
- [GJG 32] A JAU variety sheet records resistance to tikka and rust, with comparable reactions to collar rot and stem rot. Thrips damage was comparable to checks, and leaf defoliator damage was low -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gjg-32-groundnut/ (commercial page reproducing JAU data; treat as secondary)
- [GJG 32, ICGV 03043 code] Listed as tolerant of rust and collar rot in a 2025 agronomy review table -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue10/PartF/8-10-40-464.pdf
- [GJG 32] Moderate resistance to late leaf spot and rust is reported in one abstract version (ResearchGate copy of the JOR paper), but that copy carries different yield and oil figures, so it may describe a different entry; treat with caution -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378105297_GJG_32_High_oil_and_high_yielding_Spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety_for_Gujarat
- [GJG 32] A commercial listing says it resists leaf spot and rust. This is not an official source -- https://www.poojahybridseeds.in/groundnutgjg32/pid-2214149083

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- [GJG 32] Twenty-location, five-year rainfed kharif trials (2011-2016) gave mean pod yield of 3392 kg/ha, 15-23% above the checks GG 7, GJG 9 and TG 37A -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/139726
- [GJG 32] Kernel traits: 100-kernel weight 35.9 g, shelling 68.5%, oil 53.9% -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/139726
- [GJG 32] Maturity is recorded inconsistently: 109 days (JAU station table), 112 days (JAU station table, Gujarat row), 115-124 days (fuleseeds), 110-120 days (Pooja) and 120-125 days (Reno) -- https://www.jau.in/main-oilseeds-research-station-junagadh ; https://fuleseeds.com/products/gjg-32-groundnut/
- [GJG 32] Yield figures conflict: 2909 kg/ha is listed for the 2016 Zone V release and 3392 kg/ha for the 2017 Gujarat release, and a second version of the paper gives 2710 kg/ha at national level -- https://www.jau.in/main-oilseeds-research-station-junagadh ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378105297_GJG_32_High_oil_and_high_y

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GKVK 5 (groundnut)

Name note: Both the CSC name and the Seednet name are "GKVK 5". The sources write it as "GKVK-5" or "GKVK 5". No retrieved page was from seednet.gov.in, so nothing below comes from Seednet itself.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderately resistant to rust and late leaf spot, and described as drought-tolerant (listed under the GKVK-5 entry, 2016) -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
- Caveat: this is a commercial blog, not an official trial report, and it gives no trial data or stress-scoring method.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Rust and late leaf spot ratings are given as "moderately resistant" in the same blog entry -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
- No official disease or pest scoring for GKVK 5 was found (no AICRP or ICAR data).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield given as 2500-2800 kg/ha, with season listed as Kharif and Summer (2016) -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
- A review on groundnut genetic enhancement lists GKVK 5 (UAS, GKVK) in a table fragment drawn from AICRPG annual reports 2000-01 to 2020-21. The retrieved text is too fragmentary to confirm the trial values -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
- Maturity, shelling and 100-seed weight for GKVK 5: No evidence found.
- Parentage (NIICG 11915 x NRCG 12326): No evidence found. The search returned no page confirming it.
- Release/notification minutes (CSC): No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No QTL, marker or genotyping study naming GKVK 5 was retrieved. The pages returned were about other groundnut lines or general methods.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding (formerly Agricultural Botany, established 1965) at UAS Bangalore lists GKVK-5 and GKVK 27 among groundnut varieties from the department -- http://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/department-of-genetics-and-plant-breeding/
- Developing institution: University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Bangalore, GKVK campus, Bengaluru 560065.
- Named lead breeder or scientist for GKVK 5: No evidence found. The department page names a Head and faculty, but none is linked to GKVK 5.

CONTACT DETAILS (institute-level; no breeder contact found)
- Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, GKVK, Bangalore 560 065. Head: Dr. S. Ramesh, Professor and Head. Phone: 080-2333 0153, Ext. 286, +94807 04010. Emails: ramesh_uasb@rediffmail.com, hodgpb5@gmail.com -- http://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/department-of-genetics-and-plant-breeding/
- AICRP on Seed (Crops)/NSP unit, UAS GKVK, Bengaluru-560065. Special Officer (Seeds): Phone 080-23620494; Email sosnsp@gmail.com -- https://uasgkvkseeds.org/contactus
- Seed (Crops) unit page also gives Dr. K. Madhusudan (Special Officer, Seeds): nspgkvk@uasbangalore.edu.in, sosnsp@gmail.com, madhusudangkvk@gmail.com, 080-23620494, +91-9449866925, 9972842642 -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/seed-crops-gkvk-bengaluru/
- These are general seed-unit contacts. They do not name GKVK 5.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, KrishiKosh record or conference paper naming GKVK 5 was found.
- Partial reference (authors and year not shown in the retrieved text): Genetic Enhancement of Groundnut: Current Status and Future Prospects. Source: AICRPG Annual Reports 2000-2001 to 2020-2021 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects

SEED AVAILABILITY
- A dealer listing names GKVK-5 Whole Groundnut (variety GKVK-5, minimum order 100 kg, priced at ₹89/kg) from J P Industries, Bikaner, Rajasthan. The listing is for whole groundnut, not certified seed, and no phone or address was captured -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/gkvk-5-whole-groundnut-2849634179112.html
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK and SAU seed-sales listings for GKVK 5: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Karnataka. The Directorate of Oilseeds Development's state-wise list of groundnut varieties notified under the Seed Act (2008-2019) includes GKVK-5 under Karnataka -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- The same page is the only official source found for state recommendation.
- The "recommended states" field in the variety record reads "Not specified in table." The notification source above fills that gap.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: GPBD 5 HAS SHOWN GOOD RESPONSE TO WIDER SPACING, FERTILIZER LEVELS AND GYPSUM APPLICATION. GPBD 5 HAS RECORDED 18% HIGHER POD YIELD UNDER WIDER SPACING AT DHARWAD, BETTER RESPONSE TO FERTILIZER AND SPACING AT JHARGRAN AND TO SPACING, FERTILIZER AND GYPSUM AT MOHANPUR. GPBD IS COMPARABLE TO JL 24 (NC) IN QUALITY FEATURES VIZ. HUNDRED SEED WEIGHT ( 37G: 34G), SOUND MATURE KERNEL (84%; 85%) AND OIL CONTENT (46%); 45%). PODS AND KERNELS ARE UNIVORM AND ATTRACTIVE. RESISTANCE TO FOLIAR DISEASES IMPROVES THE FORAGE QUALITY.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT : 30-CM (28 TO 32 CM), SPANISH BUNCH, ERECT PLANT TYPE WITH DARK GREEN FOLIAGE.  POSSESSES BUNCH TYPE POD BEARING AND EASE TO UPROOT. LEAF SHAPE : OBLONG, LEAF SIZE : MEDIUM, FOLOAGE COLOUR : LIGHT GREEN, GROWTH HABIT : DECUMBENT 2,  POD BEAK  : SLIGHT, POD SIZE: MEDIUM, NO. OF KERNELS/POD : 2-1, CONSTRICTION : MODERATE, RETICULATION : MODERATE, SHELLING OUT TURN (%): 68, KERNEL SIZE : SMALL, TESTA COLOUR : TAN, 100 KERNEL WEIGHT (GM) 37, OIL CONTENT (%) : 46,SMK : 84
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: GPBD 5 RECORDED LOWER INCIDENCE OF DISEASES VIZ., LATE LEAF SPOT, RUST AND PBND AS COMPARED TO JL 24 (NC). GPBD 5 HAS RECORDED 4.17 (LLS), 2.92 (RUST) AND 6.59% (PBND) AS COMPARED  5.73 (LLS), 3.59 (RUST) AND 10/57% ( PBND) BY JL 24 (NC) OVER LOCATIONS AND SEASONS. UNDER FOLIAR DISEASE EPIDEMIC, GPBD 5 HAS RECORDED LOWER INCIDENCE OF RUST (7) AND LL (3) AS COMPARED TO RUST (9) AND LLS (8) BY JL 24 (NC) AT DHARWAD.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: REACTION OF GPBD 5 TO MAJOR PESTS LIKE SPODOPTERA, THRIPS, JASSIDS AND LEAF MINER IS COMPARABLE WITH JL 24 (NC). search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GPBD 5 (groundnut)

Search limit reached: I ran 4 searches, and a fifth attempt was refused by the tool. Most headings below have little or no evidence, and several findings rest on search snippets I did not open in full. Treat the gaps as open, not as negative results.

Name note: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "GPBD 5". The DOD page writes it as "GPBD-5". All findings below refer to that same name.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The search returned a 2023 Scientific Reports paper on drought-resistant groundnut genotypes (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-38581-0), but its snippet did not confirm that GPBD 5 was among the genotypes tested.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for GPBD 5 itself. The parent GPBD 4 is described as a Spanish bunch genotype resistant to rust and late leaf spot -- https://oar.icrisat.org/1109/1/RA_00382.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The Nature 2023 paper above is a possible multi-environment trial source, but GPBD 5 inclusion is unconfirmed.

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage recorded in the input is TG 49 x GPBD 4. No independent source confirmed this in the searches. No QTL or marker study was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The lead breeder for GPBD 5 was not identified. The GPBD 4 description appears in a Nuclear/ICRISAT-hosted International Arachis Newsletter item that names the National Research Centre for Groundnut (NRCG), Junagadh, Gujarat, as the developing centre for GPBD 4 -- https://oar.icrisat.org/1109/1/RA_00382.pdf. Whether NRCG developed GPBD 5 is unverified.

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute-level only, not verified as GPBD 5 contacts:
- National Research Centre for Groundnut (NRCG), PB No. 5, Junagadh 362 001, Gujarat, India -- https://oar.icrisat.org/1109/1/RA_00382.pdf
- Breeder name, role, email and phone: not found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured (year not captured). GPBD 4: A Spanish Bunch Groundnut Genotype Resistant to Rust and Late Leaf Spot. International Arachis Newsletter -- https://oar.icrisat.org/1109/1/RA_00382.pdf (GPBD 4, not GPBD 5)
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI on GPBD 5 was confirmed.
- A ResearchGate review, "Genetic Enhancement of Groundnut: Current Status and Future Prospects" -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects, covers AICRP-G releases generally and did not confirm GPBD 5 details.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- The DOD page lists GPBD-5 among recommended groundnut varieties, notified under the Seed Act from 2008 to 2019 -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx. Seller names, NSC/SSC/KVK stock and dealer listings were not found. The Seednet portal was not returned by any search.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The input record lists Jharkhand and Manipur. The DOD page includes GPBD-5 in a state-wise notification table, but the snippet did not show which state rows included it, so the input record is not confirmed. Source: https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx

YEAR OF RELEASE -- Not found. The input value "NaT" is unresolved.

MATURITY, YIELD -- No evidence found.

Open items for a follow-up session: (1) search Seednet and CSC minutes for GPBD 5 release year and notification state; (2) identify the breeding station and lead scientist (likely NRCG Junagadh, unverified); (3) search KrishiKosh and AICRP-G annual reports for GPBD 5 yield and stress data; (4) check seed suppliers in Jharkhand and Manipur.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: "RARS-T-2 Groundnut" (CSC name) returned no evidence in any search. The Seednet name "GUJARAT GROUNDNUT-2" matches the Junagadh GG-2 line, and all findings below refer to GG-2 unless stated otherwise. Parentage (J-11 x EC-16659) and the 2010 release year are from the record you supplied and were not verified. The record's "Not specified" for recommended states was not resolved.

Search note: I ran four queries in one parallel batch. The tool reported a remaining-call count after each, so I may have exceeded your 3-4 query limit. I did not run further searches.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for GG-2 drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. Searches returned only tolerance data for other varieties (Dharani, Narayani, Pratap Mungphali 1), which I have excluded. -- No GG-2-specific source found

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for GG-2 disease or pest reaction. -- No GG-2-specific source found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
GG-2 breeder seed output from the Main Oilseeds Research Station, Junagadh, is listed by year: 106.55 q (2015-16), 57.60 q (2016-17), 64.80 q (2017-18), 64.70 q (2018-19), 43.20 q (2019-20), 15.90 q (2020-21), 48.30 q (2021-22), 24.00 q (2022-23), 33.30 q (2023-24). This is a seed-production record, not a yield trial. -- https://www.jau.in/main-oilseeds-research-station-junagadh ; http://www.jau.in/index.php/component/content/article/2-init-content/research/44-res-mainoilseed
No GG-2 multi-location or on-farm yield trial found. -- No GG-2-specific source found

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for GG-2 genetics, QTL, marker studies, or confirmation of the J-11 x EC-16659 parentage. -- No GG-2-specific source found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution on the Seednet record: Research Scientist (Oilseeds), Gujarat Agricultural University, Junagadh. Current developer appears to be the Main Oilseeds Research Station (Groundnut), Junagadh Agricultural University, which was established under Gujarat Act No. 5 of 2004 and runs the AICRP Groundnut centre (since 1968). Evidence therefore suggests the Seednet institution name is outdated. -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/main-oilseeds-research-station-junagadh
Named unit head in an older station page: Dr. R. B. Madariya, Research Scientist (Groundnut), Ph.D. (Genetics & Plant Breeding). -- http://www.jau.in/index.php/component/content/article/2-init-content/research/44-res-mainoilseed
A 2025 news item names Dr R Madariya as Head of Main Oilseeds Station and Dr Sapra as a groundnut breeding scientist at the station. -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/new-high-oleic-acid-groundnut-variety-with-high-yield-potential-released-in-gujarat
Lead breeder for GG-2 specifically: not identified in evidence.

CONTACT DETAILS
Dr. R. B. Madariya, Research Scientist (Groundnut) and station unit head (older listing). Office: (0285) 2672080-90, PBX-325; (0285) 2670205. Mobile: not listed. Email: not found. -- http://www.jau.in/index.php/component/content/article/2-init-content/research/44-res-mainoilseed
Institute address (Junagadh Agricultural University, Junagadh-362 001, Gujarat), taken from a JAU variety-release document for the same station. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/AOilseedsCrops.pdf
Station contact page: https://www.jau.in/main-oilseeds-research-station-junagadh (no email or phone captured from this page).

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found for peer-reviewed papers, AICRP reports, theses or conference papers on GG-2 or RARS-T-2. The JAU variety-release compilation and release-year records are the only institutional documents found, and they are not publications. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Variety-13-years.pdf (contains 2004-05 release data for other JAU varieties; GG-2 appears only as a check)

SEED AVAILABILITY
Gujarat State Seeds Corporation (GURABIN) lists GG-2(F) in its kharif groundnut demand table, with sowing window and price per 30 kg. Price and sowing windows are on the page. -- http://www.gurabini.com/cropDetails.aspx?id=18
Private sellers: Swaraj Seeds Company Pvt. Ltd. (Chhatral, Gandhinagar) lists "Groundnut Seeds Notified Variety GG 2" as in stock. -- https://swarajseedscompany.4bz.in/products/groundnut-seeds-notified-variety-gg-2.html
Akshay Seed sells GG-2 seed. -- https://www.akshayseed.com/products/groundnut-seed-gg-2/ (cited from https://www.akshayseed.com/best-groundnut-varieties-for-gujarat/)
Apex Exports (Mahuva) lists "Groundnut Seed G-2" at 330 INR, but the listing is ambiguous and may not be GG-2. -- https://www.tradeindia.com/products/groundnut-seed-g-2-3666326.html
No NSC or KVK listing confirmed.

RECOMMENDED STATES
The Seednet record gives none. The DAC/DOD state-wise list (2008-2019) for Gujarat does not include GG-2 in the names shown. The list does include other Gujarat varieties. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
GG-2 is still sold as a Gujarat seed in 2025-26, so the state is likely Gujarat, but this is inference, not a notification record.

General information on groundnut suggests some varieties may mitigate drought stress (uou.ac.in/sites/default/files/slm/MSCBOT-603.pdf) and some research is on groundnut response to water deficit (medplants.blogspot.com/2015/04/arachis-hypogaea-groundnut-peanut.html).

heat.details: Specific heat tolerance for Gujarat Groundnut HPS 2 is not found in the provided search results.

salinity.details: Specific salinity tolerance for Gujarat Groundnut HPS 2 is not specified in the provided search results. General information mentions varieties tolerant to abiotic stresses including salinity are released (icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf) and research on salt stress tolerance in transgenic peanut exists (medplants.blogspot.com/2015/04/arachis-hypogaea-groundnut-peanut.html).

flood.details: Specific flood tolerance for Gujarat Groundnut HPS 2 is not specified in the provided search results. General information mentions varieties tolerant to abiotic stresses including flood and waterlogging are released (icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf). However, it is also noted that the groundnut crop generally does not tolerate waterlogging (uou.ac.in/sites/default/files/slm/MSCBOT-603.pdf).

disease_resistance.summary: Specific disease resistance for Gujarat Groundnut HPS 2 is not found in the provided search results. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The AAU profile for Gujarat Groundnut 34 (GG 34) gives only summer-season suitability and no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-groundnut-34
No evidence found for GG 34 disease or pest resistance under this heading. Results for GG HPS 2, GG 39 and GJG-HPS-1 were other varieties and were discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for GG 34. Retrieved resistance statements (stem rot, collar rot, rust, leaf spot) belong to Gujarat Groundnut HPS 2, Gujarat Groundnut 39 or other varieties. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx ; https://pressroom.icrisat.org/new-high-oleic-acid-groundnut-variety-with-high-yield-potential-released-in-gujarat

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
GG 34 is a Spanish bunch type with rose-red kernels, bold seed and high oil, with 100-kernel weight of 50.89 g. -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-groundnut-34
GG 34 has about 52.82% oil and a medium maturity of 117–125 days. -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-groundnut-34
In AAU testing, GG 34 averaged 3715 kg/ha pod yield, 12.14% above TG-26 (3353 kg/ha) and 21.69% above GJG 31 (3053 kg/ha). -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-groundnut-34
Release year discrepancy: the AAU profile and the AAU variety-release list give 2018 (49th State Seed Sub-Committee meeting), not the 2019-06-01 year in the input record. -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-groundnut-34 ; https://aau.in/variety_released
Multi-location trial data beyond the AAU summary: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for GG 34 QTL, marker or genomic studies.
Parentage discrepancy: the cross J-11 x EC-16659 is recorded in the ICAR-DGR compendium for GG-2 (Gujarat Groundnut-2, released 1983, notified 1985), not for GG 34. The GG 34 parentage in the input record is therefore unverified. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR_Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Anand Agricultural University (AAU), with testing at the Regional Research Station (RRS), Anand. -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-groundnut-34
AAU's variety list places Gujarat Groundnut 34 in its 2018 release group. -- https://aau.in/variety_released
Lead breeder name: No evidence found for GG 34. A breeder named Dr Jagadeesha appears in an AAU news item as having developed 25 varieties, but that item does not link him to GG 34, so it was not attributed. -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found for GG 34.
Institute-level: Anand Agricultural University, Anand, Gujarat-388 110 (address as given on an AAU Department of Agricultural Meteorology paper; not a variety-specific contact). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/263929833_Impact_of_projected_climate_change_on_groundnut_in_Gujarat
Institute website: aau.in (contact page not retrieved; no phone or email for AAU found). -- https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-29/
The ICAR-DGR phone and fax numbers in the compendium belong to a different institute and were not used.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found for a research paper, thesis, AICRP report or conference paper on GG 34.
Passing mention only (not a variety study): Bhikadiya U. and Lad Y. (year not shown in retrieved text). Market Potential of Selected Agricultural Products and Problems Identification of Groundnut Cultivation in Bhankhokhari Market, Devbhoomi Dwarka District, Gujarat. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371758961_Market_Potential_of_Selected_Agricultural_Products_and_Problems_Identification_of_Groundnut_Cultivation_in_Bhankhokhari_Market_of_Devbhoomi_Dwarka_District_Gujarat_India

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

NAME NOTE: No retrieved page uses the CSC name "Gujarat Groundnut-24" or the 2025 release. The only related record is "Gujarat Groundnut-2" (GG-2), a JAU groundnut variety released in 1986 with parentage J-11 x EC-16659. Every finding below refers to GG-2 unless stated otherwise. No page confirms that GG-2 is the same entity as the 2025 CSC/Seednet record.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in GG-2 or Gujarat Groundnut-24. A climate-impact study records a flowering-date response for GG-2 at Kesod but gives no tolerance rating -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/263929833_Impact_of_projected_climate_change_on_groundnut_in_Gujarat

DISEASE AND PEST: A germplasm table lists a GG 2 accession (Gujarat J 11 x EC 16659, Spanish bunch) with a note that it is moderately tolerant to late leaf spot (LLS); the table text is interleaved in extraction, so this pairing should be verified against the original -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/322066029_Radhamani_J_and_Singh_AK_2008_Conservation_and_Utilization_of_Genetic_Resources_of_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L_in_India_Proc_Indian_Natn_Sci_Acad_74_3131-147
Pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The JAU Main Oilseeds Research Station achievements table lists GG-2 as released in 1986 for Gujarat, with pod yield 1336 kg/ha, oil 49.6%, 98 days to maturity, and noted as early maturing and high yielding -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/main-oilseeds-research-station-junagadh
The climate-impact study records GG-2 at Kesod as having an earlier flowering response under monsoon sowing -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/263929833_Impact_of_projected_climate_change_on_groundnut_in_Gujarat
Maturity, yield and trial data for Gujarat Groundnut-24 (2025): No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL: Pedigree: the GG 2 germplasm entry gives its parentage as Gujarat J 11 x EC 16659 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/322066029_Radhamani_J_and_Singh_AK_2008_Conservation_and_Utilization_of_Genetic_Resources_of_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L_in_India_Proc_Indian_Natn_Sci_Acad_74_3131-147
QTL, marker or genomic studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Developing institution: the GG 2 entry is attributed to GAU/JAU Junagadh, Gujarat -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/

heat.basis: Counted: Seednet official statement of high-temperature tolerance; 'Evaluation of groundnut genotypes for intrinsic thermo tolerance' paper stating Greeshma proved thermo tolerant (two snippets, one document).
heat.label: Confirmed by 2+ sources

salinity.basis: No tolerance claim. Seednet only excludes saline/alkaline soils from recommended ecology; nickel-stress paper is not salinity evidence.
salinity.label: Not confirmed

flood.basis: No tolerance claim. Seednet notes waterlogging problems on clayey soils, which is a suitability caveat, not flood tolerance.
flood.label: Not confirmed

submergence.basis: No submergence evidence or official statement for Greeshma in the record.
submergence.label: Not confirmed

stress_confirmation_note: The heat level 'unknown' in the research summary conflicts with the official Seednet statement of high-temperature tolerance and the thermo-tolerance paper; the heat entry should be updated to high.

drought.details: G 2-52 is described as a gamma-ray/EMS-derived mutant of GPBD 4 with drought-tolerant performance under water stress reported in a 2022 comparison against Dh 256. Farmers in Dharwad and Haveri reported good performance in low-moisture soils. A Davanagere KVK on-farm trial reported good withstand under drought. These are secondary and farmer or on-farm reports, not controlled stress-physiology studies, and no mechanism was identified. The digest also reports CO 7 (the Seednet line, a different variety) as bred to withstand moisture stress during the critical growth period; this applies to CO 7 and is not used to rate G 2-52.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance in either G 2-52 or CO 7 in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance in either G 2-52 or CO 7 in the searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance in either G 2-52 or CO 7 in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: G 2-52: Resistant to leaf spot in the Dharwad/Haveri study; fewer leaf spot incidences reported in a Davanagere KVK on-farm trial; stem rot incidence of 4.5% in a 2021 farmer-participatory trial at Dharwad versus 8.1% for JL-24. The same Dharwad/Haveri source notes the line is usually affected by several insect pests and diseases. CO 7 (Seednet name, different line): moderately tolerant to rust and late leaf spot per TNAU; tolerance to late leaf spot and rust reported in the TNAU/ResearchGate records. No specific resistance genes identified for either line.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest-resistance scores or specific pest resistance found for G 2-52. The Dharwad/Haveri source states the line is usually affected by several insect pests and diseases, so no pest resistance is supported for G 2-52. For CO 7 (different line), the digest reports testing for resistance to major pests and diseases in Tamil Nadu farmer participatory trials, but no pest-specific results or scores were found.

agronomic_details.yield: G 2-52: 25-30 q/ha per the Dharwad/Haveri extension study; potential yield 28-30 q/ha per the Davanagere KVK table; state-reported 18.53 q/ha in the Dharwad/Haveri data against 15.71 q/ha for TMV-2. CO 7 (different line, Seednet name): rainfed 2300 kg/ha and irrigated 2806 kg/ha, which matches the input average_yield range; mean dry pod yield 2189 kg/ha, 17% and 26% above checks VRI 6 and TMV 13. The input yield range therefore corresponds to CO 7 rather than G 2-52.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability analysis was identified for either line.
agronomic_details.adaptation: G 2-52: north transitional zone of Karnataka (Dharwad and Haveri districts), with kharif sowing reported. CO 7: recommended for all groundnut-growing zones of Tamil Nadu. The CSC ground-truth adaptation_ecology record lists rainfed Chithirai pattam (April-May), Early Adipattam (June-July), Late Adipattam (Sep-Oct), and irrigated Margazhi pattam (Dec-Jan), Masippattam (Feb-March), and Early Adipattam (Jun-Jul); the digest does not confirm these seasons for G 2-52.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources. Oil content is reported for G 2-52 (49%, Davanagere KVK table) and shelling percentage (73%); no plant morphology was described.
agronomic_details.field_trials: G 2-52 trials: (1) Motagi et al. (2022) comparison reported drought-tolerant performance under water stress against Dh 256. (2) Dharwad/Haveri farmer study: duration 105-110 days, yield 25-30 q/ha, state-reported 18.53 q/ha versus 15.71 q/ha for TMV-2, good performance in low-moisture soils, and resistance to leaf spot. (3) Davanagere KVK on-farm trial: duration 110-115 days, potential yield 28-30 q/ha, shelling 73%, oil 49%, good drought withstand and fewer leaf spot incidences. (4) 2021 farmer-participatory trial (FLDs, Dharwad): stem rot incidence 4.5% versus 8.1% for JL-24. CO 7 trials (different line): mean dry pod yield 2189 kg/ha, 17% and 26% above VRI 6 and TMV 13; duration 85-90 days; rainfed 2300 kg/ha; irrigated 2806 kg/ha; oil 51%; Tamil Nadu farmer participatory trials for pest and disease resistance (results not quantified). The TNAU page lists CO 7 release as 2013, while the input 2015 release year matches G 2-52 records.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources for G 2-52 or CO 7. No SSR, SNP or marker positions were identified.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL or marker studies specific to G 2-52 or CO 7 were found. ICGV 00351, the parent line of CO 7, appears in general drought-marker and P-efficiency work, but no QTL effects for either variety were reported.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. G 2-52 was derived by EMS mutagenesis of GPBD 4. CO 7 is a cross derivative of ICGV 87290 x ICGV 87846 (ICGV 00351). No genes or pathways were identified.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Not found in searched sources. No State Seed Corporation listing was confirmed for either line.
commercial_info.kvk: Not found in searched sources as a seed-availability channel. A Davanagere KVK on-farm trial of G 2-52 is documented, but no KVK seed supply was confirmed.
commercial_info.private_dealers: Not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Variety-name check: "Groundnut" (variety_name) and "Groundnut CO7" (seednet_variety_name) do not refer to the same line. The 2015 UAS Dharwad release is G 2-52. The ICGV 87290 x ICGV 87846 parentage belongs to CO 7 (TNAU, ICGV 00351), which the Seednet name points to. The findings below are labelled by which name they support.

STRESS TOLERANCE
G 2-52: Described as a gamma-ray/EMS-derived mutant of GPBD 4, with drought-tolerant performance under water stress reported in a 2022 comparison -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Groundnut-varieties-released-in-the-last-20-years-2000-2020-for-their-cultivation-in_tbl2_357544986
G 2-52: Farmers in Dharwad and Haveri reported that it performed well in low-moisture soils -- https://www.extensionjournal.com/uploads/archives/8-6-102-410.pdf
G 2-52: A Davanagere KVK on-farm trial reported good withstand under drought and fewer leaf spot incidences -- https://iskv.in/wp-content/themes/iskv/volume-pdfs/73d2e5ceda53abd03d7a249bcf749863Journal%2011%20Supplement-247-251.pdf
CO 7 (Seednet name): Bred to withstand moisture stress during the critical growth period for drought-prone farming -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321244117_A_new_high_yielding_spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety
CO 7: Tolerance reported to late leaf spot and rust -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321244231_New_Groundnut_variety_TNAU_CO_7
No evidence found for heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in either line.

DISEASE AND PEST
G 2-52: Reported as usually affected by several insect pests and diseases, and as resistant to leaf spot in the Dharwad/Haveri study -- https://www.extensionjournal.com/uploads/archives/8-6-102-410.pdf
G 2-52: Stem rot incidence was 4.5% in a 2021 farmer-participatory trial at Dharwad, against 8.1% for JL-24 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380765335_Evaluation_of_High_Yielding_Groundnut_Varieties_for_North_Transitional_Zone_of_Karnataka_State_India
CO 7: Moderately tolerant to rust and late leaf spot -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20co7.html
CO 7: Tested for resistance to major pests and diseases in Tamil Nadu farmer participatory trials -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321244231_New_Groundnut_variety_TNAU_CO_7
No evidence found for specific resistance genes or pest-resistance scores for either line.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
G 2-52: Duration 105-110 days with yield 25-30 q/ha -- https://www.extensionjournal.com/uploads/archives/8-6-102-410.pdf
G 2-52: Duration 110-115 days, potential yield 28-30 q/ha, shelling 73%, oil 49% in a KVK table -- https://iskv.in/wp-content/themes/iskv/volume-pdfs/73d2e5ceda53abd03d7a249bcf749863Journal%2011%20Supplement-247-251.pdf
G 2-52: Kharif sowing, notified 2015 (S.O. 2680(E)/01.10.2015) -- https://researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
G 2-52: Dharwad/Haveri data showed a state-reported yield of 18.53 q/ha against 15.71 q/ha for TMV-2 -- https://www.extensionjournal.com/uploads/archives/8-6-102-410.pdf
CO 7: Mean dry pod yield 2189 kg/ha, 17% and 26% above checks VRI 6 and TMV 13 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321244117_A_new_high_yielding_spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety
CO 7: Duration 85-90 days, rainfed 2300 kg/ha, irrigated 2806 kg/ha, oil 51%, Spanish bunch, release year listed as 2013 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20co7.html
Note: the input record's 2015 release year matches G 2-52 and CO 7 notification records; the TNAU page lists CO 7 as 2013.

GENETICS AND QTL
G 2-52: Derived by EMS mutagenesis of GPBD 4 (Nadaf et al. 2009) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
CO 7: Cross derivative of ICGV 87290 x ICGV 87846 (ICGV 00351) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321244117_A_new_high_yielding_spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety
No QTL or marker studies specific to G 2-52 or CO 7 were found. ICGV 00351 appears in general drought-marker and P-efficiency work -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-022-24016-9

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
G 2-52: Developed by UAS Dharwad -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
G 2-52: Breeder seed is produced at UAS Dharwad, which supplies GPBD 4 and related varieties to Karnataka and other states -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Groundnut-varieties-released-in-the-last-20-years-2000-2020-for-their-cultivation-in_tbl2_357544986
G 2-52: Named breeders are not identified in any retrieved source; Nadaf and Motagi are cited as authors of the EMS-derived lines and appear on a UAS Dharwad groundnut popularization paper -- https://www.osti.gov/etdeweb/biblio/21265449
CO 7: Developed and released by TNAU (Tamil Nadu), from ICGV 00351 developed at ICRISAT Patancheru -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321244231_New_Groundnut_variety_TNAU_CO_7
CO 7: Co-authors include P. Vindhiyavarman and S. N. Nigam -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321244231_New_Groundnut_variety_TNAU_CO_7
Named lead breeder for CO 7 is not stated in the retrieved text.

CONTACT DETAILS
UAS Dharwad seed unit (for G 2-52 seed and breeder-seed queries): Seed unit, University of Agricultural Sciences, Dharwad, Ettinagudda Campus, Dharwad; phone 0836-2441884; email soseed@uasd.in -- https://uasd.edu/bsp/
UAS Dharwad Special Officer (Seeds) is listed as the seed-unit head -- https://uasd.edu/bsp/
TNAU oilseeds contact (for CO 7 correspondence, as printed on the paper): oilseeds@tnau.ac.in -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321244231_New_Groundnut_variety_TNAU_CO_7
No breeder-level names, personal emails or phone numbers were found for either variety.

PUBLICATIONS
Madhusudan K, Nadaf H L, Hanchinal R R, Krishna Naik L, Motagi B N, Biradar Patil N K, Hunje R, D'Souza S F, Badigannavar A M (2009). Popularization of groundnut varieties through BARC-UASD collaboration. Conference paper, OSTI record -- https://www.osti.gov/etdeweb/biblio/21265449
Vindhiyavarman P, Nigam S N et al. (2014). A new high yielding Spanish bunch groundnut variety (ICGV 00351 / CO 7). Journal not confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321244117_A_new_high_yielding_spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety
Vindhiyavarman P, Nigam S N et al. (2014). New Groundnut variety TNAU CO 7. Journal not confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321244231_New_Groundnut_variety_TNAU_CO_7
Authors not captured (2021-22). Study on impact of groundnut production technologies in Dharwad and Haveri districts (G2-52 spread). Extension journal -- https://www.extensionjournal.com/uploads/archives/8-6-102-410.pdf
Authors not captured (2021). Evaluation of high yielding groundnut varieties for north transitional zone of Karnataka (FLDs, Dharwad). Study record -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380765335_Evaluation_of_High_Yielding_Groundnut_Varieties_for_North_Transitional_Zone_of_Karnataka_State_India
Nadaf et al. (2009). EMS-derived G 2-52 development paper, cited in a review. Full reference not retrieved -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
Motagi et al. (2022). Dh 256 drought comparison against G 2-52, cited in a review. Full reference not retrieved -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Groundnut-varieties-released-in-the-last-20-years-2000-2020-for-their-cultivation-in_tbl2_357544986
No AICRP annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, or DOI-level record for G 2-52 or CO 7 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
G 2-52: UAS Dharwad's Agricultural Research Station, Madhurakhandi, lists G2-52 among groundnut seed-production programmes -- https://uasd.edu/en/seed-farms/
G 2-52: UAS Dharwad seed unit covers groundnut seed production and sales enquiries -- https://uasd.edu/bsp/
CO 7: No current seed source (TNAU, State Seed Corporation, KVK or dealer) was confirmed. Seednet portal was not reached.
Caveat: The 2015 Karnataka recommendation of G 2-52 is supported by the Karnataka field evidence above, but no current Seednet or KSDA listing was retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES
G 2-52: Karnataka, with north Karnataka adoption in Dharwad and Haveri -- https://www.extensionjournal.com/uploads/archives/8-6-102-410.pdf
CO 7: Recommended for all groundnut-growing zones of Tamil Nadu -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321244117_A_new_high_yielding_spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety
CO 7: Also listed as suitable for Tamil Nadu and nearby states in TNAU Virudhachalam records -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/

seednet_candidate_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Rainfed Chithirai pattam (April-May) Early Adipattam (June-July) Lte Adipattam (Sep-Oct)  Irrigated Margazhi pattam (Dec-Jan) Masippattam (Feb-March) Early Adipattam (Jun-Jul)
seednet_candidate_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Plant height (cm) - 25-45 cm, - Distinguishing morphological characters  i)	Primaries (No.) - 4-5, - Secondaries (No.) - Present, - Leaves - Green colour medium sized leaves, basal leaves obovate upper leaves elliptic – oblong., -	Pods - One to two seeded. Usually two seeded, medium sized pods, less prominent beak, less constriction and moderate pod reticulation., - Kernel colour - Ten testa, - 100-Kernel weight (g) - 35.0 to 44.0, - Oil content (%) - 50.5 to 51.0
seednet_candidate_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases:
Late leaf spot: The groundnut culture ICGV 00351 recorded moderate resistance reaction to late spot 3.5 score) while the check varieties VRI Gn 6 and TMV 2 recorded moderately resistant and susceptible reaction (4.0 and 7.0 score respectively) under field condition
Rust: the culture ICGV  00351 resistance reaction to rust incidence (4.5 score) while the check varieties VRI Gn 6 and TMV 7 recorded tolerance and susceptible reaction (5.0 and 8.0 score respectively) under field conditions
seednet_candidate_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: The groundnut culture ICGV 00351 recorded less pest incidence (Jassids, Thrips and leaf miner) than the check varieties namely VRI Gn 6 and VRI 2

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: Rajasthan Agril. University, Agril. Research Sub Station, Hanumangarh (Rajasthan).
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for release and cultivation in the State of Rajasthan and Punjab under irrigated timely and late sown condition of KHarif. Late Maturity - 131 days. Yield Pod 28 Q/ha.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: - Peg pigmentation: Present, - No of orimary Branches & Secondary Branches: 5-7 and 8-10, - Flower colour: Standard petal colour - yellow, Crescent colour - Orange, WIng petal colour - Garnet, - Pod beak: Present, - Pod size: 32.0 mm pod length & 13.2 mm breadth (Av of 10 pods), - Kernel nature: Medium bold, - Seed/pod: 2 kernel/pod ; 100 kernel wt. : 51 g.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: a) Plant height: 25-30 cm, b) Distinguishing morphological Characters: - Growth habit: Semi spreading- Decumbent-3 (Virginia Bunch), - Leaf shape: Elliptic, - Leaf size: Medium, - Foliage colour: Light green, - Branching pattern: Alternate, - Stem pigmentation: Absent
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: HNG-69 showed tolerance to collaborate rot, stem rot and early leaf spot (ELS) diseases under natural conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: Collar rot, stem rot and early leaf spot (ELS): described as tolerant in a secondary advisory source, not a trial report (agrifarming.in). Resistance to pod-borne or foliar diseases is not documented for HNG-69; the AICRP data cited shows only a check-variety comparison that does not state HNG-69's own reaction. Collar and root rot control at RAU uses Trichoderma seed and soil treatment for the crop generally, not specific to HNG-69, so it is not evidence of varietal resistance. Separately, HNG-69 is listed among iron chlorosis tolerant cultivars identified by ICAR-IIGR; this is a nutritional disorder, not a disease. Groundnut-wide resistance references are not HNG-69-specific.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The original record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: Original record: pod yield 28 Q/ha (2800 kg/ha). RAU source: claimed yield 2800-3000 kg/ha. Advisory source: high-yield entry with 2800 kg/ha potential. AICRP zonal trial mean for HNG 69 as check: 2696 kg/ha. DGR zone check figure for HNG 69 (kharif zone-1 comparison): 2646 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for stability across environments. The original record states 'At par with checks.' Cluster analysis (Legume Research) places HNG-69 among low-yielding cultivars.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for release and cultivation in Rajasthan and Punjab under irrigated, timely and late-sown kharif conditions (original record). Advisory source lists Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and northern Rajasthan. Release details reference the central zone kharif and Punjab, northern Rajasthan and UP. Sowing guidance lists HNG 69 for north-west Rajasthan and Punjab/UP sowing windows. Package of practices lists HNG 69 among kharif recommendations at 30 x 10 cm spacing.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: - Peg pigmentation: Present, - No of orimary Branches & Secondary Branches: 5-7 and 8-10, - Flower colour: Standard petal colour - yellow, Crescent colour - Orange, WIng petal colour - Garnet, - Pod beak: Present, - Pod size: 32.0 mm pod length & 13.2 mm breadth (Av of 10 pods), - Kernel nature: Medium bold, - Seed/pod: 2 kernel/pod ; 100 kernel wt. : 51 g. Additional (RAU source): Virginia bunch type, two-seeded pods, tan kernels, 100-kernel weight about 50 g. Note: the isasat source classifies HNG 69 as a Virginia runner type, which conflicts with the bunch-type description.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) RAU/ARS Hanumangarh release information: claimed yield 2800-3000 kg/ha. (2) Advisory high-yield listing: 2800 kg/ha potential in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and northern Rajasthan. (3) AICRP-G zonal trial: HNG 69 used as check, mean 2696 kg/ha, 100-kernel weight 59 g (this 100-kernel weight differs from the 51 g in the original record and the about 50 g RAU figure). (4) DGR zone kharif zone-1 comparison: check figure 2646 kg/ha. (5) Cluster analysis (Legume Research): HNG-69 classed among low-yielding cultivars. No trial-level statistics, locations or years were given in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
HNG-69 (groundnut)
Variety name (CSC minutes) and Seednet name: both evidence sets use "HNG-69" (DoD writes "HNG 69"). Seednet code A0402179.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as tolerant of collar rot, stem rot and ELS, with suitability for kharif; this is a secondary advisory source, not a trial report -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
- Listed among iron chlorosis tolerant cultivars identified by ICAR-IIGR -- https://www.icar-iigr.org.in/index.php/research-achievements/
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistance to pod-borne or foliar disease not documented for HNG-69 in the results; only the check-variety comparison in AICRP data, which does not state HNG-69's own reaction -- https://icar-iigr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/AICRP-G-Varieties.pdf
- Collar and root rot control recommendations at RAU use Trichoderma seed and soil treatment for the crop generally, not HNG-69 specifically -- https://raubikaner.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ARS-at-a-glance-17.08.pdf
- Groundnut-wide disease resistance reference, not HNG-69-specific -- No evidence found beyond the above.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Released 29 January 2010 as a Virginia bunch type; 100-kernel weight about 50 g, two-seeded pods, tan kernels; claimed yield 2800-3000 kg/ha -- https://raubikaner.org/arsshanumangarh/
- Listed as a high-yield entry (2800 kg/ha potential) for Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and northern Rajasthan -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
- AICRP zonal trial mean for HNG 69 as check: 2696 kg/ha; 100-kernel weight 59 g -- https://icar-iigr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/AICRP-G-Varieties.pdf
- DGR zone check figure for HNG 69: 2646 kg/ha (kharif zone-1 comparison) -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=796
- Sowing guidance lists HNG 69 under Virginia runner types for north-west Rajasthan and Punjab/UP sowing windows -- https://www.isasat.org/Volume-1,issue-2,july-2017/AARJ_1_2_8_Waghmode.pdf
- Package of practices lists HNG 69 among kharif recommendations (30 x 10 cm spacing) -- https://icar-iigr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/Package-of-Practices.pdf
- Maturity days, oil content and aflatoxin reaction for HNG-69: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage CSMG-84-1 x PG-1 with release details (RAU Hanumangarh, 29.01.2010, central zone kharif; Punjab, northern Rajasthan, UP) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
- QTL or marker studies on HNG-69: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: Rajasthan Agricultural University (RAU), Agricultural Research Station (ARS) Hanumangarh; the input's "Not explicitly stated" is resolved by this source -- https://raubikaner.org/arsshanumangarh/
- The AICRP on Groundnut was at Hanumangarh from 1987 and later shifted to ARS Bikaner; Hanumangarh still produces breeder, nucleus and TFL seed -- https://raubikaner.org/arsshanumangarh/
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute page for ARS Hanumangarh (RAU): https://raubikaner.org/arsshanumangarh/
- ARS at-a-glance document (RAU Bikaner): https://raubikaner.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ARS-at-a-glance-17.08.pdf
- Official email, phone and postal address of ARS Hanumangarh: No evidence found in the retrieved pages.
- Breeder name, role, email or phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Parent-line and release table: Genetic Enhancement of Groundnut: Current Status and Future Prospects (year not shown in retrieved text; authors not shown). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
- Cluster analysis including HNG-69 among low-yielding cultivars (authors and year not shown in retrieved text). Legume Research -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4202
- Best Management Practices for Groundnut Cultivation in India, listing HNG-69 under Rajasthan and Punjab (authors and year not shown in retrieved text). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379814988_Best_Management_Practices_for_Groundnut_Cultivation_in_India
- AICRP-G zonal variety trial report with HNG 69 check data (authors and year not shown; ICAR-IIGR). -- https://icar-iigr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/AICRP-G-Varieties.pdf
- KrishiKosh theses, peer-reviewed HNG-69 trial papers with DOI: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Official NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or RAU seed sale listing for HNG-69: No evidence found.
- Private dealer listings: No evidence found for HNG-69 (an Amazon listing for a different groundnut variety was returned and is excluded) -- https://www.amazon.in/Green-World-Groundnut-Mungfali-Researched/dp/B0C7GRWLXG
- Recommended search next: seednet.gov.in and RAU Bikaner seed sales.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- DoD list of varieties notified under the Seed Act (2008-2019) includes HNG 69 for Punjab and Rajasthan, and also Uttar Pradesh (except BKD) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Advisory source gives Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and northern Rajasthan -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
