disease_resistance.summary: Tolerance (degree not quantified in the digest) to peanut bud necrosis disease (PBND), fungal diseases (not specified), late leaf spot and rust. Tolerance to PBND, fungal diseases, late leaf spot and rust is reported for Avtar (ICGV 93468) in an Uttarakhand-related evaluation and an Indian production-practices review. Late leaf spot and rust are also listed in a table row with illegible column headings, so that row is treated as unconfirmed. No evidence found for resistance to other specific pathogens.

pest_resistance.summary: Tolerance to jassids and pod borer is reported for Avtar (ICGV 93468) in the 2025 Uttarakhand-related evaluation (degree not quantified). In a Mainpuri trial, pod borer damage of 20% to 51.85% was recorded in lower-yielding summer genotypes, with ICGV 93468 among the higher yielders; the paper gives no separate damage figure for this variety, so no variety-specific damage value is attributed. Jassids and thrips are listed in a table row for this variety, but the column headings are not legible, so that row does not confirm resistance. No evidence found for resistance to other pests.

agronomic_details.yield: 1998-1999 summer trial at the Regional Research Station, Mainpuri: about 32.62 q/ha pod yield (approximately 3.26 t/ha), among the top genotypes of 33 tested. Uttar Pradesh summer trials (1999-2000, two-year mean): 2.34 t/ha pod yield, higher than other test genotypes and the local check.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond the two multi-season or multi-location results listed under yield (Mainpuri 1998-1999; Uttar Pradesh 1999-2000 two-year mean).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Reported in Uttar Pradesh summer groundnut systems, including a Jatropha-based two-tier system where its adoption is cited as expanding summer groundnut area. Evaluated in Uttarakhand hill conditions (2022-2023), where the digest gives no result. Early maturity is reported in Uttarakhand-related evaluation work.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Early maturity is reported. No other morphological characteristics were found in the searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Summer trial, Regional Research Station, Mainpuri (CSAUA&T Kanpur), 1998-1999: about 32.62 q/ha pod yield, among the top genotypes of 33 tested. (2) Uttar Pradesh summer trials, 1999-2000 (two-year mean): 2.34 t/ha pod yield, higher than other test genotypes and the local check. (3) Seed size and quality comparison at Coimbatore (TNAU) against Chico, Gangapuri, ICGV 91114 and VRI 3: the digest names the comparison but gives no result for ICGV 93468. (4) Evaluation for growth, yield and seed quality in Uttarakhand hill conditions (2022-2023): the digest says Avtar (ICGV-93468) was included but gives no result. EVIDENCE DIGEST: JL-501 (groundnut)

Note: the search tool's quota ran out during my second pass, so the four searches below are the only evidence retrieved. Several headings are thin as a result.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found in retrieved snippets. Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance for JL-501 were not stated in the text I received.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found in retrieved snippets. No resistance data for JL-501 was retrieved.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- In a summer groundnut sowing-date and variety study, JL-501 showed higher functional leaf number, leaf area per plant, branch number and dry matter accumulation than TAG-24, and its yield-attributing traits were also reported as strong -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364385363_Effect_of_sowing_times_and_varieties_on_growth_and_yield_of_summer_groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A North Saurashtra dry-farming comparison advised growing bunch groundnut JL-501 first, ahead of TG-37A, TAG-24, and TPG-41 -- https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0005933

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The search did not return QTL or marker studies for JL-501. The parentage given in the record (selection from TAG-24) was not independently verified in retrieved text.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for the lead breeder or developing institution. The record lists the institution as "Not explicitly stated," and no retrieved text named it. A krishikosh report on groundnut genetic variability and G x E interaction lists JL-501 among released genotypes alongside TAG-24, Phule Unnati and Phule Bharati, but it does not name a breeder or station -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/9ceabcbd-a4bc-4c1c-89d0-ba38cb3ba6a6/content

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute, email, phone or address was retrieved. The institute contact page for the developing institution still needs to be located once it is identified.

PUBLICATIONS --
Researchgate study (Year not confirmed). Effect of sowing times and varieties on growth and yield of summer groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364385363_Effect_of_sowing_times_and_varieties_on_growth_and_yield_of_summer_groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L
Authors not retrieved (Year not confirmed). Groundnut genetic variability and G x E interaction studies. Krishikosh thesis/report -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/9ceabcbd-a4bc-4c1c-89d0-ba38cb3ba6a6/content
Authors not retrieved (Year not confirmed). Dry-farming bunch groundnut varietal comparison, North Saurashtra. International Journal of Agriculture Sciences -- https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0005933

SEED AVAILABILITY -- The DAC Directorate of Oilseeds Development page lists state-wise groundnut varieties notified under the Seed Act from 2008 to 2019, but the retrieved snippet did not show a JL-501 entry. Confirm on that page and on seednet.gov.in -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sale listing for JL-501 was retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The retrieved evidence supports Gujarat only, through the North Saurashtra dry-farming result above. Southern Rajasthan is not supported by anything I retrieved. The Seed Act notification list on the DOD page should be checked to confirm both states.

Open items: release year (recorded as NaT), the CSC minutes name (none differs from "JL-501" here), breeder and institution, and contact details all still need confirmation from seednet.gov.in, the ICAR/SAU release notification, or the institute site.

drought.details: Drought tolerance is reported in two sources, but neither grades it as high, medium or low. The OUAT 2022-23 release entry for the 'Dhara' variety describes it as suitable for rainfed uplands in kharif and for residual moisture in rabi. The ICRISAT/CGIAR release note says the variety tolerates drought. No mechanisms (e.g., root traits, water-use efficiency) were reported. The digest notes that the link between the 'Dhara' entry and this variety is unconfirmed. Heat, salinity, flood and submergence data were not found.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerance to foliar fungal diseases, late leaf spot and rust is reported in the CGIAR release note (the note names foliar fungal diseases generally, and late leaf spot and rust specifically). The OUAT 'Dhara' entry reports moderate resistance to leaf spot. These are described as tolerance or moderate resistance, not graded levels. Evidence is limited to these two release-level sources; no field-scored disease data were found.

pest_resistance.summary: The OUAT 'Dhara' entry reports tolerance to pod borer. No other pest reactions were found. The record field 'pest_reaction' is 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: Minikit on-farm trials (Bargarh, Bolangir, Kalahandi and Ganjam) gave a mean pod yield of 1,726 kg/ha. For the 'Dhara' entry, pod yield was 2,408 kg/ha and kernel yield 1,603 kg/ha, with 67% shelling. Yield advantage over the ruling variety Devi was 12.1% for pod and 20.7% for kernel. The record field 'average_yield' is given as 10,267 kg/ha, which conflicts with the trial figures above and appears to be a unit error. It is not used as a reliable value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for residual-moisture post-rainy cultivation, irrigated summer cultivation and rainfed uplands in kharif (CGIAR note). The 'Dhara' entry describes suitability for rainfed uplands in kharif and residual moisture in rabi. Recommended-state evidence refers to Odisha only.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Post-rainy season: 125-131 days (CGIAR release note). First picking at 100-117 days (OUAT 'Dhara' entry). Record field 'maturity_days' is 'Not specified'.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Haulm quality is described as superior (CGIAR release note). Quality traits reported: shelling outturn 72%, kernel oil 50%, 100-kernel weight 46 g, medium-bold kernels (GLDC source). The 'Dhara' entry reports 100-kernel weight 37 g. The two 100-kernel weight values differ and cannot be reconciled from the digest. Record fields 'morphological_characteristics' and 'agronomic_features' are 'Not specified'.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Minikit on-farm trials at Bargarh, Bolangir, Kalahandi and Ganjam: mean pod yield 1,726 kg/ha. (2) Comparison with the ruling variety Devi: pod yield advantage 12.1% and kernel yield advantage 20.7%. (3) OUAT 'Dhara' entry: pod yield 2,408 kg/ha, kernel yield 1,603 kg/ha, shelling 67%, 100-kernel weight 37 g, first picking at 100-117 days. No trial locations, years, replication or statistical details were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: OUAT Kalinga Groundnut-1 / KALINGA GROUNDNUT 101

NAME NOTE: The CSC record name is "OUAT Kalinga Groundnut-1". The Seednet name is "KALINGA GROUNDNUT 101". The evidence below mostly refers to "Kalinga Groundnut-101 (ICGV 02266)", released at the Odisha SVRC on 9 Aug 2021. The OUAT 2022-23 release list names "OUAT Kalinga Groundnut 1 (Dhara)". I could not confirm that "Dhara" and "Kalinga Groundnut-101" are the same entry. The 2023-05-02 release date in the record does not match the 2021 SVRC date found in the sources.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Drought tolerance is reported for the variety, which is suitable for rainfed uplands in kharif and for residual moisture in rabi, per the Dhara entry -- https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf
The ICRISAT/CGIAR release note says it tolerates drought, foliar fungal diseases, late leaf spot and rust -- https://www.cgiar.org/news-events/news/groundnut-variety-tolerant-to-drought-and-foliar-fungal-disease-with-superior-haulm-quality-released-in-odisha-india/
No heat, salinity, flood or submergence data were found. -- No evidence found for those stresses.

DISEASE AND PEST
The Dhara entry reports tolerance to pod borer and moderate resistance to leaf spot -- https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf
Tolerance to late leaf spot and rust is listed in the CGIAR release note -- https://www.cgiar.org/news-events/news/groundnut-variety-tolerant-to-drought-and-foliar-fungal-disease-with-superior-haulm-quality-released-in-odisha-india/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity: 125-131 days in post-rainy season -- https://www.cgiar.org/news-events/news/groundnut-variety-tolerant-to-drought-and-foliar-fungal-disease-with-superior-haulm-quality-released-in-odisha-india/
Maturity: first picking at 100-117 days for the Dhara entry -- https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf
Yield advantage over the ruling variety Devi: 12.1% pod and 20.7% kernel -- https://www.cgiar.org/news-events/news/groundnut-variety-tolerant-to-drought-and-foliar-fungal-disease-with-superior-haulm-quality-released-in-odisha-india/
Minikit on-farm trials at Bargarh, Bolangir, Kalahandi and Ganjam gave a mean pod yield of 1,726 kg/ha -- https://www.cgiar.org/news-events/news/groundnut-variety-tolerant-to-drought-and-foliar-fungal-disease-with-superior-haulm-quality-released-in-odisha-india/
Dhara entry pod yield 2408 kg/ha, kernel yield 1603 kg/ha, shelling 67%, 100-kernel weight 37 g. Its "average yield" of 10267 kg/ha conflicts with these figures and looks like a unit error -- https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf
Quality: shelling outturn 72%, kernel oil 50%, 100-kernel weight 46 g, medium-bold kernels -- http://gldc.cgiar.org/groundnut-variety-tolerant-to-drought-and-foliar-fungal-disease-with-superior-haulm-quality-released-in-odisha-india/
Haulm quality is described as superior -- https://www.cgiar.org/news-events/news/groundnut-variety-tolerant-to-drought-and-foliar-fungal-disease-with-superior-haulm-quality-released-in-odisha-india/

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage is not specified in the record, and no pedigree was found in the search results. The ICRISAT code ICGV 02266 is noted and the variety is described as ICRISAT-origin -- https://www.cgiar.org/news-events/news/groundnut-variety-tolerant-to-drought-and-foliar-fungal-disease-with-superior-haulm-quality-released-in-odisha-india/
QTL, marker or genomic studies specific to this variety: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Released by OUAT at the State Varietal Release Committee, Bhubaneswar, 9 Aug 2021 -- https://www.cgiar.org/news-events/news/groundnut-variety-tolerant-to-drought-and-foliar-fungal-disease-with-superior-haulm-quality-released-in-odisha-india/
Project partners were OUAT, ILRI and ICRISAT, funded by RKVY (Odisha), OFID, Tropical Legumes II and CRP-GLDC -- http://gldc.cgiar.org/groundnut-variety-tolerant-to-drought-and-foliar-fungal-disease-with-superior-haulm-quality-released-in-odisha-india/
Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found in search results.
Developing station (e.g., AICRP-Groundnut centre within OUAT): No evidence found beyond OUAT Bhubaneswar as the releasing university -- https://ouat.ac.in/
ICRISAT groundnut program background (Patancheru HQ, groundnut breeding since 1976) -- https://www.icrisat.org/crops/groundnut/overview

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute URL: https://ouat.ac.in/ (Odisha University of Agriculture and Technology, Bhubaneswar)
ICRISAT groundnut page: https://www.icrisat.org/crops/groundnut/overview
Names, roles, emails, phone numbers and postal addresses: No evidence found in search results. No OUAT groundnut breeder or Directorate of Research contact details were returned. Please check the OUAT contact page directly.

PUBLICATIONS
Dhara/Kalinga Groundnut-101 has no peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report, or KrishiKosh thesis found in the search results.

Other items: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
ICRISAT reports that a decentralised seed system in Odisha produced more than 2,000 tonnes of quality groundnut seed, with early-generation seed supplied to Bargarh, Kalahandi, Nuapada and Keonjhar, and the Odisha State Seeds Corporation procures and distributes it -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/odishas-oilseed-transformation-strengthens-indias-drive-towards-edible-oil-self-reliance
The Odisha State Seeds Corporation handles groundnut seed distribution at subsidised rates -- https://pc.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2020-03/7.Seed_Distribution_System.pdf
Variety-specific seed production or stock figures for this variety: No evidence found. The OUAT Krishi Vigyan Kendra and self-harvested seed routes are described for groundnut in general -- https://oar.icrisat.org/11904/1/Groundnut%20Variety%20Adoption%20Sep%2028.pdf
Private dealer or Seednet listing: No evidence found.

Odisha. Suitable for residual-moisture post-rainy cultivation, irrigated summer cultivation and rainfed uplands in the kharif season -- https://www.cgiar.org/news-events/news/groundnut-variety-tolerant-to-drought-and-foliar-fungal-disease-with-superior-haulm-quality-released-in-odisha-india/

disease_resistance.summary: No resistance rating for Kadiri-6 itself was found. Evidence indicates susceptibility: (1) described as susceptible to bud necrosis (Chittoor comparison with Dharani); (2) affected by leaf spot and leaf curl in a KVK Reddipalli demonstration, where the newer Kadiri Chitravathi showed better tolerance. Kadiri 6 was used as recurrent parent in a marker-assisted backcross study to introgress late leaf spot and rust resistance; the resulting lines scored 3.0-4.0 for resistance, but this is a derived-line score and not a rating of Kadiri-6.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance rating for Kadiri-6 was found. In a KVK Reddipalli demonstration, Kadiri-6 was affected by leaf miner, Helicoverpa and aphids, while Kadiri Chitravathi showed better tolerance. No resistance score for the parent is given in the marker-assisted backcross study.

agronomic_details.yield: Variety record (CSC): 1372.00 to 3770.00 kg/ha. Reported averages: 20.0 q/ha (Odisha rabi and pre-summer listing); 20-22 q/ha (variety table, Envirobiotech journal). Chittoor demonstration: 1551 kg/ha. KVK Reddipalli demonstration: 2050 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Performance was reported in single demonstrations or trials; no multi-environment stability analysis was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: Andhra Pradesh in both kharif (rainfed) and rabi (irrigated) areas; can be grown in kharif and rabi. Digest evidence: predominant kharif variety in Chittoor district; rabi trial in the Godavari zone (Rajamahendravaram, 2022-23); rabi and pre-summer bunch variety in Odisha; summer 2022 trial at SHUATS Prayagraj.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: CSC record: tall plant, light green leaves with round (obtuse) tip. Growth habit described as a popular Spanish bunch cultivar. Highest plant height at harvest (44.9 cm) among tested varieties in a Godavari region study.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Chittoor demonstration: Dharani 1796 kg/ha vs Kadiri-6 1551 kg/ha; Kadiri-6 was low-yielding relative to Dharani. (2) KVK Reddipalli demonstration: Kadiri-6 2050 kg/ha vs Kadiri Chitravathi 3375 kg/ha; Kadiri-6 showed leaf miner, Helicoverpa, aphid, leaf spot and leaf curl damage. (3) Godavari zone rabi trial, Rajamahendravaram, 2022-23: one of ten entries; Kadiri Lepakshi outperformed Kadiri-6 (no Kadiri-6 yield figure given in the digest). (4) Godavari region study: highest plant height at harvest (44.9 cm) among tested varieties. (5) SHUATS Prayagraj, summer 2022, zinc (0.5%) plus boron (0.2%) foliar spray on Kadiri 6: 2.48 t/ha seed yield, 27.87 pods per plant, 30.44% harvest index. (6) Chittoor study: reported as the predominant kharif variety in the district. (7) Seed quality test among ten varieties: highest germination (75.35%) and seedling vigour for Kadiri-6. (8) Odisha listing: 95 days, 20.0 q/ha. (9) Variety table: 100-105 days, 20-22 q/ha, 72% shelling, 100-seed weight 40-45 g, 48% oil, early, high-yielding and synchronous maturity. (10) MAS study: 100-105 days, 70% shelling, about 39.0 g 100-kernel weight.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Marker-assisted backcrossing used allele-specific, SSR and SNP markers with Kadiri 6 as recurrent parent. Marker names, chromosomal positions and map details are Not found in searched sources.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No Kadiri-6-specific QTL or marker-trait mapping was found in the digest.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. The digest reports that the marker-assisted backcross introgressed high oleic acid, late leaf spot and rust resistance into the Kadiri 6 background from donor ICGV 13193; no gene-level mechanism is described.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kadiri-6 (groundnut)
Variety name (CSC minutes) and Seednet name are both "Kadiri-6", so one evidence set applies. Sources spell it "Kadiri-6", "K-6" or "K 6".

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- Kadiri-6 is described as low-yielding and susceptible to drought and bud necrosis, in a comparison with Dharani in Chittoor district -- https://iskv.in/wp-content/themes/iskv/volume-pdfs/a8bab32ba8b6b38383dbc58201695ab3pages_204-207.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance rating for Kadiri-6 was found in the retrieved text. The drought-tolerance and submergence claims that surfaced belong to Kadiri Lepakshi (K-1812), which is a different variety and is excluded.

DISEASE AND PEST:
- In a KVK Reddipalli demonstration, Kadiri-6 was affected by leaf miner, Helicoverpa, aphids, leaf spot and leaf curl, while the newer Kadiri Chitravathi showed better tolerance -- https://www.kvkreddipalli-angrau.org/93-success-stories/166-enhancing-farmers-income-through-adoption-of-groundnut-variety-kadiri-chitravathi
- A marker-assisted backcross study used Kadiri 6 as recurrent parent to introgress late leaf spot and rust resistance; the resulting lines scored 3.0–4.0 for resistance, but this is a derived-line score, not a rating of Kadiri-6 itself -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7298065/
- The study above also reports that Kadiri 6 is a popular Spanish bunch cultivar; no resistance rating for the parent is given.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- Kadiri-6 is listed at 95 days duration and 20.0 q/ha average yield, as a bunch variety for rabi and pre-summer in Odisha -- https://rkb-odisha.in/oilseed-crops-in-odisha/groundnut/
- Kadiri-6 matures in 100–105 days, with 70% shelling and about 39.0 g 100-kernel weight -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7298065/
- A variety table gives K-6 as 100–105 days, 20–22 q/ha, 72% shelling, 100-seed weight 40–45 g and 48% oil, described as early, high-yielding and synchronous in maturity -- https://www.envirobiotechjournals.com/EEC/Vol.29,Issue3,2023/EEC-23.pdf
- In a Chittoor demonstration, Dharani gave 1796 kg/ha against 1551 kg/ha for Kadiri-6 -- https://iskv.in/wp-content/themes/iskv/volume-pdfs/a8bab32ba8b6b38383dbc58201695ab3pages_204-207.pdf
- In a KVK Reddipalli demonstration, Kadiri-6 yielded 2050 kg/ha against 3375 kg/ha for Kadiri Chitravathi -- https://www.kvkreddipalli-angrau.org/93-success-stories/166-enhancing-farmers-income-through-adoption-of-groundnut-variety-kadiri-chitravathi
- In a Godavari-zone rabi trial (Rajamahendravaram, 2022-23), Kadiri-6 was one of ten entries; Kadiri Lepakshi outperformed it -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388846242_Assessment_of_Yield_and_Economic_Performance_of_Groundnut_Cultivars_in_the_Godavari_Zone_Andhra_Pradesh_India
- In a Godavari region study, Kadiri-6 had the highest plant height at harvest (44.9 cm) among the tested varieties -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/Impact-of-Agroclimatic-Conditions-on-the-Productivity-of-Groundnut-(Arachis-hypogaea-L)-Cultivars-in-the-rabi-Season-under-Godavari-Region-G-Chalapathi-Rao-49.pdf
- Zinc (0.5%) plus boron (0.2%) foliar spray on Kadiri 6 gave 2.48 t/ha seed yield, 27.87 pods per plant and 30.44% harvest index, at SHUATS Prayagraj in summer 2022 -- https://imsear.searo.who.int/items/7c732b02-9bf8-4b57-97ed-1e312fea11a8
- A Chittoor study reported Kadiri-6 as the predominant kharif variety in the district -- https://www.ijcmas.com/8-6-2019/R.%20Prasanna%20Lakshmi,%20et%20al.pdf
- Kadiri-6 seed showed the highest germination (75.35%) and seedling vigour among ten varieties tested -- https://sasapjas.org/effect-of-vigour-levels-on-seed-quality-attributes-of-groundnut-varieties/

GENETICS AND QTL:
- Kadiri 6 was the recurrent parent in marker-assisted backcrossing (allele-specific, SSR and SNP markers) to add high oleic acid, late leaf spot and rust resistance; the donor was ICGV 13193 -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7298065/
- Kadiri-6 kernels contain about 48% oil, of which about 40% is oleic acid and 38% linoleic acid -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7298065/
- No Kadiri-6-specific QTL or marker-trait mapping was found. The drought and iron-deficiency QTL paper (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7824586/) does not

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: LGN-123 (CSC name) / LGN-1 (Seednet name), groundnut, code A0402118

Search scope: I ran the 4-search maximum. Searches 1 and 2 used "LGN-123 groundnut variety" and "LGN-1 groundnut variety Seednet". Search 3 covered the breeder and station, and search 4 covered research and parentage. No search returned a page that names LGN-123 or LGN-1 directly. The seed-availability search was not run because of the cap. Under each heading, the evidence I found relates to other varieties, the Oilseeds Research Station at Latur, or the parent cross, so it does not confirm LGN-123's own traits.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for LGN-123 or LGN-1. Related: one AICRP groundnut release notice describes a different variety with strong Spodoptera litura resistance and rust resistance -- https://icar-iigr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/AICRP-G-Varieties.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for LGN-123 or LGN-1. Related: the same AICRP notice reports rust and Spodoptera resistance in a different variety, not LGN-123 -- https://icar-iigr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/AICRP-G-Varieties.pdf. A Krishikosh paper on F8 populations, including the JL 24 x NcAc 17090 cross, evaluates rust resistance and yield components, but it does not name LGN-123 -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/items/86e14a86-4677-4bcc-b662-5d2d29a0ba35

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for LGN-123 or LGN-1 in the search results. Related: an Indian Journals pod-yield path analysis from Oilseeds Research Station, Latur (Kharif 2006) covers yield components in groundnut, but it does not identify LGN-123 -- https://oar.icrisat.org/6233/1/AgricScDigest_30_2_115-119_2010.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage (JL-24 x NcAc-17090) is recorded in the release data supplied, not confirmed by any search result. A Krishikosh F8 population study includes the same cross, which indicates the parents were used in breeding work -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/items/86e14a86-4677-4bcc-b662-5d2d29a0ba35. No QTL or marker study for LGN-123 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No breeder name was found for LGN-123. Institution listed in the release data is "Oilseeds Research Station". The VNMKV Parbhani station list includes an Oilseeds Research Station at Nanded Road, Latur district, which is the likely station but is not confirmed as the developer -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/research_ResearchStations.php

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact was found. No email, phone, or postal address was present in the retrieved text for the Latur station. Institute-level page to check manually: https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/research_ResearchStations.php (VNMKV, Parbhani; Oilseeds Research Station, Nanded Road, Latur district). Contact details on this page were not captured in the search output, so they are not reproduced here.

PUBLICATIONS --
- Five F8 populations of groundnut evaluated for rust resistance, yield and yield components (year not captured). Krishikosh record -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/items/86e14a86-4677-4bcc-b662-5d2d29a0ba35
- Pod yield path analysis, Latur, Kharif 2006 (author and year not captured). Agricultural Science Digest 30(2):115-119 (2010) -- https://oar.icrisat.org/6233/1/AgricScDigest_30_2_115-119_2010.pdf
- Breeding Groundnut for Biotic Stresses (author and year not captured). National Research Centre for Groundnut, Junagadh -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280304281_Breeding_Groundnut_for_Biotic_Stresses
No publication specifically on LGN-123 or LGN-1 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Not searched (4-search cap reached). No seed source was verified.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Release data lists Maharashtra. No search result confirmed this for LGN-123. The DAC state-wise groundnut variety list does not show LGN-123 in the retrieved text -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx

disease_resistance.summary: Maydis leaf blight (MLB) and common rust: The CCS HAU source reports HM-13 / HKH 317 as tolerant of maydis leaf blight (kharif) and common rust (rabi). A Maize Scenario in Haryana review describes HM 13 as having a high level of resistance to MLB and common rust. A 2015 benchmarking table lists HM13 as moderately resistant to MLB and common rust. The sources differ in the stated level (tolerant/high/moderately resistant), so the level should be verified. No other disease reactions were found.

pest_resistance.summary: Stem borer and Chilo partellus: The CCS HAU source reports HM-13 / HKH 317 as tolerant of stem borer and Chilo partellus. No other pest reactions were found. The CSC record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: average yield 27.50 Q/HA (recorded as '27.50Q/HA Kg/Ha'). Digest sources report higher figures: kharif average about 57-60 q/ha and rabi average about 67-70 q/ha (Maize Scenario in Haryana review). These values conflict with the CSC figure and should be verified against CSC minutes.
agronomic_details.stability: Zone III (Bihar, Jharkhand, UP, Odisha) kharif average grain yield of 59 q/ha, with less yield loss under low nitrogen. The digest also notes HM 13 is responsive to high nutrient doses. No multi-environment stability analysis was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Identified for zone I by the CCS HAU source. The 2017 review refers to the 'Northern hill zone' (CVRC, 2014). The benchmarking source lists Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and NE hills for kharif. The input record says 'Jammu, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand'. The digest flags this discrepancy and recommends checking the CSC minutes. The Zone III result is reported above but the digest does not state that HM-13 is recommended for Zone III.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Early-maturing, high-starch, yellow-grain single cross (CCS HAU source). Yellow grain, flint/semi-flint (benchmarking table entry). The digest reports kharif maturity of 88-90 days (Maize Scenario in Haryana review), which conflicts with the CSC maturity of 135 days. disease_resistance.summary: Maydis leaf blight (MLB) and common rust: The CCS HAU source reports HM-13 / HKH 317 as tolerant of maydis leaf blight (kharif) and common rust (rabi). The digest flags this discrepancy and recommends checking the CSC minutes. The Zone III result is reported above but the digest does not state that HM-13 is recommended for Zone III.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Tolerant of maydis leaf blight (kharif) and common rust (rabi), and of stem borer and Chilo partellus (name: HM-13 / HKH 317) -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1710843607.pdf

- Drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found for HM-13 in the search results.
- Seednet name M-13 (GROUNDNUT): No evidence found. No search targeted "M-13" directly, and the seed-availability search returned no Seednet page.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Tolerant of maydis leaf blight (kharif), common rust (rabi), stem borer and Chilo partellus (name: HM-13 / HKH 317) -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1710843607.pdf
- Moderately resistant to MLB and common rust, listed in a 2015 benchmarking table (name: HM13) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- Seednet name M-13 (GROUNDNUT): No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Early-maturing, high-starch, yellow-grain single cross; identified for zone I (name: HM-13 / HKH 317) -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1710843607.pdf
- Kharif average about 57-60 q/ha, rabi about 67-70 q/ha; matures in 88-90 days in kharif; responsive to high nutrient doses (name: HM 13) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328879711_Maize_Scenario_in_Haryana_A_Brief_Review
- Zone III (Bihar, Jharkhand, UP, Odisha) kharif average grain yield 59 q/ha; less yield loss under low nitrogen (name: HM-13 / HKH 317) -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1710843607.pdf
- Yellow grain, flint/semi-flint, with a 2015 benchmarking table entry for HM13 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- Multi-location trial data specific to HM-13: No evidence found. The AICRP 2016 kharif trial list shows HKH 355 and HKH 356 (other entries), not HM-13 -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/AnnualReports/Maize%20AICRP%20REPORT%20KHARIF%202016.pdf
- Seednet name M-13 (GROUNDNUT): No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage ("a selection from NC 13 of USA") is from the CSC record only. No independent source confirming it was found.
- QTL, marker, or genomic studies on HM-13: No evidence found.
- Seednet name M-13 (GROUNDNUT): No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- HM 12 and HM 13 were developed by the Maize Section, CCS HAU Regional Research Station, Karnal (name: HM 13) -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/karnal/

EVIDENCE DIGEST: TMB-37 (seednet name M-37), greengram (Vigna radiata), PAU

Search note: Four web_search queries were run in the first batch: TMB-37 variety; M-37 breeder; TMB-37 research; M-37 seed availability. A fifth attempt failed because the tool-use limit was reached, so the coverage below is thin. Searches on the seednet name M-37 returned nothing relevant. Evidence below refers to TMB-37 unless stated otherwise.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The retrieved pages do not report drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for TMB-37.

DISEASE AND PEST -- TMB-37 appears in a table of advanced breeding material for yellow mosaic disease (YMD) management in mungbean, listed with a gamma-ray mutagenic origin. The snippet does not state its resistance rating or score -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7327115/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No maturity, yield or multi-location trial data for TMB-37 were retrieved.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage given in the variety record ("a derivative of the cross between A 1-1 x C6") was supplied by you and was not confirmed by any retrieved source. The PMC review gives a gamma-ray origin for TMB-37 but no pedigree -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7327115/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No TMB-37 breeder was named in any retrieved source. The PAU site returned a general staff biography for a rice breeder, not a mungbean breeder for TMB-37 -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageLink&DO=secondLink&intLinkID=134&intSubID=21 . Institution per your record: Punjab Agriculture University (PAU), Ludhiana.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. The only PAU-related result was the staff page above; it did not give an email, phone or postal address in the retrieved text. Institute-level contact should be taken from the PAU site (pau.edu) directly, which was not reachable in the retrieved text.

PUBLICATIONS -- Gupta, S. (year not stated in the retrieved text). Yellow Mosaic Disease (YMD) of Mungbean (Vigna radiata (L.) Wilczek): Current Status and Management Opportunities. Review article including TMB-37 in a breeding-material table -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7327115/ . Authors and year are not confirmed from the retrieved text; treat them as unverified. No TMB-37 research paper, AICRP report or KrishiKosh thesis was retrieved.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for India. The only "seed availability" result was for the Punjab Seed Corporation of Pakistan (psc.punjab.gov.pk), which is unrelated to Indian Punjab and to this variety -- https://psc.punjab.gov.pk/seed-availability . Check the Punjab state seed agency, PAU seed sales and seednet.gov.in directly.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Punjab, per your variety record only. No notification or gazette source was retrieved to confirm this.

Not verified: release date (2018-01-20 per your record), variety code A0402057, and the CSC notification. None of these were found in the search results. Searches on seednet.gov.in, the CSC minutes and KrishiKosh are still needed.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE (evidence refers to PMH 4 / JH 31153, the maize name; MH-4 not found)
No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for PMH 4. The only trait notes were for other hybrids (Pusa HM4 and PMH-I), which I discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST (evidence refers to PMH 4 / JH 31153)
No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance rating for PMH 4 appeared. The AICMIP table's resistance notes belong to other entries such as HQPM-4 and NAC 6004, so I did not use them.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (evidence refers to PMH 4 / JH 31153)
- Yield around 8.3 t/ha, Kharif season, normal (non-QPM) type, listed in the ICAR-IIMR cultivar table -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
- Medium maturity in the AICMIP hybrid release table, with yellow-orange flint kernels -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- Same 8.3 t/ha figure and yellow-orange, flint, nutrient-responsive description in the maize benchmarking presentation -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- In an organic production trial, PMH-4, a medium-maturity cultivar, produced yield comparable to the late-maturing cultivars (trial site and year not shown on the page) -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Plant-height-and-chlorophyll-index-of-different-varieties-of-maize-under-organic_tbl1_311426046

GENETICS AND QTL (evidence refers to PMH 4 / JH 31153)
No evidence found. Nothing in the results confirmed the parentage given in the record ("improvement of MH2 for plant height by selection"), and no QTL or marker study on this variety was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (evidence refers to PMH 4 / JH 31153; the MH-4 Seednet entry is not confirmed)
- Developing institution in the national cultivar list is PAU, Ludhiana, released via the AICRP on Maize -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
- Conflict: the submitted record names the Oilseeds Section, Deptt. of Plant Breeding, HAU Hisar. No source connected PMH 4 to HAU Hisar, so this field is unverified and appears to be a Seednet data error.
- No individual breeder was named for PMH 4 in any source. Names I found on PAU maize pages (for example the PAU faculty directory and the 2016 AICRP kharif report) are not linked to this variety and are not attributed here.
- MH-4 (Seednet crop: groundnut): No evidence found. The MH-4 search returned only unrelated groundnut varieties from other countries and companies (for example SAMNUT and MGV lines), so none of those are attributed to this record.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The only evidence is a government notified-variety list entry (Bihar) with yield and maturity data. Ten of the eleven search results are irrelevant, matching 'POL-2' to unrelated documents such as SEC filings, college catalogs and policy codes. No stress traits, publications or citations were found, so the variety fits the 'only yield info, no stress/citation' tier. The official list is an administrative record, not research evidence.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Old release (1973); 105-day maturity; yield of 15 q/ha rainfed and 27 q/ha irrigated; Pollachi Red x AH 2105 derivative

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: POL-2 is a groundnut variety released in 1973 from a Pollachi Red x AH 2105 derivative. It matures in 105 days and yields 15 q/ha rainfed and 27 q/ha irrigated. No stress tolerance, disease or pest resistance, genetic marker or breeder data were found, and the evidence is limited to an official notification list.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: A medium-duration (105-day) groundnut released in 1973, with yields of 15 q/ha rainfed and 27 q/ha irrigated. Recommended states, agronomic features and morphology are not documented.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No evidence of drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance, or of disease or pest resistance. Search results were almost entirely irrelevant, so stress tolerance cannot be assessed.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pratap Raj Mungphali (groundnut)

Name check: The variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical ("Pratap Raj Mungphali"), and all evidence below refers to that name. I did not find evidence for the separate, similarly named Pratap Mungphali-1, -2, -3 or -4, so I have excluded them. Searches were run for the release/variety, breeder/institution, research and seed-availability topics. The Seednet portal page itself was not retrieved; the release year and variety code come from the input record only.

STRESS TOLERANCE

- Listed as early maturing and tolerant to ELS, LLS, PBND, jassids, thrips and leaf miner -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396544544_Improved_production_practices_for_sustainable_groundnut_cultivation_An_Indian_perspective
- The same trait summary appears in a 2025 review; the table lists it for Rajasthan with early maturity and tolerance to leaf spots, PBND, jassids, thrips and leaf miner -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue10/PartF/8-10-40-464.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance evidence found for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST

- Early and late leaf spot, PBND, jassid, thrip and leaf miner tolerance (as above) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396544544_Improved_production_practices_for_sustainable_groundnut_cultivation_An_Indian_perspective
- Spodoptera litura tolerance is listed in the same table entry (the source text is fragmented; I could not confirm the exact wording for Spodoptera) -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue10/PartF/8-10-40-464.pdf
- Note: the ICAR-DGR compendium entry for this variety was truncated in the search result, so no pest/disease details from that source were captured -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS

- In a 2021 kharif trial at Sub-Humid Southern Plains of Rajasthan (Pratap Raj Mungphali as a check, among 36 genotypes), it recorded 16.33 g dry pod yield per plant, 11.98 g kernel yield per plant and 73.33% shelling -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313510785_Variability_Assessment_and_Path_Coefficient_Analysis_in_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L_Genotypes_in_Sub-_Humid_Southern_Plains_of_Rajasthan
- The same study ranked it among the top genotypes for kernel yield per plant and shelling percentage -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313510785_Variability_Assessment_and_Path_Coefficient_Analysis_in_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L_Genotypes_in_Sub-_Humid_Southern_Plains_of_Rajasthan
- Maturity (days) and recommended kg/ha yield for this variety: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL

- Pedigree is given as selection from ICGV 98223 -- https://ojs.pphouse.org/index.php/IJBSM/article/download/3716/1194/2369
- A 2014 D2 genetic-diversity study at MPUAT Udaipur used Pratap Raj Mungphali as a check among 30 genotypes -- https://ojs.pphouse.org/index.php/IJBSM/article/download/3716/1194/2369
- QTL, marker or genomic studies specific to this variety: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION

- Developing institution: Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, Rajasthan College of Agriculture, MPUAT (Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology), Udaipur. Source for the institution, as given in the input record: the variety record; corroborated for the department in the sister varieties' releases -- https://oar.icrisat.org/1203/1/RA_00419.pdf
- Named breeders found in the department's releases (AK Nagda, Abhay Dashora, VN Joshi) are associated with Pratap Mungphali-1 and -2, not confirmed for Pratap Raj Mungphali -- https://oar.icrisat.org/1201/1/RA_00417.pdf ; https://oar.icrisat.org/1203/1/RA_00419.pdf
- Lead breeder for Pratap Raj Mungphali: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS

- Institute-level only: Department of Plant Breeding & Genetics, Rajasthan College of Agriculture, MPUAT, Udaipur (Rajasthan) 313 001 (postal code as printed in the release notes for sister varieties) -- https://oar.icrisat.org/1201/1/RA_00417.pdf
- Official email, phone, or institute contact page URL for this variety: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS

- Authors not captured in the search result (title only). Variability Assessment and Path Coefficient Analysis in Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.) Genotypes in Sub-Humid Southern Plains of Rajasthan. Kharif 2021 trial. Journal/Report: not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313510785_Variability_Assessment_and_Path_Coefficient_Analysis_in_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L_Genotypes_in_Sub-_Humid_Southern_Plains_of_Rajasthan
- Authors not captured. Assessment of Genetic Diversity Among Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.) Genotypes (kharif 2014, MPUAT Udaipur). Journal: International Journal of Biological Sciences and Medicine (IJBSM) -- https://ojs.pphouse.org/index.php/IJBSM/article/download/3716/1194/2369
- Authors not captured. Improved production practices for sustainable groundnut cultivation: An Indian perspective (2025). Report/Journal: not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396544544_Improved_production_practices_for_sustainable_groundnut_cultivation_An_Indian_perspective
- Authors not captured. International Journal of Research in Agronomy 2025; 8(10): 394-402. Journal: International Journal of Research in Agronomy. DOI: not captured -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue10/PartF/8-10-40-464.pdf
- Official release notification or AICRP annual report entry for this variety: No evidence found.
- KrishiKosh theses: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY

- Rajasthan State Seeds Corporation availability listing: this variety does not appear in the retrieved listing -- http://rajseeds.org/AvailabilityOfSeeds.html
- National Seeds Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales, or private dealers offering this specific variety: No evidence found. A generic dealer listing for "Mungphali Dana" was retrieved but does not name this variety, so I have not attributed it -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/mungphali-dana-peanut-seed-5012091633.html

RECOMMENDED STATES

- Rajasthan: the DOD state-wise list (notified under the Seed Act, 2008 to 2019) includes Pratap Raj Mungphalli -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Recommended states in the Seednet record: "Not specified" in the input. Other states: No evidence found.

RELEASE AND NOTIFICATION (supporting note)

- Release year 2010-10-10 (from the input record): No independent evidence found. The compendium entry was truncated, so a notification number could not be confirmed -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1

seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: IT DOES NOT WELL UNDER LATE SOWN CONDITIONS. IN NOVEMBER SOWN CROP WHICH IS CALLED AS LATE SOWN ONE, THE CROP IS EXPOSED TO HIGH TEMPERATURE AT THE TIME OF SEED FILLING AND MATURITY. THIS VARIETY HAS A TOLERANCE TO HAVE TO FOR HIGH TEMPERATURES AT MATURITY AND PERFORMS WELL. APHIS IS A MAJOR PROBLEM IN LATE SOWN CROP FOR WHICH IT HAS LOW INFESTATION AS COMPARED TO PREVAILING VARIETIES.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Input record states suitability for Rajasthan under both irrigated and drought conditions and for early sowing in irrigated conditions. A source listing RG 425 as a Spanish-bunch variety recommended for Rajasthan (Zone I) suggests a spreading-type spacing of 45-60 x 20 cm and sowing from late June to mid July. RARI describes the variety as semi-spreading, which conflicts with the Spanish-bunch classification; this discrepancy is unresolved. The ICAR-IIGR listing of RG 425 as iron chlorosis tolerant is also relevant to adaptation.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RG 425 (groundnut)

Name note: The CSC name (variety_name) and the Seednet name (seednet_variety_name) are both "RG 425," so every search result refers to the same name. I could not reach the Seednet portal record or the CSC release minutes, so the code A0402190, the 2010 release year, and the parentage ICG 5013 x RG 340 rest on the input record alone and are unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
RARI Durgapura describes RG 425 as a semi-spreading variety with drought tolerance and collar rot resistance -- https://raridurgapura.org/Scheme-Groundnut.htm
ICAR-IIGR research achievements lists RG 425 among cultivars identified as iron chlorosis tolerant -- https://icar-iigr.org.in/2015/06/research-achievements/
Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
Collar rot resistance (RARI page above) -- https://raridurgapura.org/Scheme-Groundnut.htm
Rust, leaf spot, bud necrosis and pest resistance specific to RG 425: No evidence found (the RG 382 and RG 141 entries on the same RARI page are different varieties)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Listed among Spanish-bunch varieties recommended for Rajasthan (Zone I), with a suggested spreading-type spacing of 45-60 x 20 cm and sowing from late June to mid July -- https://www.isasat.org/Volume-1,issue-2,july-2017/AARJ_1_2_8_Waghmode.pdf
Note: the same source classes RG 425 as Spanish bunch while RARI describes it as semi-spreading; this discrepancy is unresolved.
Maturity days, pod yield, and multi-location trial results for RG 425: No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage (ICG 5013 x RG 340) and any QTL or marker study on RG 425: No evidence found (only general groundnut genetics reviews, listed under PUBLICATIONS)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
RARI Durgapura is a constituent institute of Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University (SKNAU), Jobner, Jaipur, and runs the AICRP on Groundnut centre there -- https://raridurgapura.org/Scheme-Groundnut.htm
RARI Durgapura's groundnut programme is credited with developing six varieties, including RG 425 -- https://raridurgapura.org/Scheme-Groundnut.htm
Lead breeder name for RG 425: No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS
Dr. Ashok Kumar Meena, Name of Incharge, AICRP on Groundnut, RARI Durgapura; mobile 918432719252; email akmeena.pbg.rari@sknau.ac.in -- https://raridurgapura.org/Scheme-Groundnut.htm
RARI Durgapura, Jaipur, Rajasthan 302018 (institute address as printed in a best-management-practices document) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379814988_Best_Management_Practices_for_Groundnut_Cultivation_in_India
Official institute contact page URL: raridurgapura.org (homepage; the specific contact page was not found)

PUBLICATIONS
No RG 425-specific peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper found.
Related general reference only (not about RG 425): Desmae, H., Janila, P., Okori, P., et al. (2019). Genetics, genomics and breeding of groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.). Plant Breeding 138: 425-444 -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/pbr.12645 (DOI: 10.1111/pbr.12645)

SEED AVAILABILITY
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SKNAU seed-sales, or private dealer listing specific to RG 425 was found. Generic groundnut seed dealers in Rajasthan appeared in search, but none named RG 425 -- https://www.exportersindia.com/rajasthan/groundnut-seed.htm

RECOMMENDED STATES
Listed under Rajasthan among varieties notified under the Seeds Act from 2008 to 2019 -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
The input record lists recommended states as "Not specified," so this is the only state evidence found.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: RECOMMENDED FOR RELEASE & CULTIVATION IN THE STATES OF RAJASTHAN AND PUNJAB UNDER KHARIF RAINFED CONDITIONS.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: THE PROPOSED VARIETY HSA RESPONDED WELL TO THE HIGHER THAN RECOMMENDED DOSES OF NITROGENOUS AND PHOSPHATIC FERTILIZERS. THIS GAVE 4774 KG/HA POD YIELD AT 125% RECOMMENDED DOSE OF FERTILIZERS COMPARED TO 4620 KG/HA AT 100% RDF. HOWEVER, WHEN RDF WAS INCREASES FROM 100% TO 125% THE GAIN IN POD YIELD IN THE PROPOSED WAS ONLY MARGINAL (3.3%). THE PROPOSED VARIETY IS MUCH SUITED FOR ADVANCE SOWING COMPARE TO LATE SOWING.THE VARIETY HAS MEDIUM SEED SIZE (54 G/100 SEEDS) AND HIGH OIL CONTENT (49%). DUE TO ITS HIGH YIELD POTENTIAL, THE TOTAL OIL YIELD IS 858 KG/HA, WHICH IS 176 KG/HA.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT ; 19-24 RUNNER, INTERMEDIATE GROWTH HABIT; LEAFLETS SMALL, DARK GREEN AND LANCEO LATE; POD MODERATELY RETICULATED AND CONSTRICTED, 2 SEEDED; KERNELS MEDIUM WITH ROSE COLOUR TESTA
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: IT HAS LOW SPECIFIC LEAF AREA AND HIGH CHLOROPHYLL METER READING (SCMR) AND THESE ATTRIBUTES CONFER WATER USE EFFICIENCY.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: THE PROPOSED VARIETY SHOW LOWER INCIDENCE OF COLLAR ROT,STEM ROT, EARLY LEAF SPOT, RUST AND PEANUT STEM NECROSIS DISEASES.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: THE PROPOSED VARIETY HAS LOWER INCIDENCE OF THRIPS ATTACK.

disease_resistance.summary: Collar rot (seedling stage, Aspergillus niger): no field resistance rating found. An in vitro seed-treatment study by Sekhon, Sandhu, Sharma and Belludi (2019) used SG-99 seed. Tebuconazole gave the highest healthy-seedling percentage for SG-99 (88.00%). The authors report that collar rot markedly reduced germination and seedling vigour. This is a laboratory fungicide test, not evidence of genetic resistance. Rust and late leaf spot: no evidence found for SG 99. The QTL-seq papers that mention these diseases concern other parents and are not attributed to SG 99. A ResearchGate publication link is referenced in the source figure page, but its full URL was not retrieved, so it is not listed here.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SG 99 groundnut: evidence digest

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "SG 99", so every search used the same name. I did not find a separate Seednet portal page for SG 99, so no finding below comes from Seednet.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The four searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for SG 99. The only SG 99 agronomy text describes it as grown in loamy sand to sandy places during summer months, which is a soil description, not a stress rating. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/oilseeds/groundnut

DISEASE AND PEST
Collar rot (seedling stage): an in vitro study by Sekhon, Sandhu, Sharma and Belludi (2019) tested fungicide seed treatments against Aspergillus niger, using SG-99 seed. Tebuconazole gave the highest healthy-seedling percentage for SG-99 (88.00%), and the authors report that collar rot markedly reduced germination and seedling vigour. This is a laboratory germination test, not a field resistance rating. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Germination-status-of-groundnut-seeds-variety-SG-99-treated-with-different_fig1_337737539 (also https://www.researchgate.net/publication/... linked from the same figure page, "In Vitro Evaluation of Fungicides against Aspergillus niger causing Collar Rot Disease in Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.)")
Pest resistance: No evidence found.
Rust or late leaf spot resistance for SG 99: No evidence found. The QTL-seq papers that mention rust and late leaf spot name other parents (GPBD 4 and others), not SG 99. -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/pbi.12686 (not SG 99; listed for exclusion only)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity and plant traits: an SG 99 entry in a Punjab groundnut extension page gives maturity of 124 days, principal stalk length 66-68 cm, 22-24 mature pods per plant, 100-kernel weight of 54 g, and shelling outturn of 66%. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/oilseeds/groundnut
Oil content: the same page gives 52.3% oil for the SG 99 entry. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/oilseeds/groundnut
Spacing and seed rate: the page advises a 30 x 15 cm spacing for bunch-type varieties including SG 99. The page does not separate the yield figures per variety, so no yield figure is attributed to SG 99. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/oilseeds/groundnut
Field-trial or multi-location results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: a review table lists SG 99 as released in India in 2004 from the breeding programme entry "ICGV 89280", which matches the parentage in the record. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6774334/
QTL or marker studies naming SG 99: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: No evidence found that PAU developed SG 99. The record's parentage points to ICRISAT germplasm (ICGV 89280). The review table lists SG 99 with ICGV 89280 as the breeding programme name but does not name the developing institution or breeder. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6774334/
Lead breeder name: No evidence found.
Context: ICRISAT's groundnut program is the source of ICGV-series germplasm. -- https://www.icrisat.org/crops/groundnut/overview
Context: the ICAR Directorate of Groundnut Research at Junagadh names SG 99 among cultivars with low phytic acid, but it does not say who bred it. -- https://www.icar-iigr.org.in/index.php/directors-desk/

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact for SG 99 found. Institute-level contacts below are not linked to SG 99 by any retrieved text except where noted.
ICAR-Indian Institute of Groundnut Research (Directorate of Groundnut Research), Junagadh: address "At & Post: Ivnagar, Ivnagar Road, Junagadh-362015, Gujarat, India"; email director.groundnut@gmail.com. The page naming SG 99 is the Director's Desk page; the address and email appear on the breeder seed section page. -- https://icar-iigr.org.in/service-support/breeder-seed-section/ ; https://www.icar-iigr.org.in/index.php/directors-desk/
Junagadh Agricultural University, Main Oilseeds Research Station (groundnut), unit head: Dr. N. D. Dholariya, Research Scientist (Groundnut) (I/C); office (0285) 2672080-90, PBX-325; (0285) 2670205; mobile +91-7777930601; email rsoilseed@jau.in. This station page does not name SG 99. -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/main-oilseeds-research-station-junagadh
PAU (Punjab Agricultural University): no PAU contact found, and no PAU link to SG 99 found. No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Sekhon, A. S., Sandhu, P. S., Sharma, P., & Belludi, R. (2019). In Vitro Evaluation of Fungicides against Aspergillus niger causing Collar Rot Disease in Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.). Journal not shown in retrieved text (ResearchGate record, November 2019) -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Germination-status-of-groundnut-seeds-variety-SG-99-treated-with-different_fig1_337737539
Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Genetics, genomics and breeding of groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.). Journal not shown -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6774334/ (the SG 99 entry is a table row, not the paper's main text)
AICRP or ICAR annual reports on SG 99: No evidence found. KrishiKosh theses on SG 99: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. None of the seed-supplier results named SG 99. Results for GG-20, AgriBee 999 and INDO-US 999 are other varieties and were excluded. The Junagadh station page says it supplies breeder seed for Gujarat and national indents, but it does not name SG 99. -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/main-oilseeds-research-station-junagadh
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listing for SG 99 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found that SG 99 is recommended for Gujarat or Rajasthan. The Gujarat variety compendium found did not name SG 99 in the retrieved text. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-and-popular-varieties-recommended-for-gujaratenglishpdf/252255631
Release year conflict: the record gives 2016-08-12. The review table gives 2004 for SG 99. Neither the 2016 CSC notification nor a 2004 release notice for SG 99 was retrieved. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6774334/
No CSC release minutes or gazette notification for SG 99 were found. The record's release date and recommended states remain unverified.

Maharashtra paper (TMV-10, Seednet name): described as a high-yielding groundnut variety for southern Maharashtra from the Jalgaon station; no trial data figures given in the digest. (3) TNAU groundnut page (TMV-10, Seednet name): listed under semi-spreading varieties for early Adipattam sowing in all districts; listing only, no trial result. No AMV-10 trial results were found.

No evidence found for TMV-10 or AMV-10. The only pest and disease notes located concern other groundnut varieties and were excluded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
TMV-10 (Seednet name): a TNAU table lists it as a 1970 release from Argentine selection, with 135-day duration, semi-spreading habit, about 1650 kg/ha yield, 54% oil, and high shelling, described as high-yielding and high-oil. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/

TMV-10 (Seednet name): a Maharashtra Agricultural Universities journal paper (Desale et al.) describes it as a high-yielding groundnut variety for southern Maharashtra, from the Jalgaon station. -- https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=IN8102359
Release-year conflict: the CSC record gives 2020, but every TMV-10 source gives 1970 or 1980-era release. The 2020 date appears to belong to a different record. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/
AMV-10 (CSC name): no evidence found in any search result.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Parentage in the CSC record ("natural mutant from Argentina") matches the source description of TMV-10 as a natural mutant from Argentina, but no genetic or QTL study was located. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CropProduction/Oilseeds/oilseeds_groundnut01.html ; https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/suitable-groundnut-varieties-for-kharif-and-rabi/251178470

disease_resistance.summary: Rust: the ORS Tindivanam page reports the culture as completely resistant to rust disease; the EJPB paper reports only moderate resistance to rust compared with check varieties. These sources conflict and the conflict is unresolved. Late leaf spot (LLS): the ORS page reports tolerance with a score of 2.0; the EJPB paper reports moderate resistance compared with check varieties; a separate leaf spot score reports a medium resistant reaction (score 6.0) against 9.0 for susceptible checks VRI 2, CO 2 and TMV 2. Multiple sources agree on LLS tolerance or moderate-to-medium resistance, though the scales differ.

pest_resistance.summary: TMV 14 showed tolerance to Spodoptera litura, thrips, Helicoverpa armigera and leaf miner (reported in the EJPB paper and the Academia.edu copy of the same work). No quantitative pest scores were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: TMV 14 (groundnut)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "TMV 14", so one set of searches covered both. The Seednet portal itself was not returned by any search, so no Seednet-sourced evidence was found. Variety code A0402230 and the CSC release minutes were not found either.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The culture is completely resistant to rust disease and tolerant to late leaf spot (score 2.0), and it matures in 95-100 days. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/
- Drought: No TMV 14-specific drought result was found. A PEG-6000 germination screen (Umadevi et al.) lists TMV 14 in a table, but the retrieved text does not show its classification, so I have not counted it. -- https://masujournal.org/view_journal.php?id=658

DISEASE AND PEST
- For late leaf spot and rust, TMV 14 showed moderate resistance compared with check varieties, and it showed tolerance to Spodoptera litura, thrips, Helicoverpa armigera and leaf miner. -- https://www.academia.edu/90525667/Groundnut_TMV_14_A_new_high_yielding_Spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety (also in the EJPB paper, https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2019.00039.5)
- Leaf spot score: medium resistant reaction to leaf spot (score 6.0), against 9.0 for susceptible checks VRI 2, CO 2 and TMV 2. -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/9a45/4207f9b78a29dc7b42acf70e2eff76030c6b.pdf
- Note the conflict: the ORS page reports complete rust resistance, while the EJPB paper reports only moderate resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield: 2124 kg/ha in kharif, 11.5% above VRI (Gn) 6 (1904 kg/ha) and 15.2% above TMV Gn 13 (1844 kg/ha). -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-10-1-039
- Rabi yield: 2286 kg/ha under irrigation, 29.7% above VRI (Gn) 6 and 32.3% above TMV Gn 13. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-10-1-039
- Seed quality: shelling of 70.6% with 92% SMK and 38 g of 100-kernel weight. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/
- Agritech gives a different maturity (105-110 days), rainfed/irrigated averages of 2222/2360 kg/ha, and oil content of 45.01%. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20TMV%2014.html
- Rainfed weed-management trial using TMV 14 in late rabi (Swetha et al., 2022). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366555054_Novel_method_to_manage_weeds_in_the_rainfed_groundnut_var_VRI_8_and_TMV_14_using_nano_encapsulated_herbicide_formulations
- Multi-location and adaptive trials: multi-location trials were run in Kharif 2013, 2014 and 2015 under rainfed conditions, and rabi 2013-14. -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/9a45/4207f9b78a29dc7b42acf70e2eff76030c6b.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The searches returned no QTL, marker or genetic-mapping study for TMV 14. The only marker paper retrieved (Mol Biol Rep 2024) does not name TMV 14 in the retrieved text. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11033-024-09633-z
- Pedigree: cross derivative of VRI 6 x R 2001-(2), developed by pedigree method of breeding. -- https://doaj.org/article/fc2c92a9a86244b39def39f3826126e9
- Parentage conflict: agritech.tnau.ac.in lists "VR12 x TVG 0004" instead. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20TMV%2014.html

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**VL Moongphali 1 (groundnut): EVIDENCE DIGEST**

Name note: the CSC release-minute name is "VL Moongphali 1" and the Seednet name is "VL Moongphali-1". Every source found used the hyphenated form or the "VL-Moongphali-1" spelling, and none came from the Seednet portal itself. The findings below therefore refer to the same variety under both names, but no Seednet record was retrieved.

Searches run: 4 (release/traits; breeder/institute; Seednet code; research/parentage). Seednet was not reachable through search, so the variety code A0402180 is unverified.

**STRESS TOLERANCE**
- Resistant to late leaf spot (LLS) and root rot, per the DAC notified-variety table. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The sources found name only LLS and root rot resistance.

**DISEASE AND PEST**
- Resistant to late leaf spot and root rot. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx ; https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
- Pest resistance: No evidence found for this variety. Pest tolerance cited for the parent ICGV 86590 is resistance to Spodoptera litura and Sclerotium rolfsii. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/538/

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**
- Yield potential about 1943 kg/ha, listed in the DAC table. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Recommended production system: kharif (rainy season). -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Maturity days, oil content and multi-location trial data for VL-Moongphali-1: No evidence found. The 96–123 day maturity and 48% oil figures belong to the parent ICGV 86590. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/538/
- Pod yield per hectare and oil content for ICGV 86590 in its own release, from the ICAR-DGR compendium: 1,785 kg/ha pod yield and 48% oil. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1

**GENETICS AND QTL**
- Pedigree: selection from ICGV-86590 (X 14-4-B-19-8 x PI 239747), breeding method pureline selection. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
- The same parentage appears in the compendium as "X14-4-B-19-8", while the ICRISAT monograph gives the parent as "X14-4-B-19-B" crossed with PI259747. Flag this discrepancy for checking. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/538/
- QTL or marker studies for this variety: No evidence found.

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION**
- Developing institution: ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan (VPKAS), Almora, Uttarakhand. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1 ; https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.
- Station: VPKAS Almora; the ICAR page places the institute's experimental farm at Hawalbagh. -- https://www.icar.org.in/en/node/3127
- Institute director named on the ICAR page (2021): Dr. Lakshmi Kant. This is an institutional role, not a breeder credit. -- https://www.icar.org.in/en/node/3127

**CONTACT DETAILS**
- Director, ICAR-VPKAS Almora: Dr. Lakshmi Kant (as named on the 2021 ICAR page). Email, phone and postal address: No evidence found in the retrieved text. -- https://www.icar.org.in/en/node/3127
- Institute contact page URL: Not retrieved. Check https://www.icar.org.in or the VPKAS site directly.
- Breeder email/phone: No evidence found.

**PUBLICATIONS**
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, thesis or conference paper specifically on VL Moongphali-1 was found.

drought.details: No evidence found. The digest lists rainfed and irrigated yields (2448 and 2535 kg/ha, TNAU) but retrieved no explicit drought-tolerance rating or mechanism for VRI 10. The 2024 on-farm rainfed trial reports pod yield of 2493 kg/ha, which is not a stress-tolerance rating.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance in VRI 10.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance in VRI 10.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance in VRI 10.

disease_resistance.summary: Leaf spot: described as moderately resistant by TNAU (the TNAU entry is truncated after this point, so the full list is unverified) and as moderate resistance to late leaf spot in the 2024 on-farm trial paper. Root wilt: the 2024 on-farm trial paper reports higher tolerance to root wilt than some comparators, ranking second to TCGS 1694 (pod yield 2493 kg/ha); no quantitative resistance score is given. Rust, stem rot, peanut bud necrosis and PBND: no evidence found for VRI 10 specifically (the DAC listing of notified varieties has no VRI 10 row). A general tnbrdngo claim of built-in pest and disease defences has no quantitative data.

pest_resistance.summary: Sucking pests and defoliators: described as moderately resistant by TNAU (the entry is truncated, so the full list is unverified). No other pest-resistance evidence found for VRI 10.

agronomic_details.yield: TNAU: 2448 kg/ha rainfed and 2535 kg/ha irrigated (units as reported by TNAU; the CSC record lists average yield in Kg/Ha without a value). On-farm rainfed trial (2024 paper, trial around 2022-23): pod yield 2493 kg/ha, haulm yield 4587 kg/ha (highest haulm yield among varieties tested), BCR 2.86. Cluster frontline demonstrations in Cuddalore district (VRI 8 and VRI 10 combined, 2020-21 to 2022-23, 175 demonstrations, about 70 ha): yield gain over farmers' practice of 53.34 per cent (another version of the study reports 62.13 per cent). The gain is not separated by variety.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Season-wise recommendation across Tamil Nadu zones (kharif, rabi and summer) is reported by TNAU, naming Villupuram, Thiruvallur, Kancheepuram, Cuddalore, Perambalur/Ariyalur, Tiruchirappalli, Thanjavur and others. The digest does not explicitly confirm VRI 10 in each listed zone. tnbrdngo cites suitability for short-duration cropping. Multi-location or AICRP/ICAR trial data: not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 100 To 105Days (CSC record). Conflicting duration reported by TNAU and tnbrdngo: 90-95 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: THE PODS ARE LONG WITH MEDIUM TO DEEP CONSTRICTION, PROMINANT BEAK (CSC record). TNAU additionally reports growth habit bunch and oil content of 46-48%.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) 2024 on-farm rainfed trial: pod yield 2493 kg/ha, haulm yield 4587 kg/ha (highest among varieties tested), BCR 2.86, second-ranked for root wilt tolerance behind TCGS 1694 (pod yield 2493 kg/ha as reported). (2) Cluster frontline demonstrations, Cuddalore district, VRI 8 and VRI 10, 2020-21 to 2022-23: 175 demonstrations on about 70 ha, yield gain of 53.34 per cent (or 62.13 per cent in the other version) over farmers' practice. (3) TNAU reports rainfed 2448 kg/ha and irrigated 2535 kg/ha; the trial design behind these figures is not stated. (4) Multi-location or AICRP/ICAR trials: not found in searched sources.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. Parentage note (not a marker result): the CSC ground-truth parentage is EXTRACT OF A CROSS TMV 7 X FSB 7-2. TNAU lists the cross for VRI 10 as VRI 2 x NRCG CS 349 (derivative). The digest states that TMV 7 x FSB 7-2 is the documented pedigree of VRI 1 (released 1986, 105 days), not VRI 10, and that the brief's parentage was not confirmed for VRI 10. This conflict is unresolved.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. A combining-ability (line x tester) study uses VRI 10 as a line, but it is not genetic-marker or QTL work.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Seednet / NSC / Tamil Nadu State Seed Corporation: not found in searched sources (no Seednet listing for VRI-1 retrieved). Note: the Seednet name VRI-1 refers to a different release (VRI 1, released 1986), not VRI 10.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Moderately resistant to sucking pests and defoliators, and to leaf spot (the TNAU entry is truncated after this point, so the full list is unverified) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRI%2010.html
Moderate resistance to late leaf spot per the 2024 on-farm trial paper -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
Showed higher tolerance to root wilt than some comparators, ranking second to TCGS 1694 (pod yield 2493 kg/ha) -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
Described as having moderate resistance, with a general claim of built-in pest and disease defenses; no quantitative data -- https://tnbrdngo.org/how-the-wonder-nut-vri-10-is-elevating-farmers-standard-of-living/
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found (the rainfed/irrigated yields are listed, but no explicit stress-tolerance rating for VRI 10 was retrieved)

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderately resistant to sucking pests, defoliators and leaf spot -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRI%2010.html
Moderate resistance to late leaf spot; no in-situ germination of mature pods before harvest -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
Rust, stem rot, peanut bud necrosis and PBND resistance: No evidence found for VRI 10 specifically (DAC listing of notified varieties does not include a VRI 10 row) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Parentage conflict: TNAU lists the cross as VRI 2 x NRCG CS 349 (derivative), duration 90-95 days, oil 46-48%, growth habit bunch, average yield 2448 kg/ha rainfed and 2535 kg/ha irrigated -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRI%2010.html
The parentage given in the brief (TMV 7 x FSB 7-2) is the documented pedigree of VRI 1 (released 1986, 105 days), not VRI 10; the brief's parentage was not confirmed for VRI 10 -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/ and https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRI%2010.html
Duration 90-95 days and suitability for short-duration cropping -- https://tnbrdngo.org/how-the-wonder-nut-vri-10-is-elevating-farmers-standard-of-living/
On-farm rainfed trial (2022-23 or thereabouts): pod yield 2493 kg/ha and haulm yield 4587 kg/ha, the highest haulm yield among the varieties tested; BCR 2.86 -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
Cluster frontline demonstrations in Cuddalore district with VRI 8 and VRI 10 (2020-21 to 2022-23, 175 demonstrations, about 70 ha) reported a yield gain over farmers' practice of 53.34 per cent (the other version of the same study reports 62.13 per cent) -- https://indianjournals.com/article/lr-47-7-016 and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379741722_A_Study_on_Yield_and_Value_Sustainability_in_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_Through_Cluster_Frontline_Demonstrations_Approach_in_Cuddalore_District_of_Tamil_Nadu
Multi-location or AICRP/ICAR trial data for VRI 10: No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
QTL, marker-assisted or molecular characterization studies naming VRI 10: No evidence found
Combining ability (line x tester) study using VRI 10 as a line: see PUBLICATIONS below (not genetic-marker work)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Regional Research Station, Vriddhachalam (Cuddalore district) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRI%2010.html
Lead breeder or scientist name for VRI 10: No evidence found (no page named the breeder)
Groundnut breeding program at RRS Vriddhachalam, including the production of nucleus and breeder seed -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/milestone-achievements/ and http://www.tnau.ac.in/vri/
Release year 2022 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRI%2010.html
Release notification and CSC minutes (name, notification number): No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level contact (RRS Vriddhachalam): Dr. G. Nallathambi, Professor and Head, Regional Research Station, Vriddhachalam - 606 001, Cuddalore district; Phone 04143 – 260231; Fax 04143 – 261120; E-mail arsvri@tnau.ac.in -- http://www.tnau.ac.in/vri/ (page may be out of date; the contact was listed as the institute contact, not a VRI 10 breeder contact)
Breeder email, phone or personal contact for VRI 10: No evidence found
Seednet portal contact: No evidence found (no seednet.gov.in page was returned)

Agricultural Science Digest -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-5929 (VRI 10 used as a line at RRS Vriddhachalam; the study does not name VRI 10 in the title)

KVK or SAU seed sales for VRI 10: No evidence found

Tamil Nadu only -- https://tnbrdngo.org/how-the-wonder-nut-vri-10-is-elevating-farmers-standard-of-living/
Season-wise recommendation across Tamil Nadu zones (kharif, rabi and summer seasons, including Villupuram, Thiruvallur, Kancheepuram, Cuddalore, Perambalur/Ariyalur, Tiruchirappalli, Thanjavur, and others): https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/Crop-improvement%20-1.html
