seednet_fields.Parentage: Hybrid derivative of the cross between ALR 3 and AK 303
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology:
Kharif (Rainfed) and Rabi / summer (Irrigated)
Rainfed-Chitraipattam(April-May), Adipattam(June-July), Aippasipattam (Oct.) 
Irrigated-Summer(April-July), Margazhipattam(Dec-Jan), Masipattam (Feb-Mar)
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Highly responsive to fertilizers and suitable for timely sowing under rainfed conditions.  Seed rate 4-5 kg/ha
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics:
Plant medium tal with profuse branching
1.	Stem: cylindrical, dark green, slightly pubescent, non pigmented at the base
2.	Leaf: lyrate pinnatipartite, glabrous on upper epidermis and slightly pubescent on lower epidermis.
3.	Flower cylindrical two valved with flat apical beak non pubescent
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Fairy tolerant to moisture stress and lesser susceptible to biotic stress.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Moderately resistant to whire rust, resistant to staghead and downy an powdery mildew
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Comparatively less attacked by aphids as compared to existing checks.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Under rainfed condition, basal application of 30 kg N and 20 kg P2O5 is recommended for taramira.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VRI 9 / VRI-4 -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The CSC name is "VRI 9" and the Seednet name is "VRI-4". The parentage in the record (VG 5 x NC AC 17090) matches the TNAU record for VRI 4, not VRI 9. The 2022 release year does not match the TNAU record for VRI 4, which was released in 1996 and notified in 1997. I could not confirm that VRI 9 and VRI-4 are the same variety, so the findings below are labelled by name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- VRI 9 (name match): Moderate resistance to late leaf spot and rust, plus some thrips and leafhopper tolerance, is reported for VRI 9 in a 2024 trial. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for VRI 9 were found. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
- VRI 9 (name match): The same trial describes VRI 9 as showing low disease incidence and suitability for rainfed conditions, but this is a qualitative statement, not a stress-tolerance test. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
- VRI-4 (Seednet name, TNAU record): The record gives no stress-tolerance data. The Radhamani and Singh (2008) germplasm table describes VRI 4 only as high yielding and early. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/322066029_Radhamani_J_and_Singh_AK_2008_Conservation_and_Utilization_of_Genetic_Resources_of_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L_in_India_Proc_Indian_Natn_Sci_Acad_74_3131-147

DISEASE AND PEST
- VRI 9: Moderate resistance to late leaf spot and rust, with thrips and leafhopper also noted. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
- VRI-4: The TNAU record lists no disease or pest resistance. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- VRI 9 (2024 on-farm/trial comparison): Pod yield 2340 kg/ha and haulm yield 4486 kg/ha, with a duration of 115 days and an average yield of 2500 kg/ha reported. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
- VRI 9 (breeding line use): VRI 9 was used as a parental line in a combining-ability study at TNAU Vridhachalam, where it had higher mean pods per plant. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-5929
- VRI-4 (TNAU record): Duration 110 days, rainfed yield 1660 kg/ha, irrigated yield 2171 kg/ha, with small dark-green leaves and 1-4 seeded pods. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/

GENETICS AND QTL
- VRI-4 (pedigree): VG 5 x NcAc 17090 (Spanish Bunch), released 1996, notified 662(E)/17.9.97. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/
- VRI 9: No pedigree, marker or QTL study for VRI 9 was found. The only VRI 9 record is the CSC parentage in the input. No evidence found for QTL or marker work.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution (both names): Regional Research Station, Vriddhachalam, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/
- No named lead breeder for VRI 9 or VRI-4 was found in the retrieved pages. No evidence found for a named breeder.
- Institutional mandate: The station works on groundnut, sesame and cashew breeding. -- http://www.tnau.ac.in/vri/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. G. Nallathambi, Professor and Head, Regional Research Station, Vriddhachalam, 606 001 (postcode truncated in the source). Institute-level contact only. -- http://www.tnau.ac.in/vri/
- Phone: 04143-238231 / 99943 15004. Email: arsvri@tnau.ac.in. Listed for RRS Vridhachalam. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf
- Postal address (partial): Located 5 km from Vriddhachalam town on the Vriddhachalam–Cuddalore road. -- http://www.tnau.ac.in/vri/

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2024). Title not retrieved. Group paper on VRI 9 trial results. International Journal of Research in Agronomy 7(6): 224-226 -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Assessment of Combining Ability Analysis for Pod Yield and its Attributing Traits in Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.). Agricultural Science Digest. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-5929
- Radhamani, J. and Singh, A.K. (2008). Conservation and Utilization of Genetic Resources of Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.) in India. Proceedings of the Indian National Science Academy 74(3): 131-147. Lists VRI 4 with its pedigree. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/322066029_Radhamani_J_and_Singh_AK_2008_Conservation_and_Utilization_of_Genetic_Resources_of_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L_in_India_Proc_Indian_Natn_Sci_Acad_74_3131-147
- KrishiKosh, AICRP and ICAR annual reports: searched, not retrieved within this query budget. No evidence found for VRI 9 or VRI-4.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- VRI 9 and VRI-4: No seed-stock listing naming either variety was found. No evidence found from NSC, TANSEDA, KVK or dealer listings.
- Related but not admissible: The 2021 TNAU seed stock report lists VRI 8 at RRS Vridhachalam (45,142 units). This is a different variety. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf
- Contact for enquiries: RRS Vridhachalam, 04143-238231, arsvri@tnau.ac.in. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- VRI 9: No official recommendation was found. Only the input record states Tamil Nadu. No evidence found from a notification source.
- VRI-4: A TNAU seasonal table lists VRI 4 among rainfed varieties for the North Western Zone of Tamil Nadu. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/Crop-improvement%20-1.html

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: VRI-4 (variety_name and seednet_variety_name both "VRI-4"; crop "sesame" per the record, but Seednet lists GROUNDNUT)

SEARCH COVERAGE NOTE: The search tool hit its usage limit. Only one search returned usable results (query "VRI-4 sesame variety"). Results from the breeder/institution and research queries were lost to a script error, and no seed-availability search was run. Treat the headings below as incomplete.

RECORD CONFLICT (read first): The TNAU Vridhachalam groundnut table lists a different VRI 4 as a groundnut variety, with pedigree VG 5 x NcAc 17090 (Spanish Bunch), released 1996, notification 662(E)/17.9.97. That pedigree matches the parentage in this record, and the Seednet crop is GROUNDNUT. The sesame-specific page gives a different parentage (VRI 2 x GT 10) and a 2022 release year. The record may therefore mix a groundnut variety with a sesame name. The groundnut findings are not attributed to sesame below; they are listed only as a conflict.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Sesame VRI 4 page lists only the 'Moderately resistant to phyllody and root rot' trait under sesame; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found for sesame VRI 4 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/sesame%20vri%204.html
Groundnut VRI 4 (not this crop) is recorded as a special-feature line only, with no stress data -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/

DISEASE AND PEST -- Sesame VRI 4 page: 'Moderately resistant to phyllody and root rot' -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/sesame%20vri%204.html
No pest-resistance evidence found for sesame VRI 4 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/sesame%20vri%204.html

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Sesame VRI 4 page: year of release 2022; duration 85-90 days; seasons Masipattam, Chithiraipattam and Thaipattam; irrigated average yield 957 kg/ha; branching growth habit; oil content 50%; semi-erect, indeterminate, profusely branching, 4-loculed, brown seeds -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/sesame%20vri%204.html
No multi-location or rainfed trial data found for sesame VRI 4 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/sesame%20vri%204.html

GENETICS AND QTL -- Sesame VRI 4 page gives parentage as VRI 2 x GT 10, which conflicts with the record's VG 5 x NC AC 17090 -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/sesame%20vri%204.html
No QTL or marker studies found -- (none retrieved)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Regional Research Station, Vridhachalam (institute page; sesame VRI 4 listed under the sesame VRI series) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/milestone-achievements/
The milestone page lists only sesame VRI (Sv) 1, 2 and 3, not VRI 4 -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/milestone-achievements/
No lead breeder name found for sesame VRI 4 -- (none retrieved)

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact, email, phone or postal address found in retrieved content. The institute's Vridhachalam research page is the only institute source retrieved -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for sesame VRI 4. Retrieved pages were about other varieties: a mutation-study paper using VRI 1, VRI (Sv) 2 and other sesame lines -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Description-of-sesame-varieties-used-in-present-mutation-studies_tbl1_343164432 ; and TMV (Sv) 7 -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/2824 (not this variety, so excluded).

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found (seed-availability search not run because the tool limit was reached).

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found for sesame VRI 4 in the retrieved pages. The state list in the record (Maharashtra, Telangana, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu) is unverified. The record also repeats Andhra Pradesh.

NEXT STEPS: Check the CSC release minutes for whether this entry is sesame or groundnut, and confirm the parentage and variety code A0402016 against Seednet. Then rerun the breeder/contact, publications and seed-availability searches once the tool quota resets.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: Only an ambiguous yield figure from institutional annual reports is available. There are no documented stress or climate traits and no peer-reviewed citations. Under the methodology this fits 'only yield info, no stress/citation' (40). The annual reports are institutional sources, not research citations, so a score of 60 is not justified. The yield data are also unclear, so the score is tentative and could fall toward 20.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Released 2022 by AAU, Gujarat. Limited trial yield data. No stress, disease or pest data available.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: GVG 11 (Anand Bahar) is a guar variety released in 2022 and associated with Anand Agricultural University, Gujarat. The only evidence is fragmentary mentions in AAU annual reports, with ambiguous yield figures. No stress tolerance, disease or pest resistance, molecular, breeder or commercial information was found, so evidence quality is low.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Guar variety released in 2022, apparently by AAU, Anand. Maturity, parentage, adaptation and yield potential are not specified, and only unclear trial figures (106-129 q/ha) appear in an annual report.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No evidence was found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance, or for disease and pest resistance. Stress tolerance is unknown, and the Gujarat score is a tentative 40.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for Karan Guar-2 (RGS-3) itself. The searches did not return any stress-tolerance record under that name or code.
- Related line, Karan Guar 14 (RGr 18-1), not Karan Guar-2: It also showed resistance/tolerance to important diseases and insects and was recommended for different states of India -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597
- Different cultivar, HG 2-20 (CCS HAU, Hisar): suitable under rain fed situations and this variety is tolerant to drought conditions. -- https://www.agricultureinformation.com/forums/threads/officially-released-guar-varieties-details-from-agri-univerity.103226/

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for Karan Guar-2 (RGS-3). Karan Guar 14 is reported as resistant/tolerant to disease and insects (see above, https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597).
- Different cultivar: This variety is resistant to BLB and (RGC 1066, Guar Lathi; text truncated in the snippet) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384757778_Cluster_Bean_Cyamopsis_tetragonoloba

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found for Karan Guar-2 (RGS-3) yield, maturity or trial data. Note the name and code were not matched in any record.
- Karan Guar 14 was tested at one station: its seed trials ran at RARI, Durgapura, Jaipur during the rainy (kharif) season of 2016 and 2017 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597
- Karan Guar 14 yield comparison: The newly developed variety Karan Guar-14 has good galactomannan over the check RGC 1066 (1773 kg/ha), RGC 1033 (2110 kg/ha) and HG 2-20 (2180 kg/ha). -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597
- Zone-specific agronomy for Rajasthan (AINP on Arid Legumes, SKNAU Jobner) is available but does not name Karan Guar-2 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391521739_PRODUCTION_TECHNOLOGY_OF_GUAR_FOR_ZONE-IIIA_RAJASTHAN

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for Karan Guar-2 (RGS-3) parentage, markers or QTL. The user-supplied parentage is "Not specified", and no source confirmed it.
- Karan Guar 14 was developed from a cross: developed by crossing two genotypes, RGC 1038 (RGC 516 × HG 75) and RGC 1017 (Naveen × HG 75) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370515204_Karan_guar_14_A_new_high-yielding_and_quality_gum_content_variety
- Genome reference (RGC-936, not Karan Guar-2): a chromosome-scale assembly was reported at ICAR-NIPB New Delhi -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-33762-3

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution (per the user record and the CSC/Karan Guar 14 sources): Rajasthan Agricultural Research Institute, Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University (SKNAU), Durgapura, Jaipur. Verified for the sister cultivar Karan Guar 14: at Rajasthan Agricultural Research Institute, (Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University, Jobner, Rajasthan) Durgapura, Jaipur, Rajasthan -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370515204_Karan_guar_14_A_new_high-yielding_and_quality_gum_content_variety
- Institute profile: Rajasthan Agricultural Research Institute (RARI) is a constituent research institute under Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University, Jobner, Jaipur. -- https://raridurgapura.org/varieties-developed.htm
- Breeder names for Karan Guar-2: No evidence found. The RARI variety list names Karan Guar 1 and Karan Guar 14 and Karan Guar 15 but not Karan Guar-2 -- https://raridurgapura.org/varieties-developed.htm

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder name, email and phone: No evidence found.
- Institute address as printed in a sister-cultivar paper: Rajasthan Agricultural Research Institute, Durgapura, Jaipur, Rajasthan 302 018, India -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597
- Institute web page: https://raridurgapura.org/varieties-developed.htm (no email or phone was retrieved from it)

PUBLICATIONS
- Choudhury, P. R. and Singh, R. K. (year not shown in retrieved record). Growth, varietal development and cultivar diversity in seed production chain of cluster bean (Cyamopsis tetragonoloba) in India. Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences (ICAR e-pubs) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/view/125470 (covers the variety list 1976–2023, which includes Karan Guar 14 but was not checked for Karan Guar-2)
- Karan guar 14: A new high-yielding and quality gum content variety (authors and year not shown in retrieved record). Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences (ICAR e-pubs) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597
- Chauhan, P. S. and Chhabra, K. (year not shown). Cluster Bean, Chapter 4, Agronomy of Leguminous Crops (regional overview) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/341343072_Chapter_-4_Cluster_Bean_Agronomy_Leguminous_Crops_A_Regional_Overview_CHAPTER_-4_Cluster_Bean
- Pathak, R. (2015). Cluster Bean: Physiology, Genetics and Cultivation. Springer Singapore (book, cited in CABI chapter) -- https://www.cabidigitallibrary.org/doi/10.1079/9781800624658.0005
- No Karan Guar-2 (RGS-3) specific paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh record was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for Karan Guar-2 (RGS-3) from NSC, a State Seed Corporation, a KVK, SKNAU or a dealer. The seed listings found (eBay, Amazon, Amazing Seeds, Golden Hills Farm) are generic cluster bean or vegetable seed and do not name this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Karan Guar-2 (user-supplied record only, not verified by any retrieved source): Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.
- Sister cultivar Karan Guar 14 was recommended for different states of India, including Rajasthan, Haryana, Gujarat and Maharashtra. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597

drought.details: The original CSC record (ground truth) states the variety is tolerant to drought conditions, but the evidence digest contains no quantitative or source-backed drought evaluation specific to NRC 197. The level is set to medium only to reflect the unqualified 'tolerant' designation in the CSC record; the digest does not grade the degree of tolerance and no mechanisms were found. The sources cited below do not support drought tolerance: the stem fly screening paper classed NRC 197 as resistant to pests, not drought, and the khetivyapar source describes lodging tolerance and non-shattering pods. The digest also notes that the variety is reported as suitable for rainfed kharif conditions, which is not a drought-tolerance measurement.

disease_resistance.summary: No evidence found for resistance to yellow mosaic virus (YMV), pod blight, Rhizoctonia or other diseases specific to NRC 197. The digest notes that a different ICAR variety, NRC 149, is reported for those diseases, but not NRC 197. The original CSC record lists disease reaction as 'Not Specified'.

pest_resistance.summary: Stem fly: in a field screening trial, NRC 197 showed low stem fly infestation and tunnelling and was classed as resistant; the digest reports it among the genotypes with the lowest infestation (pooled two-year data). The khetivyapar source states the variety is resistant to pest attacks, particularly stem fly. Semilooper: high resistance. Spodoptera litura: moderate resistance. The original CSC record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SEARCH NOTE: Four searches were run. The Seednet name RGC-197 and the crop label "GUAR (CLUSTER BEAN/FIELD VETCH)" returned no evidence. The evidence below refers to NRC-197 (soybean), and the Seednet crop label appears to be an error.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Found as a stem fly screening trial: NRC 197 showed low stem fly infestation and tunnelling, and was classed as resistant, not as drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. -- https://arccarticles.s3.amazonaws.com/OnlinePublish/Final-article-attachemnt-with-doi-LR-5312-6089603e9087340b9bdcbbb1.pdf
- The variety is non-shattering, tolerant to lodging, and resistant to pest attacks, particularly stem fly. -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to NRC 197.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Additionally, it exhibits high resistance to semilooper and moderate resistance to Spodoptera litura. -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888
- Stem fly resistance is reported in the field screening paper, which found NRC 197 among the genotypes with the lowest infestation. -- https://arccarticles.s3.amazonaws.com/OnlinePublish/Final-article-attachemnt-with-doi-LR-5312-6089603e9087340b9bdcbbb1.pdf
- No evidence found for YMV, pod blight, Rhizoctonia or other disease resistance specific to NRC 197. (A different ICAR variety, NRC 149, is reported for those, but not NRC 197.) -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Soybean Variety NRC 197 is an early duration variety maturing in 113 days which is a very suitable option for hilly areas. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/soybean-variety-nrc-197/
- A different source gives about 112.67 days to maturity. -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888
- Its average productivity was observed to be 1624 kg/ha and a maximum production capacity of 2072 kg/ha was observed in the trials. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/soybean-variety-nrc-197/
- A different source gives about 16.24 quintals per hectare. -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888
- Rainfed kharif suitability is reported. -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888
- Trial details (number of locations, seasons, check varieties, plot design) were not found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- The variety was developed through marker-assisted selection. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/soybean-variety-nrc-197/
- It is reported to be free of Kunitz trypsin inhibitor (KTI). -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/soybean-variety-nrc-197/
- No QTL, marker names, or linked-marker studies specific to NRC 197 were found.
- Parentage ("selection from local collection of Nagour district") was not confirmed by any search result. No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Soybean Research (IISR), Indore, Madhya Pradesh. -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888
- The institute is also named ICAR-NSRI (National Soybean Research Institute) on its own pages and posts. -- https://x.com/ICARNSRI/status/1826264887900918126
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.
- Institute director named in the 2024 AICRP meeting report: Dr. K.H. Singh. -- https://icar.gov.in/en/annual-group-meet-aicrp-soybean
- Earlier director named in a news report: Dr Nita Khandekar (older source, may be outdated). -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/icar-develops-new-climate-smart-soyabean-varieties-for-cultivation/
- Release context: Four soybean varieties namely NRC 197, JS 23-03, JS 23-09, and RSC 11-42 were identified for notification. -- https://icar.gov.in/en/annual-group-meet-aicrp-soybean
- The Prime Minister dedicated NRC 197 and NRC 149 to the nation, as reported by ICAR-NSRI. -- https://x.com/ICARNSRI/status/1826264887900918126

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. No evidence found for a named breeder's email or phone.
- Institute website as given on Wikipedia: iisrindore.icar.gov.in -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Soybean_Research
- Institute location: Indore, Madhya Pradesh (coordinates only; no postal address text found). -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Soybean_Research
- Institute website from the ICAR-NSRI variety page: icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html
- No official email, phone or postal address for IISR was found in the retrieved text.

PUBLICATIONS
- Field screening of soybean genotypes for stem fly resistance, including NRC 197 (pooled two-year data). Authors, year and journal not shown in retrieved text. -- https://arccarticles.s3.amazonaws.com/OnlinePublish/Final-article-attachemnt-with-doi-LR-5312-6089603e9087340b9bdcbbb1.pdf
- Proceedings of the 54th Annual Group Meet of AICRP on Soybean, held 13-14 March 2024 at UAS Dharwad, where NRC 197 was identified for notification. Report or proceedings title and DOI not found. -- https://icar.gov.in/en/annual-group-meet-aicrp-soybean
- No KrishiKosh theses, peer-reviewed NRC 197 papers, or DOIs specific to the variety were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings for NRC 197 or RGC-197.
- Institute-level context: There are about 30 varieties are in seed chain at present. -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html (the page does not confirm NRC 197 is among them).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- It is the first variety of the northern hilly region which is free from the non-nutritious Kunitz Trypsin Inhibitor and has been found suitable for the hill districts of Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/soybean-variety-nrc-197/
- Identified as the northern hill zone variety at the 2024 Variety Identification Committee meeting. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/top-4-recommended-varieties-of-soybean-for-2024/
- Release year: the evidence supports identification in March 2024 and a formal dedication around August 2024. The record's year_of_release (2024-08-02) could not be checked against a notification gazette. -- https://icar.gov.in/en/annual-group-meet-aicrp-soybean

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for "Selection 1" or "Selection-1" specifically. Generic guinea grass tolerance is described for the species, not this clone: KAU's ad hoc Package of Practices says the grass tolerates drought and deep seasonal flooding, and it grows under coconut shade -- https://pop.kau.in/foddercrops.htm
- A general guinea grass review notes drought tolerance from a deep root system, again species-level, not variety-level -- https://masjaps.com/index.php/mas/article/download/12/8/8

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for Selection 1 or Selection-1 disease or pest resistance in any search result.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found for Selection 1 or Selection-1 yield or trial data. KAU's Package of Practices gives species-level figures (about 80-100 t/ha green fodder per year, six to seven harvests) -- https://pop.kau.in/foddercrops.htm
- KAU Vellayani's 2021-22 ZREAC report lists guinea grass varieties under evaluation as Harithasree, Culture-2 and CO(GG)-3, with no mention of Selection 1 -- https://kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/soft_copy_of_xxxix_zreac_meeting.pdf
- Tamil Nadu's forage package lists CO(GG)3 as a clonal selection from Mombasa, with 340-360 t/ha/year green fodder, but this is a different variety -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/10_Guinea_Grass.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for the parentage "clonal selection from JHGG-96-3" or for the JHGG-96-3 accession. The JHGG prefix appears in an IGFRI-style listing for Bundel Guinea-4 (JHGG-08-1), which is a different variety; any link to Selection 1 is unverified -- https://www.leafconagro.com/guinea-grass-variety-bundel-guinea-4-jhgg-08-1/
- Background only: a 2025 GWAS of 124 guinea grass accessions from CIAT's collection (not this clone) -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41469560/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No evidence found for a breeder or developing institute for Selection 1 or Selection-1. The "Institution" field in the record is unresolved.
- The Indian guinea grass varieties found in search (Bundel Guinea series, Harithasree, Punjab Guinea grass-1) are attributed to other programmes, not to Selection 1 -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1046&context=igc
- KAU lists guinea grass varieties Haritha, Marathakom and Harithashree on its Regional Agricultural Research Station (Vellanikkara/Vellayani-region) crop page; none is Selection 1 -- https://rarsvni.kau.in/crops-0

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. No email or phone number for any Selection 1 breeder was in the results.
- Institute-level fallback: Kerala Agricultural University, Thrissur (established 1971, KAU research directorate at Vellanikkara) -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/communities/f7008b74-5b73-4d58-9553-330fd59e07c7?spc.page=1&spc.sf=dc.date.accessioned&spc.sd=DESC&scope=f7008b74-5b73-4d58-9553-330fd59e07c7
- KAU Directorate of Seeds and Planting Material Production, Vellanikkara (price proceedings signed there, 2025). No phone or email shown in the extract -- https://www.kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/price_list_seeds_and_planting_materials_2025-26_website.pdf
- Regional Agricultural Research Station (Southern Zone), Vellayani, KAU: Dr. Usha C. Thomas, Professor and Head, Instructional Farm, is the PI on the fodder variety evaluation trial. This is not a Selection 1 breeder contact; no email or phone found -- https://kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/soft_copy_of_xxxix_zreac_meeting.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found for any paper, report or thesis on Selection 1 or Selection-1. The KrishiKosh search returned only the KAU community page, not a Selection 1 record -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/communities/f7008b74-5b73-4d58-9553-330fd59e07c7?spc.page=1&spc.sf=dc.date.accessioned&spc.sd=DESC&scope=f7008b74-5b73-4d58-9553-330fd59e07c7

SEED AVAILABILITY
- KAU sells guinea grass fodder slips ("Guinea grass & other varieties") at 0.75 per slip under the 2025-26 price revision. The variety name is not specified, so Selection 1 availability cannot be confirmed -- https://www.kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/price_list_seeds_and_planting_materials_2025-26_website.pdf
- KAU's 2025 price order says sale is permitted only for varieties recommended by ICAR institutes or SAUs. Selection 1 is not listed as a recommended variety, which conflicts with a Seednet release record and should be checked -- https://www.kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/price_list_seeds_and_planting_materials_2025-26_website.pdf
- No NSC, state seed corporation or private dealer listing for Selection 1 was found. The search covered this only in part, as the fourth search was used for KAU sources.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The raw record says "Kerela", which I read as Kerala. KAU's package of practices calls guinea grass suited to Kerala conditions, but it names no release for Selection 1 -- https://pop.kau.in/foddercrops.htm
- Name note: the record uses "Selection 1" (CSC minutes) and "Selection-1" (Seednet). Searches returned no evidence under either name.
- Year of release is unknown ("NaT" in the record). No CSC or Seednet notification was found, so the release status is unverified.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The search for "GM-6 greengram variety" returned CO 6 greengram (a different variety, Tamil Nadu) and nothing naming GM-6 or GPM-6 for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The same searches returned only a CO 6 yellow mosaic resistance paper (https://masujournal.org/view_archive_journal.php?id=1821), which is a different variety and was discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. The search returned a seed biopriming study using "GM-3" greengram seed (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336513295_In_vitro_Investigation_of_Seed_biopriming_in_Green_gram). GM-3 is a different variety, so it was discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. No search result mentioned QTL, marker or pedigree work for GM-6 or GPM-6.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. The query on GM-6 with Navsari Agricultural University returned a ResearchGate paper with a Navsari author (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336513295_In_vitro_Investigation_of_Seed_biopriming_in_Green_gram). It does not mention GM-6 and cannot be attributed to this variety. The release metadata supplied with the request (institution: Pulses and Castor Research Station, Navsari Agricultural University; parentage: pureline selection from Bijarpur local) is input data, not search evidence, and no page confirmed it.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No institute page, email, phone or address for the Pulses and Castor Research Station, Navsari Agricultural University, was returned.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. The only greengram research result was the seed biopriming paper, which concerns GM-3 and was discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The search for "GPM-6 horse gram Kulthi variety seed" returned only a Vikaspedia horse gram cultivation page (https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/pulses/horse-gram?lgn=en). That page is about horse gram, a different crop, so it was discarded. The Seednet name "GPM-6" is listed under horse gram, which conflicts with the greengram crop in the record. No Seednet entry was retrieved to confirm this.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found in search results. The only state listed is the one supplied in the request, Gujarat (release date 2018-08-10). Neither is confirmed by any retrieved page.

Search log: 4 searches were run (the cap). Queries: "GM-6 greengram variety"; "GM-6 greengram breeder Navsari Agricultural University"; "GM-6 greengram research paper"; "GPM-6 horse gram Kulthi variety seed". Recommended next steps: search seednet.gov.in directly for GPM-6 and check its crop field, and search the Navsari Agricultural University or KrishiKosh site for the Pulses and Castor Research Station's release notification.

seednet_fields.Resemblence to Variety: KBHG-1 BUT SEEDS BOLDER THAN KBHG -1 SEEDS AND RESISTANT TO YMV DISEASE BUT KBHG -1 IS SUSCEPTIBLE.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: 1. SOWING DATES : JUNE - SEPTEMBER BUT AUGUST TO SEPTEMBER IS IDEAL. 2. SPACING : 45X 10 CM, 3. seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT : 43-45 CMS. 1. SEMI SPREADING GROWTH HABIT 2. TALLER PLANT HEIGHT WITH HIGH BASAL BRANCHING 3. BOLD SEED SIZE.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: RESISTANT TO YMV DISEASE AND MODERATELY RESISTANT TO RHIZOCTONIA ROOT ROT DISEASE.

seednet_fields.Resemblence to Variety: NOT RESEMBLING WITH OTHER RECOMMENDED VARIETIES.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: RECOMMENDED FOR RELEASE AND CULTIVATION IN NORTHERN LOCATIONS OF INDIA COMPRISING GUJARAT, RAJASTHAN, UTTARAKHAND, JHARKHAND, UTTAR PRADESH AND MAHARASHTRA UNDER RAINFED CONDITION IN KHARIF SEASON.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: TIME OF SOWING: LAST WEEK OF JUNE TO FIRST WEEK TO JULY; FERTILIZER : 20:40:0 NPK KG/HA; LODGING : RESISTANT; SHATTERING: NIL; SHOWING : TIMELY; FODDER YIELD : HIGH.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: SEMI DETERMINATE PLANT HABIT, SEMI SPREADING GROWTH HABIT, LIGHT GREEN STEM AND FOLIAGE, ATTRACTIVE BRICK RED BOLD SEED.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT : 52 CM; WEIGHTED MEAN : 54; RANGE OVER LOCATION : 48-60; PLANT HABIT : SEMI-DETERMINATE; PLANT: GROWTH HABIT : SEMI SPREADING; DAYS TO FLOWERING : EARLY (48 DAYS); STEM: COLOUR : LIGHT GREEN; STEM ANTHOCYANIN COLOURATION : ABSENT; FOLIAGE COLOUR : LIGHT GREEN; TERMINAL LEAFLET SHAPE : OBLONG; LEAF PUBESCENCE : HIGH AND PUBESCENT; LEAF VEIN COLOUR : LIGHT GREEN; PETIOLE COLOUR : REDDISH GREEN; PETIOLE LENGTH : 2-3 CM; LEAF SENESCENCE : PRESENT; CALYX COLOUR : LIGHT GREEN; INFLORESCENCE : RECEMOSE; RECEME POSITION : 2-3 CM; POD: CONSTRICTION : SLIGHT; POD BEAK SHAPE : POINTED AND CURVED; POD SIZE : MEDIUM; POD CURVATURE : CURVED; POD SHAPE : CYLINDRICAL; SEED: COLOUR : DARK BRICK RED; SEED SHAPE : RHOMBOID; SEED: COLOUR PATTERN : UNIFORM; LUSTURE ON SEED SURFACE : SHINY; SEED SIZE (100 SEED WEIGHT) : 3.39 G.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: THE VARIETY WAS RESISTANT TO ROOT ROT AND MODERATELY RESISTANT TO POWDERY MILDEW, COLLAR ROT, CERCOSPORA LEAF SPOT AND LEAF BLIGHT. FOR ANTHRACNOSE THE INCIDENCE WAS LESSER THAN THE CHECKS.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: THE VARIETY GHG 5 WAS FREE FROM THE ATTACK OF FEEDER AND LEAF MINOR PESTS, WHILE THE POPULATION OF APHIDS, JASSIDS AND MITES WERE AT PAR WITH CHECKS WELL BELOW ETL, LEVEL.

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: DRYLAND FARMING RESEARCH STATION, DIRECTORATE OF RESEARCH, MAHARANA PRATAP UNIVERSITY OF AGRI. & TECHNOLOGY, UDAIPUR - 313001 (RAJ.)
seednet_fields.Resemblence to Variety: IT RESEMBLES WITH THE VARIETY MARU KULTHI WITH RESPECT TO SEED COLOUR.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: RECOMMENDED FOR (RAJASTHAN, GUJARAT, M.P., HARYANA, ETC) IN KHARIF SEASON (NORTHERN ZONE) FOR GRAINS AS WELL AS FODDER PURPOSE IN MARGINAL LANDS. IT IS HIGHLY DROUGHT TOLERANT AND CAN BE GROWN WHERE THE RAINFALL IS UNCERTAIN AND ERRATIC.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: IT IS MAINLY SOWN IN KHARIF SEASON WITH ONSET OF MONSOON UNDER RAINFED CONDITIONS. MOSTLY SOWN AFTER COMPLETION OF SOWING OF OTHER CROPS AND ON LOW FERTILE AS WELL AS ON MARGINAL LANDS, WHICH RESULTS IN LOWER YIELDS; SPACING : NARROW ROW SPACING (30 CM) GAVE HIGHER SEED YIELD IN COMPARISON TO BROAD SPACING (45 CM); FERTILIZER : APPLICATION OF 10 KG. N AND 30 KG. PHOSPHORUS GAVE HIGHER SEED YIELD IN COMPARISON TO 5 KG. N AND 15 KG. PHOSPHORUS APPLICATION. FURTHER IT DID NOT RESPOND SIGNIFICANTLY TO SULPHUR APPLICATION 20-25 KG/HA; SOWING TIME : KHARIF SEASON (ONSET OF MONSOON). THE VARIETY GAVE HIGHER SEED YIELD (13.9, 17.6 AND 17.3%) OVER CHECK IN EARLY, NORMAL AND LATE SOWN CONDITIONS, RESPECTIVELY IN DIFFERENT YEARS. IT SHOWS ITS SUITABILITY FOR ALL THE SOWING CONDITIONS; IRRIGATION : RAIFNED.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT : 30-50 CM; IT IS HAVING LUSH GREEN FOLIAGE WITH SOME WAXY DEPOSITION. IT HAS 2-12 PRIMARY BRANCHES WITH 23-65 PODS PER PLANT. SEED IS BOLD WITH BRICK RED COLOUR, WHICH IS PREFERRED BY THE CONSUMERS.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: NO SUCH STUDY WAS MADE BUT IT WAS OBSERVED THAT IT CAN GROW SUCCESSFULLY IN POOR SOILS AND MOISTURE STRESS CONDITION IN BARANI LANDS WHERE NO OTHER CROPS COULD PROFITABLY GROWN. BEING TOLERANT TO DROUGHT IT MAKES EFFICIENT UYSE OF AVAILABLE SOIL MOISTURE AND THRIVES WELL IN AREAS HAVING SCANTY RAINFALL. THIS WAS OBSERVED AT DFRS, ARJIA, BHILWARA IN THE YEAR 2002 THAT ALMOST ALL THE CROPS FAILED TO PRODUCE SEED YIELD EXCEPT HORSEGRAM, PARTICULARLY VARIETY AK-42 WHICH GAVE HIGHEST SEED YIELD (301 KG/HA.) IN COMPARISON TO CHECK AK-21 (218 KG/HA) IN COMPARISON TO CHECK AK-21 (218 KG/HA) IN COMPARISON TO CHECK AK-21 (218 KG/HA) WHICH WAS 38 PERCENT HIGHER, INDICATES ITS TOLERANCE TO STRESS CONDITION.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: NO INCIDENCE OF ANY DISEASES UNDER NATURAL CONDITIONS WAS OBSERVED.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: NO INSECT PEST ATTACK WAS OBSERVED UNDER NATURAL CONDITIONS.

drought.details: The variety is observed to grow successfully in poor soils and moisture stress conditions in rainfed (barani) lands, efficiently utilizing available soil moisture and thriving in areas with scanty rainfall, where other crops might not profitably grow. While no specific study for Pratap Kulthi-2 was cited in the 'stress_reaction' field, an observation from DFRS, Arjia, Bhilwara in 2002, recorded that horsegram variety AK-42 produced a high seed yield (301 kg/ha, 38% higher than check AK-21) during a period when almost all other crops failed, indicating its tolerance to stress.

agronomic_details.stability: The variety demonstrated stability across different sowing conditions, yielding 13.9%, 17.6%, and 17.3% higher than the check in early, normal, and late sown conditions, respectively, across different years. This indicates its suitability for various sowing timings.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for Kharif season, typically sown with the onset of monsoon under rainfed conditions. It is suitable for cultivation on low fertile and marginal lands. Shows suitability for early, normal, and late sowing conditions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: Trials indicated higher seed yield over checks in early (13.9%), normal (17.6%), and late (17.3%) sown conditions across different years. Recommended agronomic practices include narrow row spacing (30 cm) for higher seed yield compared to broad spacing (45 cm). Fertilizer application of 10 kg N and 30 kg Phosphorus resulted in higher seed yield compared to 5 kg N and 15 kg Phosphorus; it did not respond significantly to 20-25 kg/ha Sulphur application.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VL GAHAT 19 (VLG-19) EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name and crop notes:
- Release-minute name: "VL Gahat 19". Seednet name: "VL Gahat 10". The evidence below refers to VL Gahat 19 unless a line says otherwise.
- Crop mismatch: the input says chickpea, but every source found describes horse gram (Macrotyloma uniflorum, gahat/kulthi). Seednet also lists horse gram. No chickpea evidence was found.
- Searches run: 4 (release/agronomy, breeder/contact, research, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Horse gram as a crop is described as extremely drought-resistant, but no variety-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for VL Gahat 19 was found. -- https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/pulses/horse-gram?lgn=en
- General crop note: horse gram is grown on drylands under low-to-moderate rainfall. Not variety-specific. -- https://krishipatrika.com/2021/05/21425/
- Crop is said to tolerate winter extremes. Not variety-specific. -- https://doi.org/10.3390/metabo13020165

DISEASE AND PEST
- Horse gram yellow mosaic virus (HgYMV) causes alarming yield loss in the crop. No VL Gahat 19 resistance rating was found. -- https://doi.org/10.3390/metabo13020165
- Seed treatment with fungicide is recommended against soil fungal pathogens. Not variety-specific. -- https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/pulses/horse-gram?lgn=en
- No VL Gahat 19 disease or pest reaction data found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Release table lists VL Gahat 19 with release/notification year 2010 (Kumar 2007 table, cited in a review). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356086546_HORSEGRAM-A_SUPREMACY_NUTRITIONAL_SOURCE_A_REVIEW
- Hill sowing advisory: VL Gahat 15 and 19 for hill Gahat, sown in the first fortnight of June. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/Extension_Edu/02.05.2020_Kharif_season_Advisory.pdf
- Improved package of practice is said to give 6–10 q grain/ha, depending on monsoon. Crop-level FLD figure, not variety-specific. -- https://dpd.gov.in/Horse_gram.PDF
- No VL Gahat 19 yield table or multi-location trial data found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL, marker, or genetic study on VL Gahat 19 found. Parentage given in the input (VLG 1 x NIC 2659) was not verified by any source.
- Related but different material: induced mutant and multi-environment studies on TNAU lines and Paiyur 2 (not VL Gahat 19). -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-67282-5

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institute: ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan (VPKAS), Almora, Uttarakhand. Brand listed as VPKAS on the seed portal. -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/VLGahat19_%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%80.%E0%A4%8F%E0%A4%B2.%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B9%E0%A4%A419
- VPKAS is named as the source of VL Gahat-8 and VL Gahat-10 in the release table. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356086546_HORSEGRAM-A_SUPREMACY_NUTRITIONAL_SOURCE_A_REVIEW
- Lead breeder name: not found.
- Uttarakhand's agriculture minister said the state lacks newly certified horse gram varieties and asked ICAR for new ones. -- https://garhwalpost.in/minister-ganesh-joshi-participates-in-icars-97th-agm-in-delhi/

CONTACT DETAILS
- ICAR-VPKAS, Mall Road, Almora-263601, Uttarakhand, India (institute address as listed on an aggregator page). -- https://www.indiamart.com/icarvpkas/
- Name listed: AMIT PASCHAPUR (Scientist), VPKAS. Role and email are not verified against an official page. Phone number was hidden on the page. -- https://www.indiamart.com/icarvpkas/
- No official email or phone number for VPKAS, and no breeder email, was found in the search results.
- Institute website and seed-portal contact pages were not retrieved. Confirm contacts on the VPKAS website before use.

PUBLICATIONS
- No variety-specific paper, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis on VL Gahat 19 was found.
- Kumar (2007). Varietal releases table, horse gram (cited in a review). Source for the 2010 VL Gahat 19 release year. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356086546_HORSEGRAM-A_SUPREMACY_NUTRITIONAL_SOURCE_A_REVIEW
- Jafarullakhan S. S. et al. (2024). Assessing the yield and nutrient potential of horse gram mutants through a multi-environment-based experiment. Scientific Reports (not VL Gahat 19). -- DOI 10.1038/s41598-024-67282-5

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety is mentioned in two 2023 publications, but only in snippets that are truncated or ambiguous. No stress trait, yield figure, or Gujarat-specific data can be attributed to it with confidence. The 'at least one stress trait' criterion for 60 or 75 is not clearly met. The possible climate-resilience association and the citations nominally place it between 40 and 60, so 50 is assigned as a conservative score. A score of 40 would be defensible if the IIVR listing is judged not to be climate evidence. Full-text verification could raise or lower the score.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Kashi Bouni Sem-9 is a 2022 Indian bean (dolichos bean) variety, apparently from ICAR-IIVR and developed through inter-varietal breeding. The 30 search results are repeats of two ResearchGate documents with truncated snippets, so no stress tolerance, yield, or commercial availability can be confirmed. Evidence quality is low and the Gujarat score is 50.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Dolichos bean variety released in 2022, probably by IIVR Varanasi and developed through inter-varietal breeding. Yield, maturity, adaptation and recommended states are not documented.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: Stress tolerance is not demonstrated. The snippets that mention drought, heat, salt, and virus tolerance refer mainly to tomato or other bean varieties, and any link to this variety is unverified. The full IIVR climate-resilience paper should be consulted.

The search results are 19 duplicates of one tomato-focused review, which contain no stress, disease, pest, yield, genetic or commercial data for this variety. Evidence quality is low, and suitability for Gujarat cannot be assessed.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Indian bean variety released in 2022, with first picking at 80-85 days and peak fruiting afterward. Institution, parentage, yield, adaptation and recommended states are not specified.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No variety-specific evidence of drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance, or of disease or pest resistance. Stress snippets in the source refer to tomato. The variety cannot be classified as stress tolerant on current evidence.

drought.details: HA 4 (Lablab purpureus cv. HA-4) has demonstrated tolerance to drought stress. It was subjected to drought stress for a period of eight days during its initial growth phase under strictly controlled conditions. The variety is noted in the context of drought stress tolerance and its adaptation to semi-arid, alfisol conditions, particularly relevant in regions like Bengaluru.

heat.details: HA 4 has been mentioned in the context of stress tolerance studies, including heat stress tolerance, alongside drought stress tolerance. Its adaptation to semi-arid conditions implies some degree of heat tolerance.

salinity.details: While HA-3 and HA-4 are mentioned in discussions related to salt stress studies, and research on mapping QTLs for salt tolerance in field beans is underway, a specific level of salinity tolerance for HA 4 is not detailed in the provided search results.

flood.details: No information regarding flood tolerance for HA 4 is available in the provided search results.

disease_resistance.summary: No information regarding disease resistance for HA 4 is available in the provided search results.

pest_resistance.summary: No information regarding pest resistance for HA 4 is available in the provided search results.

agronomic_details.stability: The photoperiod insensitivity of HA 4 enhances its adaptability, suggesting potential for cultivation across different seasons or regions, which can contribute to yield stability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: HA 4 is described as photoperiod insensitive, a key characteristic for wider adaptation. It is adapted to semi-arid, alfisol conditions and has shown tolerance to a 15-day delay in onset of conditions, as observed in trials near Bengaluru (Karnataka).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: HA 4 has undergone controlled drought stress experiments during its initial growth phase. It has also been evaluated in field conditions for adaptation to semi-arid, alfisol environments, including responses to delayed onset of conditions.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Tirupati Field Bean-2 (CSC name) / Tirupati Field Bean-1 (Seednet name), field bean (Indian bean, Lablab purpureus var. lignosus), RARS Tirupati, code A0307020

Scope note: I ran four searches covering both names. None returned a page that mentions either "Tirupati Field Bean-1" or "Tirupati Field Bean-2" or the parentage "LOCAL (GP-18) x HA-3". Every heading below therefore reports either an institute-level fact or "No evidence found". Nothing here confirms the 2010 release, the parentage, or the variety code.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for either name. (Searched: "Tirupati Field Bean-2 field bean variety"; "Tirupati Field Bean-1 Indian bean RARS Tirupati developed by")

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for either name. Unrelated Indian bean varieties from other programmes report disease scores (for example, Gujarat Junagadh Indian Bean-2 had leaf spot and leaf blight intensities compared with a check) -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2019.00207.2 (not this variety).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for either name. The only trial-type result is for a different Indian bean (Gujarat Junagadh Indian Bean-2, green pod yield 112.46 q/ha vs check 89.56 q/ha) -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2019.00207.2 (not this variety).

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage LOCAL (GP-18) x HA-3 was not confirmed by any source. The HA-3 name appears only as a photo-insensitive vegetable type in an export listing -- https://bwellinternational.com/product/field-beans/ (not evidence of this cross).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Tirupati, under Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU). RARS was established in 1979 and its stated mandate centres on groundnut and cropping systems, with pulses as a verification function -- https://www.angraurabitpt.org/who-are-we. salinity.details: CSSRI's technology listing states CS 60 is recommended for saline soils up to ECe 12.0 dS/m and alkali soils up to about pH 9.5, and is highly suitable for saline-sodic soils. CSSRI's varieties page gives lower limits (ECe about 9.0 dS/m, pH about 9.3, and 6-9 dS/m in another passage), so the tolerance ceiling differs between CSSRI sources and should be verified before use. A seedling-stage metabolomics study reports that CS 60 accumulated more differentially expressed metabolites than the sensitive line CS 245-2-80-7 under salt stress, with antioxidant-defence pathways protecting against osmotic and oxidative stress and more active photosynthesis. The reported trial performance in All India Salinity Alkalinity Tolerant Variety Trials could not be confirmed because the abstract is truncated. The level is rated high on the basis of the breeder-site recommendations and the mechanistic study; the discrepancy in stated limits lowers confidence in the precise ceiling.

salinity.details: Released as a salt-tolerant Indian mustard for irrigated sodic conditions in Uttar Pradesh, sown by about 25 October. The variety is described as tolerant of sodic soil up to pH 9-9.3 (2022 annual report). Yield is 21-22 q/ha in sodic soil and 25-28 q/ha in normal soil and water, with about 39.5% oil (annual report); the PSA page gives 21-23 q/ha for sodic soil and 25-28 q/ha for normal soil. No salinity threshold values (soil ECe or irrigation water ECiw) specific to CS 61 were found. The general Indian mustard thresholds of 8.2 dS/m soil ECe and 12 dS/m ECiw come from a different source and apply to the crop, not to CS 61. The 2022 annual report describes a sowing-date trial of salt-tolerant mustard varieties on saline Vertisols, but CS 61 results were not separated out in the retrieved text. The 'high' rating reflects the release purpose and reported sodic-soil tolerance; no quantitative salinity threshold for CS 61 was found.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Annual report 2022 lists CS 61 as resistant to Alternaria blight, white rust, powdery mildew and downy mildew; the retrieved text is truncated after 'powdery and downy'. The PSA page lists CS 61 as tolerant of key diseases and aphids. No independent field-scoring data for CS 61 was found, so the evidence is self-reported by the release sources.

pest_resistance.summary: PSA page lists CS 61 as tolerant of aphids. No independent field-scoring data or pest-specific trial results for CS 61 were found.

agronomic_details.yield: Annual report 2022: 21-22 q/ha in sodic soil and 25-28 q/ha in normal soil and water, with about 39.5% oil. PSA page: 21-23 q/ha for sodic soil and 25-28 q/ha for normal soil. Original variety data record: 20-22 q/ha. Sources differ on the sodic-soil range; the CSC-preferred record (20-22 q/ha) is the closest to the annual report value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location yield data for CS 61 were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Uttar Pradesh, Rabi season, irrigated sodic conditions with timely sowing. Annual report gives a sowing deadline of 25 October.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 132 To 0Days (CSC record). Sources conflict: about 136 days in the annual report and 132 days on the PSA page.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height conflicts between sources: 168 cm in the annual report and 181 cm on the PSA page. Other morphological characteristics: Not specified in the input record and Not found in searched sources.

salinity.details: Released as a salt-tolerant Indian mustard for irrigated sodic conditions in Uttar Pradesh, sown by about 25 October. Yield is 21-22 q/ha in sodic soil and 25-28 q/ha in normal soil and water, with about 39.5% oil (annual report); the PSA page gives 21-23 q/ha for sodic soil and 25-28 q/ha for normal soil. No salinity threshold values (soil ECe or irrigation water ECiw) specific to CS 61 were found. The 2022 annual report describes a sowing-date trial of salt-tolerant mustard varieties on saline Vertisols, but CS 61 results were not separated out in the retrieved text. The 'high' rating reflects the release purpose and reported sodic-soil tolerance; no quantitative salinity threshold for CS 61 was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Name: the evidence uses "CS 13000-3-2-2-5-2 (CS 61)", which matches the Seednet name. The CSC release-minute name was not found separately.
- Released as a salt-tolerant Indian mustard for irrigated sodic conditions in Uttar Pradesh, sown by about 25 October; the variety is described as tolerant of sodic soil up to pH 9-9.3 -- https://cssri.res.in/PSSU/Publications/Annual%20Report/2022/Annual%20Report%202022%20-%20English.pdf
- Yield is 21-22 q/ha in sodic soil and 25-28 q/ha in normal soil and water, with about 39.5% oil -- https://cssri.res.in/PSSU/Publications/Annual%20Report/2022/Annual%20Report%202022%20-%20English.pdf (the PSA page gives 21-23 q/ha for sodic soil, 25-28 q/ha for normal soil -- https://www.psa.gov.in/livelihood/10096)
- Tolerant of irrigated sodic soils; no salinity threshold values specific to CS 61 were found. General Indian mustard salinity thresholds (8.2 dS/m soil ECe, 12 dS/m irrigation water ECiw) are from a different source and apply to the crop, not to CS 61 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/257957254_Assessing_effect_of_salinity_on_oil_quality_parameters_of_Indian_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_using_Fourier_Transform_Near-Infrared_Reflectance_FT-NIR_spectroscopy
- Sowing-date evidence: the 2022 annual report describes a trial of salt-tolerant mustard varieties under different sowing dates on saline Vertisols, but CS 61 results were not separated out in the retrieved text -- https://cssri.res.in/PSSU/Publications/Annual%20Report/2022/Annual%20Report%202022%20-%20English.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Name: CS 13000-3-2-2-5-2 (CS 61).
- Listed as resistant to Alternaria blight, white rust, powdery mildew and downy mildew; the retrieved text is truncated after "powdery and downy" -- https://cssri.res.in/PSSU/Publications/Annual%20Report/2022/Annual%20Report%202022%20-%20English.pdf
- Listed as tolerant of key diseases and aphids -- https://www.psa.gov.in/livelihood/10096
- No independent field-scoring data for CS 61 was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Name: CS 13000-3-2-2-5-2 (CS 61).
- Maturity conflicts between sources: about 136 days in the annual report, 132 days on the PSA page -- https://cssri.res.in/PSSU/Publications/Annual%20Report/2022/Annual%20Report%202022%20-%20English.pdf ; https://www.psa.gov.in/livelihood/10096
- Plant height conflicts: 168 cm in the annual report, 181 cm on the PSA page -- same two URLs.
- Released for timely sowing in Uttar Pradesh, with the annual report giving a sowing deadline of 25 October -- https://cssri.res.in/PSSU/Publications/Annual%20Report/2022/Annual%20Report%202022%20-%20English.pdf
- Field trials were run at the CSSRI Karnal research farm (saline Vertisol sowing-date trial, 2022). CS 61 yields from multi-location trials were not found -- https://cssri.res.in/PSSU/Publications/Annual%20Report/2022/Annual%20Report%202022%20-%20English.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Name: the variety's parentage (CS 204-1 x CS 330-1-1) is supplied in your input; no independent source confirmed it.
- No QTL or marker study specific to CS 61 was found.
- Caution on name collision: a salt-sensitive CSSRI mutant written as "CS 61 4-1-1-100-13" (also CS 614-4-1-4-100-13) is used in recombinant inbred line mapping. It is a different line from the released variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353095103_Breeding_Mustard_Brassica_juncea_for_Salt_Tolerance_Problems_and_Prospects
- CSSRI's CS 52 (a salt-tolerant Indian mustard) has been studied for salinity transcriptomics; it is a different variety -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4429966/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Name: CS 13000-3-2-2-5-2 (CS 61); developed by ICAR-Central Soil Salinity Research Institute (CSSRI), Karnal, Haryana.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Highly responsive to fertilizers and suitable for timely sown in Salt affected soils conditions with a seed rate of 5 kg/ ha
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: The proposed variety CS 15000-1-1-1-4-2 has distinct morphological characters. Its leaf length is about 30 cm and leaf width & leaf length ratio is about 1.5. Mean number of leaf lobes are 6. Further, the cultivar has fairly long main shoot length of 71 cm.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: CS 15000-1-1-1-4-2 also showed resistance to Alternaria blight under natural conditions compared to check Rohini, DLSC-1 and PT303
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Against mustard aphid, CS 15000-1-1-1-4-2 showed lesser average aphid infestation
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Apply 80 kg nitrogen, 40 kg P2O5 per hectare. Split application of nitrogen has been found very useful for rape and mustard crop.

drought.details: This variety performs well under restricted irrigations. It has been identified as contributing to drought tolerance, with its roots and F1 hybrid lines showing drought tolerance under stress conditions. It is also listed among varieties exhibiting drought stress tolerance in Indian mustard.

heat.details: The variety is relevant in the context of high temperature (heat) stress prevalence in India for rapeseed-mustard breeding, suggesting its adaptation to such conditions, though a specific tolerance level is not stated.

salinity.details: No information found regarding salinity tolerance.

flood.details: No specific information found regarding flood tolerance. While 'excess moisture in Vertisols' is mentioned as a dual problem in the region, direct tolerance of the variety to flooding is not specified.

disease_resistance.summary: The original document does not specify disease reaction. Search results mention white rust disease of rapeseed-mustard in the context of crosses involving Chhattisgarh Sarson, but direct resistance of the variety is not explicitly stated.

pest_resistance.summary: No information found regarding pest resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yield data includes 4.30 (likely quintals/hectare) for the year 2010, and values of 6.50 and 6.60 (units unspecified) from different reports. Mean oil content is 37.48% with a range of 35.8% to 40.1% across different locations.
agronomic_details.stability: The proposed strain has resistance for lodging and shattering. It demonstrates a stable oil content across different locations.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for cultivation under after/relay cropping in paddy fields with come-up/full irrigation. It is advised in ICAR Rabi Agro-Advisories for farmers and explicitly recommended for 'Whole of Chhattisgarh'.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: 1. GROWTH HABIT - ERECT 2. APPRISED SILIQUAE. Normal agronomic practices include a seed rate of 7 kg/ha (33% higher seed rate) with partial fertilizer doses of 50:25:25 NPK kg/ha, requiring come-up irrigation and full irrigations.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has been evaluated in various trials, with yield data reported in annual and project coordinator's reports from institutions like ICAR-Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research and IGKVV Jagdalpur.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No specific genetic markers (QTL, SNP, SSR) or their positions are identified in the provided search results.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs or their effects are identified in the provided search results.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The variety's parentage is PCR-20 X RH - 819. It has been utilized in breeding programs, forming crosses such as Bio-902 x Chhattisgarh Sarson, ACN9 x Chhattisgarh Sarson, PM-26 x Chhattisgarh Sarson, and Kranti x Chhattisgarh Sarson. These crosses have demonstrated useful heterosis (e.g., PM-26 x Chhattisgarh Sarson with -8.01% heterosis) and are noted for contributing to drought-tolerant rapeseed roots and their hybrid F1 lines under stress.

genetics_and_qtl.molecular_mechanisms: The variety's parentage is PCR-20 X RH - 819. It has been utilized in breeding programs, forming crosses such as Bio-902 x Chhattisgarh Sarson, ACN9 x Chhattisgarh Sarson, PM-26 x Chhattisgarh Sarson, and Kranti x Chhattisgarh Sarson. These crosses have demonstrated useful heterosis (e.g., PM-26 x Chhattisgarh Sarson with -8.01% heterosis) and are noted for contributing to drought-tolerant rapeseed roots and their hybrid F1 lines under stress.

agronomic_performance.yield: Reported yield data includes 4.30 (likely quintals/hectare) for the year 2010, and values of 6.50 and 6.60 (units unspecified) from different reports. Mean oil content is 37.48% with a range of 35.8% to 40.1% across different locations.
agronomic_performance.stability: The proposed strain has resistance for lodging and shattering. It demonstrates a stable oil content across different locations.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Suitable for cultivation under after/relay cropping in paddy fields with come-up/full irrigation. It is advised in ICAR Rabi Agro-Advisories for farmers and explicitly recommended for 'Whole of Chhattisgarh'.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: 1. GROWTH HABIT - ERECT 2. APPRISED SILIQUAE. Normal agronomic practices include a seed rate of 7 kg/ha (33% higher seed rate) with partial fertilizer doses of 50:25:25 NPK kg/ha, requiring come-up irrigation and full irrigations.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: The variety has been evaluated in various trials, with yield data reported in annual and project coordinator's reports from institutions like ICAR-Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research and IGKVV Jagdalpur.

heat.details: The variety is heat tolerant at the seedling stage and shows general tolerance to heat stress. It demonstrated higher heat use efficiency in relation to seed yield.

salinity.details: Giriraj was included in evaluations for seed yield under various conditions, but the provided results do not explicitly state its tolerance level to salinity. Another variety, CS 64, is specifically mentioned as salt tolerant in the same context.

flood.details: No information found regarding flood tolerance.

basic_info.institution: Sorghum Research Station, Deesa; Sardarkrushinagar Dantiwada Agricultural University

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to GDJ 1 (Banas Surya). A 2018 water-deficit study at Deesa lists DS 172, which the GDJ 1 paper gives as an earlier trial name, but the study never names GDJ 1, so it was excluded.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to GDJ 1 in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to GDJ 1 in the searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to GDJ 1 in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No evidence names GDJ 1 with a disease resistance rating. The statements 'moderately resistant to leaf blight and anthracnose' were attributed to GJ 45 (SDAU Jowar Moti) in the digest and were excluded for GDJ 1.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources for a confirmed pest resistance rating in GDJ 1. Shoot fly resistance: the GDJ 1 paper reports 2021-22 work at Deesa on SSR markers linked to shoot fly resistance, but the snippet does not confirm that GDJ 1 was the material studied, so this is not attributed to GDJ 1. The 'lower shoot fly and stem borer infestation' statement belongs to GJ 45 and was excluded. The SDAU Deesa centre page lists 'chemical control of sorghum shoot fly and stem borer' as an achievement, which is not tied to GDJ 1.

agronomic_details.yield: Mean grain yield of 2506 kg/ha over 21 locations (including the preliminary trial); mean dry fodder of 167.0 q/ha over 22 locations. North Gujarat: 2576 kg/ha grain and 228.7 q/ha dry fodder across seven trials.
agronomic_details.stability: Grain and fodder yields were reported across 21 to 22 locations, and North Gujarat results were reported across seven trials against checks GJ 39, GJ 42, GJ 43, GNJ 1 and CSV 20. No further stability analysis (e.g., GxE statistics) was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Developed and reported for the semi-arid region of Gujarat (per the release paper title). No agro-climatic analysis beyond this was found.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Tall plants, very long and broad leaves, semi-loose panicle, medium-bold yellow-white grain. Dual-purpose (grain and dry fodder) per the release paper title.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Preliminary evaluation trial in kharif 2016. (2) State multilocation trials in kharif 2017 to 2019. (3) Entry in the AICRP-Sorghum IVT in kharif 2018 as SPV 2565 at fifteen locations. (4) 2019 location data (Deesa, Surat, Udaipur) appear in a results table of the GDJ 1 paper; the digest gives no values for these. (5) Multilocation summary: mean grain yield 2506 kg/ha over 21 locations and dry fodder 167.0 q/ha over 22 locations. (6) North Gujarat: 2576 kg/ha grain and 228.7 q/ha dry fodder across seven trials versus checks GJ 39, GJ 42, GJ 43, GNJ 1 and CSV 20. Agronomic practice trials specific to GDJ 1: not found in searched sources.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources for GDJ 1-specific markers. The 2021-22 Deesa SSR study linked to shoot fly resistance is not confirmed as involving GDJ 1 or its parents. Pedigree (not marker data): SPV 2113 x GFS 5, developed by pedigree selection at the Sorghum Research Station, SDAU, Deesa.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL or marker-trait association for GDJ 1 was found.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Not found in searched sources. No NSC or State Seed Corporation entry for GDJ 1.
commercial_info.kvk: Not found in searched sources. No KVK entry for GDJ 1. The SDAU Deesa centre mandate includes seed production of released sorghum varieties but does not name GDJ 1 for seed sales.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No evidence names GDJ 1 with a disease resistance rating. The statements 'moderately resistant to leaf blight and anthracnose' were attributed to GJ 45 (SDAU Jowar Moti) in the digest and were excluded for GDJ 1.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources for a confirmed pest resistance rating in GDJ 1. Shoot fly resistance: the GDJ 1 paper reports 2021-22 work at Deesa on SSR markers linked to shoot fly resistance, but the snippet does not confirm that GDJ 1 was the material studied, so this is not attributed to GDJ 1. The 'lower shoot fly and stem borer infestation' statement belongs to GJ 45 and was excluded. The SDAU Deesa centre page lists 'chemical control of sorghum shoot fly and stem borer' as an achievement, which is not tied to GDJ 1.

genetics_and_qtl.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources for GDJ 1-specific markers. The 2021-22 Deesa SSR study linked to shoot fly resistance is not confirmed as involving GDJ 1 or its parents. Pedigree (not marker data): SPV 2113 x GFS 5, developed by pedigree selection at the Sorghum Research Station, SDAU, Deesa.
genetics_and_qtl.qtl_information: No QTL or marker-trait association for GDJ 1 was found.

agronomic_performance.yield: Mean grain yield of 2506 kg/ha over 21 locations (including the preliminary trial); mean dry fodder of 167.0 q/ha over 22 locations. North Gujarat: 2576 kg/ha grain and 228.7 q/ha dry fodder across seven trials.
agronomic_performance.stability: Grain and fodder yields were reported across 21 to 22 locations, and North Gujarat results were reported across seven trials against checks GJ 39, GJ 42, GJ 43, GNJ 1 and CSV 20. No further stability analysis (e.g., GxE statistics) was found.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Developed and reported for the semi-arid region of Gujarat (per the release paper title). No agro-climatic analysis beyond this was found.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Tall plants, very long and broad leaves, semi-loose panicle, medium-bold yellow-white grain. Dual-purpose (grain and dry fodder) per the release paper title.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: (1) Preliminary evaluation trial in kharif 2016. (2) State multilocation trials in kharif 2017 to 2019. (3) Entry in the AICRP-Sorghum IVT in kharif 2018 as SPV 2565 at fifteen locations. (4) 2019 location data (Deesa, Surat, Udaipur) appear in a results table of the GDJ 1 paper; the digest gives no values for these. (5) Multilocation summary: mean grain yield 2506 kg/ha over 21 locations and dry fodder 167.0 q/ha over 22 locations. (6) North Gujarat: 2576 kg/ha grain and 228.7 q/ha dry fodder across seven trials versus checks GJ 39, GJ 42, GJ 43, GNJ 1 and CSV 20. Agronomic practice trials specific to GDJ 1: not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to GDJ 1 (Banas Surya). The only drought-related hit was a 2018 water-deficit study at Deesa that lists DS 172, which the GDJ 1 paper gives as an earlier trial name. That study never names GDJ 1, so I excluded it. -- https://ndpublisher.in/admin/issues/IJAEBv14n4k.pdf
Shoot fly resistance: the GDJ 1 paper reports work at Deesa in 2021-22 on SSR markers linked to shoot fly resistance, but the snippet does not confirm that GDJ 1 was the material studied. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358562511_Electronic_Journal_of_Plant_Breeding_Research_Article_A_novel_high_yielding_dual-purpose_sorghum_variety_GDJ_1Banas_Surya_for_semi-arid_region_of_Gujarat

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found that names GDJ 1 with a disease or pest resistance rating. The "moderately resistant to leaf blight and anthracnose" and "lower shoot fly and stem borer infestation" statements belong to GJ 45 (SDAU Jowar Moti), so I excluded them. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396423609_GJ_45_SDAU_JOWAR_MOTI_-_A_NEW_DUAL_SORGHUM_VARIETY_FOR_SEMI-ARID_REGION_OF_GUJARAT_INDIA
The SDAU Deesa centre page lists "chemical control of sorghum shoot fly and stem borer" as an achievement, but this is not tied to GDJ 1. -- https://www.sdau.edu.in/Research/81

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
GDJ 1 is a sorghum entry with a maturity of 100-105 days, tall plants, very long and broad leaves, and a semi-loose panicle with medium-bold yellow-white grain. -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.017 (DOAJ record: https://doaj.org/article/aaa34372196e43929e59c0c7cede1bdb)
Yield: mean grain yield of 2506 kg/ha over 21 locations including the preliminary trial, and mean dry fodder of 167.0 q/ha over 22 locations. -- https://doaj.org/article/aaa34372196e43929e59c0c7cede1bdb
North Gujarat: 2576 kg/ha grain and 228.7 q/ha dry fodder across seven trials, against checks GJ 39, GJ 42, GJ 43, GNJ 1 and CSV 20. -- https://doaj.org/article/aaa34372196e43929e59c0c7cede1bdb
Trial history: preliminary evaluation trial in kharif 2016, state multilocation trials kharif 2017 to 2019, and entry in the AICRP-Sorghum IVT in kharif 2018 as SPV 2565 at fifteen locations. -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.017 (DOAJ record) and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396423609_GJ_45_SDAU_JOWAR_MOTI_-_A_NEW_DUAL_SORGHUM_VARIETY_FOR_SEMI-ARID_REGION_OF_GUJARAT_INDIA
2019 location data (Deesa, Surat, Udaipur) appear in a results table of the GDJ 1 paper. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358562511_Electronic_Journal_of_Plant_Breeding_Research_Article_A_novel_high_yielding_dual-purpose_sorghum_variety_GDJ_1Banas_Surya_for_semi-arid_region_of_Gujarat
No evidence found for agronomic practice trials specific to GDJ 1.

GENETICS AND QTL
Pedigree: SPV 2113 × GFS 5, developed by pedigree selection at the Sorghum Research Station, SDAU, Deesa. -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.017
No QTL or marker-trait association for GDJ 1 was found. The shoot fly SSR study mentioned above is not confirmed as involving GDJ 1 or its parents. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358562511_Electronic_Journal_of_Plant_Breeding_Research_Article_A_novel_high_yielding_dual-purpose_sorghum_variety_GDJ_1Banas_Surya_for_semi-arid_region_of_Gujarat

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Named authors of the release paper: R. A. Gami, R. N. Patel, P. R. Patel and S. K. Jain. The page does not assign lead-breeder roles. -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.017
Developing institution: Sorghum Research Station and AICRP Sorghum, Sardarkrushinagar Dantiwada Agricultural University (SDAU), Deesa-385 535, Gujarat. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358562511_Electronic_Journal_of_Plant_Breeding_Research_Article_A_novel_high_yielding_dual-purpose_sorghum_variety_GDJ_1Banas_Surya_for_semi-arid_region_of_Gujarat
The SDAU Centre for Millets Research (Deesa) lists GDJ 1 (Banas Surya) among its developed and released varieties. -- https://www.sdau.edu.in/Research/81
A CV from SKNAU lists Dr. Shailesh Kumar Jain's Deesa posting (2008-2018) and GDJ-1 among his work, but it does not state his role in releasing this variety. -- https://www.sknau.ac.in/uploads/staff/resumes/resume_209_1770999672.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
No individual breeder email or phone was found. Institute-level contact from the AICRP-Sorghum cooperating centres list: Officer In-charge, AICSIP, Sorghum Research Station, Sardarkrushinagar Dantiwada Agricultural University, Banaskantha, Deesa – 385 535; phone 02744-223673 (F), 220865 / 02744-220865 (O); email deesa@millets.res.in. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sorghum/partners/list-of-centres/
Postal address for the Deesa centre: Deesa 385 535, Banaskantha, Gujarat. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274254345_Diversity_of_Sorghum_Sorghum_bicolor_L_Moench_germplasm_from_Gujarat_India_Corresponding_Author

PUBLICATIONS
Gami, R. A., Patel, R. N., Patel, P. R., Jain, S. K. (2021). A novel high yielding dual-purpose sorghum variety GDJ 1 (Banas Surya) for semi-arid region of Gujarat. Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding 12(1): 109-121 -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.017
The SDAU research-article page lists the same title under Forage Research without a matching author list. Treat this listing as needing verification. -- https://sdau.edu.in/researcharticlesjournals/0
Not found: KrishiKosh theses, AICRP annual reports naming GDJ 1, or conference papers specific to GDJ 1.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The search returned no seed-sale listing, NSC/State Seed Corporation entry, KVK entry or SAU seed-sales page for GDJ 1. A Deesa licensed-dealer directory was returned, but it names no variety and was excluded. -- https://www.napanta.com/seed-dealer/gujarat/banas-kantha/deesa/
The SDAU Deesa centre mandate includes seed production of released sorghum varieties, but it does not name GDJ 1 for seed sales. --
